Synopsis: Altering the definition of "sexual abuse" for purposes relating to civil actions for child sexual abuse to include any act that involves an adult allowing or encouraging a child to engage in certain activities; establishing certain limitations on damages that may be awarded under the Act; repealing the statute of limitations in certain civil actions relating to child sexual abuse; repealing a statute of repose for certain civil actions relating to child sexual abuse; providing for the retroactive application of the Act; etc.
Title: Civil Actions - Child Sexual Abuse - Definition, Damages, and Statute of Limitations (The Child Victims Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Pornography -see also- Nudity and Sexual Displays; Obscenity
Torts -see also- Libel and Slander; Med Malp; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: The Child Victims Act of 2023 eliminates the statute of limitations and statute of repose for civil lawsuits alleging child sexual abuse, allowing survivors to bring claims at any time and retroactively reviving previously time-barred claims for living victims. The bill defines sexual abuse, caps noneconomic damages for revived claims against private defendants at $1.5 million, raises the liability cap for claims against the State, local governments, and county boards of education to $890,000, and establishes minimum liability insurance requirements for school boards.
responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer's Office
stakeholders: Survivors of child sexual abuse, alleged perpetrators, private and non-profit organizations, county boards of education, state and local government entities, and civil litigation attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: State reimbursable fund expenditures increase by $70,700 in FY 2024 (increasing to $96,096 by FY 2028) for the State Treasurer's Office to hire an additional claims adjuster. State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) special fund expenditures and agency general fund expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount due to litigation expenses, claims payments up to $890,000 under the Maryland Tort Claims Act, and higher agency insurance premiums. General fund costs for the Judiciary and the Office of the Attorney General may also increase to process new cases. Local government and school board expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount due to increased litigation, higher liability exposure (up to $890,000 per claimant), and higher insurance or self-insurance pool costs. Revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Treasurer's Office administers the Maryland Tort Claims Act (MTCA) and the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF). The bill increases State liability limits for sexual abuse claims to $890,000 and repeals the statute of limitations, causing a significant fiscal and operational impact on SITF, including the need to hire additional claims personnel to investigate and defend lawsuits.

The bill eliminates the statute of limitations for child sexual abuse civil actions and retroactively revives time-barred claims, which is anticipated to generate a significant volume of complex litigation in Maryland circuit courts. It also creates a statutory right to immediate interlocutory appeal on motions to dismiss based on constitutionality.

The bill amends Section 4-105 of the Education Article, requiring the State Board of Education to update and establish minimum liability insurance standards (raised to at least $890,000 for sexual abuse claims) for county boards of education across Maryland.

As the State's primary legal representative, the OAG is responsible for defending the State and its agencies against revived and prospective tort claims filed under the expanded MTCA provisions, potentially requiring additional litigation resources.

Under the amended Education Article § 4-105, the State Insurance Commissioner oversees regulations and approves the terms and conditions of individual self-insurance programs maintained by county boards of education to satisfy the increased minimum liability coverage requirements.

Synopsis: Allowing a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for certain union dues paid during the taxable year; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification - Union Dues

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes a subtraction modification against Maryland individual income tax for qualifying union dues paid during the taxable year that were deductible under the Internal Revenue Code prior to January 1, 2018, capped at up to $250 per taxable year.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland union members who pay union dues and Maryland local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $9.88 million in FY 2024, with revenue losses growing to $11.56 million by FY 2028. State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 only for one-time computer programming modifications by the Comptroller's Office. Local income tax revenues decrease by $6.45 million in FY 2024 and $7.54 million in FY 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector and administrator of individual income taxes, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing the new income tax subtraction modification for union dues, including updating tax forms, instructions, and processing systems, requiring a $50,000 expenditure in FY 2024.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose of the Maryland State Police Gun Center to include the tracking, screening, and vetting of all firearms surrendered under final protective orders in the State; and requiring each law enforcement agency to report to the Center the number and type of firearms surrendered, the jurisdictions where the firearms were surrendered, and certain information regarding the individual who surrendered each firearm under final protective orders.
Title: Maryland State Police Gun Center – Firearms Surrendered Under Final Protective Orders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Expands the role of the Maryland State Police Gun Center to include the tracking, screening, and vetting of firearms surrendered under final protective orders, requiring the Center to maintain a statewide database and directing local law enforcement agencies to report details on surrendered firearms.
responsible_party: Department of State Police (Maryland State Police Gun Center)
stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies, individuals subject to final protective orders required to surrender firearms, and petitioners seeking domestic violence protective orders.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory duties of the Maryland State Police Gun Center, requiring it to expand its purpose and maintain a statewide database to track, screen, and vet firearms surrendered under final protective orders.

The Maryland Judiciary and court system issue final protective orders requiring the surrender of firearms under the Family Law Article, and the Administrative Office of the Courts served as an information source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Repealing a certain prohibition on prosecuting a person for rape or a certain sexual offense against a victim who was the person's legal spouse at the time of the alleged rape or sexual offense.
Title: Criminal Law - Sexual Crimes - Repeal of Spousal Defense
bill_summary: Repeals the spousal defense in Maryland criminal law, thereby removing the exemption from prosecution for rape and certain sexual offenses committed against a person's legal spouse.
responsible_party: Maryland State's Attorneys and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Spouses, victims of domestic and sexual assault, and individuals charged with rape or sexual offenses
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and local incarceration expenditures increase minimally due to the expanded application of existing criminal incarceration penalties. State and local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands prosecution for rape and sexual offenses against a spouse, which will result in additional convictions and commitments to State correctional facilities overseen by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The repeal of the spousal defense expands criminal liability for sexual offenses, increasing caseloads and the demand for legal representation for indigent defendants handled by the Office of the Public Defender.
The bill removes statutory bars to prosecution, allowing new rape and sexual offense cases between spouses to be filed and adjudicated within the state court system.
The OAG represents the State in criminal appeals, which will include appellate proceedings and statutory interpretation arising from the repeal of the spousal defense.
As the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for criminal investigations, MSP will investigate reported allegations of sexual assault regardless of the marital relationship of the parties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP oversees statewide criminal justice strategies, funding, and victim services programs that support survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of General Services to establish and periodically update standards for State buildings to conserve energy and minimize adverse impacts on birds; requiring the Maryland Green Building Council to include the standards in certain requirements established for the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program; defining "State building" as one acquired, constructed, or renovated by the State or one for which 50% of the money for acquisition, construction, or renovation came from State funds; etc.
Title: Department of General Services - Energy-Conserving Standards (Maryland Sustainable Buildings Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: The Maryland Sustainable Buildings Act of 2023 requires the Department of General Services (DGS) to establish and periodically update energy-conserving and bird-friendly building standards for State-funded building projects and existing State buildings. It mandates shielding and minimizing building lighting during peak bird migration seasons and incorporates these standards into the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program, while exempting certain public works and public school construction projects.
responsible_party: Department of General Services
stakeholders: State agencies, occupants and employees of State buildings, building design and construction contractors, and local bird populations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State construction and maintenance costs across all funds cannot be reliably estimated, as design adjustments (such as alternative glass or mitigation features) and automatic lighting controls depend on feasibility within budgetary constraints. Over time, State utility costs may decrease due to reduced lighting and energy conservation. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency responsible for developing, establishing, and updating bird-friendly and energy-conserving building standards, adopting regulations, and retrofitting existing state buildings with automatic lighting controls where practicable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Green Building Council incorporate the newly established standards into the requirements of the Maryland High Performance Green Building Program for State buildings.

As noted in the fiscal note, USM manages a significant portion of State-owned buildings outside of DGS jurisdiction and will be impacted by the new construction, renovation, and operational lighting standards.
MDOT manages a substantial inventory of State-owned facilities and buildings that may be subject to the bill's standards for capital construction, substantial alterations, and lighting controls.

Synopsis: Requiring that equity be considered when State transportation plans, reports, and goals are developed; altering the membership of the advisory committee on State transportation goals; requiring the Maryland Department of Transportation to conduct transit equity analyses, cost-benefit analyses, and consult with certain communities before announcing or proposing any major service change or any reduction or cancellation of a certain capital expansion project in the construction program; etc.
Title: Equity in Transportation Sector - Guidelines and Analyses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Language -see also- Communication; Electronic Comm; Telecomm
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires equity to be incorporated into Maryland State transportation planning, reporting, and goals. It requires the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT), in collaboration with the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA), to conduct transit equity analyses, cost-benefit analyses, and community outreach before implementing major service changes or reducing/canceling certain capital expansion projects. It also requires the MTA to develop alternatives to minimize disparate impacts or disproportionate burdens and adds new representation to the State transportation advisory committee.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) and Maryland Transit Administration (MTA)
stakeholders: Public transit users—especially racial minority communities, low-income individuals, riders with disabilities, transit-reliant populations, seniors, and riders with limited English proficiency—as well as transportation consulting small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund special fund expenditures increase by $602,600 in FY 2025, reflecting costs for three new permanent positions, contractual consultants, and mandated transit equity and cost-benefit analyses. Ongoing annual costs are estimated at $544,700 in FY 2026 and $557,100 in FY 2027. State revenues are not directly affected. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary state department responsible for implementing the bill, including incorporating equity goals into the Maryland Transportation Plan, evaluating disparity indicators, and collaborating on transit equity and cost-benefit analyses.

MTA is directly tasked with developing transit equity policies, conducting equity and cost-benefit analyses before major service changes or capital project cancellations, holding public hearings, and publishing detailed impact reports.
The Department of Planning holds a statutory representative seat on the advisory committee that advises MDOT on State transportation goals, benchmarks, and indicators.
The Governor appoints the members and chair of the advisory committee on State transportation goals and receives the annual attainment report on transportation system performance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory composition and duties of the advisory committee on State transportation goals, benchmarks, and indicators, directing it to recommend indicators for racial, ethnic, disability, and low-income disparities.
The members of the Board of Public Works are designated statutory recipients of MTA's reports on proposed major service changes and capital project reductions or cancellations.
The Attorney General is named as a required recipient of the reports detailing transit equity analyses, cost-benefit analyses, and community outreach for service changes and project cancellations.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain local detention center officers of Talbot County in the event Talbot County becomes a participating governmental unit in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System; and providing that certain local detention center officers who join the Correctional Officers' Retirement System and receive certain service credit shall no longer be members of the Employees' Pension System and shall have no further rights to any benefit in the Employees' Pension System.
Title: Correctional Officers’ Retirement System – Talbot County
bill_summary: Requires local detention center officers in Talbot County to become members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) rather than the Employees' Pension System if Talbot County joins CORS as a participating governmental unit, granting them credit for past service without requiring them to pay the difference in contribution rates.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Talbot County detention center officers and Talbot County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. At the local level, assuming Talbot County elects to participate in CORS, its pension liabilities increase by $918,324, resulting in an annual increase of $94,000 in employer pension contributions for 25 years. There is no effect on local revenues and no discernible effect on contribution rates for other participating governmental units.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Employees' Pension System and the Correctional Officers' Retirement System. It is responsible for executing the transfer of memberships, creditable service, and associated assets and liabilities if Talbot County elects to participate.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations by December 31, 2026, to identify additional standards for water quality testing; requiring the Department, subject to certain funding and in consultation with the Department of Information Technology, to utilize an online portal to receive and upload certain information and to provide public access to the information; requiring the Department of the Environment to consistently share the information collected with the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments; etc.
Title: Private Well Safety Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: The Private Well Safety Act of 2023 requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to adopt regulations establishing additional water quality testing standards for private wells, conduct a study on long-term funding options for groundwater monitoring, and, subject to funding and in consultation with DoIT, implement an online portal for private well water quality data. The bill also mandates that contracts for the sale of real property served by private wells include a requirement for water quality testing prior to settlement, and establishes reporting duties for certified water testing laboratories.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Buyers and sellers of real property served by private wells, private well owners, residential tenants relying on private wells, State-certified water testing laboratories, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $186,800 in FY 2025, increasing to $250,700 by FY 2029 to fund three MDE positions to implement standards, manage reports, and conduct the study. Establishing the online portal carries an estimated contractual cost of $3,400,000 over two years, though portal requirements are subject to available funding. Indeterminate additional laboratory costs may be incurred by the Maryland Department of Health. State revenues are unaffected, and local fiscal impacts depend on the specific testing standards adopted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with adopting regulations for private well water quality testing standards, managing an online reporting portal, conducting a study on groundwater monitoring funding options, and receiving water quality test reports from certified laboratories.

MDH must receive private well water testing information shared by MDE, is encouraged to contribute data to the online portal, and may experience operational impacts on its Laboratories Administration for conducting additional water quality tests.
DoIT is statutorily required to be consulted by MDE in the planning and implementation of the private well water quality online portal.
The Governor's Office is required to receive a report from MDE by December 1, 2025, detailing findings and recommendations on long-term funding options for groundwater resource monitoring.

Synopsis: Repealing the authority of the Secretary of Transportation to designate transit-oriented development; establishing the Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund to promote the equitable and inclusive development of transit-oriented developments; authorizing the Department of Transportation to use the Fund to provide financial assistance to local jurisdictions; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an amount sufficient to ensure a Fund balance of at least $5,000,000; etc.
Title: Equitable and Inclusive Transit-Oriented Development Enhancement Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: The Equitable and Inclusive Transit-Oriented Development Enhancement Act establishes the Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund to provide financial assistance (grants and loans) to local governments for TOD design plans, public infrastructure improvements, and project gap funding. It expands the definition of transit-oriented development to include properties adjacent to planned or existing transit corridors, transfers TOD designation authority to the Smart Growth Subcabinet, mandates annual State appropriations to maintain a minimum fund balance of $5 million, and mandates an annual reporting requirement by the Maryland Department of Transportation on TOD progress.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Local jurisdictions, developers, small businesses, and Maryland residents—especially low-income and minority residents near transit facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by an estimated $5.0 million annually starting in FY 2024 to capitalize the fund (mandated beginning in FY 2025), with corresponding increases in special fund revenues and expenditures. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $258,249 in FY 2024 and roughly $200,000+ annually thereafter to support two administrative positions and consultant expenses. Local government revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local jurisdictions apply for and receive grants and revolving loans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund, awarding financial assistance to local jurisdictions, publishing scoring standards, and submitting annual reports on TOD efforts.
DHCD is specifically tasked in statute to collaborate with MDOT in supporting fund award recipients by providing technical services for studies, plans, and code changes.

MDP leads state smart growth and land use planning efforts and plays a central role in the Smart Growth Subcabinet, which is granted statutory authority by the bill to designate transit-oriented developments and establish eligibility criteria and scoring standards for the fund.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the new special fund separately and invest its moneys in accordance with state investment practices.
DBM oversees the state budget process, which is impacted by the bill's statutory mandate requiring an annual appropriation to maintain a fund balance of at least $5 million.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation in the annual budget bill sufficient to ensure a fund balance of at least $5.0 million at the beginning of each fiscal year.

As the MDOT modal administration operating light rail, subway, and bus transit facilities, MTA's transit stations, corridors, and ridership utilization data form the direct foundation of transit-oriented development designations and reporting under the bill.
The bill specifies that the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the newly created Transit-Oriented Development Capital Grant and Revolving Loan Fund.

The bill establishes legislative intent to prioritize transit-oriented development proposals when distributing funding from state infrastructure programs including MDOT SHA's Complete Streets Program.

Synopsis: Providing that a person who is the victim of an act that would constitute a violation of certain hate crime laws may bring a civil action against the person or persons who committed the act in a court of competent jurisdiction; and authorizing the court to impose an injunction and award certain economic and noneconomic damages.
Title: Hate Crimes – Civil Remedy

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a victim of an act that constitutes a hate crime under Maryland law to file a civil lawsuit against the person or persons who committed the act. The bill permits courts to grant injunctive relief, award attorney's fees and court costs, and award actual, economic, and noneconomic damages up to three times the amount of actual damages.
responsible_party: Judiciary (District Court and Circuit Courts of Maryland)
stakeholders: Victims of hate crimes, perpetrators facing civil liability, civil litigation attorneys, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local court proceedings may increase as a result of authorized civil actions, but the Judiciary can handle any additional caseload using existing resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a civil cause of action allowing victims of hate crimes to file lawsuits for damages and injunctive relief in Maryland District and Circuit courts, which are administered and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Repealing the authority of the court to decree a limited divorce; and altering certain grounds for an absolute divorce.
Title: Family Law - Grounds for Divorce
bill_summary: This bill repeals the authority of Maryland courts to grant a limited divorce and reforms the grounds for absolute divorce. It eliminates fault-based grounds such as adultery, desertion, criminal conviction, insanity, and cruelty of treatment, establishing instead that absolute divorce may be granted based on a 6-month separation (even if the parties reside under the same roof), irreconcilable differences, or mutual consent.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Spouses seeking a divorce or legal separation in Maryland, family law practitioners, and circuit court judges and personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $18,000 in FY 2024 only for the Judiciary to implement programming changes. There is no effect on state revenues, and the bill does not materially impact the ongoing operations, finances, or local circuit court workloads.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 14 alters the statutory grounds for absolute divorce and repeals limited divorce, requiring the Judiciary to update court forms, procedures, and case management software, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact of $18,000 for programming changes.

Synopsis: Requiring each public school to provide information to students, faculty, staff, and parents regarding who serves as the Title IX coordinator for the school, the process in place for filing a sexual misconduct complaint, and the support measures that are in place for filing a sexual misconduct complaint and how to access the support measures.
Title: Primary and Secondary Education – Title IX – Notice (Hear Our Voices Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: Requires each public school in Maryland to provide information to students, faculty, staff, and parents regarding the identity of the school's Title IX coordinator, the process for filing a sexual misconduct complaint, and available support measures for individuals filing a complaint and how to access them.
responsible_party: Maryland public schools and local school systems
stakeholders: Public school students, faculty, staff, and parents
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal effect. Local school systems can implement the notification requirements using existing resources, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and ensures public school compliance with state and federal education laws, including Title IX policies and sexual misconduct reporting standards.

As a state-operated public school serving pre-K through grade 12 students, the Maryland School for the Deaf is subject to public school statutory mandates, including providing notice regarding its Title IX coordinator, complaint procedures, and support measures.

Synopsis: Altering a certain statutory form for a general power of attorney by including certain provisions informing the principal and agent of certain matters, granting general authority with respect to tangible personal property and trusts and estates, authorizing the principal to grant the agent certain specific powers relating to successor agents, compensation, gifts, or transfers and opening joint accounts and beneficiary designations, and clarifying the force and effect of the form; etc.
Title: Maryland General and Limited Power of Attorney Act - Alterations
bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Statutory Form Personal Financial Power of Attorney and the Maryland Statutory Form Limited Power of Attorney. Among other changes, it clarifies and expands agent authority regarding tangible personal property, trusts and estate matters, disclaimers, and actions necessary to qualify for governmental benefits or programs. It also updates warnings to principals, outlines agent duties and loyalty standards, and adds optional powers regarding gifting, joint accounts, beneficiary designations, compensation, and the appointment of successor agents.
responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and Registers of Wills
stakeholders: Maryland residents creating powers of attorney (principals), appointed agents, estate planning attorneys, financial institutions, and applicants for governmental benefits or programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory power of attorney forms that include provisions concerning litigation, claims, guardianship nominations, and judicial proceedings. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the state court system where disputes regarding powers of attorney and guardianships are adjudicated.

The bill amends Maryland's statutory power of attorney forms relating to trust and estate matters, electing statutory elective shares of an estate, and obtaining wills from custodians. The Register of Wills oversees estate administration, probate records, and will safekeeping.

The bill explicitly expands and clarifies an agent's authority under statutory forms to perform acts and execute asset transfers/trusts (such as special needs trusts) to qualify principals for government programs, specifically referencing Medicaid, which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists to issue electronic licenses and registrations, except under certain circumstances; requiring the Board, on an applicant's request, to print a paper copy of the verification of licensure or registration and send it by first-class mail to the address on the application; repealing the requirement that the Board include certain information on each license and registration; and requiring the Board to send renewal notices by first-class mail under certain circumstances.
Title: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists - License and Registration Issuance and Renewals - Electronic Means

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists to issue licenses and registrations electronically instead of on paper, unless an applicant specifically requests a printed copy sent by mail. It also transitions license and registration renewal notices to electronic delivery by default, reserving first-class mail for instances when an electronic notice is returned as undeliverable or when specifically requested by the licensee or registrant.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
stakeholders: Licensed psychologists, registered psychology associates, and applicants for psychology licensure or registration in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The changes are procedural in nature and do not materially affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Psychologists is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, which regulates health care professionals. The bill directly alters the board's requirements for issuing licenses, registrations, and renewal notices electronically.

Synopsis: Requiring that the holder of a certificate of sale include the e-mail address of certain persons in certain notices required to be sent to certain persons with an interest in a property that is sold at a tax sale; authorizing certain persons with an interest in owner-occupied property sold at a tax sale to request the current payoff amount to redeem the property; providing that the payoff amount to redeem the property provided by the holder of the certificate to the owner of the property is valid for 30 days; etc.
Title: Property Tax - Tax Sales - Notices and Payoff Amount for Redemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: This bill requires holders of tax sale certificates of sale to include their email address and the tax collector's email address in required notices sent to property owners and interested parties before filing a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption. It also authorizes owners, mortgagees, and deed of trust holders of owner-occupied residential properties sold at tax sales (outside Baltimore City) to request the current redemption payoff amount prior to a foreclosure complaint being filed, specifying that the payoff amount must only include expenses incurred before the request and remains valid for 30 days.
responsible_party: Local tax collectors and holders of certificates of sale, with informational support from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (Office of the State Tax Sale Ombudsman)
stakeholders: Owners of owner-occupied residential properties sold at tax sales, mortgage holders and servicers, holders of tax sale certificates, and local government tax collection offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances. Any small business effect is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory requirements and notice conditions precedent to filing a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption on owner-occupied residential properties, which are civil actions adjudicated within the Maryland court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill affects homeowner redemption options and protections against tax sale foreclosure for owner-occupied residential properties, which intersects with DHCD's broader mission concerning homeownership preservation and housing stability.

Synopsis: Altering requirements relating to relocation plans for mobile home parks to require a plan for park residents who will be dislocated as a result of the change in land use; requiring the owner, 60 days prior to entering into a contract to sell the community, to provide notice of the terms of the offer to homeowners in the community and provide them the opportunity to purchase the housing community; requiring the Department of Housing and Community Development to list certain agencies to assist homeowners with the purchase of a community; etc.
Title: Mobile and Manufactured Homes - Relocation Plans and Sales of Communities (Manufactured Housing Modernization Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: The Manufactured Housing Modernization Act of 2023 alters relocation assistance requirements for mobile home park closures and establishes statutory procedures for the sale of manufactured housing communities. It lowers the park size threshold requiring relocation assistance from more than 38 sites to more than 10 sites and increases required assistance from 10 to 12 months of rent. It also requires owners selling a manufactured housing community to grant homeowners (via a homeowners organization) an opportunity to purchase the community, unless the purchaser files an affidavit agreeing to continue using the land as a manufactured housing community for at least five years and capping annual rent increases at 10% for the first three years.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Owners and resident homeowners of mobile and manufactured home communities, homeowners organizations, prospective community purchasers, and local housing agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The Department of Housing and Community Development and local housing agencies are anticipated to handle notice intake and the maintenance of a web-based financing resource list using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) with receiving notices of conditionally accepted purchase offers for manufactured housing communities and requires DHCD to maintain a public list on its website of organizations and county housing agencies that assist homeowners with financing.

The bill creates statutory civil causes of action and penalties ($10,000) for violations of purchase and affidavit requirements adjudicated in state courts, and requires affidavits regarding community use and rent limitations to be recorded in county land records maintained by court clerks.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically its Consumer Protection Division, oversees consumer and tenant protection issues arising under the Real Property Article and was consulted regarding enforcement and compliance provisions in the legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring an individual, in order to be licensed as a psychologist by the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, to have a doctoral degree in psychology from a certain school or university, to have received a postdoctoral respecialization certificate from a certain department of psychology that included a minimum of 1,750 hours in supervised internship, and to have completed at least 1,500 hours postcertification advanced training hours or precertification hours of service as a registered psychology associate; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Psychologists - Licensure Qualification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill alters the qualifications for psychologist licensure in Maryland by establishing a second pathway to qualify for a license issued by the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists. Under this new pathway, an applicant qualifies if they hold a doctoral degree in psychology from a regionally accredited institution, have completed a postdoctoral respecialization certificate with at least 1,750 supervised internship hours from an accredited program, and have completed at least 1,500 hours of qualifying advanced training or service alongside 2 years of professional supervised experience.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
stakeholders: Applicants seeking psychologist licensure in Maryland, particularly doctoral-level psychologists with nonclinical degrees who complete postdoctoral respecialization.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as altering the qualifications for psychologist licensure does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the licensure qualifications for psychologists administered by the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, which operates as a health occupations licensing board under the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Altering the composition of the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals; clarifying and altering the distribution of certain fees and penalties; and clarifying the application of certain license requirements and penalties.
Title: Environment - On-Site Wastewater Services - Board, Fees, and Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Alters the composition and geographic representation requirements of the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals, clarifies that licensing requirements and penalties for on-site sewage disposal system inspections apply specifically to inspections performed for property transfers, redirects administrative penalties from the Bay Restoration Fund to the Maryland Clean Water Fund, and specifies the distribution of application and renewal fees into the On-Site Wastewater Professionals Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: On-site wastewater professionals, septic system inspectors, property buyers and sellers, and members of the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations and has no net impact on special fund revenues. It results in a minimal shift of special fund administrative penalty revenue from the Bay Restoration Fund to the Maryland Clean Water Fund in fiscal years 2023, 2024, and 2025. There is no direct, material impact on local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for administering on-site wastewater property transfer inspection licenses, adopting implementing regulations, collecting fees for the On-Site Wastewater Professionals Fund, and collecting penalties directed to the Maryland Clean Water Fund.
The Governor appoints six members to the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals, and this bill alters the qualification and geographic representation requirements for those appointees.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state boards, and will need to apply the altered qualification criteria for seats on the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals.

Synopsis: Establishing that the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is in the Office of Resilience in the Maryland Department of Emergency Management; and altering the process for electing a cochair of the Council.
Title: Maryland Food System Resiliency Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: Establishes that the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is housed within the Office of Resilience in the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), adds a representative of the seafood industry to the council, alters the process for electing the council's cochair, and designates MDEM as the council's staffing agency.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management (Office of Resilience)
stakeholders: Maryland Food System Resiliency Council members, seafood industry representatives, local food council organizations, and Maryland residents affected by food insecurity and food system resilience.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Legislative Services determined that the bill does not require additional state expenditures or generate revenues because MDEM already provides staff for the council and the bill does not alter council duties. While MDEM estimated costs of $167,800 in FY 2024 for staffing and contractual services, DLS concluded those costs are not attributable to this bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally houses the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council in the Office of Resilience within the Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), designates the Secretary of Emergency Management as cochair with appointment authority, and establishes MDEM as the sole staffing agency for the council.
The Secretary of Agriculture or their designee serves as a statutory member and co-vice chair of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.
The Secretary of Human Services or their designee serves as a statutory member and co-vice chair of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.
The Secretary of Commerce or their designee is designated as an ex officio member of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MARBIDCO or their designee is designated as an ex officio member of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

The Dean of the University of Maryland College of Agriculture and Natural Resources serves as a member and co-vice chair of the council; the bill also relieves the college from statutory staffing responsibilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership, leadership election procedures, and administrative housing of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council, which is a state advisory body.

Synopsis: Requiring, in certain actions to repossess residential rental property, a landlord to submit to the clerk of the court evidence of compliance with local rental property licensure requirements and demonstrate that the landlord is compliant with the licensure requirements.
Title: Real Property – Actions to Repossess – Proof of Rental Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Requires residential landlords in jurisdictions requiring rental licenses to plead supporting facts on court-prescribed forms and demonstrate by a preponderance of the evidence at trial that the property is licensed, exempt from licensing, or unlicensed due to specified exceptions when filing actions to repossess property.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland (Judiciary)
stakeholders: Residential rental property owners/landlords, residential tenants, and the District Court in Maryland jurisdictions that require rental property licenses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected; the Judiciary can absorb any form revisions and programming costs using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the District Court of Maryland by requiring landlords filing repossession actions to submit pleadings in a form prescribed by the Judiciary demonstrating rental licensure compliance or exceptions, and requires court proceedings to adjudicate these claims.
The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General enforces consumer protection and landlord-tenant statutes and served as an information source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from making certain telephone solicitations to a certain called party in a certain manner by restricting the methods, times, and identifying information that the person making the call may utilize; providing that the Act does not apply to certain entities and circumstances; and making a violation of the Act an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice that is subject to enforcement and penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
Title: Commercial Law - Consumer Protection - Telephone Solicitation (Stop the Spam Calls Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices

bill_summary: The Stop the Spam Calls Act of 2023 regulates telephone solicitations by prohibiting automated dialing systems or recorded messages without prior express written consent, restricting call times to between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., limiting calls on the same issue to no more than three times within a 24-hour period, and prohibiting caller ID spoofing and voice-altering attempts to defraud. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforceable under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland telephone consumers and residents, commercial telemarketers, and businesses engaging in telephone solicitation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Office of the Attorney General may experience minimal costs to handle additional consumer complaints, and application of existing penalty provisions has no material fiscal impact. There is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes violations of its telephone solicitation restrictions as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is directly enforced and investigated by the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.
The bill explicitly exempts certain noncommercial solicitations for nonprofit entities only if they are registered with the Secretary of State under Title 6 of the Business Regulation Article.
The bill provides that violations are subject to civil actions and misdemeanor criminal penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which are adjudicated within the Maryland court system.

The bill references telecommunications definitions under the Public Utilities Article and preserves the continued applicability of existing provisions regarding automated dialing systems and telephone solicitations overseen under the Public Utilities Article.

Synopsis: Exempting up to $500 in a deposit account or other accounts of a judgment debtor held by a depository institution from execution on the judgment without an election by the debtor to exempt the money; establishing procedures a depository institution is required to follow on receipt of a writ of garnishment or other levy or attachment under certain circumstances; establishing a $6,000 limit on the cumulative value of property and cash that may be exempted; etc.
Title: Courts - Judgments - Exemptions From Execution
bill_summary: Exempts up to $500 in a judgment debtor's deposit or other depository institution account from execution or garnishment on a money judgment automatically, without requiring the debtor to elect the exemption. It outlines compliance and response procedures for depository institutions, caps the combined value of this exemption and existing elective exemptions at $6,000, and directs writs of garnishment to specify that only amounts exceeding the exempted sum are subject to garnishment.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Judgment debtors, judgment creditors, and depository institutions (banks, credit unions, and trust companies)
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. The State's Central Collections Unit rarely utilizes bank garnishments, and local governments are not anticipated to experience any material fiscal impact from the $500 automatic exemption.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory exemptions from execution on money judgments and requires writs of garnishment issued for bank accounts to include specific instructions regarding the automatic $500 exemption. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the state courts, including updating court forms, writ templates, and case management procedures.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which is responsible for collecting delinquent debts owed to the State. Although the fiscal note notes that CCU rarely executes judgments via bank account garnishments, the bill establishes rules that govern any such state debt collection efforts against depository accounts.

Synopsis: Requiring each county to establish a process for a person entitled to  any balance over the amount required for the payment of taxes, interest, penalties, and costs of sale to claim the balance after a tax sale foreclosure; and requiring the collector of taxes for a county to notify the prior property owner, within 90 days after delivering a deed to a purchaser, of the amount of a certain balance and the process for claiming the balance.
Title: Property Tax - Tax Sales - Payment of Balance After Foreclosure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: Requires each county to establish a uniform process for an entitled person to claim the remaining balance of a tax sale foreclosure purchase price without requiring a court order unless disputed, and requires the county tax collector to notify the prior property owner of record within 90 days after deed delivery regarding the balance amount and the claims process.
responsible_party: County governments and county tax collectors
stakeholders: Prior property owners whose properties undergo tax sale foreclosure, tax sale purchasers, and county tax offices
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that a county's process for claiming surplus tax sale proceeds may not require a court order unless there is a dispute over the balance, potentially reducing routine court filings and clarifying when judicial proceedings are required.

Synopsis: Repealing the Collaborative Care Pilot Program; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to and provide reimbursement for services provided in accordance with the Collaborative Care Model under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program – Collaborative Care Model Services – Implementation and Reimbursement Expansion

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Repeals the Collaborative Care Pilot Program and requires the Maryland Department of Health to implement and reimburse services provided under the Collaborative Care Model statewide in primary care settings serving Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) recipients.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medicaid recipients with behavioral health needs, primary care providers, and behavioral health care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by up to $15.7 million ($6.1 million general funds, $9.6 million federal funds) in FY 2024 and $20.9 million annually ($8.2 million general funds, $12.8 million federal funds) beginning in FY 2025, with federal fund revenues increasing matching amounts. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) implement and reimburse services under the Collaborative Care Model statewide through the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), resulting in an estimated fiscal impact of up to $20.9 million annually.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and fiscal management, which will be impacted by the ongoing general fund expenditure increases of over $8 million annually required to fund the expanded Medicaid entitlement services.

Synopsis: Codifying the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council as an instrumentality of the State to submit, monitor, implement, and evaluate the State Plan under the federal Rehabilitation Act in conjunction with Centers for Independent Living in the State; and requiring the Attorney General to be the legal advisor to the Council.
Title: Human Services - Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill codifies the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council as an instrumentality of the State, establishing its authority to submit, monitor, implement, and evaluate the State Plan for Independent Living under the federal Rehabilitation Act in conjunction with Centers for Independent Living. It also outlines Council governance, membership appointment criteria, operational authorities, tax-exempt status, and designates the Attorney General as its legal advisor.
responsible_party: Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities in Maryland, Centers for Independent Living, and the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and federal fund revenues may increase beginning in FY 2024. The Office of the Attorney General estimated an expenditure increase of $212,545 in FY 2024 and at least $258,000 annually thereafter for two positions to provide legal support, though the Department of Legislative Services was unable to independently validate this estimate. The bill does not materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Attorney General as the legal advisor to the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council, and the fiscal note outlines a potential expenditure increase for legal and support staff within the agency.

The Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS) within the Maryland State Department of Education serves as the Designated State Entity responsible for administering the federal Rehabilitation Act, providing administrative support/disbursements, and conducting annual audits of the Council's books and records.
The bill codifies an entity originally created by executive order and requires the Governor to appoint and hold the authority to remove members of the Council.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for state boards and councils, including the members of the Council.

As the primary state agency responsible for coordinating and improving the delivery of services to Maryland residents with disabilities, the Department's policy area directly aligns with the mission of independent living centers and the Council.

The bill explicitly specifies that the members and employees of the Maryland Statewide Independent Living Council are subject to the Public Ethics Law, which is administered and enforced by the State Ethics Commission.

Synopsis: Repealing certain limitations on the authority of certain local governments to set the time by which a property with taxes in arrears must be sold by the tax collector.
Title: Property Tax – Tax Sales – Requirement to Sell

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: House Bill 57 repeals statutory deadlines requiring local tax collectors to sell properties with taxes in arrears within specified timeframes (previously no later than two years, and one year in Calvert County), allowing local governments the flexibility to set their own timelines for property tax sales under local law.
responsible_party: Local tax collectors and county governing bodies
stakeholders: Property owners with delinquent property taxes, county and municipal governments, and small businesses participating in or affected by tax sales.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund (property tax) revenues and local government revenues may be delayed starting in fiscal year 2024 if local governments allow properties to remain in arrears longer before conducting a tax sale. State expenditures are unaffected, and the exact fiscal impact cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill may cause delays in Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues, which are derived in part from state property taxes. The State Treasurer's Office oversees state funds and general obligation bond debt service, which is funded through the ABF.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judiciary, which handles judicial tax sale foreclosures of rights of redemption; changes to the timing and volume of municipal and county tax sales can affect court caseload timing.

Synopsis: Establishing enhanced requirements under the Open Meetings Act for the State Ethics Commission; and requiring the Department of Information Technology to provide technical staff, support, and equipment necessary to livestream the open meetings of the State Ethics Commission.
Title: Open Meetings Act - State Ethics Commission (Maryland State Agency Transparency Act of 2023)

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill subjects the State Ethics Commission to enhanced requirements under the Open Meetings Act, including posting meeting agendas and related voting documents online at least 48 hours in advance, publishing open meeting minutes within two business days of approval, livestreaming open meetings, and maintaining minutes and archived video recordings online. It also requires the Department of Information Technology to provide the technical staff, support, and equipment necessary to livestream the commission's open meetings.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission and the Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: Members of the public seeking access to State Ethics Commission proceedings, as well as the staff and members of the State Ethics Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,000 in FY 2024 only for the State Ethics Commission to reimburse the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) for video streaming equipment and support services. Commensurately, reimbursable revenues and expenditures for DoIT increase by $10,000 in FY 2024. Ongoing support costs are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly subjects the State Ethics Commission to enhanced requirements under the Open Meetings Act, including advance publication of meeting materials and agendas, posting meeting minutes online, and providing live and archived video streaming of open meetings.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of Information Technology provide the technical staff, support, and equipment necessary to livestream open meetings of the State Ethics Commission.

Synopsis: Prohibiting local jurisdictions from imposing any unreasonable limitations, including land use restrictions, on utility-designated pollinator areas maintained by a public service company under certain conditions; requiring certain public service companies to mow utility designated pollinator areas in a manner which minimizes disturbances to habitats; stating the intent of the General Assembly related to State and local laws regarding weed control and vegetation management by public service companies outside of pollinator areas; etc.
Title: Land Use - Public Service Companies - Pollinator-Friendly Vegetation Management and Utility-Designated Pollinator Areas

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Prohibits local jurisdictions from imposing unreasonable limitations or land use restrictions on utility-designated pollinator areas maintained by public service companies, provided the company meets specific conservation agreements or mowing and integrated vegetation management practices.
responsible_party: Local jurisdictions and the Maryland Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Public service companies, local governments, property owners adjacent to utility rights-of-way, and native wildlife and pollinator populations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes statutory provisions regarding vegetation management and mowing practices by public service companies, which are regulated by the Public Service Commission (including existing PSC standards on utility vegetation management).

The bill references Department of Agriculture native plant classifications and includes specific legislative intent protecting state and local weed control laws administered under the Agriculture Article.

The bill amends the Maryland Land Use Article to limit local government zoning and land use restrictions on utility-designated pollinator areas, directly intersecting with the Department of Planning's role in guiding local land use and planning frameworks.

Synopsis: Altering the Certified Local Farm Enterprise Program to be the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program; expanding the purpose of the Program to include food from certified Chesapeake invasive species providers in the overall percentage goal of 20% of the unit's total dollar value for certain procurement contracts; and altering the Certified Local Farm Enterprise Food Aggregation Grant Fund to be the Certified Local Farm and Fish Food Aggregation Grant Fund.
Title: Certified Local Farm and Fish Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Renames the Certified Local Farm Enterprise Program to the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program and expands its scope to allow State agencies and public universities to count food purchased from certified Chesapeake invasive species providers (such as blue catfish harvesters) toward their 20% local food procurement goal. The bill also renames the associated grant fund and adds annual reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Commercial watermen and seafood dealers harvesting or processing Chesapeake invasive species, certified local farmers, and State agencies and public universities purchasing food.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement the expanded program and consolidated annual reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State agencies' food expenditures and State revenues are not expected to be discernibly affected. The bill affects only State agencies, resulting in no local government impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA houses the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program, which is responsible for administering the program, certifying providers, setting guidelines, adopting regulations, maintaining the directory, and submitting annual reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is statutorily designated to administer the Certified Local Farm and Fish Food Aggregation Grant Fund, which provides grants and near-equity investments to support food aggregation and storage infrastructure and facilitate program participation.
BPW receives the annual report of waivers requested and granted under the program, approves the format of annual agency reporting, and maintains records to submit to legislative committees.

The bill defines eligible certified invasive species providers based on seafood dealer licenses issued under the Natural Resources Article and prioritizations established under the Maryland Aquatic Nuisance Species Management Plan.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding the definition of 'local' for the Maryland Farm-to-School Meal Grant Program, conforming it to the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program.
As the primary procurement authority for state agencies, DGS is affected by procurement preferences, goals, and reporting requirements related to food purchasing contracts.
The University System of Maryland is explicitly designated under State Finance and Procurement law as subject to the requirements of the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program.
Morgan State University is explicitly specified in the State Finance and Procurement Article as subject to the requirements and procurement goals of the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program.
St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly specified in the State Finance and Procurement Article as subject to the requirements and procurement goals of the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of the service charge from $10 to $30 that may be imposed by a circuit court or the District Court for a dishonored check.
Title: Circuit Courts and District Court - Dishonored Checks - Service Charges

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Increases the service charge that a Maryland circuit court clerk or the District Court may impose for a dishonored check from $10 to $30.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts and District Court)
stakeholders: Individuals and entities paying fees, costs, or fines to Maryland circuit courts or the District Court using checks that are dishonored.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by a minimum of $7,600 in FY 2024 and a minimum of $10,100 annually thereafter due to the increased service charge fee. Additionally, special fund revenues for the Central Collection Unit (CCU) in the Department of Budget and Management may experience a minimal increase. There is no material impact on State expenditures or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the District Court and circuit courts across the state by increasing the service charge they can impose for dishonored checks from $10 to $30, directly affecting court administrative processes and revenues overseen by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU) within the Department of Budget and Management requires a $30 minimum threshold to initiate debt collection efforts. Increasing the fee to $30 enables courts to refer delinquent check fees to CCU for collection, potentially generating a minimal increase in special fund revenues.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Transportation to implement all possible incremental near-term safety improvements as soon as practicable if a new approved pedestrian or bicycle safety construction or improvement project is projected to take more than 12 months to complete.
Title: Safe Access for All (SAFE) Roads Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The Safe Access for All (SAFE) Roads Act of 2023 requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to implement context-driven design elements for pedestrian and bicycle safety and to carry out all possible incremental, near-term safety improvements as soon as practicable when a newly approved pedestrian or bicycle safety construction or improvement project is projected to take more than 12 months to complete.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Pedestrians, bicyclists, transit users, and motorists in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances may see minimal redirection of capital program funding starting as early as FY 2023 to implement near-term safety improvements, though no overall net increase in expenditures or specific dollar amounts are projected due to the limited scope of applicable projects. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) recommend and implement context-driven pedestrian and bicycle safety design elements on construction, maintenance, and improvement projects, and require immediate incremental, near-term safety improvements on approved projects projected to take longer than 12 months to complete.

As the modal administration within MDOT responsible for state highways, pedestrian crossings, bicycle infrastructure, and roadway safety improvements, the State Highway Administration is directly responsible for executing the required design elements and incremental safety countermeasures.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "charitable contribution" to exclude an authorization for or a discount on the use of certain services or materials, equipment, or facilities for purposes of provisions of law regulating charitable organizations and charitable representatives; authorizing the Maryland Secretary of State to accept certain documentation in place of an audit or review in connection with a charitable organization's registration statement; etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Charitable Organizations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'charitable contribution' under Maryland law to exclude authorizations for or discounts on the use of services, materials, equipment, or facilities (including advertising and broadcast airtime). It also authorizes the Secretary of State to accept alternative supporting documentation and an affidavit in place of a required CPA audit or review for certain qualifying charitable organizations that primarily solicit in-kind property donations for free distribution.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
stakeholders: Charitable organizations operating in Maryland, their governing boards and donors, and Maryland residents receiving redistributed donated goods.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not materially affected. State expenditures could increase if the Secretary of State experiences an influx of requests to submit alternative documentation in lieu of CPA audits or reviews, potentially requiring additional staff; however, the exact operational and financial impact cannot be reliably determined. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is the primary agency responsible for the registration and oversight of charitable organizations in Maryland. The bill directly affects its operations by redefining charitable contributions and authorizing the Secretary of State to accept alternative documentation in lieu of independent audits or reviews for charitable registration.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Secretary of State regarding regulatory enforcement and statutory interpretation under the Maryland Charitable Solicitations Act, and served as an information source on this legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education, before the start of the 2024-2025 school year, to adopt, implement, and publish guidelines in accordance with the State school health service guidelines to reduce the risk of exposure to anaphylactic major food allergens in classrooms and common areas; requiring each public school to develop a system to disclose the major food allergens contained in the foods served in the school; requiring each county board to make a good faith effort to adopt certain guidelines; etc.
Title: Public Schools - Anaphylactic Food Allergies - Guidelines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health to jointly update school health service guidelines for managing anaphylactic food allergies, and requires local boards of education to adopt, implement, and publish guidelines to reduce allergen exposure.
