It also requires public schools to implement food allergen disclosure systems, establish allergen-free cafeteria tables and food-free zones, and implement strategies to prevent bullying of students with food allergies.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Public school students (particularly those with anaphylactic food allergies), parents, educators, school administrators, and food service and operations staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not materially affected; both the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health can update the guidelines using existing budgeted resources. Local school boards and public schools can also handle guideline adoption, implementation, and allergen disclosure requirements using existing resources. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), jointly with the Maryland Department of Health, with updating the Maryland State school health service guidelines to reduce exposure to anaphylactic causative agents and major food allergens in public school classrooms and common areas.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is statutorily required to collaborate with the State Department of Education to update the state school health service guidelines regarding anaphylactic food allergies by August 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Requiring a tax collector to make certain attempts to contact a certain plaintiff or holder of a certificate of sale regarding certain expenses; and authorizing a collector to redeem certain property without a certain satisfaction letter if a plaintiff or holder of a certificate of sale fails to respond within 5 days after certain attempts by the collector to make contact.
Title: Property Tax - Tax Sales - Redemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires a local tax collector to attempt to contact a tax sale certificate holder or plaintiff by phone and email if they fail to respond to a request from an owner or mortgage holder regarding reimbursable expenses needed to redeem a property. If the certificate holder fails to respond within five business days of the collector's contact attempts, the collector is authorized to redeem the property without requiring a satisfaction letter certifying that expenses have been paid.
responsible_party: Local county and municipal tax collectors
stakeholders: Property owners seeking to redeem properties sold at tax sales, mortgagees and mortgage servicers, holders of tax sale certificates of sale, and local tax collection offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 83 alters provisions concerning the redemption of property sold at tax sale and the reimbursement of expenses in actions to foreclose the right of redemption, which are adjudicated within the Maryland Circuit Courts administered and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Authorizing, subject to certain limitations, the disclosure of a business entity's federal employer identification number, name, physical address, mailing address, contact name, e-mail address, and phone number to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board and its authorized contractors for the purposes of administering the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program and Trust.
Title: Disclosure of Tax Information – Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board – Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Comptroller to disclose specific business tax information—including federal employer identification numbers, entity names, addresses, and contact information—to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board and its contractors to assist in administering the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program and Trust.
responsible_party: Maryland Comptroller
stakeholders: Maryland business entities, small business employers, and employees participating in or eligible for the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Comptroller's Office can handle the expanded disclosure authorization and any associated workload using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Tax - General Article to authorize the Comptroller to disclose specified business tax information to the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board and establishes conditions, limitations, and safeguard requirements for such disclosures.

The program is administered by the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, which directly receives the authorized business tax data under the bill to streamline employer registration and track participating businesses.

The State Treasurer serves on the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board and contributed analysis to the fiscal note regarding how data access will help expand access and streamline program operations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing bodies of counties and municipalities to adopt ordinances to regulate invasive bamboo, including by prohibiting a person from selling, planting, and allowing invasive bamboo to grow on the property of the person without proper upkeep and appropriate containment measures.
Title: Local Government - Regulatory Powers - Regulation of Invasive Bamboo

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Authorizes county and municipal governing bodies to adopt local ordinances regulating invasive bamboo, including prohibiting its sale, planting, or growth without containment measures, and allowing enforcement through civil fines and required mitigation of damages.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipalities
stakeholders: Property owners growing or affected by invasive bamboo, local governments, and small businesses including plant retailers and landscaping services
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal effect. Local governments can implement regulations with existing resources, and may experience a potential increase in local fine revenues if civil fines are established; specific dollar estimates are not provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) administers the state's invasive plant regulations and classifies species into Tier 1 and Tier 2 invasive categories (including certain types of bamboo). While this bill grants local governments direct authority to prohibit the sale, planting, and uncontained growth of invasive bamboo, it directly intersects with MDA's subject-matter oversight of plant health and invasive flora.

The Department of Natural Resources is responsible for conserving the state's natural resources and public lands, and maintains statewide lists of native plants to combat invasive species. DNR provided information for the bill's analysis regarding the ecological impacts and management of invasive plants.

Synopsis: Establishing that ground leases or amendments that are not posted on the State Department of Assessments and Taxation's website are not considered registered or amended; prohibiting a ground lease holder from collecting or attempting to collect rent, late fees, interest, collection costs, and other expenses related to a ground lease unless the ground lease is registered with the Department; etc.
Title: Ground Leases - Collection of Rent, Interest, Fees, and Other Expenses - Registration Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc

bill_summary: Establishes that ground leases and amendments are not considered registered until posted on the State Department of Assessments and Taxation's (SDAT) online registry, prohibits ground lease holders from collecting or attempting to collect ground rent, late fees, interest, or collection costs on unregistered ground leases, and creates an administrative complaint process within SDAT with subsequent circuit court judicial review for leasehold tenants challenging improper collections.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Ground lease holders and leasehold tenants
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and the Judiciary can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. SDAT is explicitly prohibited from charging fees to carry out the bill, and state revenues are not affected. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes ground lease holders or leasehold tenants to file a de novo civil action in circuit court following a final decision by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and requires the court to enter specific orders regarding ground lease registrations. The fiscal note notes that the Judiciary can handle the resulting caseload with existing budgeted resources.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition against a tenant who is seeking to redeem or extinguish ground rent providing certain documentation and payments to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation earlier than 90 days after an application for redemption or extinguishment has been posted on the Department's website.
Title: Residential Ground Leases - Redemption and Extinguishment - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc

bill_summary: This bill repeals the prohibition preventing leasehold tenants seeking to redeem or extinguish a ground rent from submitting required payments and documentation to the State Department of Assessments and Taxation earlier than 90 days after their application is posted online, while maintaining that the department cannot issue the certificate until the application has remained posted for at least 90 days.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Residential leasehold tenants, ground lease holders, and Baltimore City local government officials involved in property redevelopment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or local government finances and operations, though it likely results in operational efficiencies for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary / Administrative Office of the Courts supports the circuit courts, which maintain county land records where ground rent redemption certificates are recorded and handle any judicial dispute or interpleader proceedings. AOC was consulted as an information source on the bill's fiscal note.

Synopsis: Altering the types of elements and units for which a council of unit owners is required to maintain certain property insurance and altering certain requirements for the property insurance policy; and requiring owners of detached units to carry homeowners insurance on the entirety of the unit.
Title: Condominiums - Mandatory Insurance Coverage - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Alters mandatory condominium property insurance requirements by specifying that a council of unit owners must maintain property insurance on both the common elements and units for attached or multifamily dwellings, but only on the common elements for detached units. In addition, the bill requires owners of residential, detached condominium units to carry homeowners insurance covering the entirety of their unit.
responsible_party: None (governed by condominium councils of unit owners and private property owners)
stakeholders: Condominium unit owners (particularly owners of residential detached units), condominium councils of unit owners, and property and casualty insurance companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 98 alters mandatory property insurance requirements for condominium councils of unit owners and mandates homeowners insurance coverage for owners of detached condominium units, referencing policy cancellation standards in the Insurance Article. The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating property and casualty insurance policies and insurer practices in Maryland.

The Secretary of State oversees the registration of residential condominium regimes in Maryland. While the bill directly amends insurance requirements rather than registration filings, it alters the statutory requirements governing condominium governance and operations under the Maryland Condominium Act.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Agriculture to publish a fact sheet on the protection of pets in the event of an eviction or any other loss of possession of real property; requiring a landlord to provide a link to the fact sheet on the Department's website at the execution of a lease on or after November 1, 2023; requiring the Maryland Judiciary to provide a link to the fact sheet at certain times; requiring a sheriff or any other official to return a pet to a tenant or certain other person or to contact an animal shelter or rescue organization; etc.
Title: Real Property - Actions for Possession - Pet Protections

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Establishes protections for pets during evictions and property repossession actions. Requires the Maryland Department of Agriculture to create and update a fact sheet on pet care resources during eviction, mandates that landlords and the Judiciary provide links to this fact sheet, requires officials carrying out evictions to inspect for pets and reunite them with owners or coordinate with animal shelters, and prohibits abandoning pets on public property.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Tenants with pets, landlords, property owners, sheriffs and constables, and local animal shelters and rescue organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Maryland Judiciary can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and the bill is not anticipated to materially impact local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 102 explicitly directs the Maryland Department of Agriculture to develop, publish on its website, and regularly update a fact sheet on the care and protection of pets during evictions or loss of possession of real property.
The bill requires the Maryland Judiciary to include a link to the Department of Agriculture's pet protection fact sheet with warrants of restitution issued in actions for possession of real property.

Synopsis: Modifying the manner in which the chief executive officer of a municipality may fulfill certain notice requirements concerning proposed municipal charter amendments; and requiring the municipality to maintain certain records or receipts and make the records or receipts available to the public.
Title: Municipalities - Charter Amendments - Notice

NarrowSubjects.Name: Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill provides an alternative method for municipalities to give public notice of proposed charter amendments and referendum submissions by allowing the publication of a fair summary in a local newspaper at least once alongside delivery of the summary to every residence by hand, mail, or municipal newsletter. It also requires municipalities to retain proof of delivery records under public information laws and extends the required posting period for voter petition-initiated charter amendments prior to a referendum from 4 weeks to 40 days.
responsible_party: Chief executive officers of Maryland municipalities and municipal governments
stakeholders: Residents and voters of Maryland municipalities, municipal officials, and local newspapers
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect municipal expenditures and does not affect municipal revenues.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program by January 1, 2025, to enroll individuals, based on certain eligibility, in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and the Maryland Children's Health Program; and requiring the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance to submit a final report to certain committees of the General Assembly by January 1, 2024, of its findings and recommendations, including recommended legislative and regulatory changes.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children's Health Program, and Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program by January 1, 2025, to enroll and renew individuals in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and Maryland Children's Health Program based on SNAP eligibility determinations. It also extends the reporting deadline for the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance to submit a final report by January 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Low-income individuals and families receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits who are eligible for Medicaid and MCHP, as well as low-income utility customers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact on Maryland Department of Health revenues and expenditures to implement the Express Lane Eligibility Program is indeterminate; however, any eligible costs would receive a 61% federal matching rate. The Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance can complete its final report with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, required to establish an Express Lane Eligibility Program to enroll individuals in Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program based on SNAP eligibility determinations and apply for any necessary federal § 1115 waivers.

DHS administers the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), whose eligibility data will be used by MDH for Express Lane Eligibility determinations requiring interagency data-sharing agreements. Additionally, DHS staffs the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance, which is mandated by the bill to complete and submit a final report by January 1, 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly extends the reporting duties of the Workgroup on Low-Income Utility Assistance, requiring it to submit a final report with recommendations to legislative committees by January 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Establishing an Ocean City promoter's license in Worcester County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Worcester County to issue the license to a for-profit organization to sell and serve beer, wine, and liquor at an entertainment event that is held on premises located within the corporate limits of the Town of Ocean City, owned by the Town of Ocean City, and approved in writing by the Ocean City Police Department; and authorizing a license fee of $5,000 per entertainment event.
Title: Worcester County - Alcoholic Beverages - Ocean City Promoter's License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Establishes an Ocean City promoter's license in Worcester County, allowing the Worcester County Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to for-profit organizations to sell and serve beer, wine, and liquor at entertainment events held on town-owned premises in Ocean City approved by the Ocean City Police Department.
responsible_party: Worcester County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: For-profit event organizers and promoters, entertainment event attendees, local Ocean City businesses, and the Town of Ocean City.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Worcester County revenues are estimated to increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 based on an anticipated five licenses issued at a fee of $5,000 per entertainment event. Any additional enforcement can be handled with existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcoholic beverage industry and collects state alcohol excise and sales taxes. While this legislation specifically authorizes the local Worcester County Board of License Commissioners to issue promoter's licenses with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's broader alcoholic beverages framework.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a leasehold tenant of an unregistered ground lease from being required to hold more than 3 years of ground rent in escrow; requiring a ground lease holder to mail certain notices or bills to a leasehold tenant in a certain manner under certain circumstances; requiring the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to make available on its website the form a ground lease holder must use to provide a leasehold tenant bills or notices; etc.
Title: Ground Leases – Notices and Billing – Forms and Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill establishes stricter notice and billing requirements for ground lease holders, requiring bills and default notices to be sent by both first-class and certified mail to both the tenant's last known address and the premises address without passing mailing costs to the tenant. It caps escrow requirements for unregistered ground leases at three years, requires ground lease transferees to notify the state and tenants of transfers, and directs the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to create standardized forms for these notices and bills.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Ground lease holders, ground lease transferees, and leasehold tenants
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can fulfill the requirements of developing and posting online forms using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the procedural and notice prerequisites that a ground lease holder must satisfy before bringing an action for possession for nonpayment of ground rent in court. The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the administration and operations of the state court system handling these civil actions.

Synopsis: Requiring a treatment plan for an individual with a mental disorder admitted to a certain health care facility to include a discharge goal and an estimate of the probable length of the inpatient stay before the individual can be transferred to a certain setting; requiring certain facility staff to review and reassess a plan of treatment within certain time periods; requiring the Department of Health to report annually to the General Assembly on the Resident Grievance System and the grievances received related to State facilities; etc.
Title: Mental Health - Treatment Plans for Individuals in Facilities and Resident Grievance System

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill establishes requirements for mental health treatment plans in health care facilities, including mandatory long-range discharge goals and estimated lengths of stay. It provides a process for patients to consent to the involvement of family members or other authorized individuals in treatment team meetings and creates a procedure to request reviews, reassessments, and appeals through the Resident Grievance System for patients in State facilities. Additionally, it requires State facilities to arrange and coordinate external treatment if unable to meet a patient's rehabilitation needs, and mandates an annual report to the General Assembly regarding the Resident Grievance System.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals admitted to mental health facilities and State facilities, their families or authorized representatives, and facility treatment staff and providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount depending on the volume of review requests and appeals requiring additional Maryland Department of Health staff, as well as potential costs for coordinating and providing treatment outside State facilities. Regulations and annual reporting can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the operation of State mental health facilities administered by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). It requires MDH to adopt regulations governing an appeals process for treatment plan reconsiderations through the Department's Healthcare System Chief Medical Officer, coordinate outside care when State facilities cannot provide necessary treatment, and submit an annual report to the General Assembly regarding the Resident Grievance System.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain plug-in electric drive vehicles for which a permit has been issued by the Motor Vehicle Administration to use high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes regardless of the number of passengers in the vehicles; requiring the Administration to charge a fee, not to exceed $20, for issuing the permit; and requiring, on or before January 1 each year, a report to be submitted to the Governor and the General Assembly on the effect of the use of the plug-in electric drive vehicle permits on the operation of HOV lanes.
Title: Vehicle Laws – HOV Lanes – Plug–In Electric Drive Vehicles

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Reauthorizes eligible plug-in electric drive vehicles with a permit from the Motor Vehicle Administration to travel in high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes at all times regardless of passenger count, establishes a permit fee not to exceed $20, and mandates an annual joint report on the program's impact on HOV lane operations.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Owners and drivers of plug-in electric drive vehicles, as well as general commuters using Maryland HOV lanes
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues may increase by up to $380,000 through FY 2026 if the Motor Vehicle Administration charges the maximum authorized $20 fee for an estimated 19,000 permits. TTF expenditures are expected to increase minimally by up to $26,220 to purchase decals ($1.38 per decal). Programming and annual reporting requirements will be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency responsible for processing applications, issuing HOV permits/decals to plug-in electric drive vehicle owners, setting and collecting the permit fee, and co-authoring the annual report.

SHA designates HOV lanes, may consult on the permit design, provides recommendations to MVA on limiting permit numbers to prevent HOV lane degradation, and co-authors the annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.
MDOT is the parent agency of both the MVA and SHA; the bill impacts the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) through permit fee revenues and decal procurement expenditures.
The Department of State Police is authorized to consult with MVA and SHA to design the HOV permit and is responsible for enforcing traffic laws and HOV lane restrictions across the state.
The Governor's Office receives the annual joint report from MVA and SHA regarding the effect of electric vehicle permits on HOV lane operations.

bill_summary: This bill repeals obsolete, duplicative, or unnecessary statutory reporting requirements across various Maryland state agencies and institutions. It also consolidates, modifies deadlines for, and reschedules certain mandated reports to improve administrative efficiency and practicality.
responsible_party: Various Maryland State departments and agencies (including the Maryland Higher Education Commission, Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center, Comptroller, Alcohol and Tobacco Commission, Maryland Department of Health, and Department of the Environment)
stakeholders: State agencies, public higher education institutions, local school boards, the General Assembly, and the public entities that submit or receive mandated reports
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local finances because it is procedural in nature. Some State agencies may experience operational efficiencies resulting from the repeal, consolidation, or rescheduling of reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Centralizes the state employee telework program reporting into one consolidated annual report prepared and submitted by DBM on behalf of all state agencies, rather than requiring separate reports from each unit.

Assumes primary responsibility from GOCPP for collecting data and submitting mandated reports on State-funded home visiting programs, and has obsolete reporting requirements regarding rural health complexes and health disparities repealed.

Modifies annual reporting dates and consolidation requirements for several environmental reports, including climate change mitigation, Bay Restoration Fund wastewater projects, solid waste management, and recycling.

Modifies or repeals multiple reporting mandates, including data submissions for Complete College America, evaluation metrics for the Community College Promise Scholarship, and reporting duties concerning foster youth tuition exemptions.

Modifies or repeals multiple reporting mandates, including data submissions for Complete College America, evaluation metrics for the Community College Promise Scholarship, and reporting duties concerning foster youth tuition exemptions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Modifies inmate annual report contents by removing place of birth data, renumbers rehired retiree reporting, and repeals participation in the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program reporting requirement.
Extends the reporting deadline for annual beer production and sales by license holders from October 1 to December 1, and is referenced regarding audits of 9-1-1 fee collections.
Repeals annual reporting requirements concerning service of process on nonresident drivers and organ donor designations on driver's licenses and ID cards.

Reduces the reporting frequency of its general activities from quarterly to every six months and repeals a duplicative annual reporting requirement regarding the Maryland Technology Incubator Program.
Updates responsibilities for developing and maintaining online graphic data dashboards regarding foster youth and homeless youth higher education outcomes and dual enrollment data.
Reduces the reporting requirement on minority business enterprise participation in the Energy Efficient Homes Construction Loan Program from every six months to annually.
Designated as the primary department responsible for submitting the annual report on the progress of implementing the outcomes evaluation system for children and family services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Relieved of responsibility for State-funded home visiting program reporting (transferred to MDH) and annual reporting on the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.
Repeals obsolete annual reporting requirements by the Board of Trustees to the Joint Committee on Pensions regarding rehired retirees and the Alternate Contributory Pension Selection.
Repeals the requirement to track and report consumer complaints and recommendations regarding Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) services.
Repeals a duplicative annual report on the procurement system and broad-based competition, and removes the Board as a recipient of an annual report on alternative financing for school construction.
Repeals the annual reporting requirement regarding the use of alternative financing mechanisms to finance public school construction in Maryland.

Repeals several reporting mandates across the system, including the Board of Regents report on business entities, UMCEED annual reporting, UMBC reporting on the Maryland Technology Internship Program, and School of Nursing Wellmobile reporting.
Extends the submission deadlines for its general annual report and the Clean Energy Center Fund investment outcome report from October 1 to December 1.
Modifies the transmission of precinct boundary descriptions to allow electronic receipt from the State Administrator and maintains joint reporting with MDE on wastewater growth impacts.
Permits the State Administrator to electronically transmit precinct boundary descriptions and maps rather than requiring physical documents.
Repeals an obsolete annual reporting mandate regarding corporate headquarters compliance with conditional grant and loan criteria.
Repeals the statutory requirement to submit copies of independent CPA annual audit reports to the Department of Legislative Services.
Adjusts the annual reporting deadline from November 1 to December 1 regarding expenditures and outcomes from the Cigarette Restitution Fund and related programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Repeals an obsolete requirement that the office receive reports regarding employee demographics from the Baltimore City video lottery licensee.
Relieved of the requirement to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly regarding the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.
Relieved of the requirement to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly regarding the P.R.O.T.E.C.T. program.

Oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, whose annual reporting requirements regarding Next Generation 9-1-1 transition, staffing, and audits are modified and rescheduled.
Serves as the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which sees multiple annual reporting mandates repealed under this bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the District Court, in aid of enforcement or execution of a money judgment resulting from a certain small claim action, from ordering the appearance of an individual for an examination or ordering an individual to answer interrogatories.
Title: District Court - Small Claims - Enforcement of Money Judgments
bill_summary: Prohibits the District Court from ordering an individual to appear for an examination or to answer interrogatories in aid of enforcement or execution of a money judgment resulting from a small claims action.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Small claims litigants, judgment debtors, judgment creditors, and small businesses seeking to enforce small claims judgments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances. Alterations to District Court operations, forms, brochures, and webpages can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is a potential meaningful impact on small businesses that may face difficulties collecting on small claims judgments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the operations and procedures of the District Court of Maryland by prohibiting judges from ordering examinations or interrogatories in aid of enforcing small claims money judgments. The Administrative Office of the Courts must update District Court forms, brochures, websites, and judicial procedures to reflect the change in law.

Synopsis: Converting enhanced underinsured motorist coverage from an opt-in offering of coverage into an opt-out coverage option under provisions of law establishing requirements for private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance; requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to conduct a study on the impact of converting enhanced underinsured motorist coverage to an opt-out coverage option and report its findings to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by December 31, 2026, and December 31, 2028; etc.
Title: Private Passenger Motor Vehicle Liability Insurance - Enhanced Underinsured Motorist Coverage - Opt-Out Option

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicle Insurance -see also- MD Auto Insurance Fund

bill_summary: Converts enhanced underinsured motorist (EUIM) coverage for private passenger motor vehicle liability insurance policies from an opt-in offering to an opt-out coverage option, requiring insurers to provide EUIM coverage unless the insured affirmatively waives it in writing, and directs the Maryland Insurance Administration to study and report on the impact of the change.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Private passenger motor vehicle owners and insured drivers in Maryland, as well as motor vehicle liability insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2024 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Potential minimal increase in general fund revenues from the 2% insurance premium tax resulting from higher EUIM policy premiums. MIA can handle reviews and study reporting with existing resources. No impact on local finances or the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary regulatory agency responsible for overseeing motor vehicle liability insurance in the state. Under the bill, the Insurance Commissioner must approve or require the waiver form used by insurers, review rate and policy form filings, conduct a detailed multi-year study on the impact of shifting to opt-out enhanced underinsured motorist coverage, and submit interim and final reports to the Governor and the General Assembly.

MAIF is the state's independent insurer of last resort for motor vehicle liability coverage. The bill directly impacts statutory provisions governing private passenger motor vehicle liability policies and explicitly references rights of recovery involving MAIF under Title 20 of the Insurance Article.

The Governor's Office is mandated to receive both an interim report (by December 31, 2026) and a final report (by December 31, 2028) from the Maryland Insurance Administration evaluating the impact and implementation of the coverage change.

Synopsis: Repealing the crime of unnatural or perverted sexual practice.
Title: Criminal Law – Unnatural or Perverted Sexual Practice – Repeal
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 796

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals the criminal offense of unnatural or perverted sexual practice from Maryland law, makes technical and conforming updates to related statutes regarding sexual abuse and exploitation, and establishes that prior convictions for the repealed offense cannot be expunged if committed without consent, with a minor under age 16, or under other specified nonconsensual or prohibited circumstances.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District and Circuit Courts) and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals previously charged or convicted of unnatural or perverted sexual practices, victims of human trafficking seeking to vacate convictions, criminal justice system personnel, and law enforcement.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a criminal statute and modifies provisions concerning court procedures, petitions for expungement under § 10-105 of the Criminal Procedure Article, and motions to vacate judgments under § 8-302, directly impacting court dockets, records, and judicial administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions related to Tier III sex offender registry classifications under § 11-701 of the Criminal Procedure Article, affects criminal records maintenance, and governs compliance with expungement orders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a criminal offense and affects eligibility for post-conviction relief, expungements, and motions to vacate judgments for human trafficking victims, all of which directly involve indigent defense services.

The bill amends the definition of 'sexual molestation or exploitation' in Section 5-701 of the Family Law Article, which directly governs child abuse and neglect assessments and investigations conducted by local departments of social services under DHS.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is affected by the repeal of criminal offenses from the Criminal Law Article and must process expungement orders for applicable police records.
The bill affects the handling and expungement of permanent court and state criminal records maintained in state repositories.

Synopsis: Altering certain qualifications for a journeyman license to provide heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration services to require having held an apprentice license for 4 rather than 3 years and having completed at least 6,000 rather than 1,875 hours of training under the direction and control of a licensed contractor.
Title: Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Services - Journeyman License - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill increases the qualification requirements for an individual applying for a heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) journeyman license by requiring them to hold an apprentice license for at least four years (up from three) and complete at least 6,000 hours of training (up from 1,875 hours) under a licensed contractor before taking the licensing examination.
responsible_party: State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors within the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: HVACR apprentices seeking a journeyman license, licensed HVACR contractors, and small businesses that employ and train apprentices.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund licensing revenues may be delayed as applicants must spend additional time in training before applying for a journeyman license. Overall, the bill is not expected to materially affect State finances or operations, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors and oversees the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program. The bill directly alters the licensing qualifications, required apprentice years, and training hours administered and regulated by the department.

Synopsis: Limiting the percentage of the weekly benefits amount that the Secretary of Labor may deduct from weekly benefits payable to a claimant to recover certain overpayments of unemployment insurance benefits to 50% of the weekly benefit or 25% if the benefit is less than $100; and clarifying the circumstances under which the Secretary may use certain methods to recover overpayments of unemployment insurance benefits.
Title: Unemployment Insurance - Recovery of Benefits - Limitation and Methods

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Limits the percentage of weekly unemployment insurance (UI) benefits the Maryland Secretary of Labor may deduct to recover non-fraudulent overpayments to no more than 50% of future weekly benefits, or no more than 25% if the weekly benefit amount is $100 or less.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Unemployment insurance claimants who have received non-fraudulent overpayments of benefits
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor estimates a one-time programming cost of approximately $16,400 in FY 2024, anticipated to be covered with existing federal funds or general funds if necessary. Nonbudgeted Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund (UITF) expenditures increase beginning in FY 2024 due to slower benefit offset recoupment (MDL noted $9.0 million as illustrative for 2022), partially offset by an increase in UITF revenues as other recovery methods are utilized, resulting in a net negative impact to the fund. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor's Division of Unemployment Insurance is the primary implementing agency. The bill directly restricts the percentage of weekly benefits the Secretary of Labor may deduct to recover non-fraud overpayments and requires the Secretary to adopt regulations governing recovery processes.
The bill allows claimants to elect to have benefit overpayments collected by civil suit instead of assessment, which directly involves the state court system for collection proceedings.

Synopsis: Renaming the Commission on LGBTQ Affairs to be the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs; increasing the number of members of the Commission from 15 to 21; altering certain qualifications for members appointed to the Commission; staggering the terms of Commission members; and altering the duties of the Commission.
Title: State Government – Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs – Alterations

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Renames the Commission on LGBTQ Affairs to the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs within the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives, expands the membership from 15 to 21 members with staggered terms, updates member qualification criteria, and broadens the Commission's scope and duties to include questioning, intersex, asexual, agender, aromantic, and other identities.
responsible_party: Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs, within the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives
stakeholders: Members of Maryland's LGBTQIA+ communities, including questioning, intersex, asexual, agender, and aromantic individuals, as well as State agencies and newly appointed Commission members.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected; expense reimbursements for additional commission members and operational changes can be handled within existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 141 directly alters the name, membership size, structure, and statutory duties of the Commission on LGBTQIA+ Affairs, which is an established unit housed within the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the mandate, member qualifications, staggered term structure, and size of an ongoing executive statutory commission.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the 21 members of the Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, and retains the authority to remove members for incompetence or misconduct.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing nominations for state boards and commissions, and will handle the expanded 21-member roster and staggered appointment cycles.

Synopsis: Requiring a person who fails to reactivate a real estate broker license on inactive status within 3 years to comply with specified requirements to obtain a license.
Title: Real Estate Brokers - Inactive Licenses - Requirements After Expiration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill requires real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons who fail to reactivate an inactive license before it expires after three years to comply with standard initial licensing requirements in order to obtain a new license.
responsible_party: Maryland Real Estate Commission
stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and real estate salespersons with inactive licenses
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, as the Maryland Real Estate Commission can implement the procedural changes using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Maryland Real Estate Commission within its Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing, which is directly responsible for licensing real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons and enforcing the reactivation and licensing requirements under the bill.

Synopsis: Exempting applications for changing certain resident agents from the requirement that the Board of License Commissioners for Howard County hold a public hearing on the applications; and authorizing the Board to hold a public hearing on certain applications if the Board determines there is good cause for the hearing.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages - Public Hearing Ho. Co. 13-23
bill_summary: Exempts certain alcoholic beverages license holders in Howard County from the public hearing and hearing notice requirements when applying to become the resident agent for their license, provided they have previously appeared and been approved at a nonviolation hearing for the same license, while authorizing the Board of License Commissioners to hold a hearing if there is good cause.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders and resident agent applicants in Howard County, as well as the Howard County Board of License Commissioners
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Howard County expenditures for hearings related to resident agent changes decrease by up to approximately $14,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 because each hearing costs an estimated $1,400 to conduct. County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry. While this bill specifically addresses local procedural hearing requirements for the Howard County Board of License Commissioners regarding resident agent changes with no state fiscal impact, it falls under the broader statutory area of alcoholic beverage regulation overseen at the state level.

Synopsis: Altering the entity that must administer or approve an apprenticeship program for electricians; substituting the term "uninsured" for the term "inactive" in certain provisions of law relating to liability insurance requirements for certain electricians; prohibiting a certain electrician from contracting to provide electrical services unless the electrical work is covered by certain liability insurance; specifying who is authorized and required to purchase certain insurance; etc.
Title: Maryland Electricians Act - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: House Bill 149 revises the Maryland Electricians Act by updating references to designate the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning as the approving entity for electrician apprenticeship programs, replacing the term 'inactive' status with 'uninsured' status for electrician licenses, and allowing uninsured master electricians to work as journeypersons under an insured master electrician. It also clarifies liability and property damage insurance mandates for contracting electrical work, specifies who may purchase the required insurance, and requires the State Board of Electricians to denote insurance compliance on each license.
responsible_party: State Board of Electricians (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: Master electricians, journeyperson electricians, apprentice electricians, electrical contractors and businesses, and electrical inspectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as the State Board of Electricians can manage administrative changes with existing resources, and there is no impact on State revenues. Local government finances and operations are likewise unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses both the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning—which is explicitly designated in the bill as the entity approving electrician apprenticeship programs—and the State Board of Electricians, which oversees licensing, uninsured status, and liability insurance verification.

Synopsis: Establishing that adaptive reuse, retrofitting, and repurposing of existing buildings to develop new affordable multifamily housing is an eligible use of certain financial assistance provided by the Department of Housing and Community Development; requiring the Department to notify applicants for certain financial assistance that adaptive reuse is an eligible use of funds; and providing that the notice requirement does not apply to individuals applying for loans from the Department that are not focused on housing.
Title: Housing and Community Development - Adaptive Reuse

bill_summary: Establishes that the adaptive reuse of existing buildings to create affordable multifamily housing is an eligible use of loan proceeds from relevant programs administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development, and requires the Department to notify applicants that adaptive reuse is an eligible use of funds.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Affordable housing developers, loan applicants under Department of Housing and Community Development housing programs, and low- to moderate-income residents seeking affordable multifamily housing.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. The Department of Housing and Community Development already issues loans for adaptive reuse multifamily housing projects under current law and can satisfy the notification requirement using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs loan programs administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), establishing that adaptive reuse for affordable multifamily housing is an eligible use of loan proceeds and mandating that the department notify loan applicants accordingly.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a landlord from including a certain term in a lease pertaining to electronic delivery of the notice of a rent increase; requiring a landlord to notify a tenant in writing before increasing the tenant's rent through first-class mail or, if elected by the tenant, electronic delivery; requiring a county or municipality that adopts a certain local law related to limitations on rent increases to report annually certain information on building permits issued for multifamily dwellings intended as rental housing; etc.
Title: Real Property - Residential Leases - Notification of Rent Increases

bill_summary: This bill establishes requirements for landlords to provide advance written or electronic notice to residential tenants before increasing rent, with notice periods varying by lease duration (e.g., 90 days for tenancies longer than one month). It prohibits landlords from requiring electronic delivery of rent increase notices as a lease condition. Additionally, the bill requires local jurisdictions that adopt laws limiting rent increases to submit reports and annual multifamily rental housing building permit data to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Local jurisdictions (counties and municipalities) and the Maryland General Assembly
stakeholders: Residential tenants, residential landlords and property managers, and local county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Reporting requirements for qualifying local jurisdictions can be handled within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory notice requirements for residential rent increases and restricts lease terms, which directly impacts landlord-tenant disputes, defenses, and eviction proceedings adjudicated in the Maryland court system.
The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces statutory provisions and consumer protections governing residential landlord-tenant leases and unlawful lease terms.
The Department of Housing and Community Development monitors state and local rental housing policies and conditions affecting rental affordability and tenant protections.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose and contents of and the requirements and qualifications under the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund; requiring the Governor, in each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029, to include at least $100,000 for the Fund in the annual budget bill; establishing the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to recommend guidelines, policies, and practices for the implementation of the Grant Program; and requiring the Advisory Committee to report to certain committees of the General Assembly by December 30, 2023.
Title: Department of Agriculture - Urban Agriculture Grant Programs - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's Urban Agriculture Grant Program and Fund by establishing a mandated annual appropriation of at least $100,000 from fiscal year 2025 through 2029, broadening grant eligibility beyond Baltimore City to include urban agricultural producers statewide, higher education institutions, and qualifying nonprofits. It also creates an Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee to advise on program implementation and expands the statutory definition of an "urban agricultural producer" under both the Urban Agriculture Grant Program and the Urban Agriculture Water and Power Infrastructure Grant Program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Urban agricultural producers and farmers (particularly socially disadvantaged farmers), nonprofit agricultural organizations, institutions of higher education, and urban communities seeking improved access to locally grown food.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2029 due to a mandated appropriation. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund increase correspondingly by at least $100,000 per year. The bill does not materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA is the primary administering agency responsible for operating the Urban Agriculture Grant Program and Urban Agriculture Water and Power Infrastructure Grant Program, managing the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund, providing staff support to the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee, and making appointments to the committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is specifically designated by statute to appoint a member to the newly established Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new formal advisory entity, the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee, to recommend guidelines, policies, and practices for the grant program and submit annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

DBM oversees the state budget process and is responsible for incorporating the bill's mandated annual appropriation of at least $100,000 to the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.

The Governor is mandated by the bill to include at least $100,000 annually in the state budget bill for the fund from FY 2025 through FY 2029 and receives the annual report from the Urban Agriculture Advisory Committee.

Institutions of higher education are made qualified applicants eligible to receive grants to provide direct training and technical assistance to urban farmers, with potential fiscal impacts on revenues and expenditures.
As a public institution of higher education with agricultural and urban research programs, MSU is an eligible applicant for grants under the program, which may affect revenues and expenditures.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Urban Agriculture Grant Fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the special, nonlapsing Urban Agriculture Grant Fund separately.

Synopsis: Altering the voting rights of and the process for selecting a student member of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; prohibiting the student member from voting on matters before the board relating to personnel and collective bargaining decisions; establishing the Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by April 1, 2024.
Title: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners - Student Members and Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members

bill_summary: Expands the voting rights and access to executive sessions for the student member of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, changes the selection method so the student member is elected by middle and high school students, and establishes a task force to study board member compensation and the addition of a second student member.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners
stakeholders: Baltimore City Public School System students (particularly middle and high school students), the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, and the Baltimore City Mayor's Office
fiscal_impact_summary: State expense reimbursements for task force members are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. At the local level, Baltimore City Public Schools and the Baltimore City Mayor's Office can implement the bill's requirements and task force staffing using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is responsible for the leadership and oversight of Maryland's 24 public school systems. The bill amends the Education Article regarding the governance, student voting rights, and selection process for the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state entity, the Task Force to Study Compensation and Student Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, to evaluate board member compensation and membership structure.
The Task Force created by the bill is required to report its findings and recommendations on school board member compensation and student representation to the Governor by April 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Providing that a resident of the State meets certain residency requirements for an applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Howard County.
Title: Howard County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Residency Requirements Ho. Co. 11-23
bill_summary: Allows any Maryland state resident to satisfy the residency requirements for an alcoholic beverages license application in Howard County, altering previous requirements that mandated county residency.
responsible_party: Howard County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Maryland residents, business owners, partnerships, corporations, and limited liability companies applying for alcoholic beverages licenses in Howard County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, and the bill is not anticipated to materially affect Howard County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and maintains statutory oversight over alcoholic beverage license application standards under the Alcoholic Beverages Article, though this bill specifically amends local applicant residency requirements for Howard County with no fiscal impact on the agency.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority from issuing bonds beginning June 1, 2023; requiring the Department of Legislative Services to evaluate the Authority providing enough detail for the General Assembly to determine whether the Authority should continue in its current form; etc.
Title: Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority - Evaluation, Termination of Bond Authority, and Assumption of Functions, Employees, and Contracts (Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority Sunset Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority (NMWDA) from issuing new bonds beginning June 1, 2023, while preserving obligations under existing bonds and contracts. It requires the Department of Legislative Services to conduct an evaluation of NMWDA and draft legislation to merge it into the Maryland Environmental Service (MES), and requires MES to review and report on NMWDA's functions, employees, and contracts by December 1, 2024. Additionally, MES is required to temporarily assume NMWDA's functions, employees, and contracts during any future merger.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services and Maryland Environmental Service
stakeholders: Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority (NMWDA), its employees, and its member jurisdictions (Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Carroll, Frederick, Harford, Howard, and Montgomery counties and Baltimore City)
fiscal_impact_summary: State: Nonbudgeted expenditures and matching nonbudgeted fee revenues increase by $100,000 in FY 2024 for MES to hire a consultant to conduct the required review; potential increase in DLS general fund expenditures in FY 2024 and FY 2025 if contractual assistance or extra staff is required; nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures may increase significantly (likely not before FY 2026) if MES temporarily assumes NMWDA operations. Local: Potential increase in member jurisdiction expenditures in FY 2024/2025 (around $100,000 in staff, legal, and accounting support costs funded through membership fees) and reduced project financing options from the loss of NMWDA bond authority.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Environmental Service to conduct a comprehensive review and analysis of the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority's functions, employees, and contracts, submit a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024, and temporarily assume all functions, employees, and contracts of the Authority during any future merger.

The bill requires an evaluation of the potential impact that discontinuing or merging the Northeast Maryland Waste Disposal Authority would have on the State Retirement and Pension System and its participating members.

Synopsis: Requiring membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for certain local law enforcement officers of the Crisfield Police Department under certain circumstances; providing that a certain individual is entitled to eligibility service and creditable service that was earned before the effective date of the Crisfield Police Department's participation in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System; providing for the transfer of creditable service for a certain individual; etc.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System - Crisfield Police Department

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires mandatory membership in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) for permanent full-time police officers of the Crisfield Police Department if the department becomes a participating governmental unit. It grants prior service credit in LEOPS for past service with Crisfield, transfers members out of the Employees' Pension System, and exempts transferring officers from paying retroactive member contributions for their past service.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Current and future permanent full-time police officers of the Crisfield Police Department and the City of Crisfield.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: None. Local Effect: Contingent on the City of Crisfield electing to participate in LEOPS, total pension liabilities for the City increase by $1.0 million and annual employer contributions increase by approximately $120,700. There is no material fiscal effect on other participating governmental units in LEOPS and no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the Employees' Pension System (EPS). SRA is directly responsible for administering the transfer of service credits, membership transitions, and asset transfers if the Crisfield Police Department joins LEOPS.

Synopsis: Altering the list of crimes included within a certain definition of "crime of violence" to include sexual abuse of a minor if the offender is at least 21 years old and the victim is under the age of 16 years; and requiring a sentence for certain persons convicted of certain sexual abuse crimes to include a term of lifetime sexual offender supervision.
Title: Sexual Offenses - Crime of Violence and Lifetime Supervision

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Harassment; Threats

bill_summary: Expands the definition of a 'crime of violence' to include sexual abuse of a minor when the offender is at least 21 years old and the victim is under the age of 16 involving specified sexual acts. It also broadens mandatory lifetime sexual offender supervision to include sexual abuse of a minor under 13 committed by an adult, sexual abuse of a minor under 16 committed by an offender at least 21 years old, and certain pre-October 1, 2017 second-degree sexual offenses and attempts committed by adults.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of sexual abuse of a minor and specified sex offenses, child victims of sexual abuse, state correctional and parole/probation staff, and the state court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services increase minimally beginning in out-years due to longer sentences, lower diminution credits, and expanded lifetime supervision requirements. State revenues are unaffected, and local finances and operations will not be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency affected by the bill. Its Division of Parole and Probation oversees lifetime sexual offender supervision, and its correctional facilities house inmates serving longer sentences with restricted diminution credits resulting from expanded 'crime of violence' designations.

The Judiciary is directly responsible for sentencing qualifying offenders to lifetime supervision, establishing and modifying special conditions of supervision, ordering required presentence investigations, and adjudicating petitions for discharge.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings and will represent clients facing these charges, mandatory sentencing enhancements for crimes of violence, and lifetime supervision requirements or violation proceedings.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) to provide energy efficiency and conservation programs for low-income electricity customers to achieve specified incremental gross energy savings targets through 2026. It establishes labor standards for participating contractors, creates the Green and Healthy Task Force to coordinate housing resources, requires DHCD to plan for low-income energy retrofits by 2031, and directs a disparity study on minority- and women-owned businesses in the energy efficiency sector.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Low-income electricity customers and renters, affordable housing property owners, energy efficiency and weatherization contractors and their workers, and electric utility ratepayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for DHCD increase substantially beginning in FY 2024 to satisfy energy savings targets, estimated by DHCD at $39.8 million in FY 2024 and rising to $214.2 million by FY 2028. Special fund revenues will increase correspondingly through the EmPOWER surcharge on utility customer bills to cover program costs. Local governments and housing authorities will see increased revenues and expenditures from program grants, while all electricity customers will absorb higher utility rates to recover program costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency under the bill, tasked with procuring and providing energy efficiency and conservation programs to achieve specific annual incremental gross energy savings targets for low-income residential customers, submitting regular plans and updates to the Public Service Commission, adopting weatherization regulations, providing staff for the newly created Green and Healthy Task Force, and coordinating funding for whole-home retrofits.

PSC is the primary regulatory oversight body responsible for reviewing DHCD's energy efficiency plans, working with DHCD and electric utilities to establish operational procedures and secure cooperation, and incorporating low-income program metrics into its annual report to the General Assembly.

MEA is consulted by PSC on the annual energy efficiency report, is a designated member of the Green and Healthy Task Force, coordinates on Strategic Energy Investment Fund allocations, and is required to apply for all available federal funds, potentially requiring additional staff.

As the State's designated MBE certification agency, MDOT is mandated (jointly with GOSBA) to conduct a disparity study regarding energy efficiency and conservation services procured by DHCD to assess compliance with constitutional requirements for remedial measures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is required to co-lead the disparity study evaluating remedial contracting measures for minority- and women-owned businesses in the energy efficiency sector, and submit study findings to the General Assembly by December 31, 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Green and Healthy Task Force, a temporary statutory body charged with meeting quarterly for three years to coordinate resources and recommend policies for healthy, energy-efficient, and low-emissions low-income housing.
DHCD is explicitly required to coordinate with DBM to identify additional funding sources to support the possible expansion of whole-home energy efficiency and maintenance programs.
The Secretary of Human Services or the Secretary's designee serves as a statutory member of the Green and Healthy Task Force.
A representative of the Office of People's Counsel serves as a statutory member of the Green and Healthy Task Force representing residential ratepayer interests.
OAG must be consulted by MDOT and GOSBA during the development of the energy efficiency contracting disparity study regarding compliance with constitutional equal protection standards.
The Secretary of Health is designated to receive annual findings and recommendations reports from the Green and Healthy Task Force.
The Secretary of the Environment is designated to receive annual findings and recommendations reports from the Green and Healthy Task Force.
The Governor's Office receives the annual reports and recommendations of the Green and Healthy Task Force, as well as DHCD's whole-home funding coordination plan.
