bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Board of Physicians to approve licensed athletic trainers to perform dry needling as a specialized task, establishes educational and hands-on training requirements for approval, and provides disciplinary grounds for performing dry needling without authorization.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Licensed athletic trainers, supervising physicians, and patients/athletes receiving athletic training services
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $31,900 in FY 2024 and $6,400 in FY 2025 to fund a part-time contractual licensure analyst and a $5,000 one-time software modification to update the licensing system. Special fund revenues may increase beginning in FY 2024 if the Maryland Board of Physicians establishes an application fee to cover administrative costs. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians, which is a licensing and regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, is the primary entity responsible for approving licensed athletic trainers to perform dry needling, verifying training requirements, updating licensure systems, and handling any associated disciplinary actions. MDH/MBP also incurs special fund operational and contractual staffing expenditures under the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain assistant State's Attorney with knowledge of the case to meet with a victim of sexually assaultive behavior or the victim's representative within 20 days after receiving a request from the victim regarding a decision by the Office of the State's Attorney  not to file a charging document or to dismiss charges against an alleged suspect; requiring the assistant State's Attorney, at the meeting, to explain the justification for a certain decision; and establishing certain requirements for the meeting.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Victims of Sexually Assaultive Behavior
bill_summary: Requires an assistant State's Attorney with knowledge of a case to meet with a victim of sexually assaultive behavior or their designated representative within 20 days of a request to explain the justification when the State's Attorney's Office decides not to file charges or dismisses charges against an alleged suspect.
responsible_party: Office of the State's Attorney
stakeholders: Victims of sexually assaultive behavior, their designated representatives, and prosecutors in State's Attorneys' Offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. Local State's Attorneys' Offices can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 174 establishes statutory procedural rights for crime victims by requiring assistant State's Attorneys to meet with victims of sexually assaultive behavior upon request when charges are dismissed or not filed. As the state's coordinating agency for criminal justice policy and victim services administration, this change directly aligns with GOCPP's policy and victim advocacy focus.

Synopsis: Authorizing the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital and operating budget matters; requiring certain members of the county board and the executive leadership of the Baltimore County public school system to develop a certain draft curriculum for budget training for student members of the county board and submit the draft curriculum to the county board for review; and requiring each student member of the board to complete the budget training within 2 months of the student's election to the board.
Title: Baltimore County Board of Education - Student Member - Voting and Training

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education to vote on capital and operating budget matters, provided the student completes required budget training within two months of being elected. It also mandates that a workgroup of school board members and Baltimore County Public Schools leadership develop a draft budget training curriculum by December 31, 2023, to be facilitated by the school system's Division of Business Services.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of Education and Baltimore County Public Schools
stakeholders: Student members of the Baltimore County Board of Education, students in Baltimore County Public Schools, and the Baltimore County Board of Education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Baltimore County Public Schools and the Baltimore County Board of Education can implement the training and curriculum requirements using existing resources, and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the governance and voting rights of the student member of the Baltimore County Board of Education. While the implementation and training requirements fall entirely on the local school system with no state fiscal impact, MSDE holds broad statewide oversight over Maryland's 24 public school systems.

Synopsis: Designating Maryland Rye or Maryland Rye Whiskey as the State spirit.
Title: State Designations – State Spirit – Maryland Rye

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.

bill_summary: Designates Maryland Rye or Maryland Rye Whiskey as the official State spirit of Maryland.
responsible_party: Maryland State Archives
stakeholders: Maryland distillers, rye whiskey producers, local agricultural growers, and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: Designating a State spirit does not materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives is responsible for documenting official state history and maintains the Maryland Manual On-Line, which catalogues and publishes all official Maryland state symbols and designations.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time within which a person is required to file a Maryland estate tax return for the purpose of allowing a surviving spouse to take into account the deceased spousal unused exclusion amount to be consistent with the time for making a federal election; and applying the Act retroactively to any decedents dying on or after January 1, 2019.
Title: Maryland Estate Tax - Portability - Time Period for Election
bill_summary: This bill aligns Maryland estate tax law with federal law by altering the deadline to file a Maryland estate tax return solely for electing portability of the deceased spousal unused exclusion (DSUE) amount to match the federal time period (up to five years). It requires the Comptroller to adopt conforming regulations and applies retroactively to decedents dying on or after January 1, 2019.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Surviving spouses, personal representatives/executors of estates, and estates of decedents dying on or after January 1, 2019.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may potentially decrease beginning in FY 2024 because extending the filing window enables more estates to claim the deceased spousal unused exclusion amount. Administrative expenditures for the Comptroller's Office to update forms, issue regulations, and process returns can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary tax administrator responsible for administering the Maryland estate tax, receiving estate tax returns, and is specifically mandated by the bill to adopt regulations aligning the State's election time period with federal standards.

Registers of Wills handle estate administration and probate, and under estate tax filing provisions, they certify the amount of inheritance tax paid for decedents when requested for estate tax return reconciliations.

Synopsis: Altering eligibility for and the amount of a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for a taxpayer who adopts a child during the taxable year.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Adoption Expenses - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Adoption - see also- Parents and Guardians

bill_summary: Increases the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for taxpayers who adopt a child to $12,000 for a child with special needs and $10,000 for a child without special needs, removing prior restrictions based on whether the child was a Maryland resident at the time of adoption.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Adoptive parents in Maryland adopting children through public child welfare agencies or licensed private nonprofit adoption agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $91,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 due to the expanded tax subtraction. General fund expenditures increase by $43,000 in FY 2024 only for one-time computer system changes by the Comptroller's Office. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $54,000 annually beginning in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering state personal income tax returns and forms. The agency incurs a fiscal impact of $43,000 in FY 2024 to implement one-time changes to tax systems to accommodate the altered subtraction modification.

The Department of Human Services oversees Maryland's public child welfare agencies, foster care, and adoption services, which are involved in placing children for adoption and making special needs determinations referenced under the statute.

Synopsis: Authorizing a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification to an unlawfully restrictive covenant for a property within the boundaries of the county or municipality after providing persons with an ownership interest in the property with 30 days' written notice; and providing that persons with an ownership interest in property that is subject to an unlawfully restrictive covenant may decline action by a county or municipality to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification.
Title: Real Property - Unlawfully Restrictive Covenants - Modification by Counties or Municipalities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to execute and record a restrictive covenant modification to remove unlawfully restrictive covenants (restrictions based on race, religious belief, or national origin) for properties within their jurisdictions, subject to providing at least 30 days' written notice to property owners, who hold the right to decline the action.
responsible_party: County and municipal governments, Clerks of the Circuit Court, County Attorneys, and the Administrative Office of the Courts
stakeholders: Property owners with deeds containing unlawfully restrictive covenants, local governments, and neighborhood communities
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Any operational or fiscal impact on local governments (such as costs for mailings and document review) is anticipated to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under § 3-112 of the Real Property Article referenced in the bill, restrictive covenant modifications must be accompanied by an intake sheet on a form provided by the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC), containing information AOC considers necessary. Additionally, the clerks of the circuit courts, administratively supported by AOC, are responsible for processing and recording these modifications.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain employee or certain exclusive representative to initiate a grievance procedure under certain provisions of law; requiring certain decision makers in a grievance procedure in certain higher education systems to award certain damages under certain circumstances; requiring certain employee grievance procedures to include certain redress for certain violations; requiring the Secretary of Transportation to be consistent with certain provisions of law and include redress for certain violations; etc.
Title: State Personnel - Education and Transportation - Grievance Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: House Bill 184 authorizes employees—and their exclusive representatives—of the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) and Maryland public higher education institutions to initiate grievance procedures if payroll information is not timely or accurately reported. It requires the personnel and grievance procedures of MDOT, the University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, and Baltimore City Community College to provide redress for wage violations, including the mandatory award and payment of statutory damages.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT), public State institutions of higher education (University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, St. Mary's College of Maryland, Baltimore City Community College), and the Office of Administrative Hearings
stakeholders: Employees and exclusive employee bargaining representatives of the Maryland Department of Transportation and Maryland public colleges and universities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund and higher education expenditures increase to the extent that new grievances are filed and wage damages are awarded, though the overall impact is anticipated to be minimal absent widespread payroll errors. Reimbursable revenues and expenditures for the Office of Administrative Hearings increase to the extent cases are referred for adjudication (averaging approximately $4,556 per case). There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 184 directly amends Transportation Article § 2-103.4, requiring MDOT to update its human resources management regulations and grievance procedures to include redress and damage awards for wage and payroll reporting violations, impacting the Transportation Trust Fund.

The bill directly amends Education Article §§ 13-201 and 13-203, expanding the definition of employee grievances and requiring USM grievance decision-makers to award back pay and statutory damages for wage withholding and payroll reporting failures.

The bill directly amends Education Article § 14-302, mandating that decision-makers in grievance procedures at Morgan State University award statutory damages if wages were unlawfully withheld under State Personnel and Pensions provisions.

The bill directly amends Education Article § 14-408, requiring St. Mary's College of Maryland to incorporate provisions for the redress of wage payment violations, including the award and payment of damages, within its independent personnel system.

OAH adjudicates unresolved state personnel grievances and MDOT grievance appeals; the bill is anticipated to increase reimbursable revenues and expenditures for OAH as additional wage-related grievance cases are referred.

As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees the State Personnel Management System and state grievance standards that MDOT and higher education systems must align with under the amended State Personnel and Pensions Article § 2-407.

The Comptroller houses the Central Payroll Bureau (CPB), which processes state payrolls; the bill's provisions directly concern appointing authorities failing to report accurate and timely payroll information to CPB and subsequent reporting of missing wages and damages.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Board of Education from issuing a certificate of approval to noncollegiate educational institutions that do not have a policy prohibiting the administration of corporal punishment; requiring regulations adopted by the State Board for the registration of family child care homes and large family child care homes and the licensing and operation of child care centers to prohibit corporal punishment; and requiring the State Board to identify certain methods in a certain overall plan.
Title: Nonpublic Schools and Child Care Providers - Corporal Punishment - Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits the State Board of Education from issuing a certificate of approval to any noncollegiate educational institution (nonpublic school) that does not maintain a policy prohibiting staff from administering corporal punishment to discipline students. It also requires the State Board to include methods to eliminate corporal punishment in its statewide education plan and mandates regulations banning corporal punishment in family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Nonpublic schools, child care centers, family child care providers, educators, staff, and enrolled students and children.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education can comply with the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 185 directly mandates that the Maryland State Board of Education (and MSDE) update its overall educational plan to eliminate corporal punishment, deny certificates of approval to nonpublic schools without corporal punishment prohibitions, and update child care licensing and registration regulations to prohibit corporal punishment.

Synopsis: Providing for the stable funding and support of trauma-informed, high-quality programs and services for victims of crime; requiring the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to help support certain programs providing services for victims of crime; requiring the Office to consult with certain individuals and organizations regarding the allocation of certain funding; and requiring the Governor to include certain funding in the State budget.
Title: Victim Services Programs – Supplementing Federal Funding and Support (Victim Services Stabilization Act)

bill_summary: The Victim Services Stabilization Act requires the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to support crime victim services programs across Maryland and mandates that the Governor include an appropriation in the annual state budget that, combined with federal Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) funds from the prior year, totals $60 million annually to stabilize program funding.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
stakeholders: Crime victims throughout Maryland, as well as public and private nonprofit organizations operating victim services programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2025, the bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation that, combined with prior-year federal VOCA awards, totals $60.0 million. Because current state budgets already provide $35.0 million in general funds alongside federal funding (approximately $26.4 million in FY 2022), general fund expenditures and state revenues are not anticipated to be affected assuming funding levels hold; however, if federal funding decreases, state general fund expenditures will increase to meet the $60.0 million requirement. Local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 186 establishes the Victim Services Stabilization Act, directly tasking this office (formerly known as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) with administering the victim services programs, awarding grants, coordinating unified processes with federal VOCA funding, consulting with stakeholder groups, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual State budget that, combined with federal VOCA funding from the prior year, totals an aggregate $60 million.

As the agency responsible for preparing the Governor's annual budget and managing State expenditures, DBM must implement and account for the mandated annual appropriation totaling $60 million in aggregate state and federal victim services funds.

Synopsis: Increasing the membership of the Wildlife Advisory Commission; requiring the Governor to appoint a member to the Wildlife Advisory Commission who is an academic researcher with expertise in wildlife biology, wildlife conservation, wildlife management, or ecology; and requiring the membership of the Commission to include representation from the farming, hunting, wildlife preservation, and passive wildlife recreation communities.

bill_summary: Increases the membership of the Wildlife Advisory Commission from 9 to 10 members by adding an academic researcher with expertise in wildlife biology, conservation, management, or ecology, and specifies required representation from farming, hunting, wildlife preservation, and passive wildlife recreation communities.
responsible_party: The Governor of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Wildlife researchers and academics, farmers, hunters, wildlife preservationists, passive wildlife recreationists, and members of the Wildlife Advisory Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Wildlife Advisory Commission is established within the Department of Natural Resources to advise on wildlife management, conservation, and regulations.
The bill requires the Governor to solicit nominations and appoint the additional academic researcher member and ensure required representation on the Wildlife Advisory Commission.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing appointments to state boards and commissions, which includes the Wildlife Advisory Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory composition, member qualifications, and terms of the Wildlife Advisory Commission.

Synopsis: Clarifying the language of provisions of law requiring the expungement of certain records maintained by the State or a political subdivision of the State relating to the charging of certain offenses under certain circumstances and notification of a certain right to expungement.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Clarifies statutory language regarding the automatic expungement of records and associated notice requirements for civil cannabis offenses or crimes (excluding non-must-appear transportation violations) that result in dispositions of acquittal, dismissal, not guilty, or nolle prosequi without required treatment.
responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository)
stakeholders: Individuals charged with qualifying civil offenses or crimes whose cases resulted in favorable dispositions (acquittal, dismissal, not guilty, or unconditional nolle prosequi), law enforcement agencies, and the state court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill clarifies existing statutory language and does not substantively change state or local operations, expenditures, or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs court procedures for the automatic expungement of records and mandates court clerks to send notices of charge dispositions and expungement eligibility to the Central Repository, law enforcement, and defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which receives statutory notices from the courts and must expunge eligible criminal history records under the clarified criteria.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police maintains arrest and police records that are subject to notification and automatic expungement under the amended provisions.
The bill explicitly clarifies expungement application regarding criminal and payable offenses under the Transportation Article, and MDOT served as an informational source on the legislation.

As the MDOT modal administration responsible for driver records and citations under the Transportation Article, the MVA is implicated by statutory clarifications concerning non-appearance offenses under the Transportation Article.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain persons subject to campaign finance regulation from making or accepting monetary contributions or monetary donations using any currency other than United States currency; prohibiting a campaign finance entity or a person acting on behalf of a campaign finance entity from making a monetary expenditure using any currency other than United States currency; authorizing the State Administrator of Elections or the Administrator's designee to investigate certain potential violations of the Act; etc.
Title: Currency - Campaign Finance Prohibitions - Disclosures by Financial Institutions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits making, accepting, or expending campaign contributions, donations, or disbursements using any currency other than United States currency, including cryptocurrency. It authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to investigate violations, issue subpoenas, and allow the State Board of Elections to impose civil penalties or refer willful violations to the State Prosecutor. Additionally, it expands the definition of financial institution to include regulated virtual currency money transmitters, permitting the Comptroller to obtain information and seize assets to satisfy state tax liens.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Political candidates, campaign finance entities, donors, entities making independent expenditures or electioneering communications, virtual currency money transmitters, and delinquent taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase beginning in FY 2024 to the extent the Comptroller recovers unpaid taxes by seizing property held by virtual currency money transmitters. Special fund revenues (Fair Campaign Financing Fund) may also increase from civil penalties (up to $1,000 per violation) or criminal fines (up to $25,000). The State Board of Elections and Comptroller can implement and enforce the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Elections and the State Administrator of Elections with enforcing new prohibitions on non-U.S. currency (such as cryptocurrency) in campaign finance, granting them subpoena and investigative authority as well as the power to assess civil penalties.

The bill expands the definition of financial institution to include virtual currency money transmitters, directly authorizing the Comptroller to obtain information, request assistance, and seize or attach property to enforce State tax laws and collect tax liens.

The bill specifies that the State Board of Elections may refer potential willful and knowing violations of the campaign finance currency prohibitions to the State Prosecutor for criminal investigation and prosecution.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to stay the entering of a conviction, defer further proceedings, and place a certain defendant on probation subject to reasonable conditions if the court finds facts justifying a finding of guilt; authorizing the State and a certain defendant to enter into a probation agreement under certain circumstances; providing that the entry of a probation agreement under the Act shall be considered a probation before judgment for all other purposes under State law; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a court to place a criminal defendant on probation before judgment when the defendant pleads not guilty, provided the State consents, the defendant agrees in writing, and the court finds facts justifying a finding of guilt beyond a reasonable doubt while withholding an actual finding of guilt.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Criminal defendants (particularly noncitizens facing adverse federal immigration consequences under standard probation before judgment pleas), State's Attorneys, and the State court system
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $33,400 in FY 2024 only for Judiciary computer programming changes. State revenues and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article concerning AOC responsibilities to maintain lists of approved treatment programs, alters court procedures regarding probation before judgment agreements, and incurs a direct fiscal expenditure of $33,400 in FY 2024 for court IT programming modifications.

The bill amends the Health - General Article and Criminal Procedure Article regarding the department's role in reviewing, approving, and notifying the courts of substance abuse and alcoholism education and treatment programs required under probation orders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new procedure for probation before judgment agreements entered into by defendants pleading not guilty, directly affecting the legal strategy, plea advisements, and representation of indigent defendants by OPD attorneys.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department's Division of Parole and Probation oversees individuals placed on probation before judgment and custodial confinement terms authorized under the Criminal Procedure Article.

Synopsis: Making the proposed appropriations contained in the State Budget for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024, in accordance with Article III, Section 52 of the Maryland Constitution; etc.
Title: Budget Bill (Fiscal Year 2024)
bill_summary: House Bill 200 serves as the Maryland State Budget Bill for Fiscal Year 2024, establishing appropriations and spending authorizations for the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches of Maryland State government, public education, higher education institutions, and local aid programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies and employees, local governments, public school systems, higher education institutions, healthcare and social service providers, and Maryland residents receiving state-funded services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes Maryland's comprehensive operating and capital budget for Fiscal Year 2024 along with deficiency appropriations for Fiscal Year 2023. Total FY 2024 appropriations across all fund types (general, special, federal, and higher education funds) exceed $63 billion, net of reversions and contingent reductions, funding state agency operations, education aids, healthcare and public safety initiatives, transportation, and capital grants to local jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary fiscal and administrative agency executing the State Budget, managing statewide employee personnel expenses, COLAs, position allocations, and reporting requirements.
Directly receives operating appropriations across multiple divisions, is directed to conduct a tax penalty/interest study, and manages state accounting controls and revenue disbursements.

Receives major multi-billion dollar appropriations for Medicaid, public health, developmental disabilities, and behavioral health, along with numerous staffing and program reporting requirements.
Receives major appropriations for public education aid, Blueprint for Maryland's Future implementation, compensatory education, nonpublic schools (including BOOST), and special education programs.
Receives operating and capital funding for highway, transit, port, and aviation projects, as well as Consolidated Transportation Program reporting mandates and debt caps.
Receives operating and grant appropriations for social services, child welfare, adult services, assistance payments (SNAP/TANF), and home energy assistance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Receives extensive funding for correctional facilities, parole and probation, pretrial detention, and staffing, alongside specific reporting requirements on overtime and hiring.
Receives operational appropriations and oversees substantial capital PAYGO miscellaneous grants and state facility maintenance and construction.
Receives operational and capital funding for state parks, Program Open Space, natural resources police, and Chesapeake Bay restoration programs.
Receives appropriations for water quality, drinking water revolving loan funds, bay restoration, clean air administration, and compliance reporting.
Receives substantial appropriations for neighborhood revitalization, rental housing programs, broadband infrastructure deployment, and homeownership loans.
Receives funding for economic development financing programs, business tax credit reserve funds, tourism development, and arts grants.
Receives funding for workforce development, adult education, unemployment insurance, racing oversight, and implementation of the Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program.
Receives operational appropriations for youth detention facilities, community operations, education programs, and interagency child placement coordination.
Receives appropriations for agricultural land preservation, animal health, resource conservation, fair boards, and rural development programs.
Receives funding for enterprise IT security, the Major Information Technology Development Project Fund, and telecommunications oversight across executive agencies.
Receives funding for field operations, aviation command helicopter radios, criminal investigations, and licensing division positions, along with crime reporting requirements.
Receives general and special fund higher education appropriations across all constituent institutions, along with capital project allocations and academic reporting mandates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Receives grant and administrative appropriations, including VOCA crime victim services, local law enforcement grants, and state aid for police protection.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Receives operational appropriations for its establishment, the Service Year Option Program, and the absorption of the Maryland Corps and Volunteer Maryland programs.
Receives operational and contingency fund appropriations and miscellaneous grants to nonprofits, and holds statutory oversight of emergency position creation and contract approvals.
Receives substantial judicial branch funding for court operations, legal aid programs (Access to Counsel), and judicial IT projects.
Receives funding across civil, criminal, antitrust, consumer protection, and independent investigations divisions, including funding contingent on civil rights enforcement legislation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the creation of a State Debt in the amount of $1,218,639,000, the proceeds to be used for certain necessary building, construction, demolition, planning, renovation, conversion, replacement, and capital equipment purchases of the State, for acquiring certain real estate in connection therewith, and for grants to certain subdivisions and other organizations for certain development and improvement purposes; etc.
Title: Creation of a State Debt – Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2023, and the Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loans of 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, and 2022
bill_summary: The Maryland Consolidated Capital Bond Loan of 2023 (Capital Budget) authorizes the creation of State general obligation debt to finance building, construction, demolition, planning, renovation, and capital equipment purchases for State facilities, public schools, higher education institutions, environmental initiatives, and various local and community grant projects. It also adjusts prior bond authorizations and preauthorizes capital debt funding for future fiscal years.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works
stakeholders: State agencies, local governments, public school systems, higher education institutions, healthcare organizations, nonprofit community groups, and Maryland property owners and residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: Authorizes $1,218,639,000 in State general obligation bonds for FY 2024 capital projects, which is offset by $13,639,000 in reductions to prior State debt authorizations, yielding $1,205,000,000 in net new debt authorizations, along with $29,100,000 in bond premium allocations for a total authorization of $1,247,739,000. It also preauthorizes general obligation debt for future years: $629,689,000 for FY 2025, $239,789,000 for FY 2026, and $32,307,000 for FY 2027. Bond debt service will be paid through an annual State property tax on assessable property. Local governments and nonprofit grantees receive substantial capital grant revenues, though some must provide matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is the primary implementing and approving authority for the issuance of State general obligation bonds under the MCCBL, approving project expenditures, contracts, and matching fund requirements.

The Comptroller accounts for bond proceeds, manages loan fund accounts, executes transfers and adjustments, and tracks bond premium allocations.
The State Treasurer's Office receives cash proceeds from bond sales, pays bond issuance expenses, and determines bond premium transfers to the Annuity Bond Fund.
The Department of General Services manages construction and facilities for State agencies and is statutory co-author with DBM of the annual report on the Construction Contingency Fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing or altering the distribution of certain revenue; repealing a certain required appropriation to the Revenue Stabilization Account; altering the areas in which certain faculty must specialize to be assigned to provide clinical care at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center; reducing the budgeted Medicaid Deficit Assessment for fiscal year 2024; etc.
Title: Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: The Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2023 enacts various statutory changes to balance the State operating budget for fiscal year 2024. Key provisions include altering medical faculty assignment specializations at the UM Capital Region Medical Center, reducing the required fiscal 2024 appropriation to the Revenue Stabilization Account by $500 million to transfer funds to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, lowering the Medicaid Deficit Assessment on hospitals by $50 million, repealing the 15-year repayment schedule to the Local Reserve Account for recalculated Homeowners' Tax Credits, reducing fiscal 2023 appropriations for the Department of Human Services Assistance Payments Program by $7.5 million, reallocating $9.25 million of merger funds for natural gas infrastructure repairs, and extending property transfer deadlines for the Bainbridge Naval Training Center site.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management (along with the Maryland Department of Health, Department of Human Services, Maryland Energy Administration, and State Department of Assessments and Taxation)
stakeholders: Maryland Medicaid recipients and participating hospitals, public school systems and students funded through the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, homeowners receiving property tax credits, public assistance recipients, natural gas customers in the Washington Gas service area, and Baltimore County library users.
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2023, general fund expenditures decrease by $200,000. In FY 2024, general fund expenditures increase by $49.5 million, special fund revenues decrease by $50.0 million, and special fund expenditures decrease by $40.8 million, resulting in a net negative state fiscal impact of $58.7 million in FY 2024. For FY 2025 and FY 2026, general fund expenditures decrease by $500,000 annually. In FY 2027, general fund expenditures decrease by $500.5 million and special fund expenditures increase by $500.0 million due to the utilization of transferred Blueprint funds. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal fiscal and budget agency for the State, DBM oversees the implementation of the Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act (BRFA), which alters mandated appropriations, directs fund transfers, and balances the state operating budget.
The bill directly reduces the budgeted Medicaid Deficit Assessment for fiscal year 2024 by $50 million and requires MDH and HSCRC to adopt policies preserving the State's Medicare waiver.
The bill explicitly requires the Commission, along with the Department of Health, to adopt policies regarding hospital assessment revenues and the reduction of the Medicaid Deficit Assessment.
The bill reduces the fiscal year 2023 general fund appropriation for the Assistance Payments Program within DHS by $7.5 million.
The bill authorizes MEA to use $9.25 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) derived from the AltaGas/WGL merger to support natural gas infrastructure repairs.

The bill provides flexibility for the University of Maryland School of Medicine regarding the specialization areas required for faculty assigned to provide clinical care at the UM Capital Region Medical Center.
The bill extends the deadline by which a portion of the Bainbridge Naval Training Center site must be transferred to DNR for the Port Deposit State Historical Park from June 1, 2023, to June 1, 2025.
As an Administration bill, it modifies statutory budget mandates for the Governor's proposed budget and authorizes the Governor to transfer capital appropriations by budget amendment.
The bill repeals the statutory requirement for the Governor to include annual appropriations repaying the Local Reserve Account, which is maintained and administered by the Comptroller's Office.

By eliminating the fiscal 2024 appropriation to the Revenue Stabilization Account, the bill facilitates the contingent transfer of $500 million to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, which supports MSDE education funding.
The bill amends statutory general fund surplus distributions under § 7-311, referencing appropriations to the Maryland Equity Investment Fund administered by TEDCO.
The bill touches upon § 7-311 statutory provisions directing general fund surplus allocations to the accumulation funds of the State Retirement and Pension System.

stakeholders: Members of the Baltimore County Board of Education, the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, and Baltimore County voters and public school students.

bill_summary: House Bill 214 establishes the Commission on Public Health to evaluate and provide recommendations to improve the delivery of foundational public health services across Maryland. The commission is charged with assessing the foundational capabilities of the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments, holding statewide public meetings, establishing specialized workgroups, and submitting an interim report by December 1, 2023, and a final report by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Commission on Public Health
stakeholders: Maryland residents receiving foundational public health services, Maryland Department of Health, local health departments, public health workforce, and academic institutions providing public health programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are unaffected. MDH and other consulting State agencies can absorb any administrative impacts within existing budgeted resources. Higher education expenditures for public academic institutions represented by the commission cochairs may increase in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to provide staff support, though they can likely absorb this within existing resources; specific dollar estimates are unavailable. Local health departments can absorb any impact within existing budgeted resources with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Commission on Public Health to assess the foundational public health capabilities of the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and local health departments. Key MDH officials, including the Deputy Secretary for Public Health, Deputy Secretary for Behavioral Health, and the Director of the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities, serve on the Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary statutory body—the Commission on Public Health—tasked with studying Maryland's public health delivery and making comprehensive reform recommendations before sunsetting on June 30, 2025.

The legislation requires the Governor to appoint a faculty member from a public health program at an HBCU (such as Morgan State University's School of Community Health and Policy) to serve as a cochair of the Commission, and requires the cochair's institution to provide staff support.

The bill requires representatives from State academic institutions with public health expertise to be appointed to the Commission, serve as cochair, and provide staff support for the Commission's work and meetings.
The Governor is responsible for appointing multiple members of the Commission, designating cochairs, and receiving the interim and final reports outlining recommended public health reforms.
The bill statutorily requires the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Maryland Health Care Commission as appropriate and necessary in performing its duties.

The bill statutorily requires the Commission on Public Health to consult with the Health Services Cost Review Commission as appropriate and necessary in conducting its assessments and developing recommendations.

The Commission on Public Health is required to consult with the Department of Budget and Management, particularly as it develops recommendations regarding funding and public health workforce personnel structures.

The Commission on Public Health is required to consult with the Department of General Services, particularly as it examines procurement reforms and contractor oversight within public health operations.
The Commission on Public Health is mandated to consult with the Maryland Department of Disabilities as appropriate to evaluate health equity and foundational public health service delivery.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the newly established Commission.
