Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: House Bill 226 expands the definition of a 'person in a position of authority' under Maryland's fourth-degree sexual offense statute to include individuals working for pay or volunteering in schools as well as youth programs (such as sports, arts, tutoring, day care, scouting, camps, and religious institutions) who supervise or interact with minors. It prohibits such individuals from engaging in sexual acts, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with a minor enrolled in the school or participating in the program (provided the minor in a program is at least six years younger). Additionally, the bill specifies that the offense cannot be treated as a lesser included crime unless specifically charged by the State, and authorizes consecutive or concurrent sentencing.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District Court and Circuit Courts), State's Attorneys, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Minors participating in schools and youth programs; employees and volunteers at schools, camps, sports leagues, tutoring centers, child care facilities, and religious institutions; law enforcement; prosecutors; and correctional facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. State general fund revenues and expenditures will see minimal increases due to expanded application of existing fines and potential incarceration in State correctional facilities or county reimbursement costs. Local revenues and expenditures will likewise see minimal increases from circuit court fines and local detention center costs. The Judiciary, State's Attorneys' Association, and the Office of the Public Defender can absorb any operational impacts using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal prohibitions for fourth-degree sexual offense involving persons in positions of authority, leading to potential additional convictions and commitments to State correctional facilities.
The judiciary is responsible for adjudicating expanded misdemeanor charges and sentencing provisions under fourth-degree sexual offense statutes across District and Circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office may experience an increase in caseload and workload to provide legal representation for indigent defendants charged under the expanded statutory provisions.

The bill directly defines and regulates conduct for persons in positions of authority working or volunteering at public and private schools, academic enrichment programs, and child care settings overseen by MSDE.

Synopsis: Requiring the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to release certain personal information of a minor who has a work permit to employers and apprenticeship sponsors, educational programs and institutions, and local workforce development boards that have requested and have registered with the Maryland Department of Labor for the purpose of receiving the information, if a parent or legal guardian of the minor or the minor elects to allow the sharing of the information.
Title: Employment for Minors - Opportunities for Work

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to share the name, home address, and telephone number of a minor who is at least 16 years old and holds a work permit with registered employers, apprenticeship sponsors, educational institutions, and local workforce development boards, provided the minor or their parent or guardian opts in to permit the release of information.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry, Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Minors aged 16 and older with work permits, parents and guardians of working minors, employers, apprenticeship sponsors, educational programs and institutions, and local workforce development boards.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the requirements and release the information to registered organizations using existing budgeted resources. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Commissioner of Labor and Industry and the Maryland Department of Labor with releasing personal contact information of eligible minors who opt in to registered employers, apprenticeship sponsors, educational institutions, and local workforce boards, as well as adopting the necessary regulations to implement the program.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations on or before December 1, 2023, establishing requirements for the sale of new zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles in the State; defining a "heavy-duty vehicle" as one with a gross vehicle weight rating equal to or greater than 14,001 pounds; requiring the Department, in consultation with certain units of State government, to prepare and submit to the General Assembly a certain needs assessment and deployment plan by December 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Department of the Environment - Zero-Emission Medium- and Heavy-Duty Vehicles - Regulations (Clean Trucks Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: The Clean Trucks Act of 2023 requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to adopt regulations by December 1, 2023, establishing requirements for the sale of new zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, incorporating California's Advanced Clean Trucks regulations starting in model year 2027. It authorizes MDE to delay implementation if deemed infeasible based on a required needs assessment and deployment plan due by December 1, 2024. The bill also modifies the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program administered by the Maryland Energy Administration, increasing the mandated annual appropriation from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to at least $10,000,000 for fiscal years 2024 through 2027 and focusing grants on commercial and industrial vehicles.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Commercial and industrial vehicle purchasers, medium- and heavy-duty vehicle manufacturers and dealers, local governments, electric utilities, and residents of overburdened and underserved communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by $474,200 in FY 2024 for MDE administrative and contractor costs, followed by $157,600 to $181,100 annually through FY 2028. Strategic Energy Investment Fund special fund expenditures increase by $5.25 million in FY 2024 and $5.0 million annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027 to satisfy the $10.0 million annual grant program appropriation. State agencies and local governments may face higher initial purchase costs for zero-emission vehicles starting in model year 2027, though local governments may also receive increased grant funding. State revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency tasked with adopting regulations incorporating California's Advanced Clean Trucks standards, conducting stakeholder outreach, establishing a vehicle credit compliance program, and leading the development of the needs assessment and deployment plan.

MEA administers the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program, which receives an increased mandated appropriation of at least $10 million annually from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) along with altered grant caps, eligibility criteria, and preferences. MEA is also a statutory consulting partner on the needs assessment and deployment plan.

MDOT is explicitly designated in statute to consult with MDE on preparing the needs assessment and deployment plan and evaluating whether to delay implementation of the regulations based on feasibility.

DGS manages state facilities and state fleet operations and is required by statute to consult with MDE on the needs assessment and deployment plan, particularly regarding charging infrastructure and transitioning the State vehicle fleet to zero-emission vehicles.
PSC is statutorily mandated to consult with MDE on the needs assessment and deployment plan to evaluate additional electrical grid capacity, transmission, distribution demands, and utility readiness.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual budget appropriation of at least $10 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund for the grant program for fiscal years 2024 through 2027.

DBM is responsible for drafting the annual state budget and incorporating the bill's mandated funding increases from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, as well as overseeing state vehicle procurement and fleet budget planning.

Synopsis: Providing that the use of cannabis by a parent or certain other individuals who care for a child does not qualify as neglect except in certain circumstances for purposes of provisions of law relating to children in need of assistance.
Title: Child in Need of Assistance – Neglect – Cannabis Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: Clarifies that cannabis use by a parent, guardian, or caregiver does not constitute child neglect for the purposes of Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings unless the use harms or creates a substantial risk of physical harm or mental injury to the child.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Parents, legal guardians, and caregivers who use cannabis, as well as children subject to or at risk of Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS and its local departments of social services are responsible for child protection, investigating allegations of child abuse and neglect, and initiating Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings. The bill directly modifies the legal threshold of neglect related to cannabis use.

CINA cases are judicial proceedings governed by the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article and adjudicated in the juvenile/circuit courts, which are supported and administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent parents in CINA and parental defense proceedings where neglect is alleged, making the statutory definition of neglect directly relevant to their caseload and legal defense strategies.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to take disciplinary action against an applicant or a licensee for failing to comply with a Board order; authorizing the Board to grant a stay of enforcement of a Board order in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act; prohibiting a Board order from being stayed pending judicial review; authorizing the Board to reinstate a suspended or revoked license only in accordance with the terms and conditions of the order or an order of reinstatement issued by the Board; etc.
Title: State Board of Chiropractic Examiners - Disciplinary Actions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Chiropractic Examiners to discipline applicants or licensees for failing to comply with board orders, allows the Board to grant stays under the Administrative Procedure Act while barring orders from being stayed pending judicial review, allows the Board to appeal decisions that reverse or modify its orders, and establishes conditions for license reinstatement.
responsible_party: State Board of Chiropractic Examiners
stakeholders: Chiropractic license applicants and licensed chiropractors and chiropractic assistants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill can be implemented using existing budgeted resources, with no impact on state revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Chiropractic Examiners operates within the Maryland Department of Health, which regulates health care professionals in the state. The bill directly alters the Board's disciplinary authority, stay procedures, and license reinstatement provisions.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and representation to state licensing boards, including representing the Board of Chiropractic Examiners in disciplinary matters and exercising the bill's authority to appeal court decisions that reverse or modify Board orders.

The bill impacts judicial review of Board decisions by specifying that an order of the Board may not be stayed pending judicial review and authorizing the Board to appeal decisions reversing or modifying its orders in court.

Synopsis: Prohibiting in all counties, rather than Baltimore City only, a holder of a certificate of sale from filing a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption for owner-occupied residential property until 9 months from the date of sale; prohibiting in all counties, rather than Baltimore City only, a certain notice from being sent to certain persons with an interest in owner-occupied residential property sold at tax sale until 7 months after the date of sale; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Owner-Occupied Property - Foreclosure, Notice, and Reimbursement of Expenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: This bill extends statutory timelines regarding tax sales for owner-occupied residential property statewide to match existing rules in Baltimore City. It prohibits certificate of sale holders across Maryland from filing a complaint to foreclose the right of redemption until nine months after the tax sale date (up from six months), and delays the required initial foreclosure notice and eligibility for expense reimbursements until seven months after the sale (up from four months).
responsible_party: Local county tax collectors and the Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts)
stakeholders: Homeowners residing in owner-occupied properties subject to tax sales, tax sale certificate purchasers/investors, and local government tax collection offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. Any effect on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory timelines governing when certificate holders can file complaints in circuit court to foreclose the right of redemption for owner-occupied residential properties sold at tax sale. As the central administrative support entity for the Maryland Judiciary, the Administrative Office of the Courts manages court processes and case management systems impacted by these civil foreclosure filings.

Synopsis: Expressing the intent of the General Assembly that at least 2% of the balance in the Homeowner Protection Fund be spent each year to conduct outreach in a certain manner to homeowners in tax sale to encourage the homeowners to enroll in the Homeowner Protection Program; authorizing the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to conduct outreach using State employees and resources or to contract with a private vendor; requiring that certain State and local government agencies provide certain information to facilitate outreach efforts; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protection Program - Outreach

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill establishes the intent of the General Assembly that at least 2% of the Homeowner Protection Fund balance be spent annually on outreach to homeowners in tax sales to encourage enrollment in the Homeowner Protection Program. It authorizes the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to conduct this outreach using State resources or by contracting with a private vendor, requires certain State and local agencies to share contact details upon request, and mandates reporting on outreach activities in the annual tax sale report.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman within the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
stakeholders: Homeowners in Maryland whose properties are subject to or sold at tax sale, particularly those eligible for the Homeowner Protection Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Homeowner Protection Fund) expenditures may increase by up to $204,200 in FY 2024 (and approximately $187,100 to $202,100 annually in future years) for staff, call center vendor contracting, and system programming. Special fund revenues may experience an indeterminate decrease beginning in FY 2025 if funds used for outreach reduce the purchase of recoverable homeowner tax liens. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller, notwithstanding tax confidentiality provisions under § 13–202 of the Tax – General Article, to provide the State Tax Sale Ombudsman with telephone numbers of homeowners included on tax returns. The fiscal note also identifies a $30,000 programming cost for the Comptroller's Office to query its database to produce these contact numbers.

Synopsis: Extending, until July 1, 2036, the termination date applicable to an exemption from the sales and use tax for certain construction material or warehousing equipment purchased for use in a certain target redevelopment area in Baltimore County.
Title: Sales and Use Tax Exemption - Redevelopment Areas in Baltimore County - Sunset Extension
bill_summary: Extends the termination date from June 30, 2026, to June 30, 2036, for a sales and use tax exemption on eligible construction materials and warehousing equipment purchased solely for use in designated target redevelopment areas in Baltimore County formerly owned by Bethlehem Steel Corporation.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Businesses, property owners, and contractors purchasing construction materials or warehousing equipment within the designated Baltimore County target redevelopment area, as well as competing businesses not eligible for the exemption.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will continue to decrease through FY 2036 due to the extended tax exemption, though the exact amount is indeterminate as it depends on the volume of eligible purchases made. State expenditures are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's sales and use tax. Under the bill's provisions, the Comptroller is responsible for issuing evidence of eligibility to buyers seeking the sales and use tax exemption for construction materials and warehousing equipment in the target redevelopment area.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to grant a stay of enforcement of a Board order in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act; prohibiting an order of the Board from being stayed pending judicial review; authorizing the Board to appeal a decision that reverses or modifies its order; altering the grounds for disciplining massage therapists and procedures related to the discipline of massage therapists, including appeals procedures and reinstatement procedures; etc.
Title: Massage Therapy - Discipline

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill updates the disciplinary and regulatory framework for massage therapy in Maryland. It adds failure to comply with a board order as grounds for disciplinary action, establishes procedures for stays of enforcement and appeals, and outlines specific requirements for reinstating a suspended or revoked license or registration. Additionally, it repeals the requirement to publish notice of license suspensions or revocations in the Maryland Register within 24 hours and exempts practitioners whose licenses or registrations expired fewer than six months prior from certain criminal misdemeanor penalties for unlicensed practice.
responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, individuals with expired or disciplined credentials, and the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected; the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill's changes using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners operates within the Maryland Department of Health to regulate massage therapy professionals. The bill directly alters the Board's disciplinary procedures, reinstatement requirements, enforcement stays, and penalties.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to health occupations licensing boards and represents the state in judicial appeals; the bill authorizes the Board to appeal judicial decisions that reverse or modify its disciplinary orders.

Synopsis: Establishing the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force to survey and document a representative sampling of the variety of ordinances, laws, codes, and policies regarding the development and operation of accessory dwelling units in areas zoned for single-family residential use; and requiring the Task Force to report to the Governor and General Assembly on its activities on or before November 1, 2023, and its findings and recommendations on or before June 1, 2024.
Title: Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 798

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Establishes the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force to survey State and local codes and policies regarding accessory dwelling units (ADUs) in single-family residential zones, study best practices for permitting, and make policy recommendations and best practices for local governments concerning practical development issues and impacts on housing markets and neighborhood livability.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Single-family homeowners, local governments, residential builders, architects, realtors, community associations, and individuals seeking affordable housing in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 only for the Maryland Department of Planning to hire a consultant to support the Task Force's work and recommendations. Task force members serve without compensation but are eligible for travel reimbursements. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Planning as a member of the Task Force, tasks the Department of Planning with staffing the Task Force, and requires $50,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2024 for the department to hire a consultant.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force, which addresses accessory dwelling units and affordable housing policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Accessory Dwelling Unit Policy Task Force as a temporary advisory body to conduct a study and issue recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Governor is required to appoint eleven members to the Task Force, designate its chair, and receive the Task Force's interim and final reports.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing the eleven gubernatorial appointments to the newly created task force.

Synopsis: Authorizing an application for special death benefits to be made for the death of certain members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Special Death Benefits - Applicability

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Authorizes the surviving spouse of a Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) member who died by homicide on or after June 1, 2001, in the course of duty, to apply for and receive a retroactive special death benefit by December 31, 2023, adjusted for previously paid general death benefits and compounded annually at 4% interest.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: The surviving spouse of a deceased correctional officer (specifically Correctional Officer Gregory Collins) and the State Retirement and Pension System.
fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities or employer contributions because the bill is expected to apply to only one individual. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System, which is administered by the Maryland State Retirement Agency, with receiving applications, calculating retroactive lump sum payments with interest and reductions, and administering the special death benefit for qualifying Correctional Officers' Retirement System members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation directly pertains to a correctional officer employed by the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services who died in the line of duty, resolving pension benefit issues stemming from service with the department.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "massage therapy"; altering the date after which the option to be registered by the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to practice massage therapy in a setting that is not a health care setting will no longer be available; and repealing a provision of law that provides that certain provisions of law do not require a nonprofit health insurance plan, an insurer, a health maintenance organization, or a person acting as a third party administrator to reimburse certain individuals for services rendered.
Title: Massage Therapy - Definition, Registration, and Reimbursement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: This bill modifies the definition of massage therapy by striking the exclusion of treatment of illness, disease, or injury from the definition. It repeals a statutory provision specifying that health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, HMOs, and third-party administrators are not required to reimburse licensed massage therapists or registered massage practitioners. Additionally, it delays by one year (from October 1, 2023, to October 1, 2024) the deadline after which the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can no longer issue initial registrations to practice as a registered massage practitioner.
responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, massage therapy students/applicants, health insurance carriers and third-party administrators, and massage therapy patients.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees health occupation regulatory bodies, including the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners, which is directly responsible for administering the licensure, registration, and regulation of massage therapists and practitioners impacted by this bill.

The bill repeals a statutory exemption that expressly provided health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans were not required to reimburse licensed massage therapists or registered practitioners, impacting health insurance carrier reimbursement frameworks regulated by the Administration.

Synopsis: Transferring the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency;  requiring program grant applicants to include the distribution of books to children in low-income zip codes within the applicants' areas of service; requiring the Governor to include $350,000 in the annual budget bill for the Program; requiring the State Library Board, beginning December 1, 2024, to report every other year to the General Assembly on the effectiveness of the Program; etc.
Title: Baltimore City Young Readers Program and Young Readers Matching Grant Program - Alterations (Young Readers Program Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Transfers the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program from the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to the Maryland State Library Agency under the administration of the State Librarian. It authorizes public libraries to apply for matching grants, requires prioritization of book distribution to children in low-income zip codes, institutes biennial reporting requirements, and increases the annual mandated appropriation for the matching grant program from $250,000 to $350,000.
responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
stakeholders: Young children (particularly in low-income areas), public library systems, local governments, and nonprofit early reader/book-gifting organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 to fund the increased statutory mandated appropriation for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program (increasing from $250,000 to $350,000). In FY 2024, $746,193 previously budgeted under GOCPYVS transfers to the Maryland State Library Agency, which incurs approximately $42,300 in administrative costs from existing funds. Local revenues and expenditures increase for local public libraries and county governments that apply for and receive matching grant awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 243 directly transfers the administration of the Baltimore City Young Readers Program and the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to the Maryland State Library Agency. The State Librarian is tasked with administering both programs, processing grant applications from public libraries and affiliated services, and the State Library Board must collect data and report biennially to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the programs and their associated budgeted funds away from this office (formerly the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) to the Maryland State Library Agency.
The bill modifies mandated annual appropriations that must be included in the State budget bill, increasing the required annual funding for the Young Readers Matching Grant Program to $350,000.

Synopsis: Requiring a register of wills to accept certain documents filed electronically through a system established by the register of wills; and prohibiting a register of wills from refusing to accept a document based on the manner in which it was signed.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Registers of Wills - Electronic Filing and Signatures
bill_summary: Requires Maryland registers of wills to accept documents (excluding original wills) filed electronically through an established system and in accordance with Maryland Rules, and prohibits registers from rejecting documents based on the manner in which they were signed while continuing to permit paper filings.
responsible_party: Maryland Registers of Wills
stakeholders: Individuals filing estate and probate documents, estate planning and probate attorneys, testators, personal representatives, and the offices of the Registers of Wills.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by a relatively minimal amount beginning in FY 2024 due to decreased administrative costs from reduced paper filings (illustratively estimated at at least $40,000 annually statewide). State expenditures are not affected because the web-based electronic filing system was already budgeted. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that Registers of Wills accept documents filed electronically through a system established by the registers and prohibits them from rejecting documents based on the manner of signature, directly impacting their administrative and filing operations.

Electronic filings with the Registers of Wills must comply with the Maryland Rules established for the judicial system, and the Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch and oversees court rules and electronic filing standards statewide.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to include an attestation that all units required to report are represented in its annual report beginning December 31, 2023; requiring the Office to conduct a certain periodic audit to ensure the accuracy of the attestation; requiring a certain annual report to be submitted to the Joint Committee on Fair Practices and State Personnel Oversight; etc.
Title: Minority Business Enterprise Program - Reporting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Governor’s Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA) to include an attestation in its annual Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) report confirming that all required Executive Branch units are represented. The bill also directs GOSBA to conduct an audit of Executive Branch entities every three years starting by December 31, 2023, requires the Office of State Procurement to maintain a list of reporting units, and updates legislative reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA)
stakeholders: Executive Branch state procurement units, certified Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs), and state contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. GOSBA can comply with the reporting and triennial audit requirements using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is the primary implementing agency for this bill, responsible for including an attestation in its annual MBE report that all required units are represented, conducting triennial audits of the Executive Branch to identify all qualifying units, and submitting the report to designated legislative committees.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Office of State Procurement within the Department of General Services maintain a comprehensive list of the state units required to submit annual MBE procurement reports.
The Board of Public Works receives the annual MBE summary report from GOSBA and oversees and approves the form of the reports submitted under the statute.
As the State's designated MBE certification agency referenced in the statute, MDOT receives annual MBE procurement reports from units alongside GOSBA.

Synopsis: Extending to October 1, 2028, the authority of the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to impose a transfer tax on certain instruments of writing.
Title: St. Mary's County - Transfer Tax - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill extends the authority of the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to impose a local transfer tax on instruments of writing from October 1, 2024, to October 1, 2028.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County
stakeholders: Property buyers and sellers in St. Mary's County and residents benefiting from county capital improvement projects.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. St. Mary's County maintains approximately $8.0 million annually in local transfer tax revenues through FY 2028, with an estimated $2.0 million collected in FY 2029 reflecting three months of collections prior to expiration. County expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends St. Mary's County's authority to impose a transfer tax on instruments of writing recorded with the Clerk of the Circuit Court for St. Mary's County, which operates under the administrative and technological support of the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County to issue a Class B-ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) license for use at certain Towson University events.
Title: Baltimore County - Class B-ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) License - Towson University

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class B-ECF/DS (Education Conference Facility/Dining Service) beer, wine, and liquor license to an authorized individual on behalf of Towson University for use at certain university-related events catered by the university's dining contractor.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County
stakeholders: Towson University, campus dining contractors, event attendees, and Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Baltimore County revenues increase by $2,500 in FY 2024 from application and license fees, and by $2,000 annually thereafter for license renewal fees. Enforcement can be handled with existing county resources. Retail sale profits are deposited into Towson University's auxiliary services account.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Towson University is a member institution of the University System of Maryland. The bill directly impacts the university by authorizing it to designate an individual to hold a Class B-ECF/DS alcoholic beverages license for campus events and deposit sales profits into its auxiliary services account.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person who applies for certain property tax exemptions for real property in Baltimore City to request that the exemption be applied retroactively for up to 3 taxable years, subject to certain requirements; requiring Baltimore City and the State to pay a refund of excess real property taxes paid due to a retroactive exemption that is granted; and requiring the Baltimore City Department of Finance to submit a report on the number of requests made and the amounts refunded by December 1 each year from 2023 to 2027.
Title: Baltimore City - Property Tax - Retroactive Exemption
bill_summary: Authorizes individuals and organizations applying for specified real property tax exemptions (such as for charitable, religious, or educational purposes) in Baltimore City to request that the exemption apply retroactively for up to three taxable years upon showing good cause. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation must grant approved exemptions subject to review and approval by the Baltimore City Solicitor and Department of Finance, and both the State and Baltimore City must refund any excess property taxes paid.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
stakeholders: Nonprofit, charitable, and religious organizations owning real property in Baltimore City, Baltimore City government, and the State of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues decrease by approximately $14,200 annually from FY 2023 through FY 2027. Baltimore City real property tax revenues decrease by approximately $285,000 annually over the same period due to refunds paid for retroactive exemptions. Baltimore City can handle the associated reporting requirements using existing resources, and State expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Baltimore City Department of Finance submit an annual report to the Governor detailing the number of retroactive property tax exemption requests received and approved, as well as amounts refunded, through December 1, 2027.

The bill requires the State to pay refunds for excess real property taxes paid due to granted retroactive exemptions, which impacts state revenue administration and disbursements handled by the Comptroller as Maryland's chief financial officer and tax collector.

Synopsis: Repealing certain geographic and temporal restrictions on the issuance of Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Class A-7 Licenses
bill_summary: This bill removes geographic and temporal restrictions on Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City by allowing them to be issued in the 43rd legislative district and repealing the previous July 1, 2022 termination deadline for issuing such licenses.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license holders (particularly Class B-D-7 holders seeking an exchange), business owners seeking Class A-7 licenses in Baltimore City (including the 43rd legislative district), and local consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Baltimore City revenues will increase minimally beginning in FY 2024 depending on the number of licenses issued or exchanged. For each new Class A-7 license issued, city revenues increase by $2,100 initially ($600 application fee plus $1,500 annual license fee) and $1,500 annually thereafter; for each Class B-D-7 license exchanged, revenues increase by $780 initially and $180 annually thereafter. Enforcement can be handled with existing city resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry. While the bill specifically alters local licensing provisions administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it falls generally under the Comptroller's broader regulatory subject matter.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations to exempt an on-farm composting facility from the requirement to obtain a permit if the on-farm composting facility uses 10,000 square feet of area or less for active food scrap composting, composts only certain materials, records the amount and source of off-site type 2 organics composted and the date and time the off-site type 2 organics arrived on the farm, retains the records for 5 years, provides records on request, and meets any other condition for a permit exemption; etc.
Title: Environment - On-Farm Composting Facilities - Permit Exemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations exempting certain on-farm composting facilities using 10,000 square feet or less for active food scrap composting from permit requirements, provided they meet specific feedstock and recordkeeping criteria and give prior written notice to the department. It also establishes construction and operational standards for new composting facilities and requires a report on on-farm composting impacts by December 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Maryland farmers, farm operators, and agricultural businesses engaging in on-farm composting
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can promulgate regulations, handle enforcement, and prepare the required report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local governments. Qualifying farm operators may experience a minimal positive impact from reduced regulatory burdens and lower solid waste management costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency tasked with adopting regulations to establish the on-farm composting facility permit exemption, collecting required notices and records, and submitting an impact report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028.

The bill directly impacts agricultural operations and references compliance with agricultural nutrient management plans under COMAR 15.20.07 as well as soil conservation and agricultural waste management system plans, areas regulated and supported by MDA.

Synopsis: Requiring that a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Caroline County be a resident of the State rather than a resident of the county; and requiring that a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Queen Anne's County be a resident of the State rather than a resident of the county.
Title: Caroline and Queen Anne's Counties - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Residency Requirement
bill_summary: Alters the residency requirements for certain alcoholic beverages license applicants in Caroline County and Queen Anne's County, establishing that at least one applicant must be a resident of Maryland rather than of the county, and requiring that at least one applicant maintain Maryland residency for the license to remain valid.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Caroline County and Board of License Commissioners for Queen Anne's County
stakeholders: Applicants for and holders of alcoholic beverages licenses in Caroline and Queen Anne's counties, including partnerships, limited liability companies, clubs, and corporations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and is not anticipated to materially affect the operations or finances of Caroline or Queen Anne's counties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and prescribes standard alcoholic beverage license application forms referenced in the statute. Although local licensing boards administer these county-level licenses, the bill directly concerns alcohol licensing statutory requirements.

Synopsis: Establishing a licensing and regulatory system for sign language interpreters under the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters in the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing; establishing the Sign Language Interpreters Fund to be used exclusively to cover the documented direct and indirect costs of fulfilling the Board's duties, including development of programs to assist licensure of marginalized interpreters, development of certain mentorship programs, and financial assistance for certain applicants; etc.
Title: Maryland Sign Language Interpreters Act

bill_summary: The Maryland Sign Language Interpreters Act establishes a licensing and regulatory system for individuals providing sign language interpretation services in Maryland. The bill creates the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters within the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, establishes standard and provisional licensing requirements and fees, creates the dedicated Sign Language Interpreters Fund, sets disciplinary procedures and penalties for practicing without a license, and mandates a one-time appropriation in fiscal year 2025.
responsible_party: State Board of Sign Language Interpreters in the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
stakeholders: Sign language interpreters, deaf and hard of hearing individuals, deafblind individuals, interpreting service agencies, courts and the Maryland Judiciary, and educational institutions such as the Maryland School for the Deaf.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $94,300 in FY 2024 for one-time Judiciary IT programming. State general and special fund expenditures for the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing increase by $159,500 in FY 2024 and $374,000 in FY 2025 (reflecting new personnel and operating costs), including a mandated $100,000 general fund appropriation in FY 2025. Special fund revenues from license fees and training workshops are projected at $90,000 in FY 2025, increasing to $224,000 by FY 2028. Local circuit courts may experience delays or higher costs for securing qualified interpreters.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 260 establishes the State Board of Sign Language Interpreters within the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing (ODHH). ODHH is responsible for staffing the board, administering the new Sign Language Interpreters Fund, establishing nomination processes, and reporting annually on the board's licensing and complaint activities.

The bill mandates annual reporting by the Maryland Judiciary regarding sign language interpreter requests, scheduling delays, postponements, and emergency usage in court cases. The fiscal note also identifies a $94,300 expenditure in FY 2024 for IT modifications to the Judicial Information System as well as potential operational impacts on court proceeding delays.

The Governor is responsible for appointing all seven members of the new State Board of Sign Language Interpreters, exercising authority over the board, receiving annual reports, and including a mandated $100,000 general fund appropriation in the FY 2025 state budget.

The fiscal note specifically notes that the Maryland School for the Deaf may face operational and fiscal impacts if the new licensing framework limits the supply of available sign language interpreters or increases the costs of retaining interpreters for student instruction and support services.
The bill requires the Board to pay all collected licensing fees to the Comptroller, who must distribute them to the Sign Language Interpreters Fund and account for the fund.
The bill establishes the Sign Language Interpreters Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund that must be held separately and invested by the State Treasurer.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, which will include the newly created State Board of Sign Language Interpreters.

Synopsis: Requiring producers of any cement or concrete mixture used in the construction of an eligible project to submit environmental product declarations to the Department of General Services by December 31, 2024; requiring the Department to establish a maximum acceptable global warming potential for certain categories of eligible materials by January 1, 2026; establishing an Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund to support the development of certain environmental product declarations; etc.
Title: Eligible Projects - Procurement of Construction Materials (Buy Clean Maryland Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: The Buy Clean Maryland Act requires the Department of General Services (DGS), in consultation with the Maryland Department of Transportation, to establish maximum acceptable global warming potential levels for cement or concrete mixtures used in state-funded capital construction projects. Producers of eligible materials must submit environmental product declarations (EPDs), and contractors must submit EPDs before installing materials on eligible projects starting July 1, 2026. The act also creates an Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund administered by the Department of Commerce to provide grants to material producers through December 31, 2024.
responsible_party: Department of General Services and Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Cement and concrete producers and manufacturers, construction contractors bidding on state capital projects, state agencies, and community colleges.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $200,000 in FY 2024 to capitalize the grant fund, with special fund revenues and expenditures increasing commensurately. General fund expenditures also increase by $50,000 in FY 2025 for consulting services and $217,876 in FY 2026 for DGS staffing, growing to $485,100 by FY 2028. Total state and local capital spending caps remain unchanged, but increased costs for low-carbon materials may lead to project delays or cancellations, including for state-aided local community college capital projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency for the Buy Clean Maryland Act. It is responsible for analyzing environmental product declarations (EPDs), establishing and periodically updating the maximum acceptable global warming potential (GWP) for eligible materials, monitoring contractor compliance on State capital projects, processing waivers, and submitting annual implementation reports to the General Assembly.

The bill assigns the Department of Commerce direct administrative oversight of the newly created Environmental Product Declaration Assistance Fund, which awards grants to producers of eligible materials to support the development and transparency of EPDs.

MDOT is explicitly mandated by statute to consult with DGS in establishing the maximum acceptable global warming potential for eligible construction materials, and its capital construction projects using concrete and cement are affected by the procurement standards.

Synopsis: Authorizing a police department that takes an abandoned vehicle into custody to notify any secured party electronically if that form of notice is agreed to by the police department, the tower, and the secured party in a certain manner; and altering the application of a provision of law authorizing a police department to provide certain alternative public notice of custody of an abandoned vehicle to include circumstances where electronic notice is unacknowledged or undeliverable.
Title: Abandoned Vehicles - Secured Parties - Electronic Notification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes a police department that takes an abandoned vehicle into custody to notify a secured party electronically rather than by certified mail, provided that the police department, tower, and secured party agree to electronic notification in writing or by electronic communication. It also permits alternative public notice via circuit court posting if an electronic notice is returned as undeliverable or is unacknowledged.
responsible_party: Maryland State Police and local police departments
stakeholders: Secured parties (lienholders/vehicle lenders), towing companies (towers), local and state police departments, and owners of abandoned vehicles
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations, although operational efficiencies and minimal cost savings from reduced certified mail expenses may be realized. The effect on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary statewide law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing motor vehicle laws and patrolling state highways, the Maryland State Police routinely takes abandoned vehicles into custody and is directly authorized under the bill to utilize electronic notification for secured parties.

The MVA maintains vehicle titling, registration, and lienholder records referenced in the statute to determine the identity of secured parties entitled to notice when an abandoned vehicle is impounded.
MDOT oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and state transportation facilities where abandoned vehicle removals and highway clearance protocols are implemented.
The bill updates conditions under which police departments must post abandoned vehicle notices in local circuit courts if electronic notification is unacknowledged or undeliverable.

Synopsis: Authorizing a certain senior activity center to conduct gaming events, bunco games, and card games in St. Mary's County; prohibiting a senior activity center in St. Mary's County from awarding prize money in excess of $50 to a winner in each session or charging a participant more than $25 to play one session; requiring any money that remains after prizes are awarded to be used to support future programming at the senior activity center; etc.
Title: St. Mary's County - Gaming - Senior Activity Centers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles

bill_summary: Authorizes senior activity centers in St. Mary's County to host gaming events, bunco games, and card games, subject to limits of a maximum $25 entry fee per session and a maximum cash prize of $50 per session. Any remaining proceeds after prizes are paid out must be used to fund future programming at the center.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County State's Attorney and St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office
stakeholders: Senior citizens and their spouses participating in programs at senior activity centers in St. Mary's County, as well as the senior activity centers themselves.
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. While gaming events could potentially draw small amounts away from State lottery and casino facilities, any impact is negligible. Local fiscal effects are also negligible, with no substantial impact on St. Mary's County revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's regulatory body for gaming and lottery operations, the agency monitors gaming revenues and legal gaming activities across Maryland, and was consulted regarding potential competition with state gaming revenues.

The bill directly impacts the programming, fundraising, and recreational activities permitted at senior activity centers, which fall under the service purview and population supported by the Department of Aging.
State Police officers have statutory authority to inspect records of organizations conducting gaming events in the county, though operations are not anticipated to be substantially impacted.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to order child abduction prevention measures if the court finds there is a credible risk of abduction of the child; authorizing certain parties to petition the court for child abduction prevention measures; requiring a petition to be verified, include a copy of any existing child custody determination, and specify the risk factors for abduction; requiring the court to consider certain evidence of a credible risk of abduction; establishing requirements for an abduction prevention order; etc.
Title: Family Law - Maryland Child Abduction Prevention Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Child Custody -see also- Parents and Guardians
Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: The Maryland Child Abduction Prevention Act authorizes a court to order child abduction prevention measures in child custody proceedings upon finding evidence of a credible risk of child abduction. The bill establishes petition requirements, statutory risk factors, conditions for abduction prevention orders, and procedures for issuing ex parte warrants for physical custody of a child to prevent imminent abduction.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts) and law enforcement officers
stakeholders: Parents, legal guardians, and children involved in child custody or visitation proceedings where there is a risk of child abduction
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. It may, however, have an operational impact on the Judiciary and circuit courts due to requirements to schedule and conduct hearings on the next business day following the execution of an ex parte warrant.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enacts the Maryland Child Abduction Prevention Act, establishing new judicial procedures, evidentiary standards, abduction prevention orders, and ex parte warrants for physical custody in child custody proceedings. As highlighted in the fiscal note, the required expedited hearings following the execution of an ex parte warrant create operational impacts for the Judiciary and circuit courts.

The bill allows courts to issue ex parte warrants directing the physical custody and safe interim placement of children at credible risk of abduction, which may intersect with local departments of social services child welfare and protection responsibilities. DHS was also consulted as an information source for the legislation.

The bill authorizes courts to direct law enforcement officers to execute warrants for immediate physical custody of children, enter private property, and make forcible entry under exigent circumstances to locate and recover children at risk of abduction.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2025 an appropriation of $12,000,000 to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund for the purpose of designating and maintaining 9-8-8 as the universal telephone number for a national suicide prevention and mental health crisis hotline and for developing and implementing a statewide initiative for the coordination and delivery of behavioral health crisis response services in the State.
Title: 9–8–8 Trust Fund – Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill requires the Governor to include a $12,000,000 appropriation in the fiscal year 2025 annual budget bill for the 9-8-8 Trust Fund to support the State's behavioral health crisis hotline and related response services.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals experiencing mental health crises or seeking suicide prevention services, behavioral health care providers, crisis call centers, mobile crisis teams, and local health jurisdictions.
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2025, State general fund expenditures and special fund revenues increase by $12.0 million due to the mandated appropriation to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund. Special fund expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2025 to fund behavioral health crisis response services, including $94,023 in FY 2025 for personnel costs to hire one permanent administrator. Local revenues and expenditures may increase for local jurisdictions operating crisis response services that receive trust fund awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the 9-8-8 Trust Fund and the statewide behavioral health crisis hotline. The bill provides a $12 million mandated appropriation to the fund in FY 2025, which MDH will manage and expend on crisis response services and administrative personnel.
DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and must incorporate the bill's statutory mandated appropriation of $12 million into the fiscal year 2025 executive budget.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of $12 million to the 9-8-8 Trust Fund in the fiscal year 2025 annual budget bill.
Under the re-enacted statutory provisions of the 9-8-8 Trust Fund, the State Treasurer is required to hold the fund separately and invest its balances.
Under the statute governing the 9-8-8 Trust Fund, the Comptroller is responsible for maintaining the accounting for the fund and its appropriations.
The statute specifies that the 9-8-8 Trust Fund remains subject to periodic audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

Synopsis: Altering the education requirements for an applicant for licensure as an environmental health specialist; altering the grounds for which the Board may take disciplinary action against an applicant or a licensee to include misfeasance and malfeasance while performing the duties of an environmental health specialist; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Environmental Health Specialists - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill alters the education and experience qualifications for licensure as an environmental health specialist, allowing applicants with a baccalaureate degree to qualify with 30 rather than 60 science credit hours and deferring specific laboratory requirements to Board regulations while repealing the 24-month training pathway. It also permits the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists to approve an outside examination provider, repeals statutory reexamination application and fee requirements, and adds misfeasance and malfeasance to the grounds for disciplinary action.
responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists
stakeholders: Licensed environmental health specialists, applicants seeking licensure as environmental health specialists, and environmental health specialists-in-training
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's changes are largely technical in nature and do not directly affect State governmental finances. Local government operations and finances are also not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is housed within the Maryland Department of Health under the Health Occupations Article. The bill directly alters the licensing qualifications, examination procedures, and disciplinary grounds administered by the Board.

Environmental health specialists enforce state and local environmental and sanitation laws, collaborating extensively with MDE programs, making the professional licensing standards directly relevant to environmental regulatory enforcement.

Synopsis: Providing certain funding for each county public library system for fiscal year 2028 and each fiscal year thereafter.
Title: Education - Libraries - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties

bill_summary: This bill codifies funding for county public library systems participating in the minimum library program at $19.10 per resident for fiscal year 2027 and each fiscal year thereafter, maintaining enhanced funding levels previously established under prior law.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: County public library systems, local governments, and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies existing funding levels established under Chapters 496 and 497 of 2022 for local public library systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is the official state entity responsible for the coordination, leadership, and state funding oversight for Maryland's 24 public library systems, which are directly governed by the minimum library program funding formulas amended by this bill.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for developing and supervising the state budget, which includes incorporating mandated State aid funding levels for county public library systems.

Synopsis: Providing that the restriction on holding or having a financial interest in other retail alcoholic beverages licenses for holders of a Class 7 micro-brewery license does not apply to a holder of a Class B-BWL (clubhouse/lodge) license in Montgomery County who is issued a Class 7 micro-brewery license.
Title: Montgomery County – Alcoholic Beverages – Holders of Class B–BWL (Clubhouse/Lodge) License and Class 7 Micro–Brewery License MC 16–23
bill_summary: Exempts holders of a Class B-BWL (clubhouse/lodge) license in Montgomery County who obtain a Class 7 micro-brewery license from the general statutory restriction limiting micro-brewery licensees to holding or having a financial interest in only one other retail alcoholic beverages license.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners and Maryland Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
stakeholders: Montgomery County Revenue Authority, golf course and clubhouse/lodge facility operators, local micro-brewery operators, and patrons in Montgomery County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect state governmental operations or finances and is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcoholic beverage industry and oversees manufacturer's licenses under Title 2 of the Alcoholic Beverages Article, which includes Class 7 micro-brewery licenses addressed by this bill.

Synopsis: Defining "clinical nurse specialist" and "practice as a clinical nurse specialist" for the purpose of authorizing clinical nurse specialists to prescribe drugs and durable medical equipment under regulations adopted by the State Board of Nursing; designating a clinical nurse specialist as an "authorized prescriber" under the Maryland Pharmacy Act; and authorizing a licensed physician to personally prepare and dispense a prescription written by a clinical nurse specialist.
Title: Health Occupations - Clinical Nurse Specialists - Prescribing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc

bill_summary: This bill defines "clinical nurse specialist" and authorizes certified clinical nurse specialists to prescribe drugs and durable medical equipment under regulations adopted by the Maryland Board of Nursing. It also adds clinical nurse specialists to the definition of authorized prescribers under the Maryland Pharmacy Act and permits licensed physicians to personally prepare and dispense prescriptions written by advanced practice registered nurses practicing in the same office setting.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Nursing
stakeholders: Clinical nurse specialists, advanced practice registered nurses, licensed physicians, pharmacists, and patients receiving direct care.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively impact state governmental operations or finances, as the Maryland Board of Nursing can implement the changes using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Nursing and the State Board of Pharmacy, which are directly responsible for regulating nursing practice, adopting rules for clinical nurse specialists' prescriptive authority, and regulating drug dispensing.

As a division of the Maryland Department of Health responsible for registering prescribers and regulating the prescribing of controlled dangerous substances, the expansion of prescriptive authority to clinical nurse specialists affects practitioner registration and compliance oversight.

Synopsis: Reestablishing the requirement that the Prescription Drug Affordability Board, under certain circumstances, draft a plan of action for implementing a process to set upper payment limits for certain prescription drug products; reestablishing the authority of the Board to set upper payments limits, under certain circumstances, for prescription drug products that are purchased or paid for by or through certain State or local government entities, plans, or programs; etc.
Title: Prescription Drug Affordability Board - Upper Payment Limits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Reestablishes the authority and requirements for the Prescription Drug Affordability Board (PDAB) to draft an action plan to set upper payment limits on certain high-cost prescription drugs purchased or paid for by State and local government entities, employee health plans, and Medicaid. It also reestablishes an appeals process and requires PDAB to submit a report by December 1, 2026, evaluating whether to expand upper payment limits to all prescription drug purchases and reimbursements in Maryland.
responsible_party: Prescription Drug Affordability Board
stakeholders: State and local government employees, Medicaid recipients, individuals receiving care at state hospitals or clinics, state and local government agencies, health care payers, and prescription drug manufacturers and purchasers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government expenditures decrease to the extent that upper payment limits are approved, implemented, and result in reduced prescription drug prices for government health plans, facilities, and Medicaid. Revenues are not affected. Specific dollar savings are indeterminate and cannot be reliably estimated at this time.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Prescription Drug Affordability Board (PDAB) and its Stakeholder Council, which fall under independent state boards and advisory bodies, are the primary entities responsible for drafting the plan of action, establishing upper payment limits, monitoring drug availability and shortages, hearing appeals, and submitting required reports to the General Assembly.

The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and operates State hospitals, both of which are explicitly designated entities whose prescription drug purchases and payments will be subject to upper payment limits set by the Board, directly impacting health care expenditures.

The bill provides that if the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve the Board's plan of action within 45 days, the plan must be submitted to the Governor and the Attorney General for approval before any upper payment limits can take effect.

The Attorney General shares approval authority with the Governor over the Board's plan of action if the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve it, and serves as legal counsel on statutory implementation and potential litigation.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and oversees the state budget. The upper payment limits apply to prescription drugs paid through health benefit plans on behalf of state government entities, impacting state health care spending.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: State correctional facilities are explicitly identified in the statute as entities whose prescription drug purchases will be subject to upper payment limits established by the Board, impacting pharmaceutical procurement for incarcerated individuals.

Health clinics at State institutions of higher education are explicitly listed as entities subject to the upper payment limits, and USM was consulted as an information source regarding fiscal and operational impacts.

MIA regulates health benefit plans operating in the state and was consulted as an information source regarding the application of payment limits and the future study evaluating limits across all commercial payor reimbursements.

The bill provides that any person aggrieved by a final decision of the Board regarding an upper payment limit may petition for judicial review under the Administrative Procedure Act in the Maryland court system.
OAH was identified as an information source for the bill regarding potential administrative appeals and hearings arising from the Board's decisions and upper payment limit determinations.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning on January 1, 2024, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to provide gender-affirming treatment in a nondiscriminatory manner; requiring that the gender-affirming treatment be assessed according to nondiscriminatory criteria that are consistent with current clinical standards; prohibiting the issuance of an adverse benefit determination related to gender-affirming treatment unless a certain experienced health care provider has reviewed and confirmed the appropriateness of the determination; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Gender-Affirming Treatment (Trans Health Equity Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: The Trans Health Equity Act requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), beginning January 1, 2024, to provide coverage for medically necessary gender-affirming treatment in a nondiscriminatory manner consistent with clinical standards of care. It prohibits Medicaid from categorizing such treatments as cosmetic services or categorically excluding specific procedures, requires adverse benefit determinations to be reviewed by experienced providers, and mandates annual reporting and directory updates on participating providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medicaid recipients seeking gender-affirming care (including transgender, nonbinary, intersex, two-spirit, and other gender-diverse individuals), Medicaid managed care organizations, and healthcare providers offering gender-affirming treatment.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate but likely significant amount beginning in FY 2024 to cover expanded services.
