Federal matching funds increase accordingly (90% for fertility preservation, and 64.5% declining to 63.9% for other services). For illustrative purposes, the Fiscal Note estimates that annual expenditure increases could range from $2.1 million to $7.6 million based on varying utilization by an assumed 125 individuals. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill directly mandates that the Program cover medically necessary gender-affirming care, sets clinical review requirements for adverse benefit determinations, and requires MDH to compile and publish annual reports on provider geographic access.

The bill expands an entitlement benefit under Medicaid, resulting in an indeterminate but likely significant increase in state General Fund expenditures beginning in FY 2024, impacting state budget development and fiscal planning overseen by DBM.

Synopsis: Requiring the owners and operators of grocery stores with annual gross incomes greater than $10,000,000 or restaurants with annual gross incomes of more than $1,000,000, beginning on January 1, 2024, to place an automated external defibrillator in a prominent, accessible area and maintain the functionality of the defibrillator; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems jointly to adopt certain regulations.
Title: Grocery Stores and Restaurants - Automated External Defibrillator Program (Joe Sheya Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: The Joe Sheya Act requires owners and operators of certain larger grocery stores and restaurants, beginning January 1, 2025, to install and maintain a functional automated external defibrillator (AED) in an area accessible to employees and customers. It excludes these businesses from the Public Access AED Program, requires them to register with MIEMSS, provides civil liability immunities for businesses and individuals rendering or failing to render aid, and directs MDH and MIEMSS to jointly adopt regulations and report on the program.
responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS) and Maryland Department of Health (MDH)
stakeholders: Owners, operators, employees, and customers of qualifying Maryland grocery stores and restaurants, as well as individuals experiencing sudden cardiac arrest
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund) expenditures increase by at least $41,400 in FY 2024 for MIEMSS to hire a part-time administrator, adopt regulations, and manage the registration and reporting requirements, increasing to $53,100 by FY 2028. State revenues are unaffected. Local government finances are not materially affected, though local health departments may incur minimal costs if tasked with AED inspections. Qualifying small business grocery stores and restaurants will incur costs to purchase AED units ($500 to $1,700 each) and maintain them.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is a primary implementing agency tasked with establishing and overseeing the registration system for grocery stores and restaurants placing AEDs, jointly adopting regulations with the Maryland Department of Health, providing maintenance and recall notices, and completing two evaluation reports for legislative committees.

The Maryland Department of Health is mandated to jointly adopt regulations with MIEMSS establishing guidelines for periodic AED inspections and annual maintenance, and assisting grocery store and restaurant owners in complying with the law.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Forestry Education Fund to expand and enhance the Maryland Forestry Foundation's capacity to provide certain education and resources to forest landowners, the ability of district forestry boards and the knowledge of local governments to achieve healthy and sustainable forests, and the ability of businesses to test innovative best management practices in forestry; and requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill $250,000 for the Fund in fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
Title: Maryland Forestry Education Fund - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Forestry Education Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Maryland Forestry Foundation. The fund supports educational programming, training, outreach, and small grants for forest landowners, district forestry boards, local governments, and businesses to advance sustainable forest management and test innovative forestry practices.
responsible_party: Maryland Forestry Foundation
stakeholders: Maryland forest landowners, district forestry boards, local governments, and forestry-related businesses
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually in FY 2025 and FY 2026 due to a mandated appropriation to the fund, with indeterminate amounts in subsequent years if discretionary funding is provided. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $250,000 in FY 2025 and FY 2026. Local government grant revenues and expenditures may increase in FY 2025 and FY 2026 to the extent localities receive grant awards and benefit from forestry training.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Forestry Education Fund within the Natural Resources Article to support forestry education, healthy forest management, and district forestry boards, which are established and overseen by the Department of Natural Resources.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Forestry Education Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The statute specifically designates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Maryland Forestry Education Fund.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of $250,000 to the fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
As the agency responsible for developing and executing the State budget, DBM must incorporate and supervise the mandated $250,000 general fund appropriation in fiscal years 2025 and 2026.

Synopsis: Altering the Maryland Dent-Care Program; establishing a requirement regarding the reimbursement of dental-related services under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; establishing requirements on the Maryland Department of Health regarding the creation and distribution of plain language materials related to dental services; requiring the State Board of Dental Examiners to publish a searchable list of licensed providers who provide mobile dental services or portable dental services in the State; etc.
Title: Public Health - Dental Services - Access

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Dent-Care Program to include dental hygienists and alters grant amounts to at least $50,000 annually for dentists and up to $10,000 annually for dental hygienists. It requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to annually evaluate Medicaid dental reimbursement rates, create and distribute plain language educational materials on dental care, convene a workgroup to study grant or loan programs for practices in underserved areas, study provider participation in the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program, and study Medicaid reimbursement for community health workers. Additionally, it requires the State Board of Dental Examiners to maintain a searchable public list of mobile and portable dental service providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Licensed dentists, dental hygienists, Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) recipients, and dental patients seeking mobile or portable dental care.
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2024, State general fund expenditures increase by $86,400 ($75,000 for contractual plain language materials support and $11,439 for MHEC/MDCAPS system modifications), and Medicaid expenditures increase by $100,000 ($50,000 general funds, $50,000 federal funds) for a provider study, offset by $50,000 in federal fund revenues. In FY 2025, Medicaid expenditures increase by $20,000 ($10,000 general funds, $10,000 federal funds), offset by $10,000 in federal fund revenues. Additional indeterminate general fund expenditures may occur to fund increased Dent-Care grant amounts and future reimbursement rate increases. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for the bill's provisions, including annually evaluating Medicaid dental reimbursement rates, creating and distributing plain language dental health materials, conducting studies on Medicaid provider participation and community health worker reimbursement, and housing the State Board of Dental Examiners and Office of Oral Health.

MHEC's Office of Student Financial Assistance administers the Maryland Dent-Care Program, which is altered by the bill to include dental hygienists and modified award amounts, requiring administrative updates to the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the convening of a stakeholder workgroup to study the establishment of a grant or no-interest loan program for dental providers to open practices in underserved areas and report findings to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Altering the educational requirements that individuals must meet to be licensed as clinical or graduate alcohol and drug counselors.
Title: Health Occupations - Clinical and Graduate Alcohol and Drug Counselors - Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill alters the educational qualifications for licensure as a clinical alcohol and drug counselor (LCADC) or licensed graduate alcohol and drug counselor (LGADC). It requires applicants to hold a master's or doctoral degree in a professional counseling field (rather than health and human services) from an accredited educational institution approved by the Board, eliminates an alternative educational equivalency pathway for LCADCs, and removes specific statutory course credit requirements for LGADCs.
responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors (Maryland Department of Health)
stakeholders: Applicants seeking licensure as clinical alcohol and drug counselors or licensed graduate alcohol and drug counselors.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The changes are procedural in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, which oversees the licensure, education standards, and regulation of clinical and graduate alcohol and drug counselors amended by this bill.

Synopsis: Exempting certain family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers that serve only dependent children of military personnel and are located on a military base or federal property or are certified as a family child care provider by a branch of the U.S. Department of Defense or the Coast Guard from certain registration and licensing requirements; authorizing certain entities to assume responsibility for approving or determining which children may be served by exempted child care providers; etc.
Title: Child Care Providers - Registration and Licensing - Exemptions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Exempts certain family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers from State licensing and registration requirements if they exclusively serve dependent children of military personnel and are either situated on military or federal property or certified by a branch of the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. Coast Guard.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Military personnel and their dependent children, as well as child care providers operating on military bases or federal properties or certified by the U.S. Department of Defense or Coast Guard
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations, and has no local fiscal impact. Qualifying small business child care providers may benefit from the elimination of duplicative State licensing and registration requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary state agency responsible for the registration, licensing, and oversight of family child care homes and child care centers. This bill directly amends provisions under the Education Article governing MSDE's child care licensing authority by creating exemptions for child care programs serving military dependents on federal property or certified by the U.S. Department of Defense or U.S. Coast Guard.

The Adjutant General oversees the Maryland Military Department, which was consulted as an information source on this legislation regarding military installations, personnel, and base-related child care operations.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families is responsible for supporting active-duty service members and their families in Maryland. While not an implementing agency, the bill directly concerns child care access and regulatory exemptions specifically tailored to military families.

Synopsis: Altering procedures that a law enforcement officer and a court are required to follow when the law enforcement officer or court has reason to believe that a child who has been detained is a victim of sex trafficking or a victim of human trafficking; providing that a minor may not be criminally prosecuted or proceeded against under certain provisions of law for a certain offense if the minor committed the offense as a direct result of being a victim of sex trafficking or being a victim of human trafficking; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Victims of Child Sex Trafficking and Human Trafficking - Safe Harbor and Service Response

NarrowSubjects.Name: Child Custody -see also- Parents and Guardians
Controlled Dangerous Substances -see also- Drugs; Subst Abus
Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Motor Vehicle Insurance -see also- MD Auto Insurance Fund
Nudity and Sexual Displays -see also- Obscenity; Pornography

bill_summary: This bill establishes safe harbor protections and service response requirements for child victims of sex trafficking and human trafficking. It alters procedures for law enforcement officers detaining a suspected child victim, requiring referral to regional navigators and local child welfare agencies, and prohibits detaining such children in juvenile detention facilities for qualifying offenses. Additionally, it prohibits criminal prosecution or juvenile delinquency proceedings against minors for qualifying offenses, violations, or sex trafficking offenses committed as a direct result of being trafficked, requiring courts to stay proceedings and dismiss charges under those circumstances. It also expands the list of offenses eligible for a motion to vacate judgment for human trafficking victims to include unauthorized use of a motor vehicle and soliciting prostitution.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Human Services (DHS), and State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Minors and individuals who are victims of sex trafficking or human trafficking, law enforcement officers, juvenile courts, State's Attorneys, defense attorneys, and local child welfare agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's procedural changes and service referral requirements can be handled within existing budgeted resources and are not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Law enforcement must immediately report suspected child victims of human and sex trafficking to local child welfare agencies within DHS, custody can be transferred to them for child protection, and juvenile courts are required to notify DHS upon staying proceedings for qualifying offenses.

The bill directly bars law enforcement from detaining a suspected child victim of sex or human trafficking in a DJS juvenile detention facility for qualifying offenses, and alters juvenile intake and delinquency proceedings.

The bill mandates court procedures in juvenile courts, requiring judges to stay proceedings, conduct evidentiary hearings within set timeframes, make findings on trafficking victim status, dismiss qualifying charges, and handle expanded motions to vacate judgments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys represent juveniles facing delinquency proceedings who are eligible for mandatory stays and dismissals under safe harbor provisions, as well as individuals seeking post-conviction relief through motions to vacate judgments for expanded qualifying offenses.

State Troopers and law enforcement officers must follow revised custody and detention procedures for suspected child victims, including required notifications to regional navigators and local child welfare agencies, and prohibitions on detention facility placement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP oversees victim services grant programs and coordinates statewide public safety policy, including grant funding and coordination aligned with Safe Harbor regional navigators and human trafficking response.

Synopsis: Establishing the Rare Disease Advisory Council to study and make recommendations on matters relating to individuals with rare diseases in the State; requiring the Council to convene public hearings, make inquiries, and solicit comments from the public on the needs of rare disease patients, caregivers, and health care providers; requiring the Council to report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1 each year beginning in 2024 and to provide recommendations on ways to address the needs of persons with rare diseases in the State; etc.
Title: Public Health - Rare Disease Advisory Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Rare Disease Advisory Council to study, research, and make policy recommendations regarding the needs of individuals living with rare diseases, their caregivers, and health care providers in Maryland, while requiring an annual report and public webpage.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals diagnosed with rare diseases in Maryland, their families and caregivers, health care providers, health insurance carriers, biopharmaceutical representatives, and academic researchers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations can be managed within existing budgeted resources by the Maryland Department of Health and participating agencies. To the extent the council receives federal grant funding, federal fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for staffing the Rare Disease Advisory Council. Additionally, the Secretary of Health (or designee), a representative of the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, and a representative of the Office of Minority Health and Health Disparities serve on the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new permanent advisory body within the executive branch, the Rare Disease Advisory Council, to study issues, consult experts, conduct surveys, and make annual policy recommendations.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner must designate a representative from the Maryland Insurance Administration to serve as a member of the Council, and the Council evaluates insurance and utilization management practices.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 14 members of the Council, designating the initial chair, and receiving the Council's annual report.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and appointment process for the 14 gubernatorial appointees to the newly created Council.

Synopsis: Authorizing an applicant for State employment or a State employee to file a complaint alleging harassment by an employer within 2 years after the alleged violation that is the basis of the complaint; and increasing, from 30 days to 1 year, the period of time for an applicant or employee to file a complaint alleging certain prohibited personnel actions.
Title: State Employee Rights and Protections - Personnel Actions and Harassment - Complaints

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Expands the deadline from 30 days to one year for Executive Branch State employees and applicants to file a complaint alleging prohibited personnel actions based on political affiliation or other nonmerit factors, and authorizes employees and applicants to file a complaint alleging employer harassment within two years of the alleged violation.
responsible_party: Heads of principal units across Executive Branch State agencies and the Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Executive Branch State employees and job applicants for Executive Branch positions
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures across all funds may increase beginning in FY 2024 if the extended filing deadlines result in more complaints requiring additional staff or contractual assistance to investigate and manage; however, the exact cost cannot be reliably estimated without actual experience under the bill. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland overseeing executive branch employee policies and resources, DBM is directly responsible for personnel administration and highlighted in the fiscal note regarding the administrative burden and operational costs of investigating equal employment opportunity complaints under extended timeframes.

MCCR investigates and enforces unlawful employment practices and harassment complaints under Section 20-606 of the State Government Article, and the fiscal note notes potential regulatory overlap and interactions between MCCR's existing harassment complaint processes and the newly authorized internal executive branch complaint process.
OAH serves as the central administrative adjudicative body that hears contested state personnel cases and grievance appeals arising from executive agency employment actions.

Synopsis: Establishing a certain income tax checkoff for voluntary contributions to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund; requiring the Comptroller to include certain information in each individual income tax return package; etc.
Title: Income Tax Checkoff - Maryland Veterans Trust Fund

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill establishes a voluntary income tax checkoff on Maryland individual income tax return forms for contributions to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund. The Comptroller is required to include the checkoff option and explanatory information on return forms, deduct necessary administrative costs, and remit the remaining collected funds to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
stakeholders: Maryland individual income taxpayers, Maryland military veterans and their families, and organizations providing support services to veterans
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by $150,600 in FY 2026 ($79,000 for one-time Comptroller tax system modifications and $71,598 for one MDVA grants specialist), followed by ongoing MDVA personnel costs of $90,500 in FY 2027 and $95,300 in FY 2028. Nonbudgeted revenues to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund increase by an indeterminate amount starting in FY 2026, which may cause an indeterminate decrease in revenues to other income tax checkoff funds due to donation shifting. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is directly responsible for implementing the bill, which requires adding the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund checkoff to individual income tax return forms and packages, collecting contributions, deducting administrative expenses, and distributing the net proceeds.

The agency (formerly the Department of Veterans Affairs) houses and staffs the Maryland Veterans Trust, which receives the checkoff contributions into the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund and will require additional staff to handle increased grant and fund administration.
The bill specifies that the Comptroller must account to the State Treasurer for all checkoff contribution monies collected.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Agriculture, in consultation with certain State and federal agencies, to study the use of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in pesticides in the State; and requiring the Department to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor, the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment, and the House Health and Government Operations Committee on or before November 1, 2023.
Title: Pesticides - PFAS Testing - Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Agriculture, in consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment, the Maryland Department of Health, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, to study the use of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in pesticides in Maryland and report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by November 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Pesticide manufacturers, distributors, agricultural producers, public health and environmental advocates, and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Agriculture and consulting agencies are expected to handle the study and reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Agriculture is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting the study on the use of PFAS in pesticides in Maryland and reporting the findings and recommendations.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of Agriculture to consult with the Department of the Environment in conducting the study on PFAS in pesticides.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of Agriculture to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to evaluate health impacts during the study.
The Governor is a designated recipient of the final study findings and recommendations submitted by the Department of Agriculture.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "student data" for purposes of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System to include student disability data by specific disability category.
Title: Maryland Longitudinal Data System - Definition of Student Data - Alteration
bill_summary: Expands the definition of "student data" collected, analyzed, and reported by the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center to include student disability data categorized by specific disability.
responsible_party: Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center
stakeholders: Maryland students with disabilities, public school students, educational researchers, and education policymakers
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center and the Maryland State Department of Education can incorporate and transmit existing disability data using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 320 directly alters the definition of 'student data' collected, analyzed, and reported by the Maryland Longitudinal Data System (MLDS) Center to include student disability data by specific disability category.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) collects student disability data by specific category and will work directly with the MLDS Center to transfer and incorporate this data into the MLDS repository.

Synopsis: Requiring the Cigarette Restitution Fund to include a separate account consisting of payments received by the State from certain enforcement actions related to the sale and marketing of electronic smoking devices; and providing that distributions from the separate account may be used, consistent with any other State law, to supplement General Fund appropriations designated for certain programs with the purpose of reducing the use of tobacco products by individuals under 21 years of age.
Title: Cigarette Restitution Fund - Payments for Sale and Marketing of Electronic Smoking Devices - Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Smoking and Vaping -see also- Cannabis; Cigarettes

bill_summary: This bill establishes a separate account within the Cigarette Restitution Fund to hold revenues received by the State from judgments, settlements, penalties, or enforcement actions related to the sale and marketing of electronic smoking devices. Funds distributed from this account may only be used to supplement General Fund appropriations for programs that aim to reduce the use of tobacco products by individuals under the age of 21.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals under age 21, youth tobacco prevention and cessation programs, electronic smoking device manufacturers/retailers, and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not significantly affect overall State revenues or expenditures, but it redirects how certain enforcement revenues are spent. Specifically, Maryland is expected to receive at least $13.0 million over 5 to 9 years from the multi-state JUUL Labs settlement; instead of being distributed under the standard Cigarette Restitution Fund statutory formula (e.g., 30% to Medicaid), these funds will be deposited into a separate account to supplement General Fund spending for youth tobacco reduction programs beginning in FY 2025. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH administers the State's tobacco use prevention and cessation programs and is statutorily responsible for strategies preventing individuals under 21 from accessing and using tobacco products; it anticipates receiving funding from this new separate account to support these programs.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, including managing the allocation of special funds within the Cigarette Restitution Fund and establishing the budgetary framework for the new separate account.

OAG litigates and negotiates settlements, judgments, and enforcement actions regarding the sale and marketing of electronic smoking devices (such as the multistate JUUL settlement), which directly generate the revenues credited to this separate account.

The statute governs the Governor's annual budget requests and specifically requires the Governor to develop key performance indicators, goals, and annual outcome reports to the General Assembly for programs funded under the section.

The Comptroller serves as the State's chief financial officer and is responsible for maintaining the State's accounting records, processing revenues, and administering the separate account within the fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to and provide reimbursement for intensive in-home services, case management, and wraparound services; requiring, beginning in fiscal year 2024, the Behavioral Health Administration to fund 100 slots in the mental health case management program for children or youth at risk of out-of-home placement who are not eligible for program services; requiring the Governor to include funding in the annual budget bill for customized goods and services for certain youth; etc.
Title: Public Health - Home- and Community-Based Services for Children and Youth

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Home Care Services -see also- Respite Care
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to expand access to and provide reimbursement for wraparound, intensive in-home, and case management services for children and youth with intensive behavioral and mental health needs, including funding 100 slots in the mental health case management program for youth ineligible for Medicaid who are at risk of out-of-home placement, establishing mandated annual appropriations for customized goods and services, and conducting program reviews and reporting.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Children and youth with complex emotional, behavioral, or mental health needs, their families, and behavioral health care providers and care coordinators
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $3,496,500 in FY 2024, $779,700 in FY 2025, $891,200 in FY 2026, $1,003,200 in FY 2027, and $1,018,200 in FY 2028. This includes mandated appropriations for customized goods and services of $150,000 in FY 2025, $250,000 in FY 2026, and $350,000 annually thereafter. Additional indeterminate general and federal fund expenditures and matching federal revenues will occur for service reimbursements. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health and its Behavioral Health Administration are the primary implementing entities, responsible for expanding wraparound and intensive in-home services under the 1915(i) model, funding additional case management slots, establishing reimbursement rates, conducting pilot programs, and completing annual studies and reports.

The bill statutorily mandates that the Governor include specific appropriations in the annual operating budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2025 ($150,000 in FY 2025, $250,000 in FY 2026, and $350,000 in FY 2027 and subsequent years) to fund customized goods and services for qualifying youth.

As the principal agency responsible for preparing and supervising the execution of the state budget, DBM must accommodate the bill's mandated appropriations starting in fiscal year 2025 and oversee the related general fund expenditures.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of Home Energy Programs to enroll households, based on certain eligibility, in any fuel and utility assistance program; and altering the eligibility requirements for the electric universal service program to provide assistance to customers with annual incomes at or below 200% of the federal poverty level.
Title: Social Services Programs - Eligibility and Enrollment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Requires the Office of Home Energy Programs within the Department of Human Services to enroll households receiving SNAP, TANF, SSI, or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits into fuel and utility assistance programs, and expands the Electric Universal Service Program income eligibility ceiling from 175% to 200% of the federal poverty guidelines.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services (Office of Home Energy Programs)
stakeholders: Low-income households, recipients of SNAP, TANF, SSI, and means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits, and electric utility customers with household incomes up to 200% of federal poverty guidelines.
fiscal_impact_summary: Department of Human Services special fund expenditures increase by at least $15,024,000 in FY 2024 and by $30,048,000 annually thereafter due to auto-enrollment and broadened eligibility for the Electric Universal Service Program. Special fund revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 323 directly impacts the Department of Human Services (DHS), which houses the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP). The bill requires OHEP to enroll eligible households receiving SNAP, TANF, SSI, or means-tested Veterans Affairs benefits into fuel and utility assistance programs, resulting in an estimated special fund expenditure increase of at least $15 million in FY 2024 and $30 million annually thereafter.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article governing the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP), which the Public Service Commission is statutorily mandated to establish and oversee, expanding annual income eligibility across all customers to 200% of the federal poverty level.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners to issue a license to an animal control facility to administer rabies vaccines; requiring the Board to establish an expedited process to authorize a veterinary practitioner who holds a current, valid license to practice veterinary medicine in another state or jurisdiction to become licensed to practice veterinary medicine in the State; requiring the Secretary of Health to allow certain veterinary technicians or other clinical staff to administer rabies vaccines; etc.
Title: Provision of Veterinary Services - Practice of Veterinary Medicine and Rabies Vaccines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners to establish an expedited licensing process for out-of-state veterinarians seeking to practice in Maryland. It also expands animal control facility licensing and authorizes registered veterinary technicians and qualified clinical staff at animal shelters or animal control facilities to administer rabies vaccines under specified conditions.
responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners and the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Out-of-state veterinarians, veterinary technicians and clinical staff, animal shelters, animal control facilities, and shelter animals
fiscal_impact_summary: State general/special fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 only for IT portal programming to implement the expedited licensing process. Special fund revenues to the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners Fund may experience an indeterminate increase beginning in FY 2024 from license application and annual renewal fees. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is housed within the Department of Agriculture. The bill requires the Board to establish an expedited licensing process for out-of-state veterinary practitioners, expand licensing authority for animal control facilities to administer rabies vaccines, and submit a required report to the General Assembly.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to require the Secretary of Health to establish protocols permitting registered veterinary technicians and animal shelter clinical staff to administer rabies vaccines under specified conditions, and requires the Department of Agriculture/Board to consult with MDH on implementing regulations.

Synopsis: Establishing invoicing and prompt payment requirements for certain State grants; requiring the State to make payment under certain grant agreements within 37 days of the payment becoming due under the agreement or after receiving a proper invoice; and authorizing interest accrual at the rate of 9% per year on any amount that is due and payable but remains unpaid after a certain time.
Title: State Finance and Procurement - Grants - Prompt Payment Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes prompt payment policies and invoice processing procedures for State grant agreements with 501(c) nonprofit organizations. It sets a policy for the State to pay proper grant invoices within 37 days, after which the grant-making agency is liable to pay interest on late payments at an annual rate of 9% from its operating budget.
responsible_party: State grant-making agencies and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: 501(c) nonprofit organizations receiving Maryland state grants and State grant-making agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures may increase by up to $8,100 in FY 2023 and up to $97,100 annually thereafter to pay 9% interest penalties on late grant payments to nonprofit organizations. Staffing increases at agencies are not anticipated unless penalty costs exceed hiring costs. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Comptroller with processing grant payments within five business days once a proper invoice is submitted by a State grant-making entity, and defines the Comptroller's liability regarding late payment interest.

As a major State grant-making agency, MDH is specifically highlighted in the fiscal note as facing notable operational impacts, noting a potential need for up to six additional full-time staff costing over $650,000 annually to comply with prompt invoice processing and payment deadlines.

As a principal grant-awarding entity, DNR is specifically cited in the fiscal note regarding substantial potential operational impacts, estimating a need for up to nine additional staff costing over $700,000 to meet the required invoice review and processing timelines.

MDOT awards grants and is specifically noted in the fiscal note regarding operational conflicts between the bill's prompt payment requirements and existing departmental grant conditions requiring annual reports before payment disbursement.

The bill explicitly exempts grants funded from general obligation bond proceeds or from general fund capital appropriations to the Board of Public Works from the prompt payment statutory requirements.

OLA's comprehensive audit findings on State operating and capital grant awards were directly utilized by the Department of Legislative Services to determine the volume, baseline data, and fiscal estimates of the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements related to the reimbursement of out-of-pocket costs paid by certain hospital patients who were eligible for free care, including requirements related to the consideration of data and the reporting and disclosure of certain information; authorizing the Commission to impose a fine of up to $50,000 per violation if a hospital fails to provide refunds to qualifying patients; making a violation of the Act an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to penalties under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act; etc.
Title: Hospitals - Financial Assistance - Medical Bill Reimbursement Process

NarrowSubjects.Name: Consumer Protection -see also- Unfair Trade Practices

bill_summary: This bill establishes a process and requirements for hospitals to identify and reimburse patients who paid more than $25 out-of-pocket for hospital services between calendar years 2017 and 2021 despite being eligible for free care. It requires state agencies to share tax and public benefit data with hospitals to verify eligibility, mandates that hospitals implement Option 3 from the Health Services Cost Review Commission's December 2022 report, requires hospitals to reimburse state agencies for costs incurred to administer the program, and classifies noncompliance by a hospital as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to fines and enforcement under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Hospitals in Maryland, hospital patients eligible for free care between 2017 and 2021 who paid out-of-pocket medical bills, the Health Education and Advocacy Unit, and local education agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to implement the data-matching and refund process, including approximately $28,000 annually for the Comptroller's Office for contractual staffing, alongside indeterminate costs for the Department of Human Services, the Maryland State Department of Education, and the Office of the Attorney General. However, state revenues increase by an equal amount because hospitals are required to reimburse state entities for all implementation costs, resulting in no net effect on state finances. Local school systems may experience operational or fiscal impacts to supply free and reduced-cost meal data.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the primary agency tasked with developing, overseeing, and modifying the hospital financial assistance refund process, determining hospital reimbursement obligations to state entities, reporting to the General Assembly, and assessing fines up to $50,000 for hospital noncompliance.

The bill mandates that the Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU) within OAG assist patients in securing medical bill reimbursements and authorizes it to request necessary patient data; additionally, hospital violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforceable under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act by OAG.

The Comptroller is required to match hospital patient data against state tax records to verify income eligibility, share relevant tax information, and receive cost reimbursements from hospitals for implementing the process.

DHS is required to coordinate with HSCRC and perform data matching using SNAP and state energy assistance program records to establish presumptive eligibility for free hospital care reimbursements, with associated costs reimbursed by hospitals.

MDH is required to coordinate with HSCRC and verify presumptive eligibility for free care by matching patient data against federal Special Supplemental Food Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) records, with costs incurred reimbursed by hospitals.

MSDE must coordinate with HSCRC to verify presumptive eligibility using free and reduced-price school meal program data, share required information, and receive reimbursement from hospitals for expenses incurred.

Synopsis: Extending the time for the submission of the final report of the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission to December 1, 2025; and extending the termination date for the Commission to June 30, 2026.
Title: Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission - Reporting and Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission from June 30, 2024, to June 30, 2026, and extends the deadline for submitting its final report of findings and recommendations from December 1, 2023, to December 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission, communities and descendants of victims affected by racially motivated lynchings in Maryland, Bowie State University, and the Office of the Attorney General.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State revenues, and the commission is able to continue operations using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the operational sunset and reporting deadline of the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which is a state study commission established by the General Assembly.

The Office of the Attorney General provides a dedicated staff member to assist the commission with investigations and hearings, who is specifically authorized to issue subpoenas on behalf of the commission.
Bowie State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, provides primary staffing and operational support for the Maryland Lynching Truth and Reconciliation Commission.
The bill mandates that the commission submit its final report containing findings and recommendations to the Governor.

The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights provided information and monitoring regarding the extension of the commission, which deals directly with civil rights and restorative justice for historical racial violence.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County to include a designee of the Director of the Services and a designee of the Director of the Montgomery County Department of Police.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Advisory Board of the Alcohol Beverage Services of Montgomery County to allow designees to serve on behalf of the Director of the Services and the Director of the Montgomery County Department of Police.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services and the Montgomery County Department of Police
stakeholders: The Director of Montgomery County Alcohol Beverage Services, the Director of the Montgomery County Department of Police, their designees, and members of the Advisory Board.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state effect and is not anticipated to materially affect Montgomery County operations or finances.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination date of certain provisions of law requiring the Comptroller to distribute a certain amount of certain abandoned property funds to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund which provides grants to the University of Maryland School of Law, the University of Baltimore School of Law, and the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service to operate tax clinics for low-income Maryland residents.
Title: Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders - Funding - Repeal of Sunset

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Permanently extends funding for the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund by repealing the sunset on the annual $250,000 distribution from the State's Unclaimed Property Fund, providing ongoing grants to tax clinics operated by the University of Maryland School of Law, the University of Baltimore School of Law, and the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents facing tax disputes, the University of Maryland School of Law, the University of Baltimore School of Law, and the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2024, general fund revenues decrease by $250,000 annually due to the permanent diversion of unclaimed property proceeds to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund (TCLIM). In FY 2024, TCLIM revenues and expenditures increase by $250,000, and higher education revenues and expenditures increase by $166,700. In FY 2025 and subsequent years, general fund expenditures are assumed to decrease by $250,000 annually as mandated special funds replace discretionary appropriations. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, accounts for the fund, and is responsible for administering the Unclaimed Property Fund and distributing the $250,000 annually to the fund.

Two of the three entities receiving statutory grant distributions from the Fund are University System of Maryland constituent law schools: the University of Maryland School of Law and the University of Baltimore School of Law.
The State Treasurer's Office is statutorily required to hold the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund separately and invest the money in the Fund.

The bill impacts State general fund revenues and expenditures by permanently diverting $250,000 in abandoned property proceeds from the general fund to a special fund, which affects state budget planning managed by DBM.
The bill explicitly references the Governor's authority to include an appropriation to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund in the annual state budget.

Synopsis: Requiring the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission to hold a public hearing on the selection of a nominee for a single vacancy on the Baltimore County Board of Education in a certain manner under certain circumstances; requiring the Commission to make publicly available on its website live video streaming of certain public hearings and certain archived video recordings; and authorizing the Commission to retain and reactivate the applications of certain candidates for certain vacancies on the county board.
Title: Baltimore County - School Board Nominating Commission - Vacancy Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Alters the hearing requirements for the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission by requiring at least one public meeting instead of three when filling a single vacancy on the Baltimore County Board of Education. It also requires the Commission to provide live video streaming and unedited archived recordings of public meetings on its website, and permits the Commission to retain and reactivate candidate applications for up to two years with the applicant's consent.
responsible_party: Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission
stakeholders: Candidates applying for vacancies on the Baltimore County Board of Education, Baltimore County Public Schools, and residents of Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Baltimore County can implement the requirements using existing resources, resulting in no local expenditure or revenue impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission's purpose is to select and recommend nominees to the Governor for appointment to the Baltimore County Board of Education, and the Governor appoints board members from the submitted list and appoints eight members to the commission itself.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in reviewing, vetting, and administering gubernatorial appointments, which includes processing the Governor's appointments of members to the nominating commission and candidates to the Baltimore County Board of Education.

As the state agency providing oversight and policy leadership for Maryland's 24 local school systems, MSDE has an institutional interest in the governance and appointment processes of local boards of education, though it has no direct administrative duties under this bill.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination date on the eligibility of the Maryland School for the Blind for funding under the Public School Construction Program.
Title: Maryland School for the Blind - Public School Construction Program - Eligibility

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Permanently extends the Maryland School for the Blind's eligibility to receive funding under the Public School Construction Program by repealing the statutory termination date of fiscal year 2028.
responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction
stakeholders: Maryland School for the Blind, its students and staff, and local public school systems across Maryland that compete for school construction funding
fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: No net effect on total State expenditures or revenues for the Public School Construction Program (PSCP) beginning in FY 2029, as annual school construction funding is determined through the capital budget process. Local Effect: To the extent PSCP funds continue to be awarded to the Maryland School for the Blind in FY 2029 and beyond, fewer State matching funds will be available for local school systems' construction projects, though local funds reserved for matching may be redirected to other local capital projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) with adopting regulations and administering the ongoing eligibility of the Maryland School for the Blind for school construction and capital improvement funding under the Public School Construction Program.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees statewide education policies, funding, and special education programs. While the capital program is administered by the IAC, the bill permanently extends capital funding eligibility for the Maryland School for the Blind under the Education Article.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor annually to proclaim March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day in recognition of the service of the women of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion during World War II.
Title: 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to annually proclaim March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day in recognition of the service of the women of the battalion during World War II.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Marylanders, military veterans, and historical advocates honoring the service of the women of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor annually issue a proclamation declaring March 9 as 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion Day.

The bill commemorates the military service of the women of the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion during World War II, which aligns with the department's mission to recognize and honor Maryland veterans, though no direct operational duties are assigned to the agency.

Synopsis: Altering the threshold amount for certain indemnity mortgage transactions that are exempt from the recordation tax from less than $3,000,000 to less than $12,500,000; and applying the Act to instruments of writing recorded on or after July 1, 2024.
Title: Recordation Tax - Indemnity Mortgage Exemption - Threshold Amount

Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill increases the threshold amount of indemnity mortgages exempt from the recordation tax from $3 million to $15 million (noted as $12.5 million in the fiscal note) and requires designated local tax collectors or clerks of the circuit court to submit an annual report detailing exempt indemnity mortgages and forgone recordation tax revenues.
responsible_party: County tax collectors and Clerks of the Circuit Court
stakeholders: Commercial and residential real estate borrowers, loan guarantors, lenders, small businesses securing loans with indemnity mortgages, and local county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease beginning in FY 2025 due to reduced commissions collected and remitted by clerks of the circuit court. Local recordation tax revenues face a potentially significant reduction beginning in FY 2025 due to the higher exemption threshold, although the exact amount cannot be reliably estimated. Reporting mandates can be absorbed with existing local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Clerks of the Circuit Court, who are part of the Judicial Branch supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts. In 10 Maryland counties, the Clerks collect local recordation taxes, earn commissions that are remitted to the State General Fund, and are statutorily required under the bill to track and submit an annual report to the General Assembly regarding exempt indemnity mortgages and forgone revenue.

Synopsis: Altering the name of the Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship to be the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship.
Title: Higher Education – Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship – Altering Name of Scholarship

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Renames the Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship and its associated fund to the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Veterans and active-duty members of the U.S. Armed Forces who served in Afghanistan and Iraq, activated members of the reserve or Maryland National Guard, and their spouses and children seeking higher education scholarships in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: No net state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the scholarship name change using existing budgeted resources, absorbing an estimated $1,500 in contractual costs to update the Maryland College Aid Processing System. State revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary administering agency of the scholarship and the scholarship fund, requiring system updates in the Maryland College Aid Processing System to reflect the renamed scholarship.
Identical to MHEC; as the primary administrator of state financial aid programs, it must implement the renaming of the scholarship program within its systems and materials.
The agency assists veterans and military families in identifying and accessing state education benefits, including scholarships targeted to veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq conflicts.
Statutorily designated to account for the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.
Statutorily designated to hold the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund separately and receive deposits for the fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Secretary of Health to adopt regulations for pharmacy benefits managers that contract with managed care organizations that establish requirements for conducting audits of pharmacies or pharmacists; establishing requirements and prohibitions regarding audits by certain pharmacy benefits managers, including provisions related to audit limits, acceptance of certain documents as proof, recoupment of funds or charging of fees for prescriptions of unbreakable package sizes, and access to financial documentation; etc.
Title: Health Insurance – Pharmacy Benefits Managers – Audits of Pharmacies and Pharmacists

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: This bill establishes additional restrictions and requirements regarding audits of pharmacies and pharmacists conducted by pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs) on behalf of carriers, and requires the Secretary of Health to adopt substantively similar regulations for PBMs contracting with Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs). Among other provisions, it caps desk or site audits at 125 prescriptions, prohibits recoupment or fees regarding incorrect days-of-supply calculations for unbreakable packages under specified conditions, restricts access to pharmacy financial/bank records, requires acceptance of cash register receipts as proof of pickup or delivery, and mandates secure communication mechanisms and inquiry response times.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Secretary of Health) and the Maryland Insurance Administration (Insurance Commissioner)
stakeholders: Pharmacies and pharmacists, pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs), health insurance carriers, Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs), and health plan purchasers including the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for Medicaid and the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, as well as federal matching fund revenues, may increase by an indeterminate amount to the extent that PBMs pass along increased administrative and contract costs to purchasers. Maryland Insurance Administration workload can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Local government health care expenditures may increase if costs are passed on through fully insured health benefit plans. Specific dollar figures are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs) under the Insurance Article and is granted explicit authority under the bill to adopt regulations regarding audit procedures and documentation.

The bill requires the Secretary of Health to adopt regulations governing pharmacy benefits managers that contract with Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs) for conducting pharmacy audits, which may also have an indeterminate fiscal impact on Medicaid expenditures.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which contracts with pharmacy benefits managers; any increased operational or administrative costs incurred by PBMs may be passed along to the State Plan.

Synopsis: Prohibiting, except under certain circumstances, insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations that provide coverage for diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations from imposing a copayment, coinsurance, or deductible requirement for the examination; and requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to study and report to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by October 1, 2023 on the financial impact of eliminating cost-sharing for diagnostic image-guided biopsies for breast cancer.
Title: Health Insurance - Diagnostic and Supplemental Examinations and Biopsies for Breast Cancer - Cost-Sharing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: Prohibits health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from imposing copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles on diagnostic and supplemental breast examinations, while permitting deductibles under high-deductible health plans to maintain health savings account eligibility. It also requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to study and report on the financial impact of eliminating cost-sharing for diagnostic image-guided breast cancer biopsies.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Individuals requiring diagnostic or supplemental breast cancer screenings, health insurance carriers, employers offering fully insured medical plans, and the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in FY 2024 only from $125 rate and form filing fees, which MIA can review using existing resources. The Maryland Health Care Commission can conduct the required study with existing resources. Any expenditure impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program is indeterminate, while expenditures for local governments purchasing fully insured plans may increase if health insurance costs rise.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct a study and submit a report on the financial impact of eliminating health insurance cost-sharing for diagnostic image-guided biopsies for breast cancer.

MIA is the regulatory agency responsible for enforcing health insurance mandates, reviewing and approving carrier policy forms and rate filings for compliance with the prohibition on cost-sharing, and collecting associated filing fees.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which may experience an indeterminate fiscal impact from the prohibition of cost-sharing for diagnostic or supplemental breast examinations.
MHBE oversees qualified health plans offered on the individual and small business marketplace, which are subject to Maryland health benefit and cost-sharing statutory requirements.
MDH houses the Maryland Health Care Commission as an independent regulatory agency and oversees public health initiatives related to cancer screening and healthcare access across the state.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is required by the bill to submit its completed study and report directly to the Governor by October 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Increasing the threshold amount above which the Friendship Heights Village Council is prohibited from entering into a certain contract without a competitive bidding process; and authorizing the village council, by majority vote, to enter into a certain contract that exceeds the $20,000 threshold amount without a competitive bidding process if the procurement is in response to an emergency.
Title: Montgomery County - Village of Friendship Heights Special Taxing District - Procurement MC 15-23
bill_summary: Increases the contract value threshold from $5,000 to $20,000 above which the Friendship Heights Village Council must solicit competitive bids, and authorizes the council to enter into contracts exceeding $20,000 without competitive bidding during unforeseen emergencies affecting public health, safety, or welfare.
responsible_party: Friendship Heights Village Council
stakeholders: Residents, businesses, and contractors within the Village of Friendship Heights Special Taxing District in Montgomery County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. The bill likely has limited or no effect on the Village of Friendship Heights finances, but creates operational and administrative efficiencies by providing greater procurement flexibility and the ability to respond swiftly to emergencies.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Staff and leadership of the Office of Financial Regulation, as well as depository and non-depository financial institutions operating in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: One-time costs to update signage and related materials, as well as the salary and fringe benefits for the additional Deputy Commissioner position, can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reorganizes a key unit within the Maryland Department of Labor by officially establishing the Office of Financial Regulation under the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and splitting the Deputy Commissioner role into two distinct positions (Depository Activities and Non-Depository Activities).

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health and the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to jointly conduct a study on prescription drug claim payments made by Medicaid managed care organizations to pharmacies in calendar years 2021 and 2022 compared to Medicaid fee-for-service rates, and to recommend methodologies for calculating accurate drug ingredient costs and dispensing fees by October 31, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Prescription Drug Affordability Board
stakeholders: Medicaid managed care organizations, pharmacies, pharmacy benefits managers, and Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Maryland Department of Health and the Prescription Drug Affordability Board can conduct the study and submit the required report using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is directly mandated by the bill to jointly conduct a study with the Prescription Drug Affordability Board regarding Medicaid managed care organization (MCO) prescription drug claim payments and fee-for-service reimbursement rates, and to submit a final report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the Prescription Drug Affordability Board (PDAB), a permanent state board, to co-lead the study on prescription drug claims and cost methodologies alongside the Maryland Department of Health and report findings to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an institution of higher education from refusing to provide a current or former student with a transcript or taking other punitive measures regarding a student's transcript request because the student owes a debt to the institution of higher education.
Title: Institutions of Higher Education - Transcripts - Prohibition on Punitive Measures Related to Student Debt

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits institutions of higher education from refusing to provide a transcript, charging higher fees, conditioning transcript issuance on payment, or taking other punitive measures against current or former students who owe a debt to the institution, and bans using transcript issuance as a tool for debt collection.
responsible_party: Institutions of higher education in Maryland
stakeholders: Current and former college and university students with outstanding institutional debts, as well as public, private nonprofit, and for-profit institutions of higher education and community colleges in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local higher education revenues, as well as Central Collection Unit (CCU) special fund revenues, will decrease—potentially significantly—due to reduced ability to collect past-due student accounts. The exact financial loss cannot be reliably estimated. Public and local institutions may partially offset forgone revenues by raising tuition and fees for future students. State and local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to institutions of higher education, prohibiting them from withholding transcripts due to student debt. The University System of Maryland must change its existing tuition and fee policies and faces potentially significant reductions in debt collection revenues.

As a public four-year institution of higher education operating independently of USM, Morgan State University must comply with the transcript release prohibitions and faces potential decreases in debt collection revenues.
As a public honors college, St. Mary's College of Maryland is subject to the bill's restrictions on transcript withholding for past-due balances and may experience a decrease in collection revenues.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), which is housed within DBM, collects delinquent student debt on behalf of public institutions. The bill will restrict a key collection tool and may significantly decrease CCU special fund collection revenues.
As the state's central coordinating and regulatory agency for all public and private postsecondary education institutions, MHEC oversees statewide policies impacting higher education operations.

The Office of the Attorney General (including its Consumer Protection Division and counsel representing state higher education institutions) provides legal counsel regarding student debt collection practices and federal consumer protection standards.

bill_summary: Establishes a commercial blue and flathead catfish finfish trotline license, authorizing holders to commercially harvest blue and flathead catfish in Maryland tidal waters using finfish trotlines without requiring a tidal fish license, set at an annual fee of $15, and allows licensees to obtain a seafood dealer authorization at a reduced fee of $50.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Commercial fishers harvesting blue and flathead catfish, commercial seafood dealers, and small fishing businesses in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Fisheries Research and Development Fund increase by up to $1,500 in FY 2023 and approximately $1,500 annually thereafter from the $15 license fees. State expenditures are not affected as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a commercial blue and flathead catfish finfish trotline license under the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). DNR is the primary implementing agency responsible for adopting regulations, processing license applications, collecting license fees, and managing the fishery.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of Public Works and the State Treasurer to provide public notice of a public sale of State bonds by The Municipal Market Monitor (TM3) or a similar service or such other method deemed appropriate by the State Treasurer.
Title: Bond Sales - Notification of the Public
