bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of Public Works and the State Treasurer to give public notice of a public sale of State bonds through the Municipal Market Monitor (TM3) or a similar service or method deemed appropriate by the State Treasurer.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works and the Maryland State Treasurer
stakeholders: Municipal market participants, prospective bond bidders, investors, and state financial agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may experience a potential minimal decrease as the Board of Public Works and the State Treasurer can utilize less expensive notification methods. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Treasurer's Office by authorizing the State Treasurer to determine appropriate services or methods (such as the Municipal Market Monitor) for public notifications of State bond sales and postponed sales.

The bill explicitly governs how the Board of Public Works provides public notice when offering State bonds at public sales, allowing modernization and flexibility in notice methods deemed appropriate by the Treasurer.

Synopsis: Establishing the State Specialist for Value-Added Agriculture as a position in the Department of Agriculture to serve as the primary point of contact for individuals engaging in, or interested in engaging in, value-added agriculture in the State; and requiring the Specialist to provide information regarding State and federal regulations related to value-added agriculture and to act as a liaison between State and federal partners involved in value-added agriculture.
Title: Department of Agriculture - State Specialist for Value-Added Agriculture

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Establishes the State Specialist for Value-Added Agriculture as a position within the Maryland Department of Agriculture to serve as the primary point of contact, provide regulatory guidance, and act as a liaison for individuals and businesses involved in value-added agriculture.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Farmers, agricultural producers, processors, and small agricultural businesses engaged or interested in value-added agriculture, including meat processing and equine enterprises.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $81,473 in FY 2024 to hire one administrator for the specialist position, with costs rising to $111,800 by FY 2028 due to ongoing salary, benefits, and operating expenses. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the State Specialist for Value-Added Agriculture as a statutory position within the Department of Agriculture, appointed by the Secretary of Agriculture, with associated general fund expenditures for personnel and operations.

As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM is responsible for authorizing the newly mandated Position Identification Number (PIN) and administering the associated state personnel and budget allocations.

Synopsis: Requiring a parking citation issued by a political subdivision, a State agency, or a third-party contractor to include a box that the person issued the citation may check to indicate that the registration plates cited were not issued for the vehicle described in the citation; requiring a political subdivision, State agency, or third-party contractor that receives a parking citation from a person with the box checked to perform a certain verification process and dismiss the citation under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Parking Enforcement - Citations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Requires parking citations issued by State agencies, political subdivisions, or third-party contractors to include a checkable box allowing individuals to indicate that the cited license plate was not issued for the vehicle described. Entities receiving a checked citation must verify the registration through the Motor Vehicle Administration and dismiss the citation if the recipient is found not liable, while prohibiting individuals from checking the box fraudulently.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), State agencies that issue parking citations, and local political subdivisions
stakeholders: Vehicle owners receiving parking citations, State and local parking enforcement authorities, and third-party parking enforcement contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures increase in FY 2024 to reprint or modify parking citations, with potential minor operational costs depending on the volume of verification requests. Parking revenues may be delayed during verification but are not expected to be materially affected. Specific dollar amounts cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires issuing entities to verify vehicle and registration plate information through the Motor Vehicle Administration (the Administration under the Transportation Article) when a recipient checks the box indicating a vehicle registration mismatch.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which is tasked with providing the vehicle registration verification interface under the Transportation Article.

DGS manages state-owned facilities and parking lots and enforces parking regulations through the Maryland Capitol Police; it must update its citation forms and handle verification requests for citations issued on state property.
MSP is an authorized law enforcement agency that issues citations and will be required to reprint or update parking citation forms and follow the required verification process.

The District Court of Maryland adjudicates contested parking citations; the bill may negligibly reduce court caseloads to the extent citations are dismissed before trial through the administrative verification process.

Synopsis: Altering the means by which the State Treasurer may send notice of a denial of a claim made under the Maryland Tort Claims Act to authorize notice by e-mail or, if it is the only available means, by regular mail.
Title: Maryland Tort Claims Act - Denial of Claims - Notice

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
Torts -see also- Libel and Slander; Med Malp; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill alters the notification requirements for denying a claim under the Maryland Tort Claims Act by authorizing the State Treasurer to send written notice of denial by email, or by regular mail if regular mail is the only available means, rather than requiring certified mail.
responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer's Office
stakeholders: Individuals filing tort claims against the State of Maryland under the Maryland Tort Claims Act, their legal representatives or counsel, and the State Treasurer's Office.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures decrease by approximately $17,800 annually beginning in FY 2024 due to savings in certified mail postage and administrative handling costs. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory procedures of the Maryland State Treasurer's Office regarding how it issues final notices of denial for claims filed under the Maryland Tort Claims Act, authorizing notice by email or regular mail and saving the agency approximately $17,800 annually in postage and administrative handling costs.

Synopsis: Requiring a principal department of the Executive Branch to give certain notice to the public, the General Assembly, and any exclusive representative with certain bargaining unit employees, hold a public hearing, submit a certain report, make the report publicly available, and allow the submission of certain comments before changing the use, purpose, or function of a State facility or closing a State facility.
Title: State Government - State Facilities Changes and Closures - Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee

bill_summary: This bill establishes notice, reporting, and public hearing requirements that Executive Branch principal departments must follow prior to closing a State facility or changing its use, purpose, or function. It also expands the definition of a State facility subject to these requirements to include any facility where 25 or more State employees are regularly assigned.
responsible_party: Principal departments of the Executive Branch of Maryland State government
stakeholders: State employees, exclusive representatives (labor unions), clients, inmates, patients, and residents served by State facilities, as well as the general public in affected communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources. State operations and finances could see minimal and absorbable impacts if the mandated procedures delay the closure, reopening, or modification of a facility. There is no direct effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS manages the planning, construction, maintenance, leasing, and acquisition of state-owned and leased facilities. Expanding the procedural requirements for closing or changing the use of state facilities directly impacts its facility management and real estate operations.

MDH operates numerous state health facilities and hospitals. The bill specifically governs facilities providing health services to clients, imposing strict notice, reporting, and hearing timelines prior to any closure or change of use.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is directly subject to the bill's provisions governing facilities providing correctional services to inmates, requiring extensive public notice, legislative reporting, and public hearings before altering or closing correctional facilities.
DJS operates juvenile residential and detention facilities. The bill explicitly applies to facilities providing juvenile services, mandating rigorous closure and reprogramming protocols.

DBM oversees the state budget and serves as the central personnel agency. The bill mandates closure reports detailing budgetary impacts, employee transition assistance plans, and engagement with exclusive bargaining representatives.
Executive branch principal departments seeking to close a state facility are statutorily required to submit a comprehensive explanatory and justification report to the Governor.
BPW oversees and approves significant state real estate transactions, lease approvals, and dispositions of state property that arise when state facilities are altered, acquired, or closed.

As a principal executive department maintaining numerous facilities across Maryland with 25 or more state employees, MDOT must comply with the expanded notice and hearing procedures if altering or closing facilities.
MSP operates barracks and administrative facilities that fall under the expanded definition of state facilities with 25 or more employees, making it subject to the notice and closure requirements.

Synopsis: Repealing the limitations on investment in certain commercial paper in which the Treasurer may invest or reinvest certain unexpended or surplus funds; requiring the Treasurer to adopt regulations to establish a State investment policy with certain thresholds; and requiring the Treasurer to notify certain officials and governing bodies of certain local governmental units about the provisions of the Act.
Title: State Investment Portfolio - Investment Thresholds - Alterations

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Repeals the statutory 10% cap on State investments in commercial paper and requires the State Treasurer to adopt regulations establishing a State investment policy that specifies maximum investment thresholds for each authorized asset class. It also requires the Treasurer to notify local government entities about the changes to permit updates to local investment policies.
responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer
stakeholders: State Treasurer's Office, local government entities (counties, municipalities, Baltimore City, community colleges, and public authorities), and Maryland taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2024 if higher investment returns are achieved through expanded commercial paper investments; State expenditures are unaffected. Local government revenues may also experience minimal, indeterminate increases from increased investment flexibility, with no effect on local expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office is the primary implementing agency. The bill alters statutory limits on investments in commercial paper, requires the Treasurer to adopt regulations establishing a State investment policy with asset class thresholds, and mandates written notification to affected local government entities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is referenced in the statute governing the State investment portfolio, receiving annual reporting and collaborating on guidelines for minority business enterprise utilization in brokerage and investment management across the authorized asset classes.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "hearing aid dispensary" to include certain actions taken for the purpose of ordering certain hearing instruments and specifying that certain hearing instruments include prescription hearing aids; altering the definition of "practice audiology" for the purposes of certain provisions of law governing the licensure of audiologists; and providing that certain provisions of law do not apply to certain actions taken with respect to certain over-the-counter hearing aids.
Title: Maryland Audiology, Hearing Aid Dispensing, Speech-Language Pathology, and Music Therapy Act - Definitions and Application

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Audiology, Hearing Aid Dispensing, Speech-Language Pathology, and Music Therapy Act to conform with federal regulations regarding hearing aids. It expands the definition of practicing audiology to include prescribing, ordering, dispensing, and fitting hearing aids and osseo-integrated devices; clarifies that hearing aid dispensing includes ordering prescription hearing aids; and exempts over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids from the Act's licensing and regulatory scope.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
stakeholders: Audiologists, licensed hearing aid dispensers, speech-language pathologists, retailers and distributors of over-the-counter hearing aids, and patients with auditory or vestibular conditions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal effect. The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists can handle regulatory updates using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists, which regulates the professions affected by the bill and will need to update its licensing regulations to reflect the revised definitions and over-the-counter exemptions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office advocates for and addresses policies affecting Deaf and hard-of-hearing Marylanders, making the regulation and accessibility of hearing aids, osseo-integrated devices, and audiology services relevant to its overarching constituency and mission.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Kent County Board of Education to include a student member; providing for the initial term of the student member of the county board; requiring the student member to attend the Maryland Association of Boards of Education new student board orientation and all regular meetings of the county board; prohibiting the student member's attendance at an executive session of the county board; etc.
Title: Kent County - Board of Education - Student Member

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.

bill_summary: Adds a nonvoting student member to the Kent County Board of Education, establishing eligibility requirements, an application and election process by county high school students, a one-year term of office, and specified duties and meeting attendance requirements.
responsible_party: Kent County Board of Education
stakeholders: Kent County high school students, the Kent County Board of Education, and Kent County Public Schools
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal effect. Kent County finances are not affected because the bill codifies existing practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) provides leadership and oversight for Maryland's 24 local public school systems. This bill alters the statutory composition and selection process for the Kent County Board of Education under the Education Article, which falls within MSDE's policy and governance purview, although it has no fiscal impact on the department.

Synopsis: Authorizing counties and municipal corporations to alter a certain limitation on the combined gross income of a homeowner for purposes of a local supplement to the homeowners' property tax credit; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Property Tax - Local Homeowners' Credit Supplement - Limitation on Combined Gross Income

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, Maryland counties, and municipal corporations to alter the limitation on a homeowner's combined gross income for purposes of granting a local supplement to the State Homeowners' Property Tax Credit Program, allowing local governments to expand eligibility beyond the State's $60,000 income limit.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners with household incomes exceeding existing program thresholds and local county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None, as the State Department of Assessments and Taxation can continue administering local supplements using existing resources. Local effect: Indeterminate potential decrease in local property tax revenues beginning in FY 2024 if jurisdictions elect to raise income thresholds and expand credit eligibility.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allows local governments to alter income limits for local supplements to the homeowners' property tax credit. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding property tax assessment disputes, tax exemptions, and property tax credit determinations.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, hearing further appeals resulting from decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards concerning property tax credits.

Synopsis: Requiring a person who is not required to be licensed or permitted under certain provisions of law to obtain a free Department of Natural Resources identification number before using a snare, a trap, or another similar device to capture wildlife; and requiring a person who uses a snare, a trap, or another similar device to capture wildlife to ensure the person's Department identification number is stamped on the device or on a metal tag affixed to the device.
Title: Hunting - Snares, Traps, and Other Similar Devices - Identification Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Requires individuals who are otherwise exempt from wildlife licensing or permitting requirements to obtain a free Department of Natural Resources (DNR) identification number before using a snare, trap, or similar device to capture wildlife. Trappers must stamp their DNR identification number on the device or an affixed metal tag, unless DNR grants a waiver for devices used solely on private property owned or rented by the trapper.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Individuals who use snares, traps, or similar devices to capture wildlife (including landowners exempt from standard licensing), hunters, trappers, and the Natural Resources Police.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations. DNR can issue any additional identification numbers at no cost using its existing online COMPASS licensing system and budgeted resources. Application of existing penalties for violations is not expected to materially affect State revenue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is directly responsible for administering the bill's requirements. This includes issuing free identification numbers through its online licensing system (COMPASS), granting potential waivers for devices on private property, and receiving reports and enforcing trap identification rules through its Natural Resources Police Force.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a local board of elections from voting to change the location of a polling place without first holding a meeting to discuss the proposed change and providing an opportunity for individuals and organizations to testify; requiring each local board to submit a polling place plan to the State Board of Elections at least 6 months prior to each statewide primary election; altering the date of the 2024 statewide primary election and the primary election for municipal offices in Baltimore City to the second Tuesday in May; etc.
Title: Elections - Polling Place Plan, Prohibited Acts, and 2024 Primary Election Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires local boards of elections to hold a public meeting with at least 14 days' written notice before changing polling place locations, and submit a polling place plan to the State Board of Elections for approval at least six months prior to statewide primary elections. It also prohibits influencing or attempting to influence a voter's decision to vote by other lawful means, and moves the date of Maryland's 2024 statewide primary election and the Baltimore City municipal primary election to the second Tuesday in May.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters (particularly historically disenfranchised communities), local election officials and staff, and local and state elected officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $156,380 in FY 2024, reflecting the hiring of one full-time program administrator at the State Board of Elections and the State's 50% share of mapping services ($37,500). Ongoing State expenditures range from $109,400 to $164,500 annually through FY 2028. Local government expenditures increase collectively by at least $37,500 in FY 2024 (and similar amounts in future primary election years) for their share of mapping services, plus potential indeterminate costs for local personnel, mileage, or consultants. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary implementing agency tasked with reviewing and approving local polling place plans, providing technical assistance and mapping services to local election boards, and administering changes to the 2024 primary election date.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes violations of Maryland election laws, which the bill expands by prohibiting attempts to influence a voter's decision whether to vote by other lawful means.
The bill expands criminal misdemeanor provisions and civil penalties related to voter interference, which fall under the jurisdiction of Maryland's court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals accused of criminal violations, including the expanded misdemeanor offenses under Election Law § 16-201 which carry penalties of up to five years imprisonment.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a certain incarcerated person from violating a condition of pretrial or posttrial release or other pretrial or posttrial condition prohibiting the person from contacting, harassing, or abusing an alleged victim or going in or near an alleged victim's residence or place of employment.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Violation of Pretrial or Posttrial Condition by Incarcerated Person - Victim Contact

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse & Neg.; Elder Abuse & Neg., etc
Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom

bill_summary: Expands current law to explicitly prohibit incarcerated individuals charged with certain crimes—such as crimes of violence, stalking, sexual offenses against minors, or domestic crimes—from violating pretrial or posttrial conditions prohibiting them from contacting, harassing, or abusing an alleged victim or going near their residence or workplace.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals charged with specified offenses, alleged crime victims, state and local correctional facilities, and criminal justice personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly extends the prohibition against contacting, harassing, or abusing victims under pretrial or posttrial conditions to incarcerated persons, which directly impacts individuals held in state correctional facilities and pretrial detention centers managed by DPSCS.
The bill establishes misdemeanor criminal penalties for incarcerated persons who violate pretrial or posttrial conditions, which are adjudicated within the state court system administered by the AOC.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent criminal defendants who may face new misdemeanor charges and additional incarceration time under the expanded provisions of this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing the Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund to provide reimbursement for costs associated with educating, training, certifying, recruiting, placing, and retaining behavioral health professionals and paraprofessionals; and requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission, in coordination with certain entities, to conduct a comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment on or before October 1, 2024, and submit the assessment to certain committees of the General Assembly by October 15, 2024.
Title: Mental Health - Workforce Development - Fund Established

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund, administered by the Maryland Department of Health, to provide reimbursement for costs associated with educating, training, certifying, recruiting, placing, and retaining behavioral health professionals and paraprofessionals. The bill also requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct a comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment and submit recommendations by October 15, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Behavioral health professionals, paraprofessionals, behavioral health care providers and small business practices, educational institutions, and individuals receiving behavioral health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct the workforce assessment. General fund expenditures increase by an estimated minimum of $1,000,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 to capitalize the fund, resulting in equivalent special fund revenues and expenditures for reimbursement. Local government and health department revenues may increase to the extent they qualify for reimbursement from the fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns the Department of Health (MDH) to administer the newly created Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund and submit annual reports on fund usage. Additionally, MDH's Behavioral Health Administration must coordinate on the comprehensive workforce needs assessment.

The bill explicitly mandates MHCC to conduct a comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment and submit recommendations by October 2024, requiring an estimated $75,000 in special fund expenditures.

MHEC is statutorily required to coordinate with MHCC on the comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment, and may see revenue or program impacts from future workforce training and education allocations.

The Maryland Department of Labor is statutorily required to coordinate with MHCC on the comprehensive behavioral health workforce needs assessment to evaluate workforce capacity and training pathways.
The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the monies of the newly created Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund separately from other funds.
The Comptroller is statutorily tasked with accounting for the newly established Behavioral Health Workforce Investment Fund.
The bill explicitly subjects the newly established fund to periodic compliance audits by the Office of Legislative Audits.
USM institutions educating and training behavioral health professionals may experience an increase in special fund revenues via reimbursements from the newly created fund.

Synopsis: Requiring that the Health Services Cost Review Commission exercise its authority to consider certain standards when determining the reasonableness of certain rates in a manner that is consistent with the all-payer model contract.
Title: Health Services Cost Review Commission - Hospital Rates - All-Payer Model Contract

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Requires the Health Services Cost Review Commission to take into account objective standards of efficiency and effectiveness in a manner consistent with the All-Payer Model Contract when determining the reasonableness of hospital rates.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Maryland acute and chronic care hospitals, health care facility service purchasers, and patients
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies existing agency practices, as the Health Services Cost Review Commission already considers the All-Payer Model Contract and its successor agreements (the Total Cost of Care Model) when reviewing and establishing hospital rates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory authority and rate-setting standards of the Health Services Cost Review Commission, requiring it to consider objective standards of efficiency and effectiveness in a manner consistent with the all-payer model contract.

The Health Services Cost Review Commission operates as an independent regulatory agency within the Maryland Department of Health, and the statutory section amended includes coordination with the Secretary of Health.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain rate of interest on certain member contributions in active members' nonvested accounts in the State Retirement and Pension System if the members have not withdrawn contributions from the nonvested accounts and are not eligible to receive a certain vested allowance; providing for the retroactive application of the Act; etc.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Nonvested Accounts - Regular Interest

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the State Retirement and Pension System to pay regular interest on accumulated member contributions in nonvested accounts of former members who have not withdrawn those contributions and who are active members of an eligible state retirement or pension plan, applied retroactively to the date they rejoined the system.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Active members of the State Retirement and Pension System who hold nonvested member contribution accounts from previous membership in an SRPS plan (approximately 1,600 identified members/accounts).
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires an estimated retroactive payment of approximately $514,000 in interest across roughly 1,600 accounts, reducing system assets and causing a minimal increase in unfunded pension liabilities for the State and participating governmental units (PGUs). This results in only a negligible increase in State and PGU pension contribution expenditures and has no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 424 directly governs the calculation and payment of regular interest on member contributions in nonvested accounts within the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers SRPS and is responsible for implementing the retroactive and prospective interest payments on approximately 1,600 identified accounts.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions relating to immunity from criminal arrest, charge, or prosecution for a person experiencing a medical emergency after ingesting or using alcohol or drugs.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Medical Emergency - Immunity

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: This bill alters criminal immunity provisions for individuals experiencing a drug- or alcohol-induced medical emergency, clarifying that immunity from arrest, charge, or prosecution for certain drug and alcohol offenses applies to a person who is experiencing a medical emergency. It also extends protections to prevent individuals experiencing such an emergency from being sanctioned for violations of pretrial release, probation, or parole if evidence is obtained solely through seeking or receiving medical assistance.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Individuals experiencing drug- or alcohol-related medical emergencies, individuals assisting them, persons on pretrial release, probation, or parole, and law enforcement and criminal justice personnel
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Division of Parole and Probation as well as pretrial detention services. The bill explicitly prohibits individuals on probation, parole, or pretrial release from being sanctioned for violations if the evidence was obtained solely as a result of seeking, providing, or receiving emergency medical assistance.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP troopers are directly bound by the statutory immunity provisions prohibiting arrest and charging for specified drug and alcohol offenses when medical emergency assistance is sought or received.

The judiciary manages pretrial release, probation violation hearings, and criminal prosecutions for drug and alcohol violations, which are directly altered by the expanded statutory immunity and protection from sanctions under this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants facing criminal charges and probation, parole, or pretrial release violation proceedings. The bill provides complete statutory immunity and defense against violations for qualifying clients.
The OAG advises state agencies on statutory interpretation and represents the state in criminal appeals, where statutory immunity claims under Criminal Procedure § 1-210 are litigated.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to authorize a certain grant for the student member serving in the first year of the student's term on the Board of Regents.
Title: University System of Maryland - Board of Regents - Student Member Grant

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland (USM) Board of Regents to grant private donor funds to a student member of the board during the first year of their two-year term, covering up to the full cost of tuition and fees without exceeding the total cost of attendance.
responsible_party: University System of Maryland Board of Regents
stakeholders: Student members serving on the USM Board of Regents and the University System of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Higher education revenues and expenditures for USM may increase by an offsetting amount to the extent private donor funds are received and distributed for the grant, up to the student's tuition and fees (ranging on average from approximately $10,100 for undergraduate in-state students to up to $92,500 for certain graduate programs in FY 2024). USM can administer the grants using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the University System of Maryland (USM) Board of Regents, authorizing the board to award a grant funded by private donations to a student regent serving in the first year of a two-year term.

The bill provides an explicit statutory exemption specifying that the grant or tuition waiver awarded to the student regent may not be considered a gift or compensation under the Maryland Public Ethics Law, which is administered by the State Ethics Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Procurement Improvement Council to include the Comptroller and the Attorney General; authorizing certain members to send a designee to attend certain meetings under certain circumstances; and clarifying the duties of the Council to include discussion of strategies to increase the participation of small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses in procurement contracts.
Title: Procurement Improvement Council - Membership and Duties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Adds the Comptroller and the Attorney General (or their designees) to the Procurement Improvement Council and requires the Council to provide a forum for discussing strategies to increase the participation of small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses in State procurement contracts.
responsible_party: Procurement Improvement Council
stakeholders: Small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses seeking State contracts, as well as State procurement officials and agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly adds the Comptroller as a statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council and authorizes the Comptroller to send a designee to attend meetings.
The bill explicitly adds the Attorney General as a statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council and authorizes the Attorney General to send a designee to attend meetings.

The Department of General Services serves as the state's central procurement authority, and the Chief Procurement Officer (housed within DGS) serves as the Chair and principal staff to the Procurement Improvement Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Special Secretary is a statutory member of the Council, and the bill expands the Council's duties to explicitly provide a forum for strategies to increase the participation of small, minority-owned, and women-owned businesses in State procurement contracts.

The Board of Public Works oversees state procurements, the Board's Procurement Advisor is a member of the Council, and the Council is statutorily mandated to advise the Board on procurement issues and recommendations.
The State Treasurer is a statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council and is explicitly referenced in the statute regarding meeting attendance and designees.
The Governor appoints several members of the Procurement Improvement Council representing local government, social service providers, and minority-, women-, or veteran-owned businesses.
The Secretary of Information Technology is an existing statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council affected by the Council's operations.
The Secretary of Transportation is an existing statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council.
The Secretary of Health is an existing statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council.
The Secretary of Human Services is an existing statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services is an existing statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council.
The State Superintendent of Schools is an existing statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council.
The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland is an existing statutory member of the Procurement Improvement Council.

Synopsis: Increasing from four to five the number of full-time assistant sheriffs provided to the Sheriff of Prince George's County; and providing that the Fraternal Order of Police will negotiate on behalf of deputy sheriffs in benefit matters not related to salary.
Title: Prince George's County - Office of the Sheriff - Deputy Sheriffs and Labor Organizations PG 308-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Increases the number of full-time assistant sheriffs provided to the Sheriff of Prince George's County from four to five and updates statutory provisions regarding labor representation to reflect that non-salary benefits are negotiated by the Fraternal Order of Police rather than the Deputy Sheriffs' Association.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Office of the Sheriff
stakeholders: Prince George's County Sheriff's Office, assistant sheriffs, deputy sheriffs, the Fraternal Order of Police, and Prince George's County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George's County expenditures increase by approximately $331,600 annually beginning in fiscal year 2024 to fund the salary and fringe benefits of one additional full-time assistant sheriff. County revenues are unaffected.

Synopsis: Increasing the maximum number of speed monitoring systems that may be placed and used on Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) in Prince George's County from three to six; requiring the State Highway Administration in conjunction with a certain entity to report annually its recommendations for solutions to address accidents, injuries, and fatalities on the highway; extending the termination date for a provision of law granting the authority to place speed monitoring systems on Maryland Route 210 in Prince George's County; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) PG 304-23

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum number of speed monitoring systems (speed cameras) that Prince George's County may operate on Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) from three to six, permitting them to be mobile or stationary. It also extends the authorization for these speed cameras by five years through September 30, 2028, and requires the State Highway Administration, in conjunction with the Prince George's County Department of Public Works and Transportation, to report annually on accident solutions and fund distributions.
responsible_party: Maryland State Highway Administration and Prince George's County Department of Public Works and Transportation
stakeholders: Drivers traveling on Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway), Prince George's County residents, and the District Court
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures are projected to increase from FY 2024 through FY 2029 (estimated at several hundred thousand dollars over the period) as Prince George's County remits net speed camera revenues to the State Highway Administration for highway safety improvements. General fund revenues will likely increase slightly from penalties collected in contested District Court cases. Prince George's County revenues and expenditures will both increase from system implementation and citation collection, but will have no net local fiscal impact because county revenues are limited to cost recovery, with remaining net proceeds forwarded to the State.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates SHA, in conjunction with Prince George's County, to examine safety factors on MD Route 210, submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly, and use remitted fine revenues to implement infrastructure and safety solutions.

MDOT is the parent department of the State Highway Administration, and the bill affects Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures through the collection and use of speed camera fine revenues.
Under the statute referenced in the bill, speed camera fines collected by Prince George's County must be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration.
Increasing the number of speed monitoring systems and extending their authorization leads to an increase in contested citations and traffic trials adjudicated in the District Court.
The bill mandates that SHA submit an annual report detailing safety findings, recommendations, and fund expenditures directly to the Governor.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County, notwithstanding a certain prohibition on the transfer of a license with an off-sale privilege, to approve the transfer of a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license to a premises located in a certain alcoholic beverages district under certain circumstances; authorizing the Board to issue a Class B-DD beer, wine, and liquor license with an off-sale privilege to certain restaurants in certain areas; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Licensing PG 305-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to approve the transfer of a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license into specified alcoholic beverages districts if no other Class A license operates within one mile of the premises. It also authorizes the issuance of Class B-DD (Development District) licenses with off-sale privileges to certain qualifying restaurants located outside the Capital Beltway, establishes a $5,000 annual fee for such licenses, repeals a restriction limiting areas to six Class B-DD licenses, and authorizes up to 50 Class B-DD licenses along Central Avenue between the Capital Beltway and the District of Columbia border.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurants, alcoholic beverage license holders and applicants, and consumers in Prince George's County, particularly along Central Avenue and other designated development districts.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George's County revenues increase beginning in FY 2024 by $3,025 for each standard Class B-DD license issued and by $5,000 for each Class B-DD off-sale license issued; the total revenue increase is indeterminate as the number of licenses to be issued is unknown. Local enforcement can be handled with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcoholic beverage industry. Although this legislation specifically pertains to local licensing administered by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it falls within the Comptroller's broader regulatory subject area.

Synopsis: Changing the title of the Chief Executive Officer of the Prince George's County public school system to the County Superintendent of the Prince George's County public school system; establishing the Office of Integrity and Compliance in the Prince George's County public school system to evaluate, examine, investigate, report on, and make recommendations on certain issues related to the Prince George's County public school system; requiring the County Council of Prince George's County to appoint an Integrity and Compliance officer; etc.
Title: Prince George's County Public Schools - Alterations to Title of Chief Executive Officer and Establishment of Office of Integrity and Compliance PG 501-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse & Neg.; Elder Abuse & Neg., etc
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Renames the Chief Executive Officer of Prince George's County Public Schools to County Superintendent, returns school consolidation authority to the Prince George's County Board of Education, and establishes the Office of Integrity and Compliance to investigate fraud, waste, and abuse and evaluate operational efficiency within the school system.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of Education and Prince George's County Council
stakeholders: Prince George's County Public Schools students, administrators, staff, school system vendors, and Prince George's County taxpayers
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Local school board expenditures increase by at least $741,041 annually beginning in FY 2024 to fund the Integrity and Compliance Officer and two additional positions (financial administrator and financial analyst), assuming existing Office of Internal Audit staff are repurposed. Costs could be significantly higher if existing staff are not repurposed. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE oversees the state's 24 public school systems, including Prince George's County Public Schools. The bill amends provisions regarding the governance, leadership structure (changing the CEO title to County Superintendent), and oversight mechanisms of the Prince George's County school system, and the State Superintendent holds approval authority over the superintendent's appointment.

The bill explicitly establishes the Office of Integrity and Compliance in the Prince George's County public school system and mandates that the Integrity and Compliance Officer report allegations of serious violations of law to the State Ethics Commission.

The bill updates statutory provisions relating to the selection process for the Prince George's County Superintendent, which includes nominees recommended by a search committee that includes two members appointed by the Governor.

Synopsis: Altering the alcoholic beverages that may be sold under a certain stadium license in Prince George's County; authorizing the holder of a Class B-Stadium (baseball stadium) beer, wine, and liquor license to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption; altering a provision of law providing that the profit from the sale of certain alcoholic beverages under the license may accrue to the use of the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission or the concessionaire; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B-Stadium (Baseball Stadium) Beer, Wine, and Liquor License PG 306-23
bill_summary: Authorizes holders of a Class B-Stadium (baseball stadium) license in Prince George's County to sell liquor in addition to beer and wine for on-premises consumption at baseball stadiums owned or operated by the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC), and updates stadium license designations and quotas.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Baseball stadium attendees in Prince George's County, the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC), and contracted private concessionaires.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Prince George's County finances or operations. The existing annual license fee remains $2,420.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the scope of an alcoholic beverages stadium license in Prince George's County to include the sale of liquor. Although local licensing is administered by the county Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, the Comptroller of Maryland is the state agency responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state alcohol excise and sales taxes.

Synopsis: Requiring a court to schedule a hearing on a certain petition regarding the proposed relocation of a child who is the subject of a custody or visitation order on an expedited basis under certain circumstances.
Title: Child Custody - Relocation of Child - Expedited Hearing (Assurance of Child's Safety Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Child Custody -see also- Parents and Guardians

bill_summary: Requires Maryland courts to schedule an expedited hearing if a party files a petition regarding a proposed relocation of a child 40 or more miles away from the primary residence that would significantly interfere with the other parent's ability to maintain a predetermined parenting time schedule.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts)
stakeholders: Parents and legal guardians subject to child custody or visitation orders, and their children.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local circuit court finances or operations; any potential expenditures associated with holding expedited hearings are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial system by requiring circuit courts to schedule hearings on an expedited basis for child custody petitions involving proposed relocations of 40 or more miles that significantly interfere with parenting schedules.

The Department of Human Services oversees family services and child welfare policies in Maryland and was consulted on the legislation regarding its interaction with domestic relations and custody proceedings.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Prince George's County to enter into a payment in lieu of taxes agreement with an owner of real property that is used for low-income housing that is financed through the county's Right of First Refusal program or acquired, constructed, or rehabilitated for the purposes of operating the low-income housing.
Title: Prince George's County - Payment in Lieu of Taxes Agreements - Low-Income Housing PG 403-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Authorizes Prince George's County to enter into payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements with owners of low-income housing developments that are financed through the county's Right of First Refusal program or are acquired, constructed, or rehabilitated to operate rental housing for lower-income individuals.
responsible_party: Governing body of Prince George's County
stakeholders: Prince George's County government, affordable housing developers and owners, and low-income renters in Prince George's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Prince George's County property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2024 to the extent that qualifying low-income housing developments receive property tax exemptions; however, any revenue decreases depend on the number and assessed value of affected properties and will be partially offset by negotiated PILOT payments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development oversees the state's affordable and low-income rental housing initiatives. While this bill specifically authorizes Prince George's County to enter into local payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the financing and preservation of affordable rental housing developments within the department's policy area.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to adopt regulations to ensure that children with disabilities who need special education and related services that cannot be provided in a public county, regional, or State program be placed in an appropriate nonpublic educational program that offers these services; requiring the State and certain counties to pay for costs of salaries for teachers at certain nonpublic schools in a certain amount and proportion; etc.
Title: Nonpublic Education - Placements of Children With Disabilities - Teacher Salaries (Teacher Pay Parity Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: The Teacher Pay Parity Act requires nonpublic special education placement schools that serve children with disabilities to provide teacher salaries equivalent to those of public school teachers with similar qualifications and experience in the same county. This salary parity is phased in over three years starting in fiscal year 2024, with the additional funding shared between the State and county governments.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Teachers at nonpublic special education schools, children with disabilities placed in nonpublic educational programs, local school systems, and county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.5 million in FY 2024, rising annually to $11.4 million by FY 2028 to cover the State share of teacher salary parity (the FY 2024 State budget as passed included $3.0 million for this purpose). Local county government expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2024, rising to $16.3 million in FY 2028 for the local share. Total combined State and local expenditures increase by $8.5 million in FY 2024 up to $27.7 million by FY 2028. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for the bill. MSDE oversees nonpublic special education placements, approves placement costs, administers the state-share funding formula, and is explicitly mandated to adopt regulations to carry out the provisions of the Act.

The bill creates an increasing mandated general fund appropriation beginning in FY 2025 (reaching $11.4 million by FY 2028) for the State's share of nonpublic special education teacher salaries, directly impacting the state budget developed and supervised by DBM.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board to place a licensee on emeritus status under certain circumstances; requiring the Board, under certain circumstances, to reinstate the license of an individual who is on inactive or emeritus status; exempting licensees who are on inactive status or emeritus status from continuing medical education requirements; repealing the requirement that the Board issue a license to an individual who is on inactive status under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: State Board of Physicians - Inactive and Emeritus Status

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Board of Physicians to grant emeritus status to retired physicians who meet specified criteria, including having practiced medicine in Maryland for at least 10 years without certain disciplinary actions. It exempts licensees on inactive or emeritus status from continuing medical education requirements and the standard three-year license expiration limit. The bill prohibits inactive and emeritus licensees from practicing medicine or delegating medical acts, while allowing emeritus physicians to use titles such as 'Dr.' or 'physician' as long as they do not represent that they are authorized to practice. Additionally, it establishes requirements for reinstating a license from inactive or emeritus status.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Licensed physicians in Maryland seeking inactive or retired/emeritus status.
fiscal_impact_summary: Any additional administrative workload for the Maryland Board of Physicians can be managed using existing budgeted resources. Any net impact on Board of Physicians special fund revenues related to emeritus or inactive status licensee fees is expected to be minimal. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians is a licensing board operating within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the Board's licensing operations, fee structures, and regulations regarding inactive and emeritus physician status.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a health occupations board from requiring that an applicant provide proof that the applicant is lawfully present in the United States or have a Social Security number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number as a condition for licensure, certification, or registration; requiring each health occupations board to require each applicant for a license to disclose the Social Security number or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number of the applicant or, as permitted by federal law, provide alternative documentation; etc.
Title: Health Occupations - Licenses, Certificates, and Registrations - Lawful Presence and Identification Numbers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Prohibits Maryland health occupations boards from requiring applicants to provide proof of lawful presence in the United States, a Social Security number, or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number as a condition for licensure, certification, or registration. It authorizes applicants to provide an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number or alternative federal documentation in place of a Social Security number.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Health Occupations Boards, including the State Board of Nursing)
stakeholders: Immigrants, noncitizens, and individuals without Social Security numbers seeking professional health licenses, certificates, or registrations in Maryland, as well as healthcare employers and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount starting in FY 2024 due to additional license fees collected. Special fund expenditures for the State Board of Nursing increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2024 for one-time programming costs, and may further increase for additional staffing (estimated by the Board at $293,587 in FY 2024 and at least $337,100 annually thereafter). Implementation for other boards is expected to be absorbed within existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs health occupations boards, which operate under the Maryland Department of Health, prohibiting them from requiring proof of lawful presence or an SSN/ITIN for licensure and adjusting application data collection, resulting in operational and fiscal impacts on licensing boards (such as the Board of Nursing).

The bill amends provisions in the Family Law Article governing occupational license information shared for child support enforcement, which directly involves the Child Support Administration within the Department of Human Services.

Synopsis: Altering the authority of the Ocean Downs Race Course to use certain Purse Dedication Account funds generated from video lottery terminal proceeds for operating loss assistance to support a certain minimum number of live racing days at the racecourse.
Title: Video Lottery Terminal Proceeds - Purse Dedication Account - Ocean Downs Race Course Operating Loss Assistance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Alters and makes permanent the annual distribution from the Purse Dedication Account to Ocean Downs Race Course for operating loss assistance, authorizing up to $30,000 per live racing day rather than a flat cap of $1.2 million, and eliminates the 2024 sunset date.
responsible_party: State Racing Commission
stakeholders: Ocean Downs Race Course, standardbred horse owners, trainers, and standardbred racing participants in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on total State or local revenues or expenditures, as overall Purse Dedication Account (PDA) funding remains unchanged. However, the bill reallocates PDA funds by increasing the annual grant to Ocean Downs Race Course to approximately $1.41 million (assuming 47 live racing days), which reduces standardbred purse funds by approximately $210,000 annually in calendar 2023 and 2024 and by $1.41 million annually thereafter.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Purse Dedication Account is established under the authority of the State Racing Commission, which is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department oversees horse racing operations, live racing day requirements, and the allocation of purse funds to racecourses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates commercial gaming and video lottery terminals (VLTs), the proceeds of which directly fund the Purse Dedication Account modified by this legislation.
The Comptroller accounts for and distributes state revenue proceeds, including gaming revenues allocated to special funds such as the Purse Dedication Account.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Pharmacy to adopt regulations necessary to ensure that individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled have appropriate access to prescription labels, bag tags, and medical guides; requiring the Board to give visually impaired individuals an opportunity to comment on the regulations; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to report by December 1, 2023, to the General Assembly on the implementation process for providing accessible labels for visually impaired persons.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Accessible Prescription Labels, Bag Tags, and Medical Guides for Blind, Visually Impaired, and Print Disabled Individuals - Regulations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Pharmacy to adopt regulations by January 1, 2025, ensuring individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or print disabled have free, timely access to fully accessible prescription labels, bag tags, and medical guides. It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit a report by December 1, 2023, regarding the process and costs of implementing enhanced dispensing fees for accessible labeling.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled, and licensed pharmacies and pharmacists in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly impacted; the State Board of Pharmacy and the Maryland Department of Health can adopt regulations and submit the required report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations/finances are unaffected. Pharmacies that are small businesses may face increased operational costs to provide accessible packaging and labels, depending on the adopted regulations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Pharmacy, which resides within the Maryland Department of Health, with developing and adopting regulations for accessible prescription labels, bag tags, and medical guides. Furthermore, the bill explicitly directs the Maryland Department of Health to submit a report to the General Assembly regarding the potential process and costs for implementing enhanced dispensing fees.

As the principal agency coordinating accessibility and services for Marylanders with disabilities, the bill's policy to ensure accessible medical labels and guides for blind, visually impaired, and print-disabled individuals directly aligns with the department's mandate.

Synopsis: Repealing the School Safety Grant Program and the Aging Schools Program as of June 30, 2026; altering provisions relating to school construction approvals by the State Superintendent of Schools; altering provisions related to a public-private partnership agreement in Prince George's County; establishing that the Interagency Commission on School Construction is an independent unit of State government; repealing the requirement for the Board of Public Works to approve grants awarded under a certain capital grant program; etc.
Title: Public School Construction - Programs, Approvals, and Administration - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) as an independent unit of State government, establishes removal procedures for its appointed members, and raises cost thresholds for school construction and remodeling plans requiring State Superintendent approval. It requires local school boards to conduct 50-year life-cycle cost evaluations of building and alternative energy systems during the design phase of major school construction projects. Additionally, it increases the annual distribution from the Education Trust Fund to support Prince George's County's public-private partnership (P3) school construction agreement from $25 million to $27 million beginning in fiscal year 2025, and repeals the Aging Schools Program and the School Safety Grant Program effective June 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction
stakeholders: Local school systems, Maryland public school students and educators, Prince George's County Public Schools, and school construction contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $123,300 in FY 2024 for IAC to hire a human resources administrator, growing to roughly $2.1 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028 due to a $2.0 million general fund backfill needed as Education Trust Fund dollars are redirected. Beginning in FY 2025, annual funding to Prince George's County's P3 fund increases by $2.0 million (from $25.0 million to $27.0 million). The repeal of the Aging Schools Program and School Safety Grant Program in FY 2027 shifts an estimated $16.1 million annually into the Nancy K. Kopp Public School Facilities Priority Fund, resulting in no net change to total State school construction funding. Local school systems can generally absorb the life-cycle energy assessment requirements within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) as an independent unit of State government, alters its administrative processes, amends reporting and life cycle cost analysis duties, repeals two programs it administered (the School Safety Grant Program and the Aging Schools Program), and tasks it with administering the Prince George's County Public-Private Partnership Fund.

The bill separates the IAC from functioning within MSDE, alters statutory approval thresholds and procedures for school construction and remodeling requiring the State Superintendent's approval, and tasks the department with coordinating on life cycle cost analysis standards.

The bill increases mandated transfers from the Supplemental Public School Construction Financing Fund managed by MSA to the Prince George's County P3 Fund from $25 million to $27 million annually, requires MSA to review the P3 agreement, and mandates annual joint reporting with the county and IAC.

The bill specifically requires the Department of General Services to coordinate with the IAC and the State Department of Education to develop life cycle cost analysis standards for school construction. Additionally, the Secretary of General Services serves as an ex officio member of the IAC.

The bill mandates the Comptroller to account for the Prince George's County Public-Private Partnership Fund and increases the required scheduled deposits by the Comptroller from the Education Trust Fund into the Supplemental Public School Construction Financing Fund.

The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold and invest the moneys in the newly altered Prince George's County Public-Private Partnership Fund, as well as invest the Supplemental Public School Construction Financing Fund.

The bill repeals the requirement that the Board of Public Works approve grants awarded by the IAC under the Capital Grant Program for Local School Systems With Significant Enrollment Growth or Relocatable Classrooms.

The bill provides the Governor with removal authority over gubernatorial appointees to the IAC, authorizes the Governor to process a specific $25 million budget amendment, and mandates that certain reports on school construction progress be submitted to the Governor.
The Secretary of Planning serves as a designated statutory member on the newly independent Interagency Commission on School Construction.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Architects in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2028, the termination provisions relating to certain statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Architects - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Architects within the Maryland Department of Labor under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act, continuing the board's licensing, regulatory, and disciplinary authority through July 1, 2028.
responsible_party: State Board of Architects, Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Licensed architects, architectural firms and businesses, applicants seeking architectural licensure, and consumers of architectural services in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Architects are maintained through FY 2028. There is no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Architects is an occupational licensing board administratively housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. This bill extends the statutory authority, operations, and associated special fund revenues and expenditures of the board through July 1, 2028.

Synopsis: Authorizing an individual under the age of 16 years to use a collapsible trap, net ring, handline, or dip net when catching or attempting to catch crabs in the waters of the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries without a recreational crabbing license.
Title: Natural Resources - Recreational Crabbing Gear - Individuals Under the Age of 16 Years

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes individuals under the age of 16 to use specific recreational crabbing gear—including collapsible traps, net rings, handlines, or dip nets—without a recreational crabbing license when crabbing in the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries, pursuant to Department of Natural Resources regulations.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Individuals under 16 years of age engaging in recreational crabbing in the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances; any potential decrease in crabbing license fee revenue is expected to be negligible. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is directly responsible for regulating fisheries and recreational crabbing in the Chesapeake Bay and its tidal tributaries, including defining authorized gear and enforcing licensing requirements.
