Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to allow a person in Worcester County to hunt game birds and game mammals on a Sunday, subject to certain time restrictions, during the open season for that game bird or game mammal; authorizing the Department to allow a person in Worcester County to hunt on public land designated for hunting on Sundays, subject to certain time restrictions; and altering the safety zone from 150 to 50 yards from certain buildings occupied by human beings within which archery hunting may not take place.
Title: Worcester County - Natural Resources - Hunting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to permit Sunday hunting for game birds and game mammals on private property and designated public land in Worcester County during open season, subject to specified time restrictions, and decreases the archery hunting safety zone around occupied buildings in Worcester County from 150 yards to 50 yards.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters, private landowners, residents, and businesses (including agricultural farms, outfitters, lodging, and vehicle repair shops) in Worcester County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. Potential economic impact on small businesses is minimal overall, though potentially meaningful for local businesses in Worcester County through hunting-related expenditures, reduced crop damage, or fewer deer-vehicle collisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article to grant the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) the authority to allow Sunday hunting of game birds and game mammals on private property and designated public lands in Worcester County, subject to specific time restrictions, and adjusts archery hunting safety zone provisions enforced by the department.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the setting on fire or burning of oriented strand board for certain fire-fighting training; and establishing an administrative penalty not exceeding $500 for a first violation of the Act and a civil penalty not exceeding $1,000 for a second or subsequent violation of the Act.
Title: Environment - Fire-Fighting Training - Oriented Strand Board - Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits the setting on fire or burning of oriented strand board for fire-fighting training purposes, establishing administrative and civil penalties for violations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Firefighters, fire departments, emergency personnel, fire-fighting training entities, and manufacturers or suppliers of oriented strand board and alternative materials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $57,100 in FY 2024, $54,800 in FY 2025, and $55,000 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire a contractual compliance specialist for outreach, complaint investigations, and enforcement through FY 2026. Local expenditures may increase to purchase alternative materials and dispose of existing stock (e.g., Prince George's County estimates $15,000 annually). State and local revenues are not materially affected by penalty provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Environment Article prohibiting the burning of oriented strand board for fire-fighting training. MDE serves as the primary regulatory and enforcement agency, incurring administrative expenditures to hire compliance personnel for outreach and enforcement.

The Maryland State Police, which includes the Office of the State Fire Marshal regulating open burning for fire-fighter instruction, is impacted by regulations governing fire-fighting training practices and materials in the state.
MAA operates state airports (such as BWI Marshall) with dedicated aircraft rescue and fire-fighting personnel subject to fire-fighting training standards and prohibitions on specific burn materials.
DNR oversees the Maryland Forest Service, which engages in wildland fire suppression and fire-fighting training subject to state open-burning and training material restrictions.
MDOT oversees modal units such as the Maryland Aviation Administration that conduct fire and emergency training operations that must comply with the training burn restrictions.

Synopsis: Altering the period of time that an area may be designated as a Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) zone from 5 to 10 years; increasing the number of RISE zones that the Secretary of Commerce may approve in Baltimore City to not more than four; extending the termination date of the RISE Program to January 1, 2030; and authorizing a political subdivision to pledge certain revenues to secure the payment of obligations to the Maryland Economic Development Corporation for infrastructure improvements located in a RISE zone.
Title: Economic Development – Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise Zone Program – Alterations and Financing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date of the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone Program from January 1, 2028, to January 1, 2030, and increases the initial duration of a RISE zone designation from 5 years to 10 years. It also increases the maximum number of RISE zones that the Secretary of Commerce may approve in Baltimore City from three to four, authorizes local governments to pledge certain revenues to secure Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) obligations for infrastructure improvements in RISE zones, and directs the Department of Commerce to study the program's effectiveness by December 15, 2024.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Start-up and technology businesses located or locating in RISE zones, qualified higher education and research institutions, investors eligible for enhanced investment incentive tax credits, MEDCO, and local governments (particularly Baltimore City, Montgomery, Prince George's, and Wicomico counties).
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected through FY 2028, though Commerce general fund expenditures for rental assistance matching funds may increase minimally beginning in FY 2024 and continue through FY 2030 due to the two-year program extension. Commerce can perform the required study using existing resources. MEDCO nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2024 if local governments pledge revenues for MEDCO obligations. Locally, revenues may decrease starting in FY 2025 due to legacy property tax credits continuing for years 6 through 10 in jurisdictions with existing RISE zones. Local expenditures and matching revenues may increase starting in FY 2024 if local entities establish rental assistance programs or issue MEDCO-backed infrastructure debt.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce administers the Regional Institution Strategic Enterprise (RISE) Zone Program. The bill extends the program's termination date, expands the Secretary of Commerce's authority to approve RISE zones, and mandates that Commerce conduct an effectiveness study and report recommendations to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly expands the definition of 'MEDCO obligation' to include bonds, notes, or instruments issued to finance infrastructure improvements in or supporting a RISE zone, and authorizes political subdivisions to pledge special fund tax revenues to secure these MEDCO obligations.

The Comptroller administers state tax compliance and tax credits associated with the RISE Zone Program, including biotechnology and innovation investment incentive tax credits extended under the bill.

RISE zones are established in proximity to qualified institutions of higher education, including USM member institutions, which can co-apply for zone status, participate in rental assistance grant partnerships, and must be consulted by the Department of Commerce in the required program study.

Synopsis: Requiring, on or before August 1, 2024, certain public senior higher education institutions, in consultation with students, to develop and implement a reproductive health services plan to provide at the institution or to refer students to a comprehensive range of reproductive health services; requiring the University of Baltimore, in lieu of developing and implementing a reproductive health services plan, to provide students with access to over-the-counter contraception through certain on-campus means; etc.
Title: Public Senior Higher Education Institutions - Reproductive Health Services Plans - Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: Requires Maryland public senior higher education institutions, in consultation with students, to develop, implement, and annually update a reproductive health services plan by August 1, 2024, to provide or refer students to comprehensive reproductive health services. The University of Baltimore is permitted to instead provide students with access to over-the-counter contraception via retail establishments or vending machines on campus, and the Maryland Department of Health must provide assistance in developing plans upon request.
responsible_party: Public senior higher education institutions (University System of Maryland, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland) and the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Students attending Maryland public senior higher education institutions and university health/administrative staff
fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures increase for some institutions, particularly in FY 2024 for one-time set-up costs (such as purchasing contraceptive vending machines), though many institutions can implement the plan using existing budgeted resources. Higher education revenues may increase minimally if institutions charge student fees to offset costs. The Maryland Department of Health can likely assist institutions using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland are directly required to develop, implement, and annually update reproductive health services plans, or in the case of the University of Baltimore, provide 24-hour access to over-the-counter contraception.

Morgan State University is directly required as a public senior higher education institution to develop, implement, and annually update a reproductive health services plan in consultation with students.

Saint Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly mandated to develop, implement, and annually update a reproductive health services plan providing comprehensive reproductive health services or referrals.

The Maryland Department of Health is statutorily required, upon request, to provide technical assistance and guidance to public senior higher education institutions developing their reproductive health services plans.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Veterans Affairs to bury the eligible spouse or dependent of a veteran in a State veterans' cemetery without charge.
Title: Department of Veterans Affairs - Burial in State Veterans' Cemeteries - Spouses and Dependents

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs to bury an eligible spouse or eligible dependent of a veteran in a State veterans' cemetery without charge, including providing a grave liner at no cost.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
stakeholders: Veterans and their eligible spouses, children, and parents, as well as the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs.
fiscal_impact_summary: MDVA special fund revenues decrease by an estimated $1.24 million annually starting in FY 2024 due to the elimination of the $893 interment and liner fees previously charged for spouses and dependents (based on 1,388 interments in FY 2022). State general fund expenditures will increase correspondingly by roughly $1.24 million per year to backfill lost fee revenues and maintain the Cemetery Program. No material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the department provide burial plots, interments, and grave liners without charge to eligible spouses and dependents of veterans in State veterans' cemeteries. This has a significant operational and fiscal impact on the department's Cemetery Program, resulting in an estimated annual loss of approximately $1.24 million in special fund fee revenues that will require general fund replacement.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain previous convictions for drunk or drugged operation of a vehicle or vessel and grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel under certain provisions of law constitute prior convictions for the purpose of determining certain enhanced subsequent offender penalties.
Title: Grossly Negligent or Drunk or Drugged Operation of Vehicle or Vessel - Prior Convictions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes that convictions for drunk or drugged operation of a vessel count as prior convictions when determining enhanced penalties for subsequent motor vehicle DUI/DWI offenses, and vice versa. It also applies enhanced subsequent offender penalties for motor vehicle drunk or drugged driving offenses to individuals with a prior conviction for grossly negligent manslaughter by vehicle or vessel.
responsible_party: Judiciary (District Court and Circuit Courts), State's Attorneys, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals operating motor vehicles or vessels while under the influence of or impaired by alcohol, drugs, or controlled dangerous substances, particularly repeat offenders.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally from higher fines collected in District Court, while State general fund expenditures may increase minimally due to longer terms of incarceration and shifts of individuals to State correctional facilities. Local revenues may increase minimally from higher fines in circuit court cases, and local incarceration expenditures may decrease minimally as inmates are shifted from local detention centers to State facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Judiciary and state courts are responsible for adjudicating drunk and drugged driving and boating offenses, determining subsequent offender status, and imposing the enhanced criminal penalties and fines specified in the bill.
DNR administers the State Boat Act under the Natural Resources Article and enforces boating safety regulations, including operating a vessel while under the influence or impaired.
MDOT oversees the state's transportation laws, including Section 21-902 of the Transportation Article governing driving under the influence or while impaired.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees state correctional facilities and may experience an increase in inmate population or longer lengths of stay as repeat offenders receive enhanced incarceration sentences.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings who face more severe penalties and longer prison terms under the expanded subsequent offender provisions.
MVA maintains driving records and manages licensing sanctions related to convictions for driving under the influence and impaired driving under the Maryland Transportation Article.
MSP is the primary statewide law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing impaired driving laws on Maryland highways.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation to collect information from each local board of education on nonpublic school student busing programs other than for the transportation of students in special education; and requiring the Task Force to report by December 15, 2023, to certain committees of the General Assembly any recommendations as to how the State may support a reduction in the use of passenger vehicles for nonpublic school students and policies for certain busing programs.
Title: Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Primary Schools -see also- Education; Private or Public Sch.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation to examine existing nonpublic student busing programs, evaluate policies from other states to reduce passenger vehicle usage, and explore options such as tax credits or using public school buses. The Task Force must submit its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 15, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)
stakeholders: Nonpublic school students and their families, nonpublic school administrators, local public school systems, and school bus drivers and contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: Staffing costs for the Maryland State Department of Education and expense reimbursements for Task Force members can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected, and local school systems can provide required information using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the lead agency responsible for staffing the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation, with the Director of the Office of Pupil Transportation and Emergency Management serving as chair and designating multiple members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a temporary study body, the Task Force to Study Nonpublic Student Bus Transportation, tasked with analyzing nonpublic school busing models and reporting recommendations to the General Assembly.
The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force, which will evaluate traffic congestion and student transportation strategies.
The Task Force is required to consult with the Comptroller when evaluating the potential adoption and fiscal impact of a State income tax credit for student bus transportation expenses.

Synopsis: Altering the number of years that a school vehicle may be operated in Anne Arundel County from 12 years to 15 years.
Title: Anne Arundel County - School Vehicles - Duration of Operation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Increases the maximum allowable operational lifespan of school vehicles in Anne Arundel County from 12 years to 15 years, provided the vehicles meet required safety and maintenance standards.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Anne Arundel County Public Schools, school bus operators and contractors, and public school students in Anne Arundel County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, nor does it materially affect Anne Arundel County Public School System finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the operational lifespan of school vehicles in Anne Arundel County, which directly impacts local school transportation oversight and eliminates the need for the local school system to submit annual waiver requests to the State Superintendent.

Under the statute governing extended school vehicle lifespans, the MVA is responsible for approving preventive maintenance plans, certifying repair experts, and conducting required vehicle safety inspections.
The Automotive Safety Enforcement Division of the Maryland State Police is statutorily tasked with approving preventive maintenance plans for school vehicles operating beyond 12 years.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), which oversees vehicle standards, maintenance plans, and inspections for school buses operating up to 15 years.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Department of Education from increasing the copayment levels, reducing the reimbursement rates, reducing the income eligibility requirements, or implementing an enrollment freeze for the Child Care Scholarship Program in effect as of January 1, 2023, unless certain conditions are met.
Title: Early Childhood Development - Child Care Scholarship Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Maryland State Department of Education from increasing copayment levels, reducing reimbursement rates, reducing income eligibility requirements, or implementing an enrollment freeze for the Child Care Scholarship Program in effect as of January 1, 2023, unless it notifies specified General Assembly committees and waits until the completion of the following legislative session, or unless the Board of Public Works approves budget reductions for the program.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Low-income families participating in or eligible for the Child Care Scholarship Program, children receiving care, and participating child care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not impacted in FY 2024, but future-year fiscal impacts are indeterminate. The bill restricts MSDE's administrative flexibility to curb program costs through freezes, rate reductions, or copay increases without legislative delay or Board of Public Works budget cuts, potentially having a significant effect on general fund spending in future years. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) administers the Child Care Scholarship Program and is directly restricted by the bill from increasing copayment levels, reducing reimbursement rates, lowering income eligibility, or freezing enrollment without meeting specific legislative notification and waiting requirements or receiving Board of Public Works budget reduction approval.

The bill explicitly provides an exception allowing MSDE to alter Child Care Scholarship Program copayments, reimbursement rates, eligibility, or enrollment at any time if the Board of Public Works approves budget reductions for the program pursuant to statutory authority.

As the State's principal fiscal agency, DBM monitors state agency budget execution and expenditures. The bill restricts administrative flexibility to manage and contain program costs, potentially creating significant future general fund expenditure pressures.

Synopsis: Repealing the provisions of law establishing and governing the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot; and requiring the Governor to provide an appropriation in the State budget for fiscal year 2024 and each fiscal year thereafter to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.
Title: Rural Health Collaborative Pilot Repeal and Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Repeals the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot and requires the Governor to provide an ongoing annual appropriation in the State budget starting in fiscal year 2024 to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Residents, healthcare providers, and local health departments in the mid-shore region of Maryland (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne’s, and Talbot counties), as well as the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures of $150,000 annually are maintained beyond FY 2023 but shift from funding the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot to supporting the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition. State revenues are unaffected. Local revenues and expenditures also maintain the $150,000 shift from the Kent County Health Department for the collaborative to the regional coalition.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Rural Health Collaborative Pilot, which was established as an independent unit within the Maryland Department of Health, and directs annual state funding instead to the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition for regional public health operations.

The bill establishes a mandated annual state budget appropriation starting in FY 2024 to fund the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition, directly affecting DBM's budget development and execution responsibilities.
The bill imposes a statutory mandate on the Governor to provide an annual appropriation in the State budget for the operations of the Mid Shore Health Improvement Coalition.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Public Works, for meetings held on or after October 1, 2024, to allow members of the public to submit certain public comments electronically except under certain circumstances; requiring public comments to be included in certain meeting materials and posted and retained online; and requiring an additional staff position at the Board to carry out requirements of the Act.
Title: Board of Public Works Public Comment Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: Requires the Board of Public Works (BPW) to allow the public to electronically submit comments on agenda items for meetings held on or after October 1, 2024. Submitted comments must be included in meeting packets, posted online at least 24 hours prior to the meeting, and retained online. The bill also requires BPW to hire at least one additional staff member beyond its fiscal 2023 authorized level to manage the public comment process.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works
stakeholders: Members of the public who comment on or follow Board of Public Works agenda items, as well as BPW members and staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $227,400 in FY 2024 to hire one computer operator manager and cover one-time IT portal development costs ($150,000). Ongoing general fund expenditures for personnel and operating costs are estimated at $92,200 in FY 2025, increasing to $105,900 by FY 2028. State revenues and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the State Finance and Procurement Article governing the Board of Public Works (BPW). It mandates that BPW allow electronic submission of public comments on agenda items, include those comments in meeting packets, post and retain them online, and employ at least one additional staff position, resulting in direct fiscal and operational impacts on BPW.

The fiscal note notes that DoIT provides IT services to the Board of Public Works on a fee-for-service basis and will likely administer the new web portal required to receive, post, and store public comments.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Human Services to restore to a beneficiary any benefits lost due to theft; authorizing certain households to request a hearing within 90 days after a certain determination; requiring the State to give preference to certain vendors in the procurement process for electronic benefits distribution or administration; authorizing the Department to restore certain benefits; requiring the Department to take certain actions to reduce the vulnerability of Electronic Benefits Transfer cards to theft; etc.
Title: Department of Human Services - Electronic Benefits Transfer Cards - Theft of Benefits (Prevent Electronic Benefits Theft Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: The Prevent Electronic Benefits Theft Act of 2023 requires the Department of Human Services to restore or reimburse benefits lost by households due to theft, such as skimming or electronic benefits transfer (EBT) card fraud. It establishes procedures and timelines for reimbursement and administrative appeals, sets procurement preferences for vendors with identity fraud insurance and safeguards, mandates enhanced card security measures (including microchips), and requires annual reporting on EBT theft to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Recipients of public assistance programs utilizing EBT cards (such as SNAP, Temporary Cash Assistance, Temporary Disability Assistance, and Public Assistance to Adults) who are victims of benefit theft.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures (general and federal funds) increase by up to $1.9 million in FY 2023, $6.2 million in FY 2024, and $4.2 million annually thereafter to reimburse stolen benefits. Federal fund revenues increase correspondingly by $1.13 million in FY 2023, $4.40 million in FY 2024, and $817,200 in FY 2025, after which federal reimbursement funding ceases and costs shift to general funds. The FY 2024 State budget includes $11.4 million across FY 2023 and FY 2024 for EBT fraud victim reimbursements. Local law enforcement agencies can assist with reporting using existing resources, resulting in minimal local impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS is the primary implementing agency responsible for restoring stolen Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) benefits to eligible households, coordinating enhanced security measures with vendors, conducting investigations and hearings, and submitting an annual report on EBT card security and theft.

As the state's central procurement agency, DGS is impacted by the bill's procurement preference mandate for EBT distribution and administration vendors, requiring DGS to establish procurement guidelines, solicitation templates, and training.

Synopsis: Establishing the Greenspace Equity Program in the Department of Natural Resources to provide grants to eligible applicants for enhancing the public health and livability of overburdened and underserved communities by implementing projects to preserve, create, and enhance community greenspace; requiring the Department to submit certain grant applications to the Maryland State Clearinghouse for Intergovernmental Assistance; requiring certain grant applications to be subject to approval by the Board of Public Works; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Greenspace Equity Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Housing and Community Development, Department of
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Greenspace Equity Program within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) alongside the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board. The program provides grants to eligible local governments and land trusts to preserve, create, and enhance community greenspaces—such as parks, trails, community gardens, and urban farms—in or adjacent to overburdened and underserved communities.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Residents of overburdened and underserved communities, local governments (counties and municipalities), land trusts and environmental nongovernmental organizations, and small businesses providing land acquisition and development services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,000 in FY 2024, $365,700 in FY 2025, $361,200 in FY 2026, $479,200 in FY 2027, and $497,600 in FY 2028 for DNR personnel and program administration. Special fund grant allocations are redirected from Program Open Space (up to $5.0 million in FY 2025, $7.0 million in FY 2026, and $10.0 million in FY 2027 and each year thereafter), producing no net impact on special fund expenditures or State revenues. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2025 from grants awarded for local greenspace projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and requires the Department of Natural Resources to administer the Greenspace Equity Program and staff the new Greenspace Equity Advisory Board, redirecting Program Open Space funds to provide grants to enhance community greenspaces.
The bill specifies that all grant applications recommended for an award under the Greenspace Equity Program are subject to approval by the Board of Public Works.

The bill requires grant applications recommended for award to be submitted to the Maryland State Clearinghouse for Intergovernmental Assistance (located within MDP) for review and comment, and requires the Secretary of Planning's prior written approval for any conversion of acquired parkland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board to serve as a consultant to the Department of Natural Resources in the implementation and administration of the Program.
The Secretary of Budget and Management must provide prior written approval before any land acquired under a program grant can be converted from outdoor public recreation or open space use.
The Governor is responsible for appointing nine members to the newly established Greenspace Equity Advisory Board and designating its chair.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing the appointment of nine members to the Greenspace Equity Advisory Board.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council as an independent unit of State government with the authority to conduct and support advocacy, systems change, and capacity-building efforts to promote inclusive communities and equity in services for individuals with disabilities in the State, research best practices and provide related training and technical assistance to communities in the State, and inform State and local leaders about disability issues.
Title: Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council - Establishment

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill codifies the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council as an independent unit of State government operating in accordance with the federal Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act of 2000. The bill specifies the Council's duties—including developing a 5-year strategic plan, advocating for individuals with developmental disabilities, and advising state leadership—as well as rules regarding its membership and staff.
responsible_party: Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council
stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities and their families or guardians, disability service providers, and advocacy organizations across Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill codifies an existing council that is fully federally funded under the federal Developmental Disabilities Assistance and Bill of Rights Act of 2000. State revenues are unaffected, and any impact on participating state agencies (such as the Maryland Department of Aging) is minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council, and the Council's advocacy and policy mission aligns directly with the department's work.

The bill codifies the Council under the Health - General Article and mandates membership representation from multiple Department of Health units, including the Developmental Disabilities Administration, the Prevention and Health Promotion Administration, and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid).
The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is established as a statutory member of the Council, adding a new formal representation requirement noted in the fiscal analysis.
The State Superintendent of Schools and the Assistant State Superintendent of the Division of Rehabilitation Services (or their designees) are statutory members of the Council.

The Governor is responsible for appointing the members of the Council, and the Council is tasked with advising the Governor on policies and programs affecting individuals with developmental disabilities.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state boards and councils, including the members of the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Council.

Synopsis: Establishing that an elevator installed in a privately owned single-family residential dwelling on or after October 1, 2023, is subject to certain inspection and registration requirements; prohibiting the Commissioner of Labor and Industry from disclosing to the public any information regarding a registered elevator unit installed in a privately owned single-family residential dwelling; and requiring the Commissioner to delete certain registration information on the completion of the final acceptance inspection on a certain unit.
Title: Elevator Safety - Privately Owned Single-Family Residential Elevators - Inspection and Registration Requirements
bill_summary: Requires elevators installed in privately owned single-family residential dwellings on or after October 1, 2023, to be registered with the Commissioner of Labor and Industry and undergo a final acceptance inspection before being placed in service. It prohibits public disclosure of registration information, requires the deletion of registration records once the final acceptance inspection is complete, and exempts these residential elevators from periodic reregistration requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry)
stakeholders: Owners and lessees of single-family residential homes installing elevators or lifts, elevator manufacturers, elevator mechanics and contractors, and state elevator inspectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $171,928 in FY 2024 to hire two elevator inspectors, increasing to $235,500 by FY 2028. Special fund revenues to the Elevator Safety Review Board Fund increase by $109,700 in FY 2024 and approximately $146,300 annually thereafter from inspection fees charged at $62.50 per hour. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor (specifically the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the department) is the primary regulatory body responsible for administering the elevator registration process, conducting final acceptance inspections, and managing inspection data and fee collections.

The Elevator Safety Inspection Unit within the Department of Labor is funded through an appropriation from the Workers' Compensation Commission, potentially impacting commission assessments or fund allocations to support additional inspector personnel.

Synopsis: Requiring a county or municipal corporation to define, by law, who is a law enforcement officer or rescue worker; altering eligibility for the tax credit to include certain disabled law enforcement officers or rescue workers who were domiciled in the State as, or any time within the 5 years before the officer or worker died or was determined to be disabled; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.
Title: Property Tax Credit - Disabled Law Enforcement Officers and Rescue Workers - Definition and Eligibility

Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: Requires counties and municipal corporations to define by law who qualifies as a law enforcement officer or rescue worker for a local property tax credit, and expands eligibility for the credit to include qualifying disabled officers, rescue workers, surviving spouses, or cohabitants who were domiciled in Maryland at any time within five years prior to the officer or worker becoming disabled or dying.
responsible_party: County and municipal governments (including the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City)
stakeholders: Disabled law enforcement officers, rescue workers, surviving spouses, cohabitants, and local governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2024 to the extent the credit is authorized and additional taxpayers qualify; the exact revenue reduction cannot be reliably estimated as it depends on local adoption, eligible claimants, and property values. Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding disputes over property tax assessments, exemptions, and various property tax credits. Expanding eligibility criteria and definitions for the local property tax credit for disabled law enforcement officers and rescue workers may affect potential tax credit disputes brought before the board.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, hearing appeals from final decisions of local taxing authorities and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding property tax assessments and credits.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to publish municipal election results on its website immediately after a municipality submits its election results; and requiring, within 30 days after the results of a municipal election are certified, the municipality to submit to the State Board an electronic copy of the election results for each office or question voted on at the election.
Title: State Board of Elections - Municipal Elections - Publication of Results on Website

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Requires municipalities to submit an electronic copy of their certified election results to the State Board of Elections within 30 days after certification, and requires the State Board of Elections to establish a portal and publish these municipal election results organized by election year and municipality name on its website.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, municipal election officials, candidates in municipal elections, and the voting public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Board of Elections to receive municipal election results from municipalities and publish them on the Board's website organized by election year and municipality name.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to enforce certain prevailing wage requirements for contractors and subcontractors working on projects involving and traffic control activities related to underground gas or electric infrastructure of an investor-owned gas company, electric company, or gas and electric company; requiring certain contractors and subcontractors to request from the Department a copy of a certain wage determination and ensure that employees are paid in compliance with existing prevailing wage rates; etc.
Title: Investor-Owned Utilities - Prevailing Wage - Enforcement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to enforce prevailing wage requirements for contractors and subcontractors working on underground gas or electric infrastructure projects, as well as related traffic control activities, for investor-owned utilities. It directs the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to determine prevailing wage rates, establishes administrative procedures and deadlines for contractors to request wage determinations, and provides for the waiver of civil penalties if contractors come into compliance by March 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Investor-owned gas and electric utility companies, contractors and subcontractors performing underground utility work and related traffic control, and their employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Maryland Department of Labor can implement and enforce the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources, primarily through the Division of Labor and Industry's Employment Standards Service. State revenues are not materially affected, assuming general compliance. Local Effect: No direct effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry with enforcing prevailing wage requirements for investor-owned utility underground projects, providing wage determinations and guidance, conducting hand surveys if necessary, and managing penalty waivers.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article governing investor-owned gas and electric utilities regulated by the Public Service Commission, clarifying that prevailing wage enforcement for their underground infrastructure projects falls under the Department of Labor rather than the Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the date from February 1, 2020 and each February 1 thereafter, to July 1 each year, on which the Department of Agriculture must submit to the General Assembly a certain annual report regarding the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry to the General Assembly.
Title: Agriculture - Use of Antimicrobial Drugs - Reporting Deadlines

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Controlled Dangerous Sub; Substance Abuse
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill changes the annual deadline from February 1 to July 1 for the Maryland Department of Agriculture to submit its report to the General Assembly on the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Licensed veterinarians, livestock and poultry producers/owners (cattle, swine, and poultry), and the Maryland General Assembly
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill's modification of the reporting date is procedural in nature and does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 516 directly impacts the Maryland Department of Agriculture by altering the annual deadline—from February 1 to July 1—by which the Department must compile and submit its report to the General Assembly regarding the use of medically important antimicrobial drugs in cattle, swine, and poultry.

Synopsis: Establishing an art establishment beer and wine license in the City of Annapolis; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to sell or serve beer and wine for on-premises consumption to a nonprofit organization primarily engaged in certain arts-related activities; and providing for a license fee of $1,000.
Title: City of Annapolis - Alcoholic Beverages - Art Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Establishes an art establishment beer and wine license in the City of Annapolis, permitting the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to qualified nonprofit arts organizations for on-premises retail sale or service of beer and wine with an annual license fee of $1,000.
responsible_party: City of Annapolis Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Nonprofit art organizations, live performance venues, art instructors, artists, event attendees, and the City of Annapolis.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are unaffected. City of Annapolis revenues decrease to the extent that qualifying organizations purchase the annual $1,000 art establishment license rather than multiple single-use event licenses (in 2022, the city collected $9,950 in fees from 138 applicants for event licenses who could potentially qualify). City expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees and regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry. Although this bill creates a local retail license administered by the City of Annapolis Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it pertains to the state's alcoholic beverage framework.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland Stadium Authority; establishing the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund and the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund to enable the Maryland Stadium Authority to take certain actions; requiring the Authority to administer the funds; altering the amount the Comptroller is required to distribute from the State Lottery Fund to certain funds; establishing the Bus Rapid Transit Fund to provide grants to eligible grantees; etc.
Title: Maryland Stadium Authority - Camden Yards Sports Facilities Funds and Bus Rapid Transit Fund

Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: This bill establishes two supplemental financing funds within the Maryland Stadium Authority—the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund and the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund—to allocate lottery proceeds for debt service and costs associated with Camden Yards stadiums. It also creates the Bus Rapid Transit Fund within the Maryland Department of Transportation, alters how lottery revenues trigger bus rapid transit grants, provides a minimum $20 million annual allocation for Montgomery County under certain conditions, expands the Stadium Authority membership from 9 to 11 members, and adjusts the definition of the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor facility.
responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority and the Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Maryland transit commuters, local governments operating bus rapid transit systems (particularly Montgomery County), Prince George's County, and sports organizations and patrons using Camden Yards facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by $14.2 million in FY 2024, while Maryland Department of Transportation special fund revenues and expenditures decrease correspondingly by $14.2 million because existing debt service payments to the Maryland Stadium Facilities Fund no longer trigger bus rapid transit lottery distributions for FY 2024. Overall Maryland Stadium Authority funding remains unchanged, but lottery revenues are reallocated from a special fund to two nonbudgeted supplemental funds. Locally, Montgomery County transit grant revenues and expenditures decrease by $14.2 million in FY 2024; beginning in FY 2025, Montgomery County is set to receive at least $20.0 million annually if eligible, which may reallocate grant funding among other local jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 524 directly alters the membership and quorum requirements of the Maryland Stadium Authority (MSA) and establishes two supplemental financing funds (the Camden Yards Football and Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Funds) to be administered by MSA for debt service and facility-related expenses.

The bill creates the Bus Rapid Transit Fund within MDOT, requires MDOT to administer the fund and distribute grants to eligible local grantees, and alters qualifying triggers and grant distribution formulas, with a direct fiscal impact on MDOT special fund revenues and expenditures.

The Comptroller is mandated to distribute specified revenues from the State Lottery Fund to the newly established stadium supplemental financing funds and the Bus Rapid Transit Fund, as well as account for each of these funds.

The State Treasurer is required to separately hold and invest the moneys of the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund, the Camden Yards Baseball Sports Facility Supplemental Financing Fund, and the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies statutory allocation amounts and requirements for proceeds distributed from the State Lottery Fund, which is regulated and administered by the agency.
The bill expands the membership of the Maryland Stadium Authority and grants the Governor the authority to appoint an additional member with Senate advice and consent.
The office is responsible for vetting, recruiting, and processing the additional gubernatorial appointee to the Maryland Stadium Authority board.

Synopsis: Establishing the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program in the State Department of Education to license outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs to expand access to affordable, high-quality early learning and child care programs and investigate the benefits of outdoor, nature-based classrooms; requiring the Department to submit a final report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2027, with recommendations for modifying or expanding the Program; etc.
Title: Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds
