bill_summary: Establishes the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program within the Maryland State Department of Education to license and regulate outdoor, nature-based early learning and child care programs for four school years, expand access to early childhood education, and evaluate the benefits of nature-based classrooms.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Outdoor and nature-based child care providers, early childhood educators, preschool children, and Maryland families seeking child care
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and the Maryland State Department of Education can implement the pilot program using existing resources. There is no local government fiscal impact. Participating small business child care programs may experience a meaningful operational and economic benefit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary administering agency for the Outdoor Preschool License Pilot Program, responsible for promulgating regulations, selecting program participants, convening an advisory group, adapting Maryland EXCELS standards, and submitting required interim and final reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the creation and convening of an advisory group composed of outdoor and nature-based early learning practitioners and stakeholders to inform and support the implementation of the pilot program.
The bill specifies that priority for selection into the pilot program be given to existing outdoor programs that are currently licensed as camps by the Maryland Department of Health.
The bill requires MSDE to submit interim progress reports in 2025 and 2026, as well as a final report with program recommendations in 2027, to the Governor.

Synopsis: Transferring all the functions, powers, and duties of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County and certain personnel to the Child Support Administration of the Department of Human Services.
Title: St. Mary's County - Transfer of Child Support Unit and Personnel to the Child Support Administration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Transfers all functions, duties, and personnel of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County to the Child Support Administration within the Department of Human Services, providing for the integration of transferred staff into the State Personnel Management System with equivalent pay, seniority, and leave benefits.
responsible_party: Child Support Administration of the Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Employees of the St. Mary's County State's Attorney's Child Support Unit, St. Mary's County government, and parents and children receiving child support enforcement services in St. Mary's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Human Services increase by $236,300 in FY 2024 (annualizing to $289,300 by FY 2028), while federal fund revenues and expenditures both increase by $38,400 in FY 2024. State general fund revenues decrease by $24,200 in FY 2024 and $32,300 annually thereafter due to the cessation of county administrative fees. St. Mary's County expenditures decrease by an estimated $249,200 in FY 2024 and at least $332,300 annually thereafter, partially offset in FY 2024 by employee termination compensation and pension liability transfers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the functions, duties, and personnel of the Child Support Unit of the Office of the State's Attorney for St. Mary's County to the Child Support Administration within the Department of Human Services.
The bill mandates that the Department of Budget and Management establish and allocate new State Position Identification Numbers (PINs) to DHS for the transferred employees.

The bill provides for the Office of the Attorney General to appoint Assistant State's Attorneys providing child support services to continue as State employees providing services for the Child Support Administration.

The bill requires pension contributions for transferred employees to be shifted from the municipal pool to the State pool and mandates an actuarial valuation performed by an actuary designated by the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System.

Synopsis: Making certain members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System eligible to receive creditable service at retirement for unused sick leave accrued by the member in the State Employees' Retirement System or State Employees' Pension System; and requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to transfer certain individuals' Employees' Retirement System or Employees' Pension System service to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System on June 30, 2024.
Title: Correctional Officers’ Retirement System – Transfer of Membership – Modifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: This bill requires the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to transfer service credit from the Employees' Retirement System or Employees' Pension System to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain previously transferred state employees, unless the member elects to opt out by June 1, 2024. Additionally, it allows specified Department of Juvenile Services employees transferred to the Correctional Officers' Retirement System in 2022 to receive creditable service at retirement for accrued unused sick leave.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System / State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System who previously transferred from the Employees' Retirement System or Employees' Pension System, including certain Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and Department of Juvenile Services personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities and employer contributions across all funds will increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 due to the transfer of service credit and the inclusion of unused sick leave credit; however, a precise dollar estimate is not feasible. The bill has no effect on state revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System and is directly responsible for implementing the bill, including processing the mandatory service credit transfers, providing opt-out election forms, and calculating creditable service for unused sick leave.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill affects retirement benefits and service credit transfers for multiple cohorts of DPSCS personnel who were previously transferred into the Correctional Officers' Retirement System, including case management specialists, parole and probation agents, counselors, psychologists, and maintenance officers.

The bill directly impacts DJS personnel whose membership was transferred into the Correctional Officers' Retirement System, specifically altering rules regarding unused sick leave calculations and service credit transfers for community detention officers, resident advisors, transportation officers, and case management staff.

As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and monitors fiscal impacts on state pension contributions and liabilities resulting from the transfer of service credit to CORS.

Synopsis: Altering the distribution of certain funds from local impact grants to Baltimore City; and altering the appointment process for certain members of the Pimlico Community Development Authority.
Title: Gaming - Video Lottery Terminals - Local Impact Grants and Pimlico Community Development Authority Membership - Baltimore City

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles

bill_summary: Alters the allocation of video lottery terminal local impact grants in Baltimore City for fiscal years 2024 through 2032 by increasing the portion dedicated to capital projects consistent with the Park Heights Master Plan from 75% to 85%, while reducing the allocation for other surrounding neighborhoods. It also modifies the appointment process for certain members of the Pimlico Community Development Authority appointed by the Mayor of Baltimore City by requiring the advice and consent of the Maryland Senate.
responsible_party: Pimlico Community Development Authority and Mayor of Baltimore City
stakeholders: Residents, businesses, community organizations, and service providers in Baltimore City's Park Heights corridor and surrounding Pimlico Race Course neighborhoods, as well as members of the Pimlico Community Development Authority.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Local effect alters the internal distribution of local impact grants within Baltimore City without changing the overall total. Funding distributed consistent with the Park Heights Master Plan increases by an estimated $363,500 in FY 2024 (rising to $424,200 by FY 2028), with an offsetting equivalent decrease in grant allocations to other surrounding Baltimore City neighborhoods.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the appointment process for members of the Pimlico Community Development Authority (requiring advice and consent of the Senate) and modifies the allocation formula of video lottery terminal local impact grants overseen and utilized by the Authority.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates commercial gaming and video lottery terminal facilities across Maryland, the proceeds of which generate the local impact grant funding distributed under the provisions amended by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a local board of elections to send, not later than 43 days before an election, a ballot to voters who have made a request and qualify to vote by absentee ballot; altering the procedures for the canvassing of and curing of errors on absentee and provisional ballots; prohibiting the tabulation of absentee ballot vote totals before the polls close; requiring that the statewide primary election and the primary election for the municipal offices of Baltimore City in 2024 be held on the second Tuesday in May; etc.
Title: Election Law - Ballot Issuance, Processing, and Reporting Procedures and 2024 Primary Date

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Electronic Communication -see also- Comm; Elec.Gov; Lang; Te

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland election procedures by requiring local boards of elections to send mail-in/absentee ballots to qualifying voters at least 43 days before an election if requested at least 60 days in advance; requiring local boards to begin processing absentee ballots eight business days prior to early voting; allowing voters to cure missing signatures on absentee ballot envelopes up to 10 days after Election Day through methods such as text, email, or an online portal; establishing rules for handling multiple ballots from the same voter; altering precinct-level results reporting; and moving the 2024 statewide and Baltimore City municipal primary election from the fourth Tuesday in April to the second Tuesday in May.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters (especially absentee and mail-in voters), local boards of elections, and election workers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $84,100 in FY 2024, rising to $115,700 by FY 2028, reflecting costs for a State Board of Elections IT programmer to support the voter signature cure system; additional unquantified costs exist for contractual services and equipment (such as flash drives and scanners), shared 50/50 between the State and local boards. Local government expenditures increase beginning in FY 2024 to support early canvassing personnel, equipment, and text-messaging cure software. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary implementing agency for HB 535. The bill requires SBE to adopt regulations regarding ballot curing and oath signature omissions, update statewide election reporting to include early, absentee, and provisional votes by precinct, oversee early canvassing waivers granted by the State Administrator, and implement/maintain IT systems allowing voters to cure ballot defects, incurring direct personnel and operational expenditures.

Synopsis: Specifying that the definition of "earnable compensation" does not include certain payments requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to pay a nonvested former member's accumulated contributions to the nonvested former member's designated beneficiary or estate if the nonvested former member dies before withdrawing the member's contributions; and providing a list of individuals who immediately vest on taking certain offices.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Earnable Compensation, Nonvested Former Members, and Immediate Vesting

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Excludes retroactive lump-sum salary increases and other non-standard payments from the definition of earnable compensation in the State Retirement and Pension System, requires accumulated contributions of deceased nonvested former members to be paid to their designated beneficiary or estate, and specifies an explicit list of State officials who receive immediate retirement vesting upon taking office.
responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System Board of Trustees / State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members and nonvested former members of the State Retirement and Pension System (and their beneficiaries/estates), as well as specified appointed State agency heads and officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no discernible effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or revenues. Excluding certain retroactive lump-sum payments may negligibly reduce pension liabilities, returning contributions for deceased nonvested members conforms statute to existing agency practice, and enumerating positions entitled to immediate vesting is clarifying. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article governing the State Retirement and Pension System, which SRA administers. It specifies rules for earnable compensation, mandates the payout of accumulated contributions for deceased nonvested former members, and clarifies immediate vesting rights including for SRA's Executive Director.

Section 3 of the bill specifically provides an exemption for lump sum payments made by the Maryland Department of Transportation between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2023, representing retroactive salary increases, provided retirement contributions were made.
The bill explicitly adds the Adjutant General of the Military Department to the statutory list of officials who have immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Chair of the State Board of Contract Appeals as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the Chair of the Public Service Commission as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the Chair of the Workers' Compensation Commission as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the Chief Administrative Law Judge of the Office of Administrative Hearings as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Director of the Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the Director of the Maryland Energy Administration as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Director of the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the Director of the Office of Homeland Security as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the Director of the Office of Performance Improvement as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Director of the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (now GOCPP) as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the Insurance Commissioner of the Maryland Insurance Administration as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Special Secretary of the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the State Archivist as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.
The bill explicitly designates the State Prosecutor of the State Prosecutor's Office as having immediate vesting rights upon taking office.

Synopsis: Increasing certain dollar thresholds of spending for the purposes of defining "small procurement" for State procurement contracts.
Title: State Procurement - Small Procurement - Definition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum dollar threshold for standard State "small procurements" from $50,000 to $100,000, and doubles specialized small procurement thresholds—such as raising construction contracts for the Department of General Services and Maryland Department of Transportation, as well as capital and maintenance contracts for the Department of Natural Resources, from $100,000 to $200,000.
responsible_party: Maryland primary procurement units (including the Department of General Services, Maryland Department of Transportation, Department of Natural Resources, and State Retirement Agency) and the Board of Public Works
stakeholders: State agencies purchasing goods and services, as well as contractors and small or minority-owned businesses bidding on State procurement contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material effect on State finances, although State agencies may experience administrative efficiencies by using simplified small procurement procedures for more goods and services. There is no local fiscal impact, and the effect on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly doubles the small procurement threshold for construction contracts awarded by the Department of General Services from $100,000 to $200,000, while also raising the general small procurement threshold for state units.
The bill specifically increases the small procurement threshold for construction contracts awarded by the Maryland Department of Transportation from $100,000 to $200,000.
The bill directly raises the small procurement threshold for capital projects and maintenance contracts awarded by the Department of Natural Resources from $100,000 to $200,000.

The bill explicitly increases the annual small procurement threshold for the State Retirement Agency from $50,000 to $100,000 for independent medical evaluations by physicians and related administrative hearing testimony.

Under the amended section of the State Finance and Procurement Article, the Board of Public Works is charged with reviewing the prevailing costs of labor and materials at least every three years and recommending adjustments to small procurement ceilings.

Synopsis: Altering the percentage of the federal earned income tax credit used for determining the amount that an individual may claim as a refund under the Maryland earned income tax credit under certain circumstances; repealing a certain limitation on the amount certain individuals may claim as a refund under the credit; altering the definition of "qualified child" and income eligibility requirements for purposes of qualifying for a certain credit against the State income tax for certain dependent children; etc.
Title: Family Prosperity Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: The Family Prosperity Act of 2023 permanently extends temporary expansions to the Maryland Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) and eliminates the $530 cap on the refundable credit for individuals without qualifying children. It also permanently extends and expands the State Child Tax Credit by increasing the income eligibility threshold to $15,000 of federal adjusted gross income, including all dependent children under age six regardless of disability status, and repealing the requirement to reduce the state credit by the amount of any federal child tax credit claimed.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Low- and moderate-income Maryland taxpayers, working individuals without qualifying children, ITIN filers, and low-income families with children under age six or children under age 17 with disabilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $172.3 million in FY 2024 ($154.4 million for the earned income credit and $17.9 million for the child tax credit), growing to $186.5 million by FY 2028. General fund expenditures increase by $36,533 in FY 2024 and approximately $60,000 to $70,000 annually thereafter for the Comptroller's Office to hire one revenue examiner to process claims. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $6.1 million in FY 2024 (rising to $6.6 million by FY 2028), and Montgomery County local expenditures may increase for its earned income credit supplement program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for administering state and local income taxes, processing returns, and issuing refunds. The bill directly impacts the Comptroller's operations by expanding the Earned Income Tax Credit and Child Tax Credit, requiring adjustments to tax processing systems and requiring an additional revenue examiner to validate claims.
House Bill 547 is a key Administration bill submitted on behalf of the Governor to advance executive policy priorities concerning family prosperity and child poverty reduction.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for state budget development and revenue forecasting. The bill significantly reduces state general fund revenues by more than $170 million annually, directly impacting long-term fiscal planning.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State for purposes of developing opportunities for banking institutions and credit unions to better serve the needs of low- to moderate-income tracts; providing for certain assessment offset credits for certain banking institutions and credit unions in certain areas; authorizing the use of the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Financial Regulation - Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund - Establishment (Access to Banking Act)

bill_summary: The Access to Banking Act establishes the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund as an instrumentality of the State to develop opportunities for banks and credit unions to serve low- to moderate-income areas through innovative financial products and expanded capital access. It authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to use the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund to make an initial equity investment of up to $2.5 million and spend up to $250,000 on establishment expenses, while providing assessment offset credits to well-capitalized institutions opening or maintaining branches in qualifying tracts and allowing matching state investments through June 30, 2028.
responsible_party: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: State-chartered banking institutions, credit unions, and small businesses and residents located in low- to moderate-income census tracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $2,838,500 in FY 2024, reflecting an initial $2.5 million capital investment, $167,500 in administrative costs, and $171,000 in matching investments. In FY 2025 through FY 2028, special fund expenditures range from $328,500 down to $265,500 before rising to $310,000 for matching investments and residual startup costs. Special fund revenues decrease by an estimated $171,000 in FY 2024, rising to a $310,000 reduction in FY 2028 due to assessment offset credits granted to eligible financial institutions. Local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation is a division within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Commissioner is the primary regulator charged with establishing, governing, and making investments into the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, as well as administering the assessment offset credits for banks and credit unions.

The State Treasurer serves as the statutory custodian of the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund, from which the initial investments and expenditures for the new venture fund are drawn and to which returns are deposited.
The bill authorizes expenditures from the special fund subject to inclusion in the annual State budget or via the budget amendment process overseen by DBM.

Synopsis: Altering the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Program by extending the duration of the Program through fiscal year 2026, repealing the rebates that may be issued to retail service station dealers, and increasing the limitation on the total amount of rebates that the Maryland Energy Administration may issue in each fiscal year; altering the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program by altering the definition of "grant"; etc.
Title: Maryland Energy Administration – Energy Programs – Modifications (Clean Transportation and Energy Act)

bill_summary: The Clean Transportation and Energy Act extends the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program through fiscal year 2026, increases the annual rebate limit to $2.5 million, alters maximum individual and business rebate amounts, and removes specific rebates for retail service station dealers. It also modifies the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program to focus exclusively on commercial and industrial equipment, changes grant funding to cover up to 75% of incremental costs, prioritizes projects in overburdened or underserved communities, raises the administrative expense cap under the Strategic Energy Investment Fund from $5 million to $7.5 million, and modifies the authorized uses of Alternative Compliance Payments.
responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Maryland vehicle owners, commercial fleet operators, businesses installing EV charging equipment, local governments, and residents of low- to moderate-income and overburdened or underserved communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund (Strategic Energy Investment Fund) expenditures increase by $7,750,000 in FY 2024, $7,500,000 in FY 2025 and FY 2026, $5,000,000 in FY 2027, and by an indeterminate amount in FY 2028. Revenues are unaffected. Local governments benefit through eligibility for increased grant and rebate funding for zero-emission vehicles and charging infrastructure.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which alters the Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment Rebate Program, the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program, the allowable uses of Alternative Compliance Payments, and increases MEA's administrative expense cap under the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

The bill impacts state budget formulation by establishing a mandated annual appropriation of at least $10 million from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund from FY 2025 through FY 2027 for the Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Zero-Emission Vehicle Grant Program.
The bill requires the Governor to include specific mandatory appropriations from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027.

As a state agency overseeing vehicle fleets, transit systems, and transportation infrastructure, MDOT is directly affected by state clean transportation incentives and is eligible to participate in electric vehicle recharging equipment rebates.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of Statewide Broadband within the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study as to how the State can incentivize broadband service providers to expand broadband infrastructure to communities that are unserved or underserved; and requiring the Office to submit its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
Title: Office of Statewide Broadband - Study of Broadband Expansion Incentives

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: House Bill 551 requires the Office of Statewide Broadband within the Department of Housing and Community Development to conduct a study and submit recommendations by January 1, 2024, regarding regulatory and financial incentives to encourage broadband service providers to expand infrastructure to unserved or underserved communities, methods for deploying federal broadband grants effectively, and successful strategies used by other states to spur private investment.
responsible_party: Office of Statewide Broadband within the Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Broadband service providers, telecommunications companies, and residents in unserved and underserved Maryland communities lacking reliable broadband access.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the study can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources, though Department of Housing and Community Development expenditures could potentially increase by a limited amount (estimated by the office at $100,000 to $150,000 for consultant assistance, which could be absorbed by reallocating funds) in FY 2024 only. Revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Office of Statewide Broadband, which is housed within the Department of Housing and Community Development, to conduct a study on broadband expansion incentives and report findings and recommendations by January 1, 2024.
The bill was submitted by request of the Administration and explicitly requires the Office of Statewide Broadband to submit its final study findings and recommendations directly to the Governor.

Synopsis: Establishing the Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program in the Department of Commerce to provide funding for certain costs for infrastructure projects in eligible technology sectors; requiring certain grantees to provide matching funds and to demonstrate certain abilities; and requiring the Department to report to the Governor and the General Assembly on the projects funded through and the economic impact of the Program by July 1, 2026.
Title: Economic Development - Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund (Innovation Economy Infrastructure Act of 2023)

bill_summary: Establishes the Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and Fund within the Department of Commerce to provide grants of up to $2 million per recipient for infrastructure projects supporting innovation in eligible technology sectors, requiring recipients to provide matching funds.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Private technology and manufacturing businesses, non-profit organizations, local governments, colleges and universities, real estate developers, and construction and equipment firms in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10.0 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2027 (with FY 2024 contingent on bill enactment), with special fund revenues and expenditures increasing correspondingly for grant distributions and administrative costs. Public higher education institutions and local governments experience increases in revenues and expenditures to the extent they receive grants and provide matching funds of 200% to 400%.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Commerce as the primary administering agency for the Build Our Future Grant Pilot Program and the Build Our Future Grant Fund, tasking it with awarding grants, adopting regulations, monitoring compliance, and reporting outcomes.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Build Our Future Grant Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill explicitly tasks the Comptroller with accounting for the Build Our Future Grant Fund and its interest earnings.

Public colleges and universities are eligible grant recipients authorized to receive up to 50% of the fund's appropriations, directly impacting USM institution revenues and matching fund expenditures.
As a public university, Morgan State is an eligible recipient for grant awards dedicated to higher education institutions and would incur revenue and matching expenditure impacts if awarded funding.
As an independent public honors college, St. Mary's is eligible to compete for up to 50% of the program's grant funding for innovation infrastructure projects.
DBM oversees the state budget execution and fiscal planning for the annual $10 million general fund appropriation supporting the program.
The bill is an Administration initiative that requires the Department of Commerce to submit an evaluative report on the program's economic impact to the Governor by July 1, 2026.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of a certain subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for certain military retirement income received by individuals under the age of 55 years to $12,500 and individuals at least 55 years of age to $20,000 during the taxable year for certain military service; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Military Retirement Income (Keep Our Heroes Home Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans

bill_summary: The Keep Our Heroes Home Act increases the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for military retirement income. For tax year 2023, it allows individuals to subtract up to $25,000 of military retirement income, and for tax year 2024 and beyond, up to $40,000 of military retirement income.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Military retirees and surviving beneficiaries receiving military retirement or death benefits (approximately 33,000 individuals).
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $11,200,000 in FY 2024, increasing to $13,100,000 by FY 2028. Local income tax revenues decrease by $7,300,000 in FY 2024, increasing to $8,600,000 by FY 2028. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers state income taxes and is responsible for implementing the expanded subtraction modification on state tax returns and processing tax filings.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families is responsible for advocating for and assisting Maryland veterans and their families with state benefits and resources, including tax relief programs targeted at military retirees.
Retirees of the Maryland National Guard are explicitly enumerated as eligible service members whose retirement pay qualifies for the increased income tax subtraction modification.
The bill was sponsored by the Administration as the 'Keep Our Heroes Home Act' as part of the Governor's executive policy agenda to retain veterans and military retirees in Maryland.

Synopsis: Increasing the number of resident judges of the Circuit Court for Baltimore County from 20 to 21.
Title: Baltimore County - Circuit Court Judgeships
bill_summary: Increases the number of resident judges on the Circuit Court for Baltimore County from 20 to 21.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Baltimore County residents, litigants, court staff, and the Circuit Court for Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $365,916 in FY 2024 (included in the FY 2024 state budget) and increase to $530,200 by FY 2028, funding one additional judge, one courtroom clerk, and one law clerk. Baltimore County expenditures increase beginning in FY 2024 to fund operating expenses and an administrative assistant for the new judge. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an additional circuit court judgeship and associated staff positions in Baltimore County, directly impacting the operations, staffing, and budget of the Maryland Judicial Branch administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates to fill judicial vacancies and newly created judgeships.
The Governor is responsible for appointing individuals to new judicial seats created by statute in Maryland's circuit courts.

bill_summary: House Bill 556 establishes a comprehensive regulatory, licensing, and taxation framework for adult-use cannabis in Maryland. The bill renames the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission to the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, creates the Maryland Cannabis Administration as an independent unit to oversee adult-use and medical cannabis, establishes the Office of Social Equity, and enacts a 9% sales and use tax on adult-use cannabis starting in fiscal year 2024. It also provides for licensing across growers, processors, dispensaries, incubator spaces, and on-site consumption sites, creates multiple grant and assistance programs for social equity applicants, and establishes regulations for packaging, labeling, and advertising.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
stakeholders: Adult-use cannabis consumers (age 21 and older), qualifying medical cannabis patients and caregivers, medical cannabis licensees converting to dual-use, prospective cannabis business licensees and social equity applicants, testing laboratories, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2024, State general fund revenues are estimated to increase by $18.0 million (rising to $64.2 million by FY 2027), while special fund revenues increase by $68.0 million from cannabis sales and use tax (9%) and licensing/conversion fees. State expenditures in FY 2024 increase by $4.4 million in general funds, $63.0 million in special funds, and $2.0 million in bond funds for incubator facilities. Beginning in FY 2025, the bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $5.0 million for the Social Equity Partnership Grant Program. Local revenues increase by an estimated $1.8 million in FY 2024 from a 5% share of cannabis sales tax collections, alongside disbursements from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 556 establishes the Maryland Cannabis Administration as an independent unit of State government and the primary regulatory body responsible for licensing, oversight, enforcement, and administration of the medical and adult-use cannabis industry.

The Comptroller administers the 9% sales and use tax on adult-use cannabis, accounts for and distributes tax revenues across multiple funds, and administers the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund and the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund, requiring significant new personnel and IT resources.

The bill creates the Capital Access Program within the Department of Commerce and expands the authorized uses and funding of the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund administered by Commerce, which receives a 5% statutory allocation of cannabis sales and use tax revenues.

The bill repeals the Natalie M. LaPrade Medical Cannabis Commission housed under MDH, transferring its duties and funds to the new Administration; MDH also administers the Cannabis Public Health Fund, which receives 5% of adult-use cannabis tax revenues, and may enter into an MOU to test cannabis at a State laboratory.

MEDCO is mandated to identify potential incubator space sites across four regions of Maryland and acquire, construct, or refurbish at least one incubator space facility, supported by $2.0 million in capital bond funding.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is required to consult on disparity study reviews and develop plans and procedures for setting reasonable minority business enterprise participation goals for cannabis licensees.
DGS is required to take ownership of the incubator space facility constructed or refurbished by MEDCO and contract with a nonprofit organization to operate the facility.

The Treasurer is responsible for holding and investing multiple special funds established or altered by the bill, including the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund, Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, and Medical Cannabis Compassionate Use Fund.

OAG is required to consult with the Office of Social Equity in determining disproportionately impacted communities and consult with the Administration on disparity study evaluations, constitutional remedial measures, and MBE program participation.

The Governor appoints the Director of the Maryland Cannabis Administration, the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity, and members of the Advisory Board, and is mandated to include annual appropriations such as $5 million for the Social Equity Partnership Grant Program.

The Commissioner of Financial Regulation within the Department of Labor is specifically prohibited from taking adverse supervisory or regulatory actions against depository institutions solely for providing financial services to cannabis businesses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Advisory Board on Medical and Adult-Use Cannabis to advise the Administration and General Assembly on cannabis guidelines, rules, and regulations.
As the State's designated MBE certification agency, MDOT is consulted alongside other entities regarding disparity study findings and constitutional remedial measures for cannabis license awards.

OAH is anticipated to handle contested case hearings delegated by the Administration regarding cannabis license denials, suspensions, or disciplinary actions, potentially requiring additional Administrative Law Judge resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository within DPSCS must process state and national fingerprint-based criminal history record checks for cannabis agents and license applicants.
OLA is granted statutory authority and responsibility to audit the newly established Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund and the Medical Cannabis Compassionate Use Fund.
MDA is authorized to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Administration to co-locate and perform cannabis testing at an existing State-owned laboratory.

The bill regulates insurance practices relating to cannabis businesses, providing safe harbors and protections from State liability for insurers engaging in business with legitimate cannabis entities.
DBM oversees the state budget execution, personnel transfers, and conversion of former MMCC contractual staff to full-time merit positions under the new Administration.
Historical cannabis possession charge data from the courts is utilized by the Office of Social Equity to identify disproportionately impacted areas for fund distribution and licensing preferences.
Members of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission are required to file financial disclosure statements with the State Ethics Commission under Maryland Public Ethics Law.

Synopsis: Requiring at least one applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Carroll County to be a resident of the State, rather than the county, when an application is filed and to remain a resident of the State for the license to remain valid; etc.
Title: Carroll County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Residency Requirement
bill_summary: Alters the residency requirement for an alcoholic beverages license issued on behalf of a partnership, corporation, club, or limited liability company in Carroll County, allowing an applicant to be a resident of the State of Maryland rather than a resident of Carroll County, provided at least one applicant remains a State resident for the license to remain valid.
responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Applicants and holders of alcoholic beverages licenses for partnerships, corporations, clubs, and limited liability companies in Carroll County, as well as Maryland residents seeking to operate such businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and is not anticipated to materially affect Carroll County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and prescribes standard alcoholic beverage license application forms referenced in Title 4 of the Alcoholic Beverages Article, though this specific legislation alters local residency requirements administered primarily at the county board level.

Synopsis: Modifying the seating requirements for Class B, Class BR, and Class C beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Carroll County.
Title: Carroll County - Alcoholic Beverages - Modification of Seating Requirements
bill_summary: Modifies the seating requirements for Class B, Class BR, and Class C beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Carroll County by allowing up to 15 bar or counter seats to be included toward the minimum 50-seat requirement.
responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Hotels, restaurants, and clubs seeking or holding Class B, Class BR, or Class C beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Carroll County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Carroll County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for regulating Maryland's alcohol industry; however, this bill strictly alters dining and bar seating calculations for specific local retail licenses overseen by the Carroll County Board of License Commissioners, having minimal relevance and no state fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Establishing an annual fee of $2,000 for a multiple event entertainment alcoholic beverages license where the number of events number 41 or more per year in Carroll County; and repealing the limit on the total number of days for which a multiple event entertainment license may be used.
Title: Carroll County - Alcoholic Beverages - Multiple Event Entertainment Licenses
bill_summary: This bill repeals the 40-day annual limit on Class C multiple event entertainment beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Carroll County and creates a new licensing tier with an annual fee of $2,000 for organizations hosting 41 or more events per year.
responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: County fire departments, arts centers on West Main Street in Westminster, and event attendees in Carroll County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. The bill does not materially affect Carroll County finances or operations, though it establishes a new $2,000 fee tier for 41 or more events per year.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters local alcoholic beverages license tiers and fees in Carroll County. While administered locally by the Carroll County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, the Comptroller of Maryland is the principal state agency overseeing and regulating the alcoholic beverages industry.

Synopsis: Granting the Town of Mount Airy in Carroll County and Frederick County the authority to exercise urban renewal powers within an urban renewal area under Article III, Section 61 of the Maryland Constitution; and authorizing the municipality to levy certain taxes and issue general obligation bonds and revenue bonds to carry out urban renewal powers.
Title: Town of Mount Airy (Carroll County and Frederick County) - Urban Renewal Authority

bill_summary: Authorizes the Town of Mount Airy to exercise urban renewal powers to remediate blighted or slum areas, including the authority to acquire property through eminent domain, levy taxes, and issue general obligation and revenue bonds to finance urban renewal projects.
responsible_party: Town of Mount Airy
stakeholders: Residents, property owners, and businesses in the Town of Mount Airy (located in Carroll and Frederick counties)
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected, though a minimal indirect increase in State tax revenues could occur from revitalization. Town of Mount Airy expenditures may increase for property acquisition and project execution if eminent domain and urban renewal authority are utilized, while local revenues may increase from property sales, bond issuances, and an expanded tax base. Specific dollar amounts cannot be quantified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants eminent domain authority to the Town of Mount Airy for urban renewal and blight clearance, requiring condemnation proceedings to be conducted in court pursuant to the Real Property Article and authorizing the town to seek circuit court orders for entry and inspection.

The department oversees statewide community revitalization, housing rehabilitation, and municipal development policies, which align with the slum and blight clearance and redevelopment powers granted to the municipality.
The department advises local governments on land use planning and growth; the bill requires municipal urban renewal plans to conform substantially to municipal master planning.
The agency administers state tax collections, which could see minimal indirect increases if urban renewal projects increase property values and local economic activity.

Synopsis: Authorizing a holder of a Class 9 limited distillery license to apply for and obtain a Class 8 liquor wholesaler's license with certain privileges.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 9 Limited Distillery License - Self-Distribution

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.
Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes holders of a Class 9 limited distillery license to apply for and obtain a Class 8 liquor wholesaler's license, allowing them to self-distribute up to 27,500 gallons of their own manufactured liquor annually.
responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
stakeholders: Class 9 limited distillery licensees, alcoholic beverage wholesalers, alcohol retailers, and consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally by an estimated $1,800 in FY 2024 and $780 annually thereafter from application, licensing, and renewal fees if all six eligible Class 9 limited distilleries obtain a Class 8 liquor wholesaler license. The Alcohol and Tobacco Commission can monitor additional licenses with existing resources. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and collects related revenues. Under the bill (§ 2-308.1(e)), license holders seeking to use an additional location for warehousing, sale, and delivery of liquor must submit an application for approval to the Comptroller along with an application fee.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Attorney General to direct that an Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council committee be formed if required by a court or administrative order or settlement agreement entered into by the Attorney General; requiring the Maryland Department of Health, subject to the limitations of the State budget, to allow certain entities to choose the formulation or dosage of an opioid overdose reversal drug approved by the Food and Drug Administration with which the entity is provided through the Overdose Response Program; etc.
Title: Opioids - Opioid Restitution Advisory Council and Fund and Overdose Response Program

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health, subject to State budget limitations, to allow entities provided with opioid overdose reversal drugs under the Overdose Response Program to choose the FDA-approved formulation or dosage. It also authorizes the Attorney General to direct the formation of a committee within the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council if required by a court or administrative order or settlement agreement, and clarifies that opioid-related court judgments and settlement funds must be appropriated and distributed to political subdivisions through a grant program administered by the Secretary of Health.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Entities and providers participating in the Overdose Response Program, individuals at risk of or experiencing opioid overdoses, local political subdivisions receiving opioid restitution funds, and the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health may increase minimally to accommodate requests for specific formulations or dosages of FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drugs, though this requirement remains subject to State budget limitations. Provisions regarding the Opioid Restitution Fund and Advisory Council can be implemented with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. MDH administers the Overdose Response Program and is required, subject to state budget limitations, to allow participating entities to select the formulation or dosage of FDA-approved opioid overdose reversal drugs. Additionally, the Secretary of Health is tasked with establishing and administering the grant program distributing settlement funds from the Opioid Restitution Fund to political subdivisions.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to direct the formation of a committee within the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council pursuant to court or administrative orders or settlement agreements, establish procedures for such committees, and designate the controlling versions of opioid settlement agreements or amendments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory provisions governing the operations, committee formation, membership, and leadership of the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council, which falls under this category of state advisory bodies.

bill_summary: Establishes the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee within the Maryland Higher Education Commission to study policies, demand, best practices, and barriers regarding student mental health care at Maryland higher education institutions, requiring annual reports with findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission and participating institutions of higher education
stakeholders: College and university students in Maryland, campus mental health counselors and clinical staff, and public and private institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures for higher education institutions may increase minimally to provide staff support for the committee on a rotating basis, with costs potentially higher in FY 2024 to meet the initial reporting deadline. Expense reimbursements for committee members are assumed minimal and absorbable within existing resources. No impact on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee within the Maryland Higher Education Commission, and the Secretary of Higher Education serves as a member and appoints members to the committee.
The bill establishes the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee within the agency, with the Secretary of Higher Education serving on the committee and appointing several members.

The Chancellor (or designee) is designated as a committee member and appoints several campus mental health professionals, USM students are appointed, and USM institutions share the responsibility to staff the committee on a rotating basis.

The President of Morgan State University (or designee) is designated as a committee member, students may be appointed, and the university may incur minimal staffing costs on a rotating basis to support the committee.

The President of St. Mary's College of Maryland (or designee) is designated as a member of the committee, students may be appointed, and the college may share committee staffing responsibilities on a rotating basis.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent advisory body within the executive branch—the Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee—tasked with studying mental health services across higher education institutions.
The Access to Mental Health Advisory Committee is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor annually beginning December 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Requiring the inclusion of all State service while an individual was employed by the State in the Executive, Legislative, or Judicial Branch of government for the purpose of determining eligibility for State retiree health benefits.
Title: State Employee and Retiree Health Benefits - Creditable Service
