Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: Redefines creditable service for determining eligibility for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program to include any period an individual worked in the Executive, Legislative, or Judicial branch of Maryland State government while enrolled in either the State Retirement and Pension System or the Optional Retirement Program, allowing individuals with service across both systems to combine service credit for retiree health coverage and subsidies.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: State retirees and employees with creditable service split between the State Retirement and Pension System and the Optional Retirement Program, along with their eligible surviving spouses and dependents.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are unaffected. There is a potential minimal increase in State Other Post Employment Benefits (OPEB) liabilities and future benefit payments because certain retirees can combine service credits to qualify for health benefits or higher subsidies. Because benefits are funded on a pay-as-you-go basis, any expenditure increase occurs beyond the five-year forecast window. Exact dollar estimates are unavailable. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is the primary agency responsible for administering state employee and retiree benefits, including the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. DBM directly oversees eligibility determinations and State subsidies for retiree health insurance.

The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill directly coordinates creditable service and retirement allowances under SRPS with the Optional Retirement Program to determine retiree health benefit eligibility.

The bill impacts participants transitioning between the Optional Retirement Program (ORP)—which is predominantly utilized by faculty and staff at public higher education institutions—and the State Retirement and Pension System.

Synopsis: Repealing certain termination provisions for a tax credit against the State income tax for fresh farm and organic fresh farm food donations; altering the amounts of the tax credit from 50% to 100% of the value of an eligible food donation and from 75% to 100% of the value of the donated certified organic produce a qualified farm is eligible to receive under certain circumstances; applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022; etc.
Title: Income Tax Credit - Food Donations by Qualified Farms - Sunset Repeal and Alterations (Farmers Feeding Families Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: Permanently extends the State income tax credit for qualified farms that make eligible food donations, repealing the program's scheduled sunset. The bill also increases the tax credit value from 50% to 100% of the value of eligible food donations and from 75% to 100% for certified organic produce donations, up to the statutory limit.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland farm businesses making fresh food donations, food banks and organizations receiving food donations, and individuals experiencing food insecurity.
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount in FY 2024 and by up to $100,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to income tax credits claimed. To the extent credits are claimed against corporate income taxes, Higher Education Investment Fund and Transportation Trust Fund revenues, as well as local highway user revenues, decrease minimally. Expenditures are not affected as the Maryland Department of Agriculture can manage administration within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary implementing agency. The Secretary of Agriculture is responsible for certifying tax credit certificate administrators, establishing and publishing weekly donation values, preparing certificate forms in consultation with the Comptroller, administering the credit cap, adopting regulations, and submitting an annual report.

The Comptroller of Maryland administers the State income tax system against which this credit is claimed, receives copies of all issued tax credit certificates, consults on the certification process and certificate forms, and collaborates on adopting regulations and annual reporting.
The Governor's Office receives an annual report from the Secretary of Agriculture, in consultation with the Comptroller, regarding the use and impact of the tax credit.

Synopsis: Requiring each unit of State government to include certain specifications for certain products produced from recycled or organic materials when establishing procurement specifications for compost, mulch, or other soil amendments or aggregate; requiring the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee to establish certain specifications for purchasing of compost, mulch, or other soil amendments or aggregates produced from certain materials and publish and maintain the specifications online for use by State agencies.
Title: State Procurement - Purchasing - Compost, Mulch, and Soil Amendments and Aggregate

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee to establish and maintain online specifications for State procurement of compost, mulch, soil amendments, and aggregate made from recycled or organic materials. State agencies must include these specifications in their procurement solicitations if the products are competitively priced, readily available, and meet quality standards.
responsible_party: Maryland Green Purchasing Committee
stakeholders: State procurement agencies, vendors and suppliers of compost, mulch, soil amendments, and recycled aggregates, and local governments managing municipal solid waste.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Green Purchasing Committee can develop specifications using existing resources. Any State expenditure impact resulting from applying the specifications cannot be reliably estimated due to uncertain product availability and pricing relative to virgin materials. No effect on State revenues. Local revenues may minimally increase if the State purchases more municipal solid waste.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is explicitly referenced in the bill's statutory text regarding goals for composting landscape waste on State property. Furthermore, the Secretary of General Services chairs the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee (MGPC) and DGS provides administrative and staffing support to develop, publish, and maintain the required procurement specifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns direct statutory responsibilities to the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee (MGPC), a permanent state committee, to establish, publish, and maintain online specifications for compost, mulch, soil amendments, and aggregate.

MDOT and its modal administrations are among the largest state consumers and purchasers of aggregate, mulch, and soil amendments for transportation infrastructure, highway construction, and right-of-way land maintenance.

As the agency responsible for maintaining thousands of miles of state roadway and roadside lands, MDOT SHA is directly impacted by requirements to include green purchasing specifications when procuring aggregate, compost, and mulch for highway projects and landscaping.

DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public lands and parks where compost and soil amendments are utilized. The agency provided specific input noted in the fiscal note regarding risks associated with contaminants in products derived from food and solid waste.

MDE regulates solid waste, food waste, dredged materials, sludge, and composting facilities in Maryland, which serve as the source materials for the products subject to the bill's procurement specifications.
MDA oversees commercial fertilizers, soil conditioners, and agricultural composting standards, and participates in green procurement discussions relevant to soil amendments.
BPW oversees and approves state procurement policies and large procurement contracts governed by the State Finance and Procurement Article amended by this bill.
The State Treasurer is a statutory member of the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee, which is tasked with establishing and maintaining the green purchasing specifications.

Synopsis: Authorizing, for a certain period of time, the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to exchange a Class B-D-7 beer, wine, and liquor license in a certain area for a Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor license under certain circumstances; repealing certain geographic and temporal restrictions on the issuance of Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Baltimore City; and altering a certain period of time during which a certain alcoholic beverages license may be issued.
Title: Baltimore City - 41st District - Alcoholic Beverages - Licenses
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to exchange a Class B-D-7 beer, wine, and liquor license on the odd side of the 4000 block of Frederick Avenue for a Class A-7 license. It also repeals restrictions that barred issuing Class A-7 licenses after July 1, 2022, and within the 43rd legislative district. Additionally, it modifies the definition of a marketplace license in the 41st district to include establishments expected to open within 24 months and permits marketplace license holders to sell alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees and business owners in Baltimore City, particularly those operating in the 41st and 43rd legislative districts and along the 4000 block of Frederick Avenue.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this bill specifically governs local retail licensing administered by the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City and has no state fiscal impact, it alters provisions within the state's Alcoholic Beverages Article overseen generally at the state level by the Comptroller.

Synopsis: Altering a certain provision to prohibit a court from assessing certain costs on a certain person or governmental unit for recording and indexing an order of restitution issued by any court in the State instead of the court in which the judgment of restitution was entered.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Restitution Orders - Recording Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland courts from assessing fees or costs on a person or governmental unit for recording and indexing an order of restitution as a money judgment, regardless of which court in the State issued the original order.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Crime victims and governmental entities seeking to record restitution orders as money judgments, as well as State and local court clerks.
fiscal_impact_summary: Any potential decrease in fee revenues is anticipated to be minimal and will not materially affect State operations or finances. Local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs court fees by prohibiting state courts and court clerks from assessing costs for recording and indexing an order of restitution as a money judgment, which directly impacts judicial system administrative operations and fee collection overseen by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts crime victims seeking enforcement of criminal restitution orders without being assessed court recording fees, aligning with the agency's role in crime victim services, public safety policy, and restitution coordination.

Synopsis: Repealing the $500,000 cap on grants that may be awarded by the Maryland Transit Administration under the Maryland Senior Rides Program; repealing the $400,000 cap on the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program; establishing the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation to examine transportation needs of the elderly, persons with disabilities, and residents requiring transportation assistance to jobs, appointments, citizen programs, and other engagements; etc.
Title: Health and Human Services Transportation Improvement Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation within the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to examine needs and coordinate transportation services for transportation-disadvantaged individuals. It also repeals the statutory funding caps on grants under the Maryland Senior Rides Program and funding for the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Transportation-disadvantaged Maryland residents (including low-to-moderate income individuals, seniors, and individuals with disabilities), transit consumers, regional transportation providers, and participating state agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by $180,000 in FY 2024 and by $80,000 annually thereafter to hire consultants assisting MDOT with staffing the new coordinating committee. State revenues are not affected. Repealing the funding caps for the Maryland Senior Rides Program and the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program allows for potentially higher funding, but additional expenditures are discretionary rather than mandated. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing agency, responsible for staffing and chairing the newly established State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, with an estimated fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund of $180,000 in FY 2024 and $80,000 annually thereafter.

MTA administers both the Maryland Senior Rides Program and the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program, which have their statutory funding and grant caps repealed under the bill, and MTA assists MDOT in staffing the coordinating committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation as an ongoing interagency body to coordinate transit services across Maryland.

The Secretary of Aging is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, and the bill addresses transportation for elderly individuals.

The Secretary of Disabilities is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, which focuses heavily on the transit needs of individuals with disabilities.

The Secretary of Health is a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, which oversees coordination of transportation to medical and healthcare appointments.
The Secretary of Human Services is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of the Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Executive Board Chair of the Rural Maryland Council is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.

The Secretary of Labor is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation, which addresses transit to employment and workforce training.
The Secretary of Planning is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.
The Secretary of Veterans Affairs is designated as a statutory member of the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation.

The Governor is required to provide funding in the State budget for the Job Access and Reverse Commute Program, appoints discretionary members to the committee, and receives the committee's annual report.

Synopsis: Authorizing the correction of the designated beneficiary election for certain retirees of the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, or Judges' Retirement System who retired on or before December 31, 2012, if the retiree named an individual of the same sex to be a designated beneficiary and the retiree married the designated beneficiary on or after January 1, 2013.
Title: State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System, and Judges’ Retirement System – Surviving Spouse Benefit – Same–Sex Spouses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Authorizes certain retirees of the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, or Judges' Retirement System who retired on or before December 31, 2012, to convert an actuarially reduced optional retirement allowance to an unreduced basic allowance with full surviving spouse benefits if they subsequently married their same-sex designated beneficiary.
responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System (Board of Trustees and State Retirement Agency)
stakeholders: Retirees of the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and Judges' Retirement System who retired before 2013 and later married their same-sex designated beneficiaries, as well as their surviving spouses.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal effect on State pension assets and no discernible effect on State or local pension contribution rates given the small number of affected retirees (fewer than 109). No effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Police Retirement System, Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and Judges' Retirement System. It is responsible for providing the necessary forms, processing conversion requests and marriage documentation, and recalculating allowances and retroactive lump-sum payments.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from discriminating in the sale or rental of, or otherwise making unavailable or denying, a dwelling to an individual with a disability who has, obtains, or retains a certain service dog.
Title: Human Relations - Housing Discrimination - Service Dogs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Prohibits discrimination in the sale or rental of housing against individuals with disabilities who have, obtain, or retain a service dog, including retired service dogs kept as pets. The bill exempts such individuals from pet prohibition clauses and additional pet fees, allows them to keep a retired service dog for the remainder of its life, and holds them liable for any damage caused by the dog.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities who use or retain retired service dogs, residential landlords, housing providers, property managers, and home sellers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. Small business impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is the primary enforcement agency responsible for investigating complaints, attempting conciliation, and taking legal action regarding unlawful housing discrimination under Article - State Government, which this bill directly amends.

The Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) employs Administrative Law Judges who conduct administrative hearings and order relief or civil penalties when housing discrimination charges investigated by MCCR proceed to an administrative adjudication.

Complainants or respondents in housing discrimination disputes may elect to file civil actions in the State's circuit courts, which are supported and administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Department of Disabilities is responsible for coordinating policies and advancing accessible housing and rights for Maryland residents with disabilities, which directly intersects with protections for individuals using service and retired service dogs.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Nursing in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board; altering the exceptions to the registered nurse and licensed practical nurse licensure requirements; providing that, for a certain period of time, the Secretary of Health, rather than the Board, has authority over the infrastructure operations of the Board; etc.
Title: State Board of Nursing – Sunset Extension, Licensure Exceptions, and Board Operations and Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This emergency legislation extends the termination date of the Maryland State Board of Nursing (MBON) by two years to July 1, 2025. Through June 30, 2025, it temporarily shifts authority over the Board's infrastructure operations from MBON to the Secretary of Health and prohibits using Board special funds for these administrative operations. In addition, the bill staggers the termination of current Board members' terms, requires the hiring of an external consultant to conduct an independent evaluation and develop an action plan, modifies licensure exceptions to allow applicants to continue practicing if they have failed the licensing examination only once within a 120-day period, and establishes additional reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Nursing
stakeholders: Current and prospective registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, Board of Nursing staff and board members, healthcare facilities, and Maryland patients.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase from FY 2023 through FY 2025 as the Maryland Department of Health assumes MBON's infrastructure operations, with the FY 2024 State budget including $8.0 million in general funds contingent on the bill's enactment. Board special fund expenditures decrease correspondingly for infrastructure operations, while special fund expenditures increase by at least $150,000 in FY 2023 to hire an external consultant. MBON special fund revenues continue uninterrupted. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants the Secretary of Health temporary direct authority over the infrastructure operations of the State Board of Nursing, including hiring staff, designating an executive director, and overseeing millions in general fund expenditures to support board operations.

The Secretary of Budget and Management must consult with the Secretary of Health to determine board positions eligible for customized compensation, and the department must partner in developing an action plan to address infrastructure and staffing vacancies.

The department is specifically required to partner with the Board of Nursing, the Maryland Department of Health, and the Department of Budget and Management to develop an action plan addressing infrastructure and technology needs.

The bill terminates the terms of all 14 sitting members of the State Board of Nursing on a staggered basis in 2023, requiring the Governor to make appointments or reappointments, and mandates reports submitted to the Governor.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting candidates to fill the vacancies created by the staggered termination of all 14 Board of Nursing members.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Aging to oversee long-term care and train the staff of long-term care and dementia care navigation programs; requiring each area agency to establish a long-term care and dementia care navigation program; and requiring the Department to submit a report by October 1, 2024, and each year thereafter, to the Governor, the President of the Senate, the Speaker of the House, and certain committees of the General Assembly about the services provided by the program and to publish the report on its website.
Title: Department of Aging - Long-Term Care and Dementia Care Navigation Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Long-Term Care -see also- Continuing Care; Nursing Homes

bill_summary: Requires each Area Agency on Aging to develop and implement a long-term care and dementia care navigation program to provide information, referrals, cognitive screenings, and support for caregivers and individuals with dementia symptoms. It also mandates that the Maryland Department of Aging oversee and train navigation staff, track program data, and report annually on services provided.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Seniors, individuals with dementia or cognitive impairment, family caregivers, healthcare providers, and local Area Agencies on Aging.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $79,733 in FY 2024 for one program manager and operating expenses at the Maryland Department of Aging. Beginning in FY 2025, the bill establishes an ongoing mandated general fund appropriation of $2.4 million annually to manage the program statewide and distribute proportional funding to local Area Agencies on Aging. Local government revenues and expenditures increase accordingly beginning in FY 2025 for agencies operated by local jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly assigns the Maryland Department of Aging (MDoA) the responsibility to oversee, train staff, disseminate best practices, collect interaction data, distribute grant funding, and report annually on the long-term care and dementia care navigation programs operated through local Area Agencies on Aging.
The bill establishes a statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $2,400,000 beginning in FY 2025, which directly impacts the state operating budget managed and executed by DBM.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a $2,400,000 appropriation in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2025 and requires MDoA to submit an annual report on program services to the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifies that the work of the long-term care and dementia care navigation programs must be guided by recommendations from the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council.

Synopsis: Extending the reporting and termination dates, to July 1, 2024, and June 30, 2025, respectively, for the Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals.
Title: Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals - Extension of Dates

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Extends the reporting deadline and termination date by one year for the Workgroup on Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and Other Underrepresented Behavioral Health Professionals, requiring its final report to be submitted by July 1, 2024, and terminating the workgroup on June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the University System of Maryland
stakeholders: Black, Latino, Asian American Pacific Islander, and other underrepresented behavioral health professionals, higher education students studying behavioral health, and underserved communities in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Extending the workgroup by one year results in minimal additional expense reimbursements and staffing costs for the University System of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Health, both of which are absorbable within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for jointly staffing the Workgroup with the University System of Maryland, and the Secretary of Health appoints several members and designates the chair.

The University System of Maryland is required to jointly provide staff for the Workgroup alongside MDH, and several presidents of USM member institutions (Bowie State, Coppin State, and UMES) serve on the Workgroup.
The President of Morgan State University, or their designee, is designated by statute as a member of the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the operational life and reporting deadline of a statutory state workgroup created to examine diversity in behavioral health professions.
The Workgroup is required to submit its findings and recommendations report to the Governor by July 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Establishing the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program in the Department of Commerce to provide grants to certain small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises to assist those manufacturers with implementing new Industry 4.0 technology or related infrastructure for certain purposes; establishing the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund; and requiring the Governor to include in the budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028 an appropriation of $1,000,000 to the Fund.
Title: Economic Development - Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program and associated fund within the Department of Commerce to award competitive grants of $25,000 to $500,000 to qualifying small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) in Maryland, helping them purchase, implement, and train employees on smart manufacturing hardware and software technologies.
responsible_party: Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) manufacturers in Maryland and their employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $1.1 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028, reflecting a $1.0 million mandated annual appropriation to the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund and $123,176 in FY 2025 for Commerce administrative staffing and operating costs. Special fund revenues and grant expenditures for the fund increase by $1.0 million each year across FY 2025 through FY 2028. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Program and the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund within the Department of Commerce, requiring the department to administer the program, adopt regulations, and award grants.
Commerce is authorized to enter into a memorandum of understanding with a Title 10 State-chartered corporation, such as TEDCO, to administer the grant program.
Commerce is authorized to enter into a memorandum of understanding with a Title 10 State-chartered corporation, such as MEDCO, to administer the grant program.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $1,000,000 appropriation to the Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, including implementing the mandated annual $1,000,000 appropriation from FY 2025 through FY 2028.
The bill specifies that the State Treasurer must hold the newly created Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund separately and invest the money of the fund.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the newly created special, nonlapsing Industry 4.0 Technology Grant Fund.

Synopsis: Expanding the forms of financial assistance available under the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program; altering eligibility requirements for projects that may receive financial assistance under the Program; altering the time period when applications may be submitted under the Program; repealing certain restrictions on the amount of financial assistance that may be provided under the Program; etc.
Title: Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development by expanding eligible forms of financial assistance to include loans, guarantees, and other credit enhancements; allowing applications when a qualified project is proposed rather than completed; expanding program eligibility to sustainable communities; altering definition criteria for affordable housing and eligible expenses; and removing statutory caps on financial assistance amounts.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Affordable housing developers, individuals and business entities constructing or rehabilitating properties in low-income census tracts and designated sustainable communities, and low-income homebuyers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State operations or finances, as funding for the program has not been budgeted since its enactment. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program, which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The department is tasked with developing regulations, revising application processes, and overseeing the distribution of expanded forms of financial assistance.

Synopsis: Establishing the Human-Relevant Research Fund under the administration of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to provide grants and loans to promote State-funded research intended to develop human-relevant alternatives to using nonhuman animals in medical and product testing and research; requiring, beginning January 15, 2024, research facilities that engage in animal testing or research to pay a contribution, based on a certain number of animals, to the Secretary of Health; providing a civil penalty for a violation of the Act; etc.
Title: Animal Testing and Research - Human-Relevant Research Funding and Animal Testing and Research Contributions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
