bill_summary: Establishes the Human-Relevant Research Fund administered by the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to award grants and loans for research developing alternatives to animal testing. It requires research facilities in Maryland submitting USDA APHIS Form 7023 to pay an annual tiered contribution to the Maryland Department of Health based on the number of animals used, which is then distributed into the fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) and the Maryland Department of Health (MDH)
stakeholders: Research facilities and universities conducting medical or product testing using animals, researchers and businesses developing human-relevant animal testing alternatives, and higher education institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Human-Relevant Research Fund increase by up to $915,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 from facility contributions. Higher education expenditures increase by $120,000 annually across four public universities required to pay contributions. Local expenditures increase by $5,000 annually for the Community College of Baltimore County. MDH can absorb its administrative duties with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the Human-Relevant Research Fund, establishing a grant and loan program to fund human-relevant animal testing alternatives research, contracting with an independent scientific review board, adopting regulations, and submitting annual progress reports.

The Secretary of Health is responsible for collecting the required annual contributions from qualifying animal research facilities in the state and distributing those funds to the Human-Relevant Research Fund.

Four USM constituent institutions (Towson University, Frostburg State University, University of Maryland College Park, and University of Maryland Baltimore) are research facilities subject to annual contribution payments totaling $120,000.

The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold and invest the Human-Relevant Research Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund, with interest earnings credited back to the fund under State Finance and Procurement § 6-226.
The Comptroller is statutorily directed to account for the newly established Human-Relevant Research Fund.
The Governor receives an annual report on the progress of research funded under the program and is authorized to include an appropriation to the Human-Relevant Research Fund in the state budget bill.

Synopsis: Specifying that a certain surviving spouse of a member of the armed forces is eligible to apply for a scholarship under the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program if the service member died, suffered a service connected disability, or was declared to be a prisoner of war or missing in action under certain circumstances.
Title: Higher Education – Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program – Surviving Spouses of Service Members

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program to include surviving spouses of U.S. armed forces service members who died as a result of military service after December 7, 1941, or who were declared prisoners of war or missing in action during the Vietnam conflict.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and eligible postsecondary institutions
stakeholders: Surviving spouses of U.S. Armed Forces service members who died due to military service after December 7, 1941, or were declared POW/MIA in the Vietnam conflict, as well as postsecondary institutions in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and Edward T. Conroy and Jean B. Cryor Scholarship Fund special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an estimated $7,700 per award annually. The total annual cost is indeterminate because the number of additional recipients cannot be reliably estimated. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary regulatory and coordinating agency responsible for administering state financial aid programs, including verifying eligible student numbers and allocating funds to postsecondary institutions for the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program.

As the state's postsecondary coordinating body, the commission oversees the distribution of state financial aid and scholarship awards, including those under the Edward T. Conroy Memorial Scholarship Program.

USM institutions enroll eligible students, verify applicant eligibility, and award the scholarships. Furthermore, scholarship award amounts are statutory benchmarks linked to resident undergraduate tuition at USM institutions.

DVMF advocates for and supports active-duty service members, veterans, and their surviving families in accessing education and state-sponsored benefits, which includes communicating eligibility for programs like the Conroy Scholarship.
As a public four-year university, Morgan State University processes applications, verifies eligibility, and disburses Conroy scholarship funds to enrolled students.
As a public institution of higher education in Maryland, St. Mary's College of Maryland verifies eligibility and administers scholarship awards to qualified enrolled students.

Synopsis: Authorizing an account holder who is the victim of abuse to terminate, and requiring a utility to allow for the termination of, the account holder's future liability under a utility contract if the account holder provides the utility with certain written notice requesting termination of the account holder's future liability under the contract; requiring a utility to allow an account holder who terminates a utility contract under the Act to open a new utility account notwithstanding a certain account balance or arrearage; etc.
Title: Utility Account Holders - Victims of Abuse - Protections

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Domestic Violence -see also- Child Abuse & Neglect
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: Authorizes a utility account holder who is a victim of abuse to terminate their future liability under a utility contract upon providing written notice and documentation, such as a protective order or a report by a qualified third party. Utilities must limit the account holder's liability to charges incurred through the billing cycle in which notice is submitted and allow the individual to establish a new account at a new premises regardless of any outstanding balance or arrearage from the prior premises.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Utility account holders who are victims of abuse, domestic violence survivors, and utility providers (electric, gas, water, and sewage companies).
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, with no material effect on State finances or operations. Local utilities can also manage the requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary state regulator of electric, gas, water, and sewage disposal utilities subject to the bill's requirements and is responsible for ensuring utility compliance with the Public Utilities Article.

The Office of the People's Counsel advocates on behalf of Maryland's residential utility consumers, including protections and policies affecting utility contracts, customer billing, and account liability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy coordinates victim services and public safety policies across the state, which intersect directly with protections and resources for victims of domestic abuse.

Synopsis: Requiring that the credential reappointment process for physician staff included in certain minimum standards for hospitals licensed in the State be conducted in accordance with standards of the accreditation body that accredits a hospital, rather than every 2 years.
Title: Hospital Credentialing - Reappointment Process for Physician Staff - Modification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Modifies the minimum credentialing standards for hospital licensure in Maryland by requiring the formal physician reappointment process to be conducted according to the standards of the hospital's accreditation body rather than on a mandated two-year schedule.
responsible_party: Secretary of Health (Maryland Department of Health)
stakeholders: Hospitals licensed in Maryland, physicians employed by or holding staff privileges at Maryland hospitals, and hospital accreditation bodies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill has no effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees hospital licensing and regulatory enforcement under Health-General § 19-319. The bill alters the statutory minimum standards that the Secretary of Health must enforce regarding hospital physician credentialing and reappointment processes.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "personal information" for purposes of certain provisions of the Public Information Act to include an individual's personal e-mail address; requiring certain custodians to deny inspection of certain records of personal e-mail addresses and telephone numbers except under certain circumstances; and requiring certain custodians to allow inspection of certain records of business e-mail addresses under the same circumstances as inspection of certain records of business addresses and telephone numbers.
Title: Public Information Act - Inspection of E-Mail Addresses and Telephone Numbers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of "personal information" under the Maryland Public Information Act to include an individual's email address. It establishes rules requiring public record custodians to deny inspection of personal email addresses and personal telephone numbers of public school students and government employees, while permitting inspection of business email addresses for notaries public and licensed professionals under specified conditions.
responsible_party: Custodians of public records in State and local governmental units
stakeholders: State and local government employees, public school students and their families, notaries public, licensed professionals, and individuals submitting Public Information Act requests
fiscal_impact_summary: Any impact on Public Information Act-related activities is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is responsible for the commissioning and administration of notaries public. The bill directly amends § 4-332 of the General Provisions Article regarding the inspection and disclosure of notary public records, including business and personal email addresses.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission is explicitly named in § 4-313 as an authorized entity permitted to inspect a student's personal email address and telephone number, and is subject to statutory prohibitions against commercial use and redisclosure of that data.

The Department of Education oversees the state's public school system, and the bill amends § 4-313 concerning custodians' duties to deny or permit inspection of school district student records, specifically adding protections for personal email addresses.

The Department of Labor is the primary licensing agency for occupational and professional licensing boards. The bill amends § 4-333 regarding the public inspection and disclosure of occupational and professional licensees' business email addresses.
The Office of the Attorney General advises state agencies on compliance with the Public Information Act (PIA) and maintains and publishes the official Maryland Public Information Act Manual.

As the central personnel and human resources agency for State government, DBM is affected by § 4-331, which requires custodians to shield State employees' personal email addresses and telephone numbers from public inspection.

Synopsis: Altering the grounds on which a deputy sheriff having a rank of major or below in Washington County may be discharged after 2 years of continuous employment; providing that a special deputy sheriff in Washington County is not a State employee for certain purposes; authorizing sworn deputy sheriffs at the rank of sergeant and below and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below to engage in collective bargaining with the Washington County Sheriff and the County Administrator; etc.
Title: Washington County - Deputy Sheriffs and Correctional Deputies - Employment Conditions and Collective Bargaining

NarrowSubjects.Name: Termination of Employment -see also- Work, Labor, and Employ
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes full-time sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at the rank of sergeant and below in the Washington County Sheriff's Office to collectively bargain for wages and benefits with the Sheriff and County Administrator. It establishes procedures for union representation, negotiation, and agreement ratification, prohibits strikes, specifies that additional funding remains subject to County Commissioners' approval, and alters discharge grounds for tenured deputy sheriffs to police misconduct.
responsible_party: Washington County Sheriff's Office and the Washington County Administrator
stakeholders: Full-time sworn deputy sheriffs and correctional deputies at or below the rank of sergeant in Washington County, special deputy sheriffs, and the Washington County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Washington County expenditures may increase minimally due to potential shared costs for American Arbitration Association third-party neutral elections during certification disputes. Any wage and benefit changes resulting from collective bargaining are subject to approval by the County Commissioners and are not anticipated to materially impact county finances. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly clarifies that special deputy sheriffs in Washington County are not considered State employees for the purpose of employee benefits, which falls under DBM's purview as the central personnel agency managing State employee benefits and policies.

The bill specifies that special deputy sheriffs in Washington County are not employees of the State for the purpose of employment security (unemployment insurance), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Labor.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a Class B-GSF (golf simulator facility) license to a golf simulator facility under certain circumstances; authorizing the license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption under certain circumstances; requiring the license holder to submit an annual gross sales report to the Board before a license may be renewed; and establishing an annual license fee of $1,500.
Title: Frederick County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Golf Simulator Facility
bill_summary: Establishes a Class B-GSF (golf simulator facility) alcoholic beverages license in Frederick County, allowing qualifying facilities with at least five simulator bays to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption, subject to specified food availability and sales percentage requirements.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Golf simulator facility operators, small businesses, patrons, and the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Frederick County revenues increase by $2,250 in fiscal 2024 for each new Class B-GSF license issued (a $1,500 annual license fee plus a $750 application fee) and by $1,500 annually thereafter for each renewal. Any additional local enforcement activity can be absorbed within existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees tax collection and the general regulation of the state's alcohol industry. While this bill specifically authorizes the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners to issue a local golf simulator facility license and has no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's broader alcoholic beverages regulatory framework.

Synopsis: Increasing, from $8 to $10, the auctioneer's fee for the tax sale of property in Garrett County for each property sold.
Title: Garrett County - Tax Sales - Auctioneer Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: Increases the allowable auctioneer's fee included as an expense in tax sales of property in Garrett County from $8 to $10 for each property sold.
responsible_party: Garrett County Government
stakeholders: Garrett County tax sale auctioneers, property tax sale purchasers, and delinquent property owners in Garrett County
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Garrett County finances are not materially affected, as the increased fee is an expense of the sale paid by the property purchaser.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the allowable auctioneer fee for local property tax sales in Garrett County. The Administrative Office of the Courts is consulted regarding tax sale procedures and judicial foreclosure of the right of redemption, but the bill has no material operational or fiscal impact on the court system.

Synopsis: Updating certain provisions of law regarding Baltimore City alcoholic beverages districts to refer to the Legislative Districting Plan of 2022; and requiring the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to grant a certain exemption to certain persons under certain circumstances.
Title: Baltimore City – Alcoholic Beverages Districts – Legislative Districting Plan References
bill_summary: Updates statutory references defining Baltimore City's alcoholic beverages district boundaries to align with the 2022 Legislative Districting Plan instead of the 2012 plan, while providing an exemption to grandfather certain license holders who received approval on or before February 1, 2022, and have continuously owned the premises.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders, applicants, and establishments (such as restaurants and bars) operating within Baltimore City legislative districts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and a minimal local fiscal impact on Baltimore City, as the adjustments are technical in nature and do not directly affect city operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates statutory references to Baltimore City alcoholic beverages districts based on the 2022 Legislative Districting Plan. While implementation is handled locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, the Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcoholic beverage industry across the state.

Synopsis: Altering the timing of the annual election of the officers of the Talbot County Board of Education to be at its last meeting at the end of each calendar year, or at the meeting in December each year.
Title: Talbot County - Board of Education - Election of Officers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting

bill_summary: Alters the timing of the annual election of the president and vice president of the Talbot County Board of Education, requiring the election to occur at the last meeting at the end of each calendar year or at the meeting in December, rather than at the first meeting at the beginning of each calendar year.
responsible_party: Talbot County Board of Education
stakeholders: Members of the Talbot County Board of Education and Talbot County Public Schools
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The alteration is procedural in nature and does not affect Talbot County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the internal election timing of officers for the Talbot County Board of Education, which operates as one of the 24 local school systems under the general policy oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education.

Synopsis: Altering the requirements for the subject matter of continuing education courses for licensees issued an initial license by the Real Estate Commission.
Title: Real Estate Brokers, Salespersons, and Associate Brokers - Continuing Education Courses - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Landlords and Tenants -see also- Eviction; Leases & Rent etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Establishes specific continuing education course requirements for individuals initially licensed as real estate brokers, salespersons, or associate brokers by the State Real Estate Commission, requiring coursework in contract writing, brokerage relationships, advertising, escrow funds, common ownership communities, property management, ethics, and real estate financing.
responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
stakeholders: Initially licensed real estate brokers, associate brokers, salespersons, and real estate education course providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $42,600 in FY 2024 for information technology system changes ($25,000) and consulting costs ($17,600) to track and approve new course requirements. Ongoing consulting costs range between $2,200 and $2,500 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2028. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission is an occupational licensing unit housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department is directly responsible for administering and enforcing the new continuing education curriculum requirements, which require IT system modifications and consulting expenditures.

Synopsis: Requiring the Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to confer to identify ways the Comptroller could collaborate with the Department to enhance access to certain property tax benefits administered by the Department; and requiring the Comptroller and the Department to submit a joint report of their findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Comptroller and State Department of Assessments and Taxation - Enhancing Access to Property Tax Benefits - Report
bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) to confer and submit a joint report recommending ways to collaborate, raise awareness, enhance access, and simplify application processes for state property tax benefits, including the homeowners' tax credit, renters' tax credit, homestead tax credit, and property tax exemptions for disabled veterans and surviving spouses.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland and State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland property owners, homeowners, renters, disabled veterans, surviving military spouses eligible for property tax credits or exemptions, and state tax administrators.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $18,000 in FY 2024 for SDAT to hire a consultant to assist with the study and report. The Comptroller's Office can complete the requirements using existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Comptroller to confer with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation during the 2023 legislative interim, identify collaboration opportunities to improve access and streamline applications for property tax benefits, and submit a joint report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for a real estate appraisal license and for a certificate for residential or general real estate appraisal to include completion of certain criteria in the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal program.
Title: Real Estate Appraisers - Licensing and Certification - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Establishes an alternative pathway for individuals to qualify for a real estate appraiser license or residential/general real estate appraisal certification by allowing completion of the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) program criteria in lieu of completing 1,000 or 1,500 supervised trainee hours.
responsible_party: State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: Prospective and current real estate appraisers, appraisal trainees, certified appraisers, and consumers of real estate appraisal services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures are likely to increase due to an influx of new applicants qualifying for licensure and certification, but a reliable dollar estimate is not feasible. The Commission is required by statute to adjust licensing fees to approximate operating expenses. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies, and Home Inspectors within its Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill alters licensing and certification qualification requirements by providing an alternative pathway through the Practical Applications of Real Estate Appraisal (PAREA) program, directly impacting the department's licensing operations, fee revenues, and regulatory enforcement.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of County Commissioners for Garrett County to meet at least twice a month; authorizing the Board to hold public meetings in person or through live video streaming; and prohibiting the Board from meeting solely through live video streaming for more than two consecutive meetings without a formal declaration of a state of emergency.
Title: Garrett County - Board of County Commissioners - Meetings
bill_summary: This bill alters the meeting schedule requirements for the Garrett County Board of County Commissioners from weekly to at least twice a month. It permits public meetings to be held in person or via live video streaming, but prohibits the Board from holding more than two consecutive meetings solely through live video streaming unless a formal state of emergency has been declared.
responsible_party: Garrett County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Garrett County Commissioners and Garrett County residents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact, and altering the meeting schedule of the Garrett County Commissioners will not affect local county finances.

Synopsis: Repealing certain requirements that the Maryland Transit Administration increase fares for certain transit services according to the Consumer Price Index; and repealing certain provisions prohibiting the Administration from increasing fares under certain circumstances.
Title: Maryland Transit Administration – Fare Price Requirements – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill repeals the statutory requirements that the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) increase base fare prices every two years and commuter zone fares every five years based on the Consumer Price Index and other factors, while preserving the MTA's general authority to modify transit fares after holding a public hearing.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
stakeholders: Transit riders and commuters utilizing Maryland Transit Administration services (including local buses, Light Rail, Metro subway, commuter buses, MARC trains, and mobility/paratransit vehicles)
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (special fund) revenues decrease by as much as $6.9 million in FY 2024, $7.1 million in FY 2025, $18.1 million in FY 2026, $17.6 million in FY 2027, and $19.8 million in FY 2028 due to foregone mandated fare increases, though the loss could be mitigated if MTA uses its discretionary authority to adjust fares after public hearings. Expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly affects MTA's operations and revenues by repealing the statutory requirement for biennial and five-year CPI-based fare increases, restoring discretionary fare-setting authority subject to public hearings.

MTA is a modal administration within MDOT, and the repeal of mandated fare increases significantly impacts the Department's Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues by an estimated $6.9 million to $19.8 million annually.

Synopsis: Altering the uses of the Historic Preservation Loan Fund; and authorizing the Maryland Historic Trust to transfer funds from the Fund to a qualified cooperating nonprofit organization to pay for the acquisition, restoration, or rehabilitation of certain historic properties, to provide loans for the acquisition, rehabilitation, restoration, or refinancing of certain properties, and for necessary administrative and programmatic expenses.
Title: Maryland Historic Trust - Historic Preservation Loan Fund - Qualified Cooperating Nonprofit Organizations - Transfers

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill expands the allowable uses of the Maryland Historical Trust's Historic Preservation Loan Fund to permit transfers of funds to qualified cooperating nonprofit organizations. Such organizations may use the funds to acquire, rehabilitate, or restore historic properties; provide loans to nonprofits, local governments, businesses, and certain individuals; and cover administrative costs, subject to competitive application processes and annual reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust (within the Maryland Department of Planning)
stakeholders: Qualified statewide historic preservation nonprofit organizations, historic property owners, and individuals or entities seeking financing for historic preservation projects.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures may increase and special fund revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2024, to the extent that funds from the Historic Preservation Loan Fund are transferred directly to qualified nonprofit organizations rather than issued as revolving loans that replenish the fund through repayments. Specific dollar amounts cannot be reliably determined. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) is an agency within the Maryland Department of Planning. The bill directly alters the allowable uses of MHT's Historic Preservation Loan Fund, authorizing MHT to transfer funds to a qualified cooperating nonprofit organization for historic property preservation and loan programs.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland to study the adequacy of trauma center funding across the State for operating, capital, and workforce costs; and requiring the Commission to reports its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2023.
Title: Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland to evaluate the adequacy of funding for trauma centers across the State regarding operating, capital, and workforce costs, and requires the Commission to submit findings and recommendations by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems and the Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Trauma centers, trauma physicians and healthcare workers, emergency medical services providers, and patients requiring trauma care in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected, as the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS) and the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) can provide staff using existing budgeted resources, and any member expense reimbursements are minimal. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is a primary implementing agency; its Executive Director serves as co-chair of the Commission, and the agency is responsible for jointly staffing the Commission and providing representation on it.

MHCC is a primary implementing agency; its Executive Director serves as co-chair, the agency jointly staffs the Commission, provides representation, and co-administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund under review.
The Secretary of Health or designee is a member of the Commission and is charged with appointing numerous members representing emergency services, commissions, and trauma centers across the state.
HSCRC is designated to have a representative appointed to the Commission and is directly involved as co-administrator of the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund examined by the study.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Commission to Study Trauma Center Funding in Maryland, a temporary executive study body tasked with studying trauma center operating, capital, and workforce costs and reporting findings.
The Commission is mandated to submit its final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Making certain provisions of law governing cemeteries applicable to pet cemeteries; providing that a certain registered cemeterian, registered crematory operator, or permit holder who sells or offers to sell to the public certain services for pet remains owes a duty of perpetual care for the cemetery in which certain pet remains are interred; and requiring the Director of the Office of Cemetery Oversight to adopt regulations to enforce certain provisions of the Act.
Title: Cemeteries - Interment - Pet Remains
bill_summary: Expands cemetery regulations to include pet remains, extending the definition of interment to include pets and requiring preneed burial contracts to include pet information when applicable. It establishes that registered cemeterians, crematory operators, or permit holders who offer pet cremation or burial services with stated or implied perpetual care owe a duty of perpetual care for the cemetery where pet remains are interred, and authorizes the Office of Cemetery Oversight to adopt enforcement regulations.
responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight within the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Pet owners, pet cemetery and crematory operators, registered cemeterians, permit holders, and burial goods businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State fiscal impact is anticipated to be minimal. The Office of Cemetery Oversight can adopt regulations and enforce provisions using existing budgeted resources. Special fund revenues may experience a minimal increase to the extent pet cemeteries register with the office. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO), which is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Director of OCO is tasked with adopting regulations to enforce the bill's provisions regarding pet remains, preneed burial contracts, and perpetual care requirements.

Synopsis: Extending until fiscal year 2028 the appropriation of $500,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund that the Governor is required to include in the annual budget bill for the operation of the replica sailing vessel known as the Pride of Baltimore II.
Title: Pride of Baltimore II - Appropriations - Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill extends the statutory requirement for the Governor to include an appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund in the annual State budget for the operation of the replica sailing vessel Pride of Baltimore II through fiscal year 2028, and continues annual reporting requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Operators of the Pride of Baltimore II, tourists, students, and citizens of Maryland participating in or benefiting from historical maritime education and tourism promotion.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund special fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from FY 2024 through FY 2028, reflecting discretionary funding assumed in FY 2024 and a mandated appropriation from FY 2025 through FY 2028. State revenues are not affected, and there is no direct impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $500,000 from the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) from FY 2024 through FY 2028 for the operation of the Pride of Baltimore II, and requires the recipient entity to submit an annual expenditure, itinerary, and business plan report directly to the department.

DBM is responsible for the preparation and management of the annual state budget and must ensure the mandated appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund is properly incorporated into the state budget.
The statute explicitly requires the Governor to include a mandated appropriation of $500,000 in the annual state budget for each fiscal year from 2024 through 2028.

Synopsis: Requiring in Frederick County a license holder to frame and conspicuously display an alcoholic beverages license on the licensed premises.
Title: Frederick County – Alcoholic Beverages Licenses – Display of License
bill_summary: Alters the license display requirements for alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County by requiring that the license be framed and conspicuously displayed, removing the statewide requirement that it must be framed specifically under glass.
responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders in Frederick County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Frederick County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry. Although this legislation specifically affects local Frederick County license framing requirements and has no direct state fiscal impact, it relates generally to alcohol licensing and regulatory standards under the Alcoholic Beverages Article.

Synopsis: Increasing the total amount of credits against the State income tax that the Maryland Higher Education Commission may approve in a taxable year for certain individuals with certain student loan debt amounts; requiring the Commission to reserve a certain amount of the tax credits that the Commission is authorized to approve for certain graduates; extending, from 2 years to 3 years, the period of time that an individual who claims the credit has to prove that they used the credit to repay the individual's student loan debt; etc.
Title: Income Tax - Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill increases the annual cap on the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit from $9 million to $18 million, reserving $9 million of the total credits for State employees with priority given to those who graduated from Maryland higher education institutions where at least 40% of attendees are eligible for federal Pell Grants. The bill also extends the deadline for recipients to prove they used the credit for student loan repayment from two to three years and requires enhanced outreach to new graduates and scholarship recipients.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: State employees, individuals with qualifying student loan debt (especially graduates of Maryland colleges with at least 40% Pell Grant eligibility), and scholarship recipients.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $9.0 million annually beginning in fiscal year 2024 due to the expanded personal income tax credit cap (assumed in the FY 2024 budget). Expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency for the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit. The bill increases the cap on tax credits MHEC can approve from $9 million to $18 million, requires MHEC to reserve $9 million for State employees with specific prioritization criteria, directs its Office of Student Financial Assistance to conduct outreach to scholarship recipients, and requires annual reporting to the Governor and General Assembly.
Identical listing for the Maryland Higher Education Commission, which is the primary regulatory and administering body for the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit program altered by the bill.

The Comptroller administers State personal income tax returns, processes tax credits and refunds, and oversees tax credit recapture. The expansion of the credit results in a direct State general fund revenue reduction of $9 million annually beginning in FY 2024.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission is mandated to submit an annual report by January 1 to the Governor regarding applicant numbers, credit amounts awarded, and recipient demographic and geographic data.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to issue an apprentice hunting license to a person under the age of 17 years who has previously been issued an apprentice hunting license under certain circumstances.
Title: Natural Resources – Apprentice Hunting License – Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue a second or subsequent apprentice hunting license to individuals under the age of 17, provided the applicant repeats the required online or electronic course in firearm competency and hunter safety.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters under the age of 17 seeking to renew or obtain additional apprentice hunting licenses, along with their adult mentors and supervisors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. Any impact on hunting license fee revenue is anticipated to be minimal, and the Department of Natural Resources can implement the changes using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is directly responsible for administering hunting licenses and hunter safety education in Maryland, including issuing apprentice hunting licenses to eligible individuals under age 17 and updating necessary regulations.

Synopsis: Eliminating requirements for collection agencies and certain non-depository financial institutions to maintain separate licenses for branch locations and authorizing them to conduct business at multiple licensed locations under a single license; and altering certain other requirements and provisions governing the licensing and regulation of collection agencies and certain non-depository financial institutions, including applications, assessments, and bond requirements.
Title: Financial Regulation - Modernizing Licensing of Non-Depository Institutions and Elimination of Branch License Requirements

Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
