bill_summary: This bill modernizes the licensing structure for collection agencies and various non-depository financial institutions in Maryland by eliminating the requirement to obtain separate licenses for each branch location. Instead, it allows these institutions to conduct business across multiple locations under a single license registered in the Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System and Registry (NMLS). The bill also updates requirements concerning trade names, examination procedures, annual fee assessments, and surety bonds.
responsible_party: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (Department of Labor) and the State Collection Agency Licensing Board
stakeholders: Non-depository financial institutions operating in Maryland (including consumer lenders, sales finance companies, mortgage lenders, mortgage loan originators, check cashers, money transmitters, debt management companies, and collection agencies) and Maryland consumers using their financial services.
fiscal_impact_summary: Non-depository Special Fund revenues decrease by approximately $3,000,000 annually beginning in FY 2024 due to the elimination of branch location licensing fees. Special fund expenditures are not materially affected due to offsetting administrative efficiencies. OCFR anticipates fund reserves will sustain operations through at least FY 2027 or FY 2028 before any authorized annual assessments on licensees might be needed to replenish the fund. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the licensing, assessments, and regulatory requirements of non-depository financial institutions and collection agencies administered by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation and the State Collection Agency Licensing Board, which are housed within the Department of Labor.
The bill explicitly designates the State Treasurer as the custodian of the newly codified Non-Depository Special Fund, responsible for receiving, depositing, and investing moneys for the fund.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, enforces consumer protection laws related to financial institutions and debt collection, and was consulted on the implementation and policy impacts of the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing rules governing the exercise of the decanting power to distribute the property of a first trust to one or more second trusts or to modify the terms of a first trust; and providing for the retroactive application of the Act.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Trusts - Decanting (Maryland Trust Decanting Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Enacts the Maryland Trust Decanting Act, authorizing trustees and other authorized fiduciaries to exercise decanting power to distribute assets from an existing trust into one or more second trusts or modify the terms of the existing trust. The bill establishes notice requirements, limits on fiduciary compensation and modifications, court oversight procedures, protections for tax benefits and charitable interests, and specific provisions for special needs trusts and pet trusts, applying retroactively to qualifying trusts.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Courts with jurisdiction over trusts) and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Trustees, trust settlors, trust beneficiaries (including individuals with disabilities and charitable organizations), powerholders, and estate planning professionals
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to have a material, direct effect on State or local government operations or finances. Any impact on small businesses (such as law firms or private trust companies) is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Office of the Attorney General, conferring upon it the rights of a qualified beneficiary to represent and protect charitable interests whenever a trust containing a determinable charitable interest is subject to decanting. Fiduciaries must provide notice to the Attorney General, and the second trust cannot diminish charitable interests or alter charitable purposes without the Attorney General's consent or court approval.

The bill establishes judicial procedures and authorizes courts with jurisdiction over trusts to hear applications, provide instructions, approve or invalidate exercises of decanting powers, and appoint special fiduciaries to evaluate or execute trust decanting.

The Register of Wills administers Maryland estate and trust-related probate filings and was consulted for the fiscal note, though the operational impact on the office is minimal as decanting primarily occurs without court intervention or is handled in circuit courts.

Synopsis: Requiring that each memorandum of understanding establishing a school in the Pathways in Technology Early College High (P-TECH) School Program ensures that each P-TECH student receives a high school diploma immediately following completion of high school graduation requirements.
Title: Pathways in Technology Early College High (P–TECH) School Program – High School Diplomas

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires each memorandum of understanding establishing a Pathways in Technology Early College High (P-TECH) school to ensure that students receive a high school diploma immediately upon completing all high school graduation requirements, regardless of whether they have completed the associate degree pathway sequence, without altering existing education funding formulas.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: P-TECH students, local school systems, community college partners, and industry partners
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $14,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland State Department of Education to update the student accountability system to track P-TECH graduates continuing in the program. Local school system expenditures may increase minimally for similar IT system adjustments. State and local education funding revenues and expenditures are not materially affected because the bill explicitly does not alter education funding calculations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the administration of the P-TECH program and high school graduation requirements overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). MSDE also incurs a fiscal impact of $14,000 in FY 2024 to update its student accountability system so that P-TECH students who graduate high school early remain eligible for program funding in years five and six.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission oversees policies related to postsecondary education, including community college partners participating in the P-TECH program; however, the bill specifically specifies that higher education funding formulas are not altered and assigns no new responsibilities to the Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation.
Title: Maryland African American Museum Corporation - Board of Directors - Membership

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill alters the composition of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation by reducing the total number of members from 37 to 25, adding appointments by the President of the Senate and the Speaker of the House, and modifying the number and criteria of gubernatorial appointments.
responsible_party: Maryland African American Museum Corporation
stakeholders: Members of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation, the Reginald F. Lewis Museum of Maryland African American History and Culture, the Commission on African American History and Culture, and Morgan State University.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 690 directly alters the composition and structure of the Board of Directors of the Maryland African American Museum Corporation, reducing its membership from 37 to 25 members.
The bill explicitly mandates that one member of the MAAMC Board of Directors must be a representative of Morgan State University, approved by the university's Board of Regents.
The bill alters the Governor's statutory appointment authority regarding the MAAMC Board of Directors, modifying the number and categories of gubernatorial appointees.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state boards, including the 22 gubernatorial appointees designated under this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing that a county or a municipal corporation has the authority to approve or deny any local permit required under a certificate of public convenience and necessity issued by the Public Service Commission for generating stations, transmission lines, and qualified generator lead lines; requiring a county or municipal corporation to approve or deny the local permits in a certain manner; prohibiting a county or municipal corporation from conditioning the approval of the local permits on certain approvals; etc.
Title: Public Service Commission – Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity – Local Permits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: This bill establishes that Maryland counties and municipalities have the authority to approve or deny local permits required under a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) issued by the Public Service Commission for generating stations, transmission lines, and qualified generator lead lines. It requires local governments to process these permits within a reasonable time and under non-preempted local laws, while prohibiting them from conditioning permit approval on conditional use, special exception, or floating zone approvals.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission and local county and municipal governments
stakeholders: County and municipal governments, energy facility developers and utilities seeking CPCNs (especially renewable energy projects), and local residents in affected project areas
fiscal_impact_summary: State government finances and operations are not directly affected. Local government finances and operations are affected to the extent that counties and municipalities must process permits required under a CPCN within a reasonable time and without prohibited zoning conditions; the overall fiscal impact on any particular local government is likely minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary state entity responsible for issuing Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) for power generating stations and transmission lines. The bill directly relates to the CPCN process and defines the relationship between PSC-issued certificates and local government permit approvals.

DNR coordinates the state's environmental review for power plants and transmission lines undergoing the CPCN process through its Power Plant Research Program, and served as an information source on the bill.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the State Board of Pharmacy to include a registered pharmacy technician; authorizing a licensed pharmacist, under certain circumstances, to delegate the entry of certain data into databases or patient charts to be performed at a remote location to a registered pharmacy technician and a registered pharmacy intern; prohibiting registered pharmacy technicians and pharmacy technician trainees from making decisions requiring the professional judgment of a pharmacist; etc.
Title: State Board of Pharmacy - Board Membership, Delegated Pharmacy Acts, and Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: House Bill 693 alters the composition of the State Board of Pharmacy to add a registered pharmacy technician member, allows pharmacists to delegate remote prescription-related data entry to registered pharmacy technicians and interns, prohibits pharmacy technicians and trainees from making decisions requiring professional pharmacist judgment, permits registered pharmacy technicians to administer specified vaccines to adults of certain ages, and extends the termination date of the Board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act to July 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, registered pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technician trainees, pharmacy interns, independent and chain pharmacies, and patients receiving pharmacy or vaccination services in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Pharmacy are maintained through FY 2025 due to the sunset extension. Special fund expenditures may increase minimally to cover per diem and related expenses for the additional board member, while other administrative duties can be absorbed with existing resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Pharmacy is a licensing and regulatory health occupations board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly alters the board's membership, extends its statutory termination date under sunset review, and modifies regulatory practice scopes for pharmacy technicians.

The bill alters the statutory composition of the State Board of Pharmacy by adding a registered pharmacy technician member, which will be vetted and processed through the Governor's Office of Appointments.
The Governor is statutorily tasked with appointing the newly created registered pharmacy technician seat on the State Board of Pharmacy with the advice of the Secretary of Health.

Synopsis: Authorizing the allocation of grants from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund for certain business and workforce development activities.
Title: Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund - Allocation of Grants (Rural Communities Improvement Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Expands the allowable grant uses from the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF) under the rural entrepreneurship grant category to include agricultural development, cooperative development, and workforce development activities.
responsible_party: Rural Maryland Council
stakeholders: Rural Maryland communities, regional councils, agricultural businesses, business cooperatives, community colleges, workforce development organizations, and rural entrepreneurs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect overall State revenues or expenditures because it only modifies allowable grant categories within the existing fund formula, though grant funds may be reallocated among recipients such as community colleges and higher education institutions. The fiscal 2024 State budget as introduced includes $9.0 million in general funds for the Rural Maryland Council to be distributed through the formula.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Rural Maryland Council (RMC) administers the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund (RMPIF). The bill directly modifies the allocation categories and eligible grant uses under RMPIF to include agricultural development, cooperative development, and workforce development.

The Rural Maryland Council is administratively housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA). Furthermore, the bill explicitly broadens the grant category under RMPIF to cover agricultural development alongside entrepreneurship.

The bill expands allowable grant activities under the fund to include workforce development, specifically training workers to meet the skill needs of local employers and supporting local workforce boards.

The bill supports rural business cooperative development, feasibility studies, and entrepreneurship initiatives that intersect with the Department of Commerce's rural business development and economic expansion objectives.
The bill authorizes RMPIF grants to support workforce training and educational programs through institutions of higher education, community colleges, and career and technical education centers.

Synopsis: Establishing the Black Bass Conservation Fund in the Department of Natural Resources to further black bass management; requiring the Department to administer the Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund; requiring interest earnings of the Fund to be credited to the Fund; and requiring the Department to establish a process through which an individual who purchases a certain license online to make a voluntary donation to the Black Bass Conservation Fund.
Title: Natural Resources - Black Bass Conservation Fund - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Black Bass Conservation Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Department of Natural Resources to support black bass stocking, habitat enhancement, tournaments, and scientific conservation research. The fund is supported by voluntary monetary donations made by individuals purchasing certain recreational fishing licenses through the department's electronic licensing system, as well as interest earnings and any state appropriations.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Recreational anglers purchasing fishing licenses online, black bass tournament organizers, and conservation groups.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal year 2024 from voluntary donations and interest earnings. The Department of Natural Resources can implement the donation process and administer the fund with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary administering agency responsible for establishing the electronic donation process during fishing license purchases, managing the newly created Black Bass Conservation Fund, and deploying fund proceeds toward black bass stocking, habitat enhancement, and research.
The State Treasurer's Office is statutorily designated to hold the Black Bass Conservation Fund separately and invest its moneys, ensuring that interest earnings are credited to the fund.
The Comptroller of Maryland is required to account for the newly established Black Bass Conservation Fund within the state's accounting systems.

Synopsis: Authorizing the placement and use of a speed monitoring system at the intersection of Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) and Bonfield Avenue in Talbot County, subject to placement and signage requirements; requiring the fines collected by the Town of Oxford as a result of the speed monitoring system to be used to assist in covering the cost of roadway and pedestrian safety improvements in and around the intersection; etc.
Title: Talbot County – Speed Monitoring Systems – Intersection of Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) and Bonfield Avenue

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: Authorizes the placement and operation of one speed monitoring system at the intersection of Maryland Route 333 (Oxford Road) and Bonfield Avenue in Talbot County, requiring a proximate real-time speed display. Revenue generated from citations, after recovering local implementation and operating costs, must be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration to fund roadway and pedestrian safety improvements in and around that intersection.
responsible_party: Town of Oxford and the Maryland State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motorists traveling through Maryland Route 333 and Bonfield Avenue, pedestrians and local residents in Talbot County and the Town of Oxford, and the District Court.
fiscal_impact_summary: Local revenues and expenditures will increase between FY 2024 and FY 2029 to install and operate the speed camera system. After cost recovery, net citation fine revenues are remitted to the State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) for State Highway Administration pedestrian and roadway safety projects, resulting in a corresponding increase in TTF expenditures. District Court may see a negligible increase in general fund revenues from contested citations. An illustrative example in the fiscal note projects gross fine revenues of $71,175 in FY 2024, $94,900 annually for FY 2025–2028, and $23,725 in FY 2029, though actual amounts depend on violation volumes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires speed camera citation revenue remaining after local cost recovery to be distributed to the State Highway Administration to fund roadway and pedestrian safety improvements at the specified intersection.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, MDOT experiences an increase in Transportation Trust Fund revenues and corresponding capital/operating expenditures to execute the mandated safety improvements.
The bill explicitly requires excess speed monitoring fines collected by the Town of Oxford to be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration.
The District Court of Maryland is responsible for prescribing the uniform citation form and adjudicating any contested citations resulting from the newly authorized speed monitoring system.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, in consultation with the Secretary of Health, to set the compensation of certain Commission employees; requiring the Secretary of Budget and Management, in consultation with the Secretary of Health, to determine the positions for which the Commission may set compensation; and authorizing the Comptroller, the Treasurer, and the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scale of certain positions in their offices.
Title: Maryland Community Health Resources Commission and Offices of the Comptroller, Treasurer, and Attorney General - Compensation and Pay Scales of Employees
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 801

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, the Comptroller, the State Treasurer, and the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management (and the Secretary of Health for the Commission), to determine and set the compensation or pay scales for certain unique positions requiring specific skills or experience.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management, Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, Maryland Department of Health, Office of the Comptroller, Office of the State Treasurer, and Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Employees holding unique, specialized positions within the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, Office of the Comptroller, Office of the State Treasurer, and Office of the Attorney General.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission and general fund expenditures for the Comptroller's Office, Treasurer's Office, and Office of the Attorney General increase beginning as early as FY 2024 to fund higher compensation. Exact dollar amounts cannot be reliably estimated as they depend on determinations made by the respective agencies and the Secretary of Budget and Management. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Comptroller, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scales of unique positions requiring specific skills or experience within the Office of the Comptroller.

The bill directly authorizes the State Treasurer, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to establish pay scales for unique positions requiring specific skills or experience within the Office of the Treasurer.

The bill directly authorizes the Attorney General, in consultation with the Secretary of Budget and Management, to set the pay scales for qualifying unique positions within the Office of the Attorney General.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is statutorily required to determine, in consultation with each agency head and commission, which positions qualify for independent compensation and pay scale setting, directly impacting DBM's personnel management oversight.

The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission operates within MDH, and the Secretary of Health must be consulted regarding the determination and setting of employee compensation for eligible Commission positions.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to provide certain information regarding the acquisition of a nursing home to the Office of Health Care Quality; requiring the Secretary of Health to consider the information before taking action regarding licensure to operate a nursing home; and requiring the Commission, in consultation with certain stakeholders, to study and make recommendations regarding the expansion of the certificate of need program over acquisitions of nursing homes and report by December 1, 2023.
Title: Health Care Facilities - Nursing Homes - Acquisitions and Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Nursing Homes -see also- Continuing Care; Long-Term Care
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) to provide written findings and recommendations—including quality ratings, compliance history, inspection reports, and legal filings of the purchaser—to the Office of Health Care Quality when evaluating an acquisition or transfer of interest in a nursing home. It requires the Secretary of Health to consider this information before granting, denying, conditioning, or revoking a license to operate a nursing home. In addition, MHCC must conduct a study and report on expanding the Certificate of Need program to cover nursing home acquisitions.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland Department of Health (including the Office of Health Care Quality and Secretary of Health)
stakeholders: Nursing home owners, operators, prospective purchasers, nursing home residents, patient representatives, and organized labor
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled with existing budgeted resources by the Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) to provide written findings, quality ratings, and recommendations to the Office of Health Care Quality when evaluating notices of acquisition or transfer of nursing home interest, and requires MHCC to conduct a study and report on expanding the Certificate of Need program.

The bill requires the Secretary of Health and the Office of Health Care Quality (an agency within the Maryland Department of Health) to review and consider MHCC's findings and recommendations before approving, denying, conditioning, or revoking a nursing home operating license.

Synopsis: Establishing that every person, as a central component of an individual's rights to liberty and equality, has the fundamental right to reproductive freedom; and prohibiting the State from, directly or indirectly, denying, burdening, or abridging the right unless justified by a compelling State interest achieved by the least restrictive means.
Title: Declaration of Rights - Right to Reproductive Freedom
Status: Approved by the Governor, assigned a chapter number, enactment subject to constitutional referendum - Chapter 245

NarrowSubjects.Name: Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: Proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution to establish that every individual has a fundamental right to reproductive freedom, including the right to make decisions to prevent, continue, or end one's own pregnancy, and prohibits the State from burdening or abridging this right without a compelling State interest achieved by the least restrictive means.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, healthcare providers, and individuals seeking or receiving reproductive healthcare services
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact, nor any effect on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates submitting the proposed constitutional amendment to Maryland voters at the November 2024 general election, which the State Board of Elections is directly responsible for administering and placing on the ballot.

The Department of Health regulates health care professionals and services related to reproductive care and abortion, administers Medicaid coverage for reproductive health, and its regulatory authority is directly governed by the constitutional protections established under this amendment.

As the State's chief legal officer, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel on constitutional matters, assesses legal compliance across state agencies under the compelling interest standard, and defends state laws and constitutional provisions in court.

The bill explicitly requires that immediately after the election, all returns of the vote for and against the proposed amendment be made to the Governor in accordance with Article XIV of the Maryland Constitution.

Synopsis: Establishing the Business Facade Improvement Program in the Department of Housing and Community Development to assist qualified businesses located in sustainable communities with improving the outside appearance of the qualified businesses' buildings or facilities; requiring the Department to develop an application process for political subdivisions seeking to participate in the Program; and requiring the Governor, beginning in fiscal year 2025, to include $5,000,000 in the annual budget bill for the Program.
Title: Community Development - Sustainable Communities - Business Facade Improvement Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Business Facade Improvement Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development to distribute grant funding to political subdivisions with at least one designated sustainable community, which then distribute grants to qualified businesses to improve the exterior appearance of their buildings or facilities.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Businesses located in sustainable communities, and local governments (counties and municipalities) with designated sustainable communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State bond expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2024 from contingent capital budget funding, and general fund expenditures increase by a mandated $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 (funding 1 administrative staff position and roughly $4.9 million in local grants). Local government revenues and expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2024 and approximately $4.9 million annually thereafter as grant funds are received and passed through to qualified businesses, with possible additional local administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary agency tasked with establishing and administering the Business Facade Improvement Program, creating application and rating processes for political subdivisions, distributing funds, and adopting implementing regulations.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel resources. The bill establishes a statutory mandate requiring an annual general fund appropriation of $5,000,000 beginning in FY 2025 and requires DHCD to add staff to administer the program.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $5,000,000 for the Business Facade Improvement Program in the annual state budget bill beginning in FY 2025.
The bill originally designated the Department of Commerce to house the program before amendments shifted it to DHCD, and Commerce was consulted in the preparation of the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Establishing the Taxpayer Advocate Division in the Office of the Comptroller to assist taxpayers and their representatives in resolving certain taxpayer problems and complaints and represent taxpayers' interests in a certain manner.
Title: Office of the Comptroller - Taxpayer Advocate Division

NarrowSubjects.Name: Legislation -see also- Correct Leg; Cur Leg; Emerg Bills
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Taxpayer Advocate Division within the Office of the Comptroller to help taxpayers and their representatives resolve tax and debt collection issues, handle complaints, represent taxpayer interests, identify systemic problems, and create an online portal for direct communication.
responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers and their authorized representatives
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $294,700 in FY 2024 to hire four assistant taxpayer advocates (with two existing positions transferred) to meet the division's minimum staffing requirement, rising to $401,600 by FY 2028. Revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Taxpayer Advocate Division within the Office of the Comptroller to assist taxpayers with complaints and problem resolution, requiring new personnel and operational expenditures for the agency.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of Budget and Management coordinate with the Comptroller's Office to make appropriate personnel allocations and position reclassifications for the new division.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of the Comptroller, the Office of the State Treasurer, the Department of Budget and Management, the Department of Information Technology, and the Department of General Services, in consultation with a representative of the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission, to develop, implement, manage, and oversee the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise; and requiring the Office of the Comptroller to periodically report to the General Assembly on the status of the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise.
Title: Modernization of State Financial Systems - 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: House Bill 709 directs five key Maryland agencies—the Office of the Comptroller, the Office of the State Treasurer, the Department of Budget and Management, the Department of Information Technology, and the Department of General Services—in consultation with the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission, to plan, implement, manage, and oversee the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise. This initiative transitions the State's existing Financial Management Information System (FMIS) into a modernized, cloud-based financial management IT infrastructure, with semiannual progress reports submitted to the General Assembly through January 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller, Office of the State Treasurer, Department of Budget and Management, Department of Information Technology, and Department of General Services
stakeholders: State agencies, State financial and accounting personnel, and users of Maryland's financial management and information systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and it has no local or small business fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 709 was requested by the Comptroller and establishes the Comptroller as one of the primary departments responsible for leading, developing, managing, and overseeing the 21st Century Financial Systems Enterprise, as well as submitting regular status reports to the General Assembly through 2027.

stakeholders: Motorists traveling through residential areas in Anne Arundel County, local residents, pedestrians, and county and municipal law enforcement agencies.

Local revenues for Anne Arundel County and municipalities within the county are expected to increase potentially significantly from citation fines, exceeding initial and ongoing expenditures for camera procurement, installation, and maintenance, with remaining net revenues dedicated to local public safety purposes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill will increase the number of speed monitoring citations issued in Anne Arundel County, resulting in an increase in contested cases and caseloads heard in the District Court, which is administered and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

MDOT oversees state transportation policy and provided information for the fiscal analysis. Expansion of speed monitoring systems on eligible highways in residential districts intersects with state highway and transportation network oversight.

Under Maryland's speed monitoring laws, speed monitoring systems and associated warning signage must conform with traffic control device standards and engineering practices adopted by the State Highway Administration.
Under Maryland Transportation Section 21-809, if speed camera revenues after cost recovery exceed 10% of a jurisdiction's total revenues, any excess must be remitted to the Comptroller.

It authorizes licensed certified midwives and certified nurse-midwives to personally prepare and dispense starter doses of certain drugs and to delegate technical tasks to qualified assistants, certified medication technicians, and certified nursing assistants. It also authorizes the State Board of Nursing to appoint peer advisory committees regarding midwifery, alters the qualifications and licensure exceptions for certified midwives, and requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop recommendations to expand access to birthing services at birthing centers.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Nursing and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Certified nurse-midwives, licensed certified midwives, certified medication technicians, certified nursing assistants, pregnant women, newborns, and birthing centers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected, as the Maryland Board of Nursing and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Board of Nursing, which operates within the Department of Health, by altering licensure requirements, scopes of practice, and delegation authority for midwives and nursing assistants. Additionally, the bill specifically mandates that the Maryland Department of Health develop recommendations to expand access to birthing services in birthing centers.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "qualified conservation" for purposes of provisions of law related to forest mitigation banks; altering certain  methods of calculating forest afforestation, reforestation, and preservation requirements; authorizing local jurisdictions to adopt certain alternative afforestation, reforestation, and preservation requirements; requiring the Department of Natural Resources to establish a workgroup to evaluate and recommend incentives for private landowners to conserve forest; etc.

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland's forest preservation policy and modifies the Forest Conservation Act (FCA). It shifts the State's forest policy goal from 'no net loss' to achieving regular net gains in forest acreage and tree canopy cover. It also revises reforestation ratios (generally requiring a 1:1 replacement ratio, or 1:2 for priority funding areas not designated for retention), permanently allows qualified conservation in forest mitigation banks under specified limits, creates new exemptions for transit-oriented development and certain multifamily housing, establishes public notice and comment requirements for clearing priority retention areas, and authorizes local jurisdictions to adopt alternative forest conservation programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Private landowners, real estate and infrastructure developers, local governments and planning commissions, forest mitigation bankers, and landscaping/forestry contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning as early as FY 2025, State PAYGO general fund expenditures and local capital expenditures may increase due to higher compliance and reforestation costs on public construction projects. Revenues to the State Forest Conservation Fund and local forest conservation funds from fee-in-lieu payments will be impacted by offsetting factors (increased demand from higher reforestation requirements versus reduced payments from expanded use of mitigation banks), with the net financial effect being indeterminate. The Department of Natural Resources and the Maryland Department of the Environment expect to administer the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Forest Conservation Act, managing the Forest Conservation Fund, updating the State Forest Conservation Technical Manual, convening the workgroup on private landowner incentives, and approving local forest conservation programs.

The bill explicitly references MDE Tier II and Tier III high-quality watersheds to designate priority retention areas and links afforestation/reforestation mitigation credits to MDE environmental site design and stormwater management standards.

MDOT is directly affected by provisions establishing exemptions and mitigation ratios for transit-oriented development under the Transportation Article, and its capital construction projects are subject to the bill's modified reforestation and afforestation standards.

The bill alters exemptions and applicability standards under the Forest Conservation Act for electric generating stations and solar photovoltaic facilities that receive Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) issued by the Public Service Commission.

The bill establishes specific statutory timelines and judicial review standards under the Maryland Rules for appeals and petitions challenging approved forest conservation plans and priority area clearing determinations.

The bill clarifies agricultural activity exemptions to explicitly include orchards, tree farms, and agricultural support buildings, and requires local forest conservation programs to consider the State's agricultural land preservation goals.

As the primary agency overseeing the planning, design, and construction of state-owned facilities, DGS faces potential capital expenditure and PAYGO budget impacts to comply with modified reforestation requirements on State projects.

The bill requires local forest conservation programs to give due consideration to State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning policies, comprehensive plans, and Priority Funding Area designations administered and coordinated by MDP.

fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill codifies current practice, and the Maryland Department of Health can apply for the required federal waiver amendment using existing budgeted resources.

MSDE administers the Autism Waiver, tracks military families on the registry, and manages participant placement and service initiation when families return to Maryland.

The department advocates for active-duty service members and their families to ensure access to state benefits and support programs, including protections for relocated military families seeking waiver services.
The department coordinates policy and service delivery across state agencies for Maryland residents with disabilities, including children eligible for autism-related services and supports.

The Board of Public Works is explicitly referenced in the statute governing the approval of USM real property sales and the standard use of proceeds from those transactions.

bill_summary: Known as the Antiswatting Act of 2023, this bill prohibits knowingly making or causing to be made a false statement, report, or complaint of an emergency or crime to emergency personnel with reckless disregard of causing bodily harm. It establishes criminal penalties—a misdemeanor punishable by up to 3 years imprisonment and/or a $2,000 fine, or a felony punishable by up to 10 years and/or a $20,000 fine if the response results in serious physical injury, severe emotional distress, or death—along with civil liability and court-ordered restitution for victims. A first-time violation by a minor is treated as a civil offense under juvenile law, prohibiting out-of-home placement with the Department of Juvenile Services.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, State and local law enforcement agencies, and the Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: Victims of false emergency reports (swatting), emergency responders and law enforcement personnel, individuals accused of swatting offenses, and juvenile offenders
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances and operations. While the Office of the Public Defender noted a potential cost of $110,101 for an additional attorney to handle new cases, the Department of Legislative Services determined that any expenditures solely attributable to the bill are likely minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to prohibit committing a child to the Department of Juvenile Services for out-of-home placement if the most serious offense is a first-time violation of the newly created antiswatting statute.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police regularly receives emergency reports, deploys emergency tactical responses, and investigates criminal false reports and swatting incidents covered by this legislation.

The Judiciary is responsible for adjudicating the newly established misdemeanor and felony criminal charges, civil penalty proceedings for minors, and civil liability claims authorized under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation for indigent individuals charged with new misdemeanor or felony criminal offenses or facing juvenile court proceedings under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is responsible for correctional incarceration for individuals sentenced under the new felony and misdemeanor provisions (with penalties up to 10 years imprisonment) and community supervision through the Division of Parole and Probation.

As the agency responsible for the intake, supervision, and treatment of justice-involved youth, DJS may receive and manage additional youth processed through state juvenile courts under the concurrent jurisdiction provisions.

DBM oversees the state budget process, in which discretionary appropriations to capitalize the fund may be allocated, and supervises state personnel and agency operational budgets.

bill_summary: This bill increases the required retention period for sexual assault evidence collection kits and related evidence from 20 years to 75 years for law enforcement agencies, healthcare providers, and hospitals. It also outlines requirements for the storage, preservation, and transfer of kits (including self-administered kits and those collected prior to January 1, 2000), requires the Attorney General to adopt statewide implementation regulations, and mandates that the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee submit a report with policy recommendations by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General and the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee
stakeholders: Victims and survivors of sexual assault, law enforcement agencies, healthcare providers, hospitals, child advocacy centers, and forensic laboratories.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not expected to be materially affected in the near term, and revenues are unaffected. The Office of the Attorney General can fulfill its reporting and regulatory responsibilities with existing resources. However, State and local expenditures may increase in future years if the Department of State Police and local law enforcement agencies must acquire additional long-term storage facilities to retain evidence for 75 years rather than 20 years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Attorney General adopt regulations for uniform statewide implementation of sexual assault evidence kit requirements, direct the retention/transfer of kits collected before 2000, and consult via its Consumer Protection Division on educating consumers regarding self-administered kits.

As Maryland's primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for criminal evidence retention and will be directly impacted by extending the evidence retention requirement from 20 years to 75 years, potentially requiring additional long-term evidence storage facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee is mandated to submit a report by December 1, 2023, providing guidelines and recommendations regarding pre-2000 kits and self-administered kits, and continues to receive annual reports from forensic laboratories.
MDH regulates hospitals and health care providers that collect sexual assault evidence kits and are subject to the bill's expanded requirements on retention, storage, and transfers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the recommendations report required by the bill from the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee.

bill_summary: The Senator Delores Kelley Residents of Unlicensed Programs Protection Act requires the Maryland Department of Health or the Office of Health Care Quality to investigate allegations of neglect, exploitation, or abuse of residents in unlicensed assisted living programs. Operators of such unlicensed programs face immediate criminal prosecution if an investigation or credible allegation reveals abuse, neglect, or exploitation, or if the operator refuses to cooperate. Additionally, state and local authorities are empowered to petition a circuit court for injunctive relief against unlicensed programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Office of Health Care Quality)
stakeholders: Residents and operators of unlicensed assisted living programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local fiscal impacts are negligible. The Maryland Department of Health and the Office of Health Care Quality can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. In addition, the application of existing criminal and civil penalty provisions and circuit court petitions for injunctive relief are not expected to materially affect State or local revenues, expenditures, or court operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and its internal unit, the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), with investigating unlicensed assisted living programs for abuse, neglect, and exploitation, enforcing licensure compliance, adopting regulations, and petitioning circuit courts for injunctive relief.

The bill was introduced by request of the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). OAG is authorized to petition the circuit court for injunctive relief against unlicensed assisted living programs and enforces violations of the Consumer Protection Act associated with unlicensed operations.

The bill authorizes petitions for injunctive relief in circuit courts and establishes immediate prosecution and felony penalties for certain violations, impacting judicial case processing and court operations.

The Department of Aging protects the rights and quality of life of older adults, including long-term care advocacy and oversight of resident wellbeing, and was consulted as an information source on this legislation.

The Department of Human Services is the state's primary social service agency responsible for adult protective services and investigating allegations of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of vulnerable adults, and was consulted on the bill.

bill_summary: Prohibits price gouging by banning sellers from increasing the price of designated essential goods or services by 15% or more during a declared state of emergency, and for emergency repair and reconstruction services during and for 90 days after an emergency, subject to certain exceptions based on increased costs. It also designates violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act and requires the Secretary of State to create an electronic notification system for state of emergency declarations and covered goods.
responsible_party: Secretary of State and Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland consumers and businesses selling or purchasing essential goods, materials, and emergency repair or reconstruction services during a declared state of emergency.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2024 for the Secretary of State to develop an electronic notification system, followed by minimal ongoing licensing fees (around $350 per license annually). The Office of the Attorney General can handle enforcement with existing resources. There is no material impact on State revenues or local government operations and finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG), through its Consumer Protection Division, is the primary enforcement body for the bill. Violations are treated as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, and OAG is specifically required to provide 20 days' notice and an opportunity to present evidence before filing an enforcement action.

The bill explicitly mandates the Secretary of State to establish and maintain an electronic notification system to alert registered individuals about declared states of emergency, active price gouging protections, and designated essential goods and services, requiring $25,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2024.

The bill's price gouging prohibitions are triggered upon a state of emergency declared by the Governor and specifically apply to categories of essential goods and services designated by the Governor in an executive order.

The bill authorizes civil enforcement actions and private causes of action for damages in state courts under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, though the operational and fiscal impact on the judiciary is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates specific court procedures and motion processes in tax sale foreclosure cases, allowing local governments to petition the court to reassign certificates of sale or strike final judgments, directly impacting circuit court proceedings and administration supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Equitech Growth Fund within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to support economic competitiveness and inclusive growth in emerging and advanced industries through workforce development and infrastructure investments. It also establishes the Equitech Growth Commission to develop a long-term strategic plan and 10-year goals by July 1, 2025, for expanding Maryland's innovation economy and minority wealth creation.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
stakeholders: Public, nonprofit, and private entities, including higher education institutions, workforce development participants, technology businesses, and minority communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.0 million in FY 2024 and by $5.6 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2033 (reflecting a $5.0 million annual mandated appropriation for awards and $600,000 annually for TEDCO administrative costs). Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Equitech Growth Fund increase correspondingly. Local government and community college revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent they receive awards and provide matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the Equitech Growth Fund, adopting implementing regulations, awarding financial assistance, staffing the Equitech Growth Commission, and submitting annual reports.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Equitech Growth Commission to help develop the 10-year strategic plan for growing the State's innovation economy.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) serves on the Equitech Growth Commission, and the fund specifically targets workforce development initiatives.
The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is designated as a member of the Equitech Growth Commission.
The Executive Director of MEDCO (or designee) serves as a member of the Equitech Growth Commission.
The Chancellor of USM (or designee) serves on the Equitech Growth Commission, member institutions (including specified HBCUs) are represented and eligible for funding awards.

Morgan State University is explicitly identified among the State HBCUs whose president may be appointed by the Governor to the Equitech Growth Commission, and is eligible for higher education awards from the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Equitech Growth Commission to develop long-term strategic plans and goals for the State's innovation economy.
The Governor appoints several members to the Equitech Growth Commission, receives the Commission's strategic plan and annual reports, and is mandated to include funding in the annual budget bill.
The Comptroller is required to account for the Equitech Growth Fund, which is created as a special, nonlapsing fund exempt from standard interest accrual provisions.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the Equitech Growth Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which provides prescription drug benefits through a PBM. DBM noted that restricting step therapy protocols could result in steep prescription drug cost increases for the state plan.
