The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding executions on judgments for child support arrearages, which are administered and adjudicated through the state court system.

The bill directly concerns workers' compensation claims, indemnity benefits, and settlement proceeds, which fall under the broader statutory framework and claims handled within the Commission's purview.

Synopsis: Prohibiting institutions of higher education from entering into a contract with a certain regulated gaming entity or a certain agent of a regulated gaming entity if the institution of higher education receives certain compensation for student participation in certain sports wagering; prohibiting institutions of higher education from entering into a contract with a sports marketing entity if the entity or the institution receives certain compensation for student participation in certain sports wagering; etc.
Title: Institutions of Higher Education – Sports Wagering Contracts – Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Mobile Devices -see also- Telecommunications and IT
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Prohibits public and private institutions of higher education from entering into contracts with regulated sports wagering entities, their agents, or sports marketing entities if the contract provides bonuses, commissions, or incentive payments based on securing student participation in sports wagering. Permitted contracts entered into by public institutions of higher education are made subject to public inspection under the Maryland Public Information Act.
responsible_party: Maryland institutions of higher education
stakeholders: College and university students, institutions of higher education, regulated sports wagering operators and licensees, and sports marketing firms.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. According to the Fiscal Note, it does not affect State funding of higher education institutions, does not impact gaming revenues or expenditures, and imposes no local government costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly prohibits institutions of higher education from entering into sports wagering contracts that provide compensation based on student participation and subjects allowable contracts to public inspection under the Public Information Act.

As an independent public institution of higher education in Maryland, Morgan State University is directly restricted from entering into sports wagering incentive contracts and must make permitted contracts available for public inspection.

As an independent public honors college in Maryland, St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly bound by the prohibition on incentive-based sports wagering contracts and the public disclosure requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates sports wagering licensees and online sports wagering operators, which are the entities prohibited from entering into student incentive compensation contracts with institutions of higher education.

As the primary coordinating and regulatory agency for higher education policies and institutions across the state, MHEC maintains general regulatory oversight over the institutions impacted by this statute.

Synopsis: Altering the method by which administrative fees for participants in the State Retirement and Pension System are calculated by and remitted to the State Retirement and Pension System; and requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to provide certain notice to local participating employers.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Administrative Fees

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill alters the method and timeline for calculating and remitting administrative fees paid by participating employers to the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System to cover operating expenses of the board and the State Retirement Agency, basing fees on actual expenses from the second prior fiscal year rather than budget allowances.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Participating employers in the State Retirement and Pension System, including the State, local school boards, community colleges, and participating local governmental units.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is largely procedural in nature and has no material fiscal effect on State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and the State Retirement Agency (SRA), altering the definitions, calculation methodology, timing, and transfer of administrative fees that fund the agency's operational expenses.

The Board of Trustees must certify the percentage of membership to the Secretary of Budget and Management during the annual budget submission and provide notification of administrative fee certifications sent to local employers.

The bill mandates that upon notification by the Secretary of the Board of Trustees of a delinquent local employer, the State Comptroller must exercise the right of setoff against state monies due to that employer.
The bill requires the Governor to include an appropriation to the accumulation funds of the State Retirement and Pension System equal to the authorized administrative fees in the annual budget bill.

Synopsis: Altering the amortization periods to be used for certain unfunded liabilities or surpluses of the State Retirement and Pension System.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Amortization of Unfunded Liabilities and Surpluses
bill_summary: Alters the amortization policy for the State Retirement and Pension System by establishing specific closed periods for newly accrued unfunded liabilities and surpluses based on their source (such as experience gains and losses, actuarial assumption changes, or new legislation), authorizing the Board of Trustees to adjust amortization periods to reduce contribution rate volatility, and barring contribution rates from falling below normal cost.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Members and retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System, as well as State agencies and taxpayers funding pension contributions
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities may see potential minimal increases beginning in FY 2024, but these are not anticipated to have a discernible effect on State pension contributions. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) by altering the statutory amortization periods for unfunded accrued liabilities and surpluses, directly impacting the Board of Trustees' determination and certification of annual employer contribution rates.

As the state's principal budget and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for long-term fiscal planning and incorporating the certified annual state pension contribution rates into the executive budget.

Synopsis: Authorizing an autonomous vehicle converter to sell, transfer, lease, offer for sale, or resell a converted autonomous vehicle or a motor vehicle purchased with the intent to convert the motor vehicle into a converted autonomous vehicle; establishing that certain portions of the Act apply only to motor vehicles intended for commercial or industrial use; and prohibiting an autonomous vehicle converter from holding certain occupational vehicle licenses issued under the Maryland Vehicle Law.
Title: Vehicle Laws – Autonomous Vehicle Converters – Sale of Autonomous Vehicles

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes autonomous vehicle converters to sell, transfer, lease, offer for sale, or resell commercial or industrial converted autonomous vehicles (or vehicles purchased with the intent to convert), while excluding them from licensing requirements and definitions applicable to motor vehicle dealers, manufacturers, distributors, or factory branches.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Autonomous vehicle converters, commercial and industrial vehicle operators, and automotive dealers and manufacturers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and does not directly affect local government operations or finances. Small businesses conducting autonomous vehicle conversions may experience increased sales and revenues due to simplified regulatory processes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Title 15 of the Transportation Article, which governs occupational vehicle licenses issued and administered by the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA). It specifically excludes autonomous vehicle converters from MVA licensing requirements as vehicle dealers, distributors, factory branches, or manufacturers.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and the primary state department administering the Maryland Vehicle Law, MDOT is directly responsible for overarching policy, regulatory framework, and statutory administration regarding motor vehicles and automated driving systems.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a judge from requiring a person to give certain testimony or a statement or to produce evidence for a case involving an alleged violation of the criminal law of another state relating to health care that is legally protected in the State; prohibiting a judge from issuing an ex parte order to intercept certain communication for the purpose of investigating or recovering evidence related to legally protected health care, subject to a certain exception; etc.
Title: Reproductive Health Protection Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: The Reproductive Health Protection Act shields health care practitioners, patients, and facilitators from out-of-state legal actions regarding legally protected reproductive health care that is lawful in Maryland. The bill restricts state courts, law enforcement, and government entities from cooperating with out-of-state criminal and civil investigations, extraditions, subpoenas, wiretaps, and foreign judgments related to legally protected health care. It also protects practitioners from adverse licensing actions by health occupations boards and coverage or rate penalties by medical liability insurers, and clarifies exemption provisions for high-deductible health plans regarding abortion coverage.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Governor's Office, Maryland Health Occupations Boards, and Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health care practitioners, patients receiving reproductive health care services, state and local law enforcement agencies, state courts, health occupations licensing boards, and medical professional liability insurers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Department of Legislative Services, the bill has no material fiscal impact on State or local government operations or finances, as the provisions are primarily procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds § 1–227 to the Health Occupations Article, prohibiting health occupations licensing boards—which operate under the Maryland Department of Health—from disciplining, revoking, suspending, or taking adverse actions against health care practitioners for providing legally protected reproductive health care.

The bill amends the Insurance Article by empowering the Insurance Commissioner to determine exemptions for high-deductible health plans regarding abortion coverage, and by prohibiting medical professional liability insurers from taking adverse actions against health care practitioners who provide or refer for legally protected health care.

The bill establishes significant procedural requirements and prohibitions in the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding issuing witness summonses in criminal proceedings, circuit court filings and certifications for foreign subpoenas, issuing ex parte wiretap orders, and filing foreign judgments relating to reproductive health care.

The bill directly restricts the statutory authority of the Governor under the Uniform Criminal Extradition Act, prohibiting the Governor from surrendering a person demanded by another state for actions involving legally protected health care that are not crimes in Maryland.

The Office of the Secretary of State is responsible for processing extradition requests on behalf of the Governor, which are directly curtailed under the bill's amendments to the Criminal Procedure Article for out-of-state reproductive health investigations.

The bill enacts § 2–312 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, prohibiting State agencies, employees, and resources from being used in furtherance of out-of-state investigations into legally protected health care. DBM is the principal personnel and human resources agency managing executive branch employment policies.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal guidance on interstate subpoenas, foreign judgments, and interstate extradition, and is one of the designated authorities whose wiretap application authority is subject to the bill's restrictions.

The Office of the State Prosecutor is explicitly referenced in the Wiretap and Electronic Surveillance Act provisions affected by the bill, which restrict applications for ex parte orders to intercept communications concerning legally protected health care.

Synopsis: Altering to July 1, 2025, the termination date for certain provisions of law governing the Minority Business Enterprise Program and its application to offshore wind projects and video lottery terminals; and altering the date by which certain reports, studies, and guidelines must be submitted.
Title: State Procurement – Minority Business Enterprise Program – Extension and Reports

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) Program—including its application to offshore wind projects and video lottery terminals—by one year to July 1, 2025, and extends deadlines for the associated disparity study, related reports, and guidelines.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA) and Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT)
stakeholders: Certified Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs), small and women-owned businesses, state contractors, and developers of offshore wind and video lottery terminal projects.
fiscal_impact_summary: Extending the deadlines for the disparity study and related analyses does not affect the total cost of those studies. The bill is technical and procedural in nature, resulting in no state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is directly responsible for administering the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) Program and is mandated by the bill to complete several extended reporting requirements, establish capital project subgoal guidelines, and evaluate race- and gender-neutral approaches.

MDOT serves as the State's designated MBE certification agency and is required by the bill to conduct disparity analyses related to offshore wind projects, public-private partnerships, and brokerage/investment services, as well as consult on program guidelines.

BPW designates the MBE certification agency, oversees State procurement policy, adopts regulations supporting the disparity study, and cannot approve public-private partnerships without established MBE goals.

The bill explicitly requires the certification agency and GOSBA to consult with the Office of the Attorney General regarding constitutional compliance (Croson standards) for disparity studies, guidelines, and alternative remedial approaches.
The bill extends the application of MBE requirements to qualified offshore wind projects, for which the PSC approves offshore wind renewable energy credits and receives progress reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the sunset date for statutory MBE participation requirements applicable to video lottery terminal (VLT) applicants and licensees regulated by the agency.
As the State's primary operational support and procurement agency, DGS implements MBE statutory requirements and goal setting across major state contracts extended under this legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring a hospital to include testing for fentanyl as part of a urine drug screening; and requiring the hospital, if a urine drug screening detects fentanyl, to report the deidentified test results  to the Maryland Department of Health through the State-designated health information exchange.
Title: Hospitals - Testing for Fentanyl (The Josh Siems Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Controlled Dangerous Substances -see also- Drugs; Subst Abus
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Enacts The Josh Siems Act, requiring hospitals with chemical analyzer equipment to include fentanyl testing whenever conducting a urine drug screening to aid in diagnosing a patient, and to report deidentified positive fentanyl results to the Maryland Department of Health via the State-designated health information exchange.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Hospital patients undergoing urine drug screenings, hospital emergency departments and medical staff, and individuals impacted by opioid/fentanyl use.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state department responsible for public health and the oversight of hospital regulations under the Health - General Article, the Maryland Department of Health receives the deidentified positive fentanyl screening data reported by hospitals through the State-designated health information exchange.

The Maryland Health Care Commission oversees and designates the State-designated health information exchange (CRISP), which serves as the reporting conduit through which hospitals must transmit deidentified fentanyl test results.

Synopsis: Regulating the disclosure of certain information related to legally protected health care by custodians of public records, health information exchanges, and electronic health networks; requiring that the regulations adopted by the Maryland Health Care Commission regarding clinical information to be exchanged through the State-designated exchange restrict data of patients who have obtained legally protected health care; establishing the Protected Health Care Commission; etc.
Title: Health - Reproductive Health Services - Protected Information and Insurance Requirements

Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; Birth Control

bill_summary: This bill protects the privacy of patients receiving abortion care and sensitive reproductive health services by prohibiting health information exchanges and electronic health networks from disclosing mifepristone data and diagnosis or procedure codes without patient consent. It establishes the Protected Health Care Commission to advise the Secretary of Health on legally protected health care, limits the disclosure of health provider information under the Maryland Public Information Act, and clarifies health insurance requirements for abortion care coverage.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Patients receiving reproductive and abortion care, reproductive health care providers, health information exchanges, electronic health networks, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Care Commission special fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2024 only for contractual services to develop confidentiality standards, which MHCC can cover with existing funds. MDH can staff the new Protected Health Care Commission using existing budgeted resources. General fund revenues from potential fines (up to $10,000 per day for knowing violations starting June 1, 2024) are not expected to be material. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory purpose of the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) to include establishing policies and standards to protect the confidentiality of legally protected health care information. MHCC is required to adopt emergency regulations within nine months to restrict patient data exchanged through health information exchanges and submit quarterly progress reports to the General Assembly in FY 2024 and FY 2025, requiring $100,000 in special fund expenditures.

The Secretary of Health is mandated to adopt emergency regulations identifying protected diagnostic, procedure, medication, and related codes for abortion care and sensitive health services. Additionally, the Maryland Department of Health must provide staffing for the newly established Protected Health Care Commission and evaluate its semiannual recommendations, and MDH health occupations boards are affected by amended Public Information Act disclosure rules.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a new advisory body, the Protected Health Care Commission, charged with assessing risks and issuing semiannual recommendation reports to the Secretary of Health regarding sensitive health services that should be classified as legally protected health care.

The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding abortion care service coverage mandates to clarify application notwithstanding certain essential health benefit restrictions, involving health insurers and policies regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration.
The Attorney General (or designee) is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the newly established Protected Health Care Commission.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date of certain provisions of law that establish and govern the funding for the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program; and requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Administration, to conduct a study on available federal and State subsidies and report its findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2024.
Title: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange - State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: House Bill 814 extends the termination date of the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program by two years, from June 30, 2024, to June 30, 2026. The bill allows the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to designate up to $20 million annually in subsidies for eligible young adults purchasing individual market coverage through calendar year 2025 and requires a study on available federal and State subsidies and § 1332 waiver options by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Young adults in Maryland (ages 18 through 40) purchasing health benefit plans in the individual insurance market, health insurance carriers, and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund increase by up to $10.0 million in FY 2024, $20.0 million in FY 2025, and $10.0 million in FY 2026 to continue providing health insurance subsidies. General fund revenues may be affected to the extent that year-end reversions of unspent funds are lower than they otherwise would have been. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHBE is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, implementing the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program, tracking program performance, and conducting a study on health insurance subsidies and the State's Section 1332 waiver.

The bill requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to consult with the Insurance Commissioner and the Maryland Insurance Administration when establishing subsidy parameters and conducting the required study on federal and State subsidies and the Section 1332 waiver.

Synopsis: Requiring insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for certain lung cancer diagnostic imaging and limiting the copayment, coinsurance, or deductible that the entities can require for lung cancer screening and diagnosis; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to conduct an assessment on certain outreach, education, and health disparities in cancer screening and report the results to the General Assembly by January 1, 2024.
Title: Cancer Screening - Health Insurance and Assessment of Outreach, Education, and Health Disparities

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs

bill_summary: Requires health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for recommended follow-up diagnostic imaging for lung cancer and limits cost-sharing for such screenings and diagnoses. Additionally requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish a stakeholder workgroup and conduct an assessment on outreach, education, and health disparities related to cancer screening.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals eligible for lung cancer screening and diagnosis, communities affected by health disparities in cancer screening, health insurance carriers, and health care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,921 in FY 2024 only for contractual staff within the Maryland Department of Health to conduct the assessment and convene the stakeholder workgroup. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally from rate and form filing fees in FY 2024. Impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program is indeterminate, and local governments purchasing fully insured plans may see potential health insurance expenditure increases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is mandated to conduct an assessment on current outreach, education, and health disparities in cancer screening, establish an advisory stakeholder workgroup, and report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly, incurring direct fiscal costs in FY 2024.

MIA is responsible for regulating health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans to ensure compliance with the new coverage mandates and cost-sharing restrictions for follow-up lung cancer diagnostic imaging, receiving rate and form filings.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which may experience an indeterminate fiscal impact resulting from the mandated coverage of follow-up diagnostic imaging for lung cancer.
MHBE oversees qualified health plans offered on the individual and small business marketplaces, which are subject to state insurance benefit mandates and benchmark plan requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation establishes a temporary stakeholder workgroup tasked with advising the Maryland Department of Health on cancer screening and outreach to underserved communities.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop a scorecard to evaluate units of State government on the units' performance toward meeting certain participation goals under the Minority Business Enterprise Program and the Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise Program; establishing a certain grading scale for the scorecard; and requiring grades achieved by each unit to be published each year on the Office's website.
Title: Procurement - Minority Business Enterprises and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises - Participation Goal Scorecard

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Requires the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (GOSBA) to develop a scorecard to evaluate State government units on their progress toward meeting participation goals under the Minority Business Enterprise and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise programs. GOSBA must establish a weighted grading system, publish the agencies' grades annually on its website, and submit the results to the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
stakeholders: State procurement agencies and units of State government, certified Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs), and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises (VSBEs).
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected as the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs develop a scorecard to evaluate State agencies on their performance toward meeting MBE and VSBE participation goals, develop the weighted grading scale, publish the grades annually on its website, and submit the results to the General Assembly.

The Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs operates as a coordinating office within the Executive Department, and the scorecard directly monitors and evaluates the procurement performance of executive branch units.

Synopsis: Requiring the Division of State Documents to make at least the 15 most recent issues of the Maryland Register available to the public for online searching; altering the requirements for a unit of State government to submit certain proposed or emergency regulations, work plans, and evaluation reports to the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review, the Department of Legislative Services, and the Administrator of the Division of State Documents; etc.
Title: State Government - Regulation Procedures and the Maryland Register

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill alters the procedures for Maryland State government units to submit proposed or emergency regulations to the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review (AELR), the Department of Legislative Services (DLS), and the Division of State Documents (DSD). Among other provisions, it requires DSD to provide free public online access to at least the 15 most recent issues of the Maryland Register, sets rules and notice requirements for making substantive or nonsubstantive changes to proposed regulations before publication, extends the review period following an administrative hold override notice from 30 to 60 days, and directs the Administrator of DSD to develop and maintain an electronic filing and tracking system for regulations.
responsible_party: Division of State Documents (and its Administrator), in consultation with the Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: State agencies and units that promulgate regulations, the Joint Committee on Administrative, Executive, and Legislative Review, the Department of Legislative Services, Maryland Register subscribers, and the public.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $124,172 in FY 2024 and $122,700 in FY 2025 for contractual staff and supplemental funding to backfill lost revenue, continuing at $39,000 annually thereafter. DSD special fund subscription revenues decrease by $29,250 in FY 2024 and $39,000 annually thereafter due to free online access, with special fund expenditures decreasing correspondingly. Potential additional indeterminate IT costs (possibly several million dollars) may be incurred to complete the electronic filing system depending on existing contract terms. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Division of State Documents (DSD) is an agency within the Office of the Secretary of State. The bill directly alters DSD's statutory responsibilities regarding the publication and online availability of the Maryland Register, the administration of regulatory submissions, and the development and maintenance of an electronic filing system, with direct fiscal impacts on its revenues and expenditures.

The Department of Information Technology (DoIT) is tasked with consulting on and supporting the development, maintenance, functionality, and security of the electronic regulatory filing system (ELF 2.0) used by State units, DSD, and the General Assembly.

Synopsis: Altering the penalty for a violation of the prohibition on wearing, carrying, or transporting a handgun; requiring the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy to annually report certain information to the Governor and General Assembly; requiring the Department of State Police to transmit a certain summary of certain laws relating to firearms to certain persons; requiring the Secretary of State Police, in consultation with the Attorney General and the Maryland Department of Health, to develop a certain curriculum; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Regulated Firearms - Possession and Permits to Carry, Wear, and Transport a Handgun

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: This bill alters the penalties and qualifications regarding regulated firearms and handgun wear, carry, and transport permits. It increases the maximum incarceration penalty for a first-time violation of wearing, carrying, or transporting a handgun from three to five years, expands firearm possession disqualifiers (such as individuals on supervised probation for certain crimes or protective order violations), raises handgun permit application and renewal fees, and raises the minimum permit age from 18 to 21 with exceptions for military service members. Additionally, it removes the 'good and substantial reason' requirement, establishes enhanced firearm training and live-fire curriculum requirements, mandates regular reviews and revocations of active permits by the Department of State Police, and institutes annual reporting obligations.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Handgun permit applicants and current permit holders, regulated firearm owners, certified firearms training instructors, and law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues from increased handgun permit fees are estimated to rise by approximately $5,294,200 in FY 2024, $7,644,000 in FY 2025, and taper in future years as application surges stabilize. State general fund expenditures increase by at least $2,402,200 in FY 2024 (including $2.3 million and 26 positions for the Department of State Police to monitor active permit holders, and $90,455 and one position for the Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy for data reporting). Local governments and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services may experience minimal increases in revenues from fines and expenditures due to the extended maximum incarceration penalty.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland State Police is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for licensing and regulating handgun permits, conducting investigations, increasing permit fees, performing regular reviews of active permit holders via CJIS, developing the mandatory training curriculum, transmitting email summaries of legislative changes, and submitting extensive annual reports.

OAH adjudicates appeals from individuals whose handgun permits were denied, revoked, or limited, or whose applications were not acted on within 90 days. The bill requires OAH to conduct de novo hearings, issue written findings of facts and decisions within 90 days, and compile and submit annual statistical reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the State Police regularly review active permit holders using DPSCS's Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository. Additionally, the bill increases the maximum incarceration penalty for handgun transport violations from 3 to 5 years, resulting in a fiscal and operational impact on state correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates an ongoing annual reporting mandate for the Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy regarding charges, convictions, and sentences for specified firearms offenses disaggregated by jurisdiction, race, and gender, requiring additional dedicated staff resources.

Circuit courts hear appeals from OAH decisions regarding handgun permits, and state courts handle the adjudication and sentencing of individuals charged under the expanded disqualifications and enhanced criminal penalties established by the bill.

The Secretary of State Police is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to develop, publish, and distribute the classroom curriculum for the mandatory firearms training course (specifically covering suicide prevention and mental health topics).

The bill requires the Secretary of State Police to consult with the Office of the Attorney General in developing, publishing, and updating the curriculum of instruction on state and federal firearm laws and self-defense legal topics for certified firearms instructors.

The Governor's Office receives required annual reports from the Department of State Police, the Office of Administrative Hearings, and the State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy concerning permit processing, appeals, and sentencing data.

Synopsis: Granting the Town of Forest Heights in Prince George's County the authority to exercise urban renewal powers in areas zoned for commercial use for blight clearance and redevelopment under Article III, Section 61 of the Maryland Constitution; and authorizing the municipality to levy certain taxes and issue general obligation bonds and revenue bonds to carry out urban renewal powers.
Title: Town of Forest Heights (Prince George's County) - Urban Renewal Authority for Blight Clearance PG 410-23

bill_summary: Grants the Town of Forest Heights in Prince George's County urban renewal authority to undertake blight clearance and redevelopment projects in areas zoned for commercial use. The bill authorizes the town to acquire property using eminent domain with just compensation, levy taxes, and issue general obligation or revenue bonds to finance urban renewal projects.
responsible_party: Town of Forest Heights
stakeholders: Commercial property owners, businesses, and residents in the Town of Forest Heights and Prince George's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected, though a minimal indirect increase in State tax revenues is possible if areas are successfully redeveloped. For local government, the Town of Forest Heights may incur increased expenditures for property acquisition, eminent domain legal fees, and project execution, which may be offset by revenues from selling acquired property, bond proceeds, or an expanded tax base. Prince George's County may also experience a minimal indirect increase in tax revenues. Specific dollar figures cannot be quantified at this time.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the state agency responsible for community revitalization and municipal infrastructure projects. While the bill directly grants urban renewal and blight clearance authority to the Town of Forest Heights, DHCD monitors and supports municipal revitalization efforts across Maryland.

The Maryland Department of Planning provides policy guidance, land use technical assistance, and data analysis to local governments. The bill concerns municipal urban renewal plans, zoning, and land redevelopment in Forest Heights.

Synopsis: Establishing the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority in Prince George's County to support and develop a certain neighborhood revitalization plan in coordination with certain residents; and requiring the Authority to report its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly on or before October 31, 2025.

bill_summary: Establishes the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority to create and support a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan for target communities in Prince George's County, focusing on residents, housing, neighborhoods, economic development, and transportation.
responsible_party: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority
stakeholders: Residents, property owners, and businesses in the Prince George's County target area (Mount Rainier, Brentwood, Cottage City, Bladensburg, Colmar Manor, and North Brentwood) as well as participating local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: No direct State fiscal effect. State authority members can likely provide staff and expense reimbursements within existing resources, and the bill mandates no State appropriations. Prince George's County and participating municipalities can likely staff the authority with existing resources, though local expenditures could increase minimally if not. Local and State revenues are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under the Economic Development Article, 'the Secretary' refers to the Secretary of Commerce, who (or their designee) is designated as a statutory member of the newly established Prince George's Gateway Development Authority.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or the Secretary's designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority to support neighborhood revitalization and housing strategies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority as a temporary statutory entity with a five-year sunset to develop and report a comprehensive neighborhood revitalization plan.
The Prince George's Gateway Development Authority is required to report its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy directly to the Governor by October 31, 2025.

Synopsis: Establishing and altering certain requirements related to the installation of equipment for the charging of electric vehicles during the construction of certain housing units; clarifying that a county or municipal corporation may require a greater number of electric vehicle parking spaces; requiring the Maryland Energy Administration to study certain issues related to the installation of electric vehicle parking spaces at multifamily residential buildings and submit a report to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2023; etc.
Title: Residential Construction - Electric Vehicle Charging

bill_summary: This bill requires the construction of new residential housing units (single-family detached homes, duplexes, and townhouses) with a garage, carport, or driveway to include at least one EVSE-installed or EV-ready electric vehicle parking space. It authorizes counties and municipal corporations to mandate a higher number of EV spaces and requires the Maryland Energy Administration to conduct a study on electric vehicle parking and charging requirements for multifamily residential buildings.
responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Residential home builders and developers, homebuyers and residents of new housing units, electric vehicle owners, local government permitting and code enforcement agencies, and multifamily property owners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by up to $250,000 in FY 2024 only for the Maryland Energy Administration to hire an outside consultant to complete the required study. The Maryland Department of the Environment can assist using existing resources. There is no impact on State revenues, and local governments can handle enforcement using existing local resources with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 830 directly mandates that the Maryland Energy Administration conduct a comprehensive study on the costs, ratios, and payment options for EV-ready and EVSE-installed parking spaces in multifamily residential buildings, requiring an estimated $250,000 in special fund expenditures to complete the study and report to the Governor and General Assembly.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Energy Administration to consult with the Department of the Environment to estimate the number of electric vehicles on Maryland roads from 2024 through 2050 under the California Advanced Clean Cars II regulations.
The Maryland Energy Administration is required to submit its final report of findings and recommendations regarding multifamily electric vehicle charging spaces to the Governor by December 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Requiring the Public Service Commission to expand the EV Pilot Program to allow participating electric companies to install EV charging stations in multifamily dwellings in underserved communities; requiring the Commission to terminate the expansion of the EV Pilot Program on December 31, 2025; requiring an electric company operating an EV charging network to ensure the EV charging stations in the EV charging network maintain certain uptime standards, subject to certain exceptions; etc.
Title: Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure - Requirements (Electric Vehicle Charging Reliability Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: The Electric Vehicle Charging Reliability Act requires the Public Service Commission to expand the Electric Vehicle (EV) Pilot Program to permit participating electric companies to install EV charging stations in multifamily dwellings in underserved communities through December 31, 2025. It also establishes uptime reliability standards and quarterly reporting requirements for electric companies operating EV charging stations, mandates adequate maintenance staffing, and allows the Commission to assess civil penalties for noncompliance.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Electric companies/utilities, electric vehicle drivers, residents in multifamily housing within underserved communities, and electricity ratepayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not expected to be materially affected, as the Public Service Commission can implement the bill's provisions with existing budgeted resources. There may be a limited increase in electricity rates across all ratepayer classes—including State and local governments—as electric companies recover allowable costs determined by the Commission. Special fund revenues could indeterminately increase if civil penalties are assessed against noncompliant electric companies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory body tasked with implementing and enforcing the provisions of the bill, including expanding and overseeing the EV Pilot Program, approving uptime standards, collecting quarterly reporting data, and imposing civil penalties on noncompliant electric companies.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents the interests of residential utility customers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding utility rates and service reliability, which are directly implicated by electric company cost recovery and rate impacts under the expanded EV charging program.

Synopsis: Establishing the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force to study approaches to water and wastewater governance in the Baltimore region; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Mayor of Baltimore City, the County Executive of Baltimore County, the Governor, and the General Assembly on or before January 30, 2024.
Title: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force

bill_summary: Establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force to study approaches to water and wastewater governance in the Baltimore region, evaluate alternative governance and financing models, analyze their fiscal implications and efficiencies, and submit recommendations and necessary legislation by January 30, 2024.
responsible_party: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force (supported and staffed jointly by the Mayor of Baltimore City and the County Executive of Baltimore County, in consultation with the Maryland Department of the Environment and Maryland Environmental Service)
stakeholders: Residents and water and wastewater utility ratepayers in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel County, Carroll County, Harford County, and Howard County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are unaffected, and the Maryland Department of the Environment and Maryland Environmental Service can consult with the task force using existing budgeted resources. Baltimore City and Baltimore County staffing expenses and member travel reimbursements are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources, with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Task Force to consult with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) when developing its recommendations and report regarding regional water and wastewater governance and infrastructure.
The bill explicitly requires the Task Force to consult with the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) in developing its findings, recommendations, and report on regional water and wastewater systems.
The Governor is responsible for appointing two members to the Task Force and will receive the Task Force's final report and recommendations by January 30, 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation formally establishes a temporary statutory advisory body—the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Task Force—to conduct a specialized study on regional water and wastewater management and report recommendations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing qualified individuals to state boards, commissions, and task forces, including the two members to be appointed by the Governor under this Act.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish and maintain a website that provides certain information on the rights and responsibilities of individuals living in a common ownership community.
Title: Housing and Community Development - Common Ownership Community Website

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish and maintain a website providing information on the rights and responsibilities of individuals living in common ownership communities, including hyperlinks to local common ownership community programs and annual updates on relevant statewide legislation.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Residents and owners living in common ownership communities (condominiums, cooperative housing corporations, and homeowners associations) and local common ownership community programs in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,000 in fiscal year 2024 to contractually develop the website, followed by an indeterminate ongoing cost (anticipated to be less than $90,000 annually) in future years for website maintenance and updates. State revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 844 directly mandates that the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) establish, host, and annually update a website containing information on rights and responsibilities in common ownership communities, hyperlinks to local programs, and relevant enacted legislation, resulting in an estimated $90,000 fiscal impact in FY 2024 plus ongoing maintenance costs.

Synopsis: Establishing the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program in the Department of the Environment for the purpose of authorizing the regulated use of reclaimed water as a source for drinking water treatment facilities; providing for the issuance of potable reuse permits under the Pilot Program; applying certain public participation requirements to potable reuse permits; requiring the Department to submit a report on the status of the Pilot Program to the Governor and General Assembly on or before December 31, 2024; etc.
Title: Drinking Water - Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program - Establishment

bill_summary: Establishes the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of the Environment to authorize and regulate the use of reclaimed water as a source for drinking water treatment facilities. The bill establishes permitting, public participation, testing, treatment standards, and permit renewal criteria for potable reuse systems.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Operators of public water systems and drinking water treatment facilities, local governments, drinking water consumers, and water treatment engineering and equipment contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,022 in FY 2023, $139,858 in FY 2024, and approximately $146,000 to $159,000 annually through FY 2028 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire two contractual engineers to administer the program. Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures may also increase if additional staff is required for PFAS water testing. State revenues are unaffected as there is no permit fee. Participating local governments would incur increased expenditures to treat reclaimed water and meet permit standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), tasking the agency with creating standards, reviewing applications, issuing and revoking permits, conducting site inspections, adopting regulations, and submitting an evaluation report.

MDH's Laboratories Administration provides critical analytical support and water testing services (including PFAS testing) for public drinking water systems and MDE, which may lead to operational demands or expenditure increases as noted in the fiscal note.

MES provides operational and technical services for water and wastewater treatment to state and local government clients, who may seek to implement indirect potable reuse projects under this pilot program.

The bill requires the Department of the Environment to submit a report by December 31, 2024, to the Governor detailing the pilot program's status and recommendations for statutory or regulatory changes.

Synopsis: Altering, from 60 days to 180 days, the time period after a medical examiner files findings and conclusions resulting from an autopsy during which a person in interest may request the medical examiner to correct findings and conclusions on the cause and manner of death recorded on a certificate of death.
Title: Public Health - Chief Medical Examiner - Corrections to Autopsy Findings and Conclusions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Extends the time period from 60 days to 180 days after autopsy findings are filed during which an interested person may request that the medical examiner correct findings and conclusions on the cause and manner of death recorded on a death certificate (except in cases with a finding of homicide).
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Office of the Chief Medical Examiner
stakeholders: Surviving family members and persons in interest (such as spouses, parents, adult children, adult siblings, grandparents, or guardians) of deceased individuals who undergo an autopsy, as well as the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner and the Office of Administrative Hearings.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no local fiscal impact and no material effect on State revenues. Any potential increase in requests for corrections or administrative hearings can be handled using existing budgeted resources by the Maryland Department of Health and the Office of Administrative Hearings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Chief Medical Examiner operates within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), and the Secretary of Health oversees appeals and final orders regarding requests to correct autopsy findings and death certificates.
The Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) conducts contested case hearings when a person in interest appeals the Chief Medical Examiner's denial of a request to correct findings and conclusions.
Circuit courts may hear judicial appeals if a party seeks review of an order rejecting the administrative law judge's findings.

Synopsis: Requiring the Division of Rehabilitation Services in the State Department of Education and the Developmental Disabilities Administration in the Maryland Department of Health to enter into a memorandum of understanding, the terms of which shall include a data sharing agreement for the medical and psychological records of mutual clients in order to expedite decisions regarding eligibility for services.
Title: Division of Rehabilitation Services and Developmental Disabilities Administration - Memorandum of Understanding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires the Division of Rehabilitation Services within the Maryland State Department of Education and the Developmental Disabilities Administration within the Maryland Department of Health to enter into a memorandum of understanding with a data-sharing agreement for mutual clients' medical and psychological records to expedite eligibility determinations for services.
responsible_party: Division of Rehabilitation Services (Maryland State Department of Education) and Developmental Disabilities Administration (Maryland Department of Health)
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities and developmental disabilities who are mutual clients of both the Division of Rehabilitation Services and the Developmental Disabilities Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Health and Maryland State Department of Education can implement the data-sharing agreement using existing resources through revisions to an existing memorandum of understanding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), a division within the Maryland State Department of Education, enter into a memorandum of understanding and data-sharing agreement regarding mutual client records.

The bill directly mandates that the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), an administration within the Maryland Department of Health, enter into a memorandum of understanding and data-sharing agreement regarding mutual client records.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission to enter into contracts with the District of Columbia or the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority for the construction, maintenance, and operation of a water supply, sewer, or drainage system for certain property located within a certain distance of a certain mass transit rail station and a regional transit district or neighborhood center in Prince George's County; and requiring that a contract entered into under the Act include and address certain items.
Title: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission - Service Near Regional Transit Districts and Neighborhood Centers in Prince George's County - Contracts MC/PG 111-23

bill_summary: Authorizes the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) to contract with the District of Columbia or the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority to construct, maintain, and operate water, sewer, or drainage services for qualifying border properties in Prince George's County located near mass transit stations that lack frontage on a county right-of-way.
responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
stakeholders: Owners, developers, and residents of qualifying border properties in Prince George's County, the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, and the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, and does not materially affect the operations or finances of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines eligible border properties in part by their proximity to WMATA mass transit rail stations and qualification as expedited transit-oriented development projects. While MDOT does not implement the water and sewer contracts, it coordinates state transit initiatives and transit-oriented development and served as an information source for the legislation.

The bill explicitly references the requirement that contracts maintain authority to collect fees mandated under state environmental law, specifically citing the Bay Restoration Fee under § 9-1605.2 of the Environment Article administered by MDE.

bill_summary: Establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General to investigate and prosecute violations of State criminal environmental and natural resources laws, as well as any other criminal offenses discovered during such investigations, granting the unit the powers of a State's Attorney and subpoena authority.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Individuals and entities subject to Maryland environmental and natural resources criminal laws, resource-based small businesses, victims of pollution crimes, and state regulatory agencies including the Maryland Department of the Environment and Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $566,200 in FY 2024 to fund four new positions (Chief Counsel, two assistant Attorneys General, and one investigator) and operating costs, increasing to $796,000 by FY 2028. State general/special fund revenues and local revenues may experience an indeterminate increase beginning in FY 2024 from collected monetary penalties and restitution. Local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 874 directly establishes the Environmental and Natural Resources Crimes Unit within the Office of the Attorney General, creating new positions, granting prosecutorial and subpoena authorities, and requiring $566,200+ in general fund expenditures.

The unit investigates and prosecutes violations of criminal environmental laws, and the Attorney General must report annually on activities and any actions taken by the Department of the Environment in response to the unit's findings and recommendations.

The unit investigates and prosecutes violations of criminal natural resources laws, and the Attorney General must report annually on activities and any actions taken by the Department of Natural Resources in response to the unit's findings and recommendations.

The bill requires the Attorney General to cooperate with the Secretary of Budget and Management to set minimum salaries, qualifications, and standards of training and experience for positions within the unit.
The Attorney General is required to submit an annual report to the Governor by November 30 on the activities of the unit and agency responses.
The bill authorizes the unit to issue subpoenas enforceable through hearings and orders in the circuit courts, as well as use county grand juries to prosecute criminal cases.

Synopsis: Authorizing Baltimore City to honor certificates of guarantee that are issued by certain associations or on behalf of certain contractors in order to satisfy certain county bond requirements; and providing that Baltimore City is not required under certain provisions of law to honor certain certificates of guarantee.
Title: Baltimore City - Insurance - Certificates of Guarantee for County Bond Requirements

Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Authorizes, but does not require, Baltimore City to honor certificates of guarantee issued by an approved nonprofit association of contractors or its wholly owned subsidiary to satisfy bond requirements for public improvements or other city bond requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Baltimore City, contractors bidding on or performing public improvement and construction projects, and nonprofit associations of contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected; the Maryland Insurance Administration can enforce the bill's provisions using existing budgeted resources. Baltimore City finances are also not affected because the city is authorized, but not required, to accept certificates of guarantee. Potential minimal impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Section 1–203 of the Insurance Article regarding certificates of guarantee for bond requirements. The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the insurance market under this article and was identified in the fiscal note as having oversight with no state fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the defined term "related event" as it applies to a related event promoter's permit in Baltimore City includes events for which tickets are sold in advance or at the door or cover charges are imposed; reducing the number of days within which a person must apply for a permit, the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City must take certain actions relating to the permit, and alterations may be made to the permit; and altering the standards for determining the permit fee.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - Related Event Promoter's Permit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates

bill_summary: This bill alters provisions regarding related event promoter's permits for events associated with the CIAA Basketball Tournament in Baltimore City. It clarifies that a related event includes events where tickets are sold at the door or cover charges are imposed, shortens application and review deadlines, bases permit fee tiers on the Baltimore City Fire Marshal's maximum capacity determination rather than anticipated attendance, and extends the law's sunset date to June 30, 2025.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Related event promoters, participating Baltimore City alcoholic beverages license holders, caterers, and attendees of CIAA Basketball Tournament related events.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Baltimore City operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates the Alcoholic Beverages Article by removing an obsolete statutory reference to the Comptroller's enforcement and fining authority over State caterer's license holders, reflecting the transfer of those responsibilities to the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in a certain area of the 40th alcoholic beverages district in Baltimore City to the holder of a Class C beer and light wine license under certain circumstances; prohibiting certain license holders in certain areas of the 40th alcoholic beverages district from selling alcoholic beverages at certain times of day; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - 40th District - Alcoholic Beverages
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in the 3600 block of Hickory Avenue to a holder of a Class C beer and light wine license. It also permits the issuance of a Class A-7 beer, wine, and liquor license in the 1200 block of West North Avenue under specified conditions, exempts this Class A-7 license from the 300-foot distance restriction from schools and places of worship, and expands the geographic boundaries on West North Avenue subject to restricted sales hours (prohibiting sales before 10:00 a.m. or after 10:00 p.m.).
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license applicants, existing license holders, clubs, and residents/businesses in the 40th alcoholic beverages district of Baltimore City, including the Penn North Community Association.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City revenues will increase minimally beginning in FY 2024 to the extent licenses are issued. For an issued Class C BWL license, revenues increase by $1,150 in FY 2024 and $600 annually thereafter (reflecting a $550 annual license fee, a $600 initial application fee, and a $50 annual renewal fee). For an issued Class A-7 BWL license, revenues increase by $2,100 in FY 2024 and $1,550 annually thereafter (reflecting a $1,500 annual license fee, a $600 application fee, and a $50 annual renewal fee).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions of the Alcoholic Beverages Article regarding local retail licenses and hours of sale in Baltimore City. While implementation and licensing are handled locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, the Comptroller is the state entity responsible for overseeing and regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state alcohol excise taxes.

Synopsis: Requiring the St. Mary's County Metropolitan Commission to obtain the approval from the Commissioners of St. Mary's County before submitting a loan application where the Commission seeks to incur debt upon the full faith and credit of the county; requiring the Commission to cause studies, plans, and estimates to be made for new facilities in certain portions of the county; requiring any excess revenue made by the Commission in the sale or transfer of certain debt to be exempt from taxation; etc.
Title: St. Mary’s County – Metropolitan Commission – New Facilities
