bill_summary: This bill establishes the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Towing and Recovery within the Department of State Police (DSP) to recommend approved maximum towing and recovery rates and a complaint resolution process. It requires DSP to set approved rates by January 1, 2024, mandates tow companies on the tow list to ban per-pound billing by October 1, 2023, and modifies the procedures and timeline for vehicle release during fee disputes between commercial vehicle owners and authorized towing companies.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Commercial motor vehicle owners and operators, authorized medium- and heavy-duty towing companies, and commercial trucking businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of State Police increase by $44,700 in FY 2024 (and between $50,300 and $58,000 annually in FY 2025–2028) to fund a part-time administrator to support the committee, coordinate meetings, and assist with complaint handling. State revenues are not affected, and local government operations and finances have no material impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police is the primary implementing agency for this legislation. It is required to establish approved maximum rates for police-initiated commercial vehicle towing and recovery, ban per-pound billing, develop a complaint adjudication process, provide staff support to the newly created advisory committee, and incurs fiscal expenditures for staff.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Towing and Recovery to evaluate rates, meet triennially, and recommend rate modifications and complaint resolution processes.
The Secretary of Transportation appoints a representative of the Maryland Transportation Authority Police to the Committee, and the department oversees both MDTA and the State Highway Administration.
The Administrator of the State Highway Administration is tasked with appointing a representative from the administration to serve as a member of the newly created Committee.
The Maryland Transportation Authority Police has a designated seat on the Committee on Rate Setting and Complaint Resolution for Police-Initiated Medium-Duty and Heavy-Duty Towing and Recovery.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner appoints a representative of the Maryland Insurance Administration to serve on the newly established Committee.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Wicomico County to create a sanitary district.
Title: Wicomico County - Sanitary District - Authorization

NarrowSubjects.Name: Sanitary Districts -see also- Wash Sub Sanitary District

bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Wicomico County to establish sanitary districts and governing sanitary commissions within the county to address water and sewer infrastructure needs.
responsible_party: Wicomico County Council
stakeholders: Residents and property owners in Wicomico County, particularly those in areas with failing septic systems requiring water and sewerage infrastructure.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. For Wicomico County, there is a potential increase in expenditures and revenues to the extent that sanitary districts are established and facilities are constructed; however, specific cost and revenue figures cannot currently be determined.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 9 of the Environment Article to authorize Wicomico County to establish a sanitary district to address water and sewerage needs (such as failing septic systems). The Maryland Department of the Environment oversees water and wastewater regulatory frameworks and county water and sewer plans, although the direct fiscal and operational impact is local to Wicomico County.

Synopsis: Reducing from 150 yards to 50 yards the size of the safety zone for archery hunters in Howard County who are under the authority of a deer management permit or who are actively participating in a hunting program administered by the county within which archery hunting may not take place except under certain circumstances; and requiring certain archery hunters in Howard County to be in an elevated position when hunting any wild bird or mammal within 50 to 150 yards of certain buildings.
Title: Howard County – Archery Hunting – Safety Zone and Position of Archery Hunter Ho. Co. 15–23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Decreases the archery hunting safety zone in Howard County from 150 yards to 50 yards from occupied buildings for individuals hunting under a deer management permit or participating in a county hunting program, and requires those hunters to be in an elevated position to shoot in a downward trajectory when hunting within 50 to 150 yards of occupied buildings or schools.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Archery hunters in Howard County hunting under a deer management permit or county-administered program, as well as Howard County property owners and residents near hunting areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article governing hunting safety zones and elevated shooting requirements for archery hunters in Howard County. The Department of Natural Resources regulates hunting seasons, oversees wildlife conservation, enforces hunting safety laws through the Natural Resources Police, and issues Deer Management Permits referenced in the legislation.

Synopsis: Providing that, notwithstanding any other provision of law, except for regulations issued by the Department of the Environment, no provision of the State building code or other law or regulation may prohibit or otherwise limit the use of a refrigerant if the refrigerant is designated as acceptable for use under federal listing requirements and any appliance containing the refrigerant meets federal safety standards and use conditions.
Title: Public Safety – Refrigerants – Limitations on Use

NarrowSubjects.Name: Hazardous and Toxic Substances -see also- Asbestos; Radiatn

bill_summary: Provides that, except for regulations issued by the Maryland Department of the Environment, no provision of the State building code or other law or regulation may prohibit or restrict the use of a refrigerant if it is designated as acceptable under federal Clean Air Act standards and the appliance containing it complies with federal safety standards and use conditions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Manufacturers, retailers, technicians, and owners of household and commercial appliances using refrigerants (such as air conditioners, refrigerators, chillers, and freezers), as well as local building code officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly carves out and preserves the regulatory authority of the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), ensuring that MDE regulations may still regulate or limit refrigerant use in accordance with environmental and emissions goals.

The Maryland Department of Labor adopts and maintains the Maryland Building Performance Standards (MBPS) and the International Mechanical Code, which govern building codes and heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration systems affected by this bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing Prince George's County to exercise powers of eminent domain to acquire and develop or redevelop, for a public purpose, certain neglected property located in the county that has been designated as a transit-oriented development and is located within a business improvement district; and prohibiting land or property taken by the county through the use of eminent domain under the provisions of the Act to be taken without just compensation, as agreed on between the parties, or awarded by a jury.
Title: Prince George's County - Land Use - Development of Neglected Property PG 406-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes Prince George's County to exercise eminent domain to acquire and develop or redevelop neglected, blighted, or abandoned property located within a designated transit-oriented development area and a business improvement district for economic development and public purposes, provided just compensation is paid.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Government
stakeholders: Owners of neglected, blighted, or abandoned properties located within transit-oriented development areas and business improvement districts in Prince George's County, as well as local developers, residents, and businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes condemnation of neglected property in designated transit-oriented development (TOD) areas, which are statutorily designated by the Secretary of Transportation and includes light rail stops along the Purple Line transit corridor.

The Maryland Department of Planning oversees state land use policy, sustainable growth, and planning coordination, and was consulted regarding the land use and redevelopment provisions authorized by the bill.
The bill involves the exercise of eminent domain powers and just compensation determinations that are subject to judicial proceedings and jury awards administered through the Maryland court system.

Synopsis: Requiring educational professionals employed by a county board of education, the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, or a county public library system who transfer to the Juvenile Services Education Program to be given credit as State employees for certain years of service for the purpose of establishing leave accrual rates; authorizing an individual who transfers to the Program to transfer leave balances in excess of a certain limit under certain circumstances; and applying the Act retroactively.
Title: Juvenile Services Education Program - Transfer of Locally Employed Educational Professionals

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Provides that qualifying locally employed educational professionals who transfer to the Juvenile Services Education Program within the Department of Juvenile Services receive credit as State employees for previous years of service when establishing leave accrual rates, and authorizes the transfer and retention of verified accumulated leave balances without diminution under specified conditions.
responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services
stakeholders: Locally employed educational professionals (such as certified public school teachers, librarians, and public library associates) transferring to the Juvenile Services Education Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a material impact on State finances or operations. While the Department of Juvenile Services and Department of Budget and Management will need to track specialized leave rules, administrative costs are minimal and can be absorbed within existing resources. The bill does not affect local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Juvenile Services Education Program (JSEP), which is housed within and administered by DJS. DJS must implement the provisions regarding the placement, leave accrual, and accumulated leave transfers of qualifying local educational professionals transferring to the program.

As the State's central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee classifications, benefits, leave administration, and position identification numbers (PINs). DBM is required to coordinate with DJS to establish and track the special leave accrual and transfer rules for qualifying employees under the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Transit Administration to submit a report by December 1, 2023, and each year thereafter on assaults on public transit operators to each local executive authority, the State's Attorney for each county, and certain committees of the General Assembly; and requiring the report to include information on the nature of each assault, the mode of transit involved, the location of the assault, whether the police were involved, and the outcome of any investigation.
Title: Transportation – Assaults on Public Transit Operators – Report

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Harassment; Threats
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) to submit an annual report by December 1 each year on assaults on public transit operators to county and municipal executive authorities, county State's Attorneys, and specified legislative committees. The report must include data on assaults, comparisons to other states, and transit industry best practices, with the initial December 1, 2023 report including five years of historical data and evaluations of safety technologies and the feasibility of a statewide local transit safety officer.
responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
stakeholders: Public transit operators (including bus, rail, subway operators, and station managers employed by MTA, WMATA, or local political subdivisions), local transit systems, local executive authorities, and State's Attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Transportation Trust Fund) expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 only for MTA to hire a consultant to evaluate the feasibility of establishing a statewide local transit safety officer; other reporting requirements can be absorbed with existing resources. Local governments can provide data and receive reports within existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Transit Administration to compile and submit an annual report on assaults on public transit operators, evaluate prevention technology, and assess the feasibility of establishing a statewide local transit safety officer, incurring an estimated $50,000 cost in FY 2024.

The Maryland Transit Administration is a modal administration of MDOT, and the bill impacts MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund by $50,000 in FY 2024 to fund the required safety officer feasibility evaluation.

Synopsis: Authorizing an applicant to appeal a certain decision issued by the State Public Information Compliance Board; authorizing a party aggrieved by a final judgment of a circuit court in a proceeding for judicial review of a certain decision of the Board to appeal to the Appellate Court of Maryland.
Title: Public Information Act - Decisions of the State Public Information Act Compliance Board - Appeals

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: House Bill 1051 authorizes an applicant under the Public Information Act to appeal a decision issued by the State Public Information Act Compliance Board to a circuit court, establishing venue where the applicant resides or has a principal place of business for disputes involving allegations that a request was frivolous or in bad faith. The bill also authorizes an aggrieved party to appeal a circuit court's final judgment in such proceedings to the Appellate Court of Maryland.
responsible_party: State Public Information Act Compliance Board and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Public Information Act applicants, custodians of public records, state and local government agencies, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances, and small business effects are minimal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing the State Public Information Act Compliance Board (PIACB), authorizing applicants to appeal PIACB decisions to circuit courts and establishing the automatic stay of board decisions pending appeal.

The bill establishes judicial procedures for appeals of PIACB decisions in circuit courts, sets venue requirements, and expressly authorizes aggrieved parties to appeal final circuit court judgments to the Appellate Court of Maryland.

The Office of the Attorney General publishes the Public Information Act Manual, provides legal counsel and administrative support to the PIACB, and represents state agencies and custodians in legal proceedings and appeals under the Public Information Act.

Synopsis: Establishing in Harford County a performing arts theater beer and wine license that authorizes the holder to sell or serve beer and wine in certain performing arts theaters at retail for on-premises consumption; and establishing an annual license fee of $500.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Performing Arts Theater License

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: Establishes a performing arts theater beer and wine license in Harford County that allows nonprofit organizations operating performing arts theaters to sell or serve beer and wine for on-premises consumption during and around performances, subject to certain conditions and an annual fee of $500.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Nonprofit performing arts theaters in Harford County, theatergoers, and local alcoholic beverages wholesalers.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Harford County local revenues are projected to increase by $500 annually starting in FY 2024 based on the estimated issuance of one license. Additional local enforcement activity can be managed using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees state alcohol and sales tax collection. While this bill establishes a local alcoholic beverages license administered by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners, license holders are required to purchase beer and wine from state-authorized and licensed wholesalers.

Synopsis: Altering the quota used to determine the maximum number of certain alcoholic beverages licenses that the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County may issue from one for every 3,000 individuals to one for every 4,000 individuals.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Alteration of License Quota
bill_summary: Increases the population quota from 3,000 to 4,000 individuals per specified Class A alcoholic beverages license in Harford County, and restricts the Board of License Commissioners to issuing no more than one Class A, Class A-1, or Class A-2 off-sale license per quota threshold.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Prospective and current alcoholic beverages license applicants and retailers, as well as residents in Harford County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references population data specified by the Maryland Department of Health to determine the quota formula for alcoholic beverages licenses issued in Harford County.

Synopsis: Establishing a 6-day and a 7-day Class HC (health club) beer and wine license in Harford County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County to issue the license to a person who sells health club services; exempting the holder of the license from certain distance requirements related to places of worship and schools; establishing an annual fee of $1,300 for a 6-day license and $1,400 for a 7-day license; etc.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class HC (Health Club) License
bill_summary: Establishes 6-day and 7-day Class HC (health club) beer and wine licenses in Harford County for qualifying health clubs that offer a swimming pool or pickleball courts and have at least 150 dues-paying members. The license authorizes on-premises sales of beer and wine from 1:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. in pool bar areas or indoor lounges, and exempts holders from certain distance requirements from places of worship and schools.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Harford County
stakeholders: Harford County health clubs, health club members and patrons, and Harford County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Harford County local revenues increase beginning in fiscal 2024 by an estimated $1,400 annually, based on an expected single 7-day license being issued (the annual fee is $1,300 for a 6-day license and $1,400 for a 7-day license). The county can monitor the licenses with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a local Class HC beer and wine license in Harford County to be issued by the local board of license commissioners. The Comptroller oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry and alcohol excise taxation, but has minimal involvement as this is a local licensing measure with no state fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention to develop strategies to prevent and respond to hate crime activity and evaluate State laws and policies relating to hate crimes; and requiring the Commission to report to the General Assembly on or before December 1 each year, beginning in 2024, on legislative recommendations to address hate crimes in the State.
Title: Hate Crimes - Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention within the Office of the Attorney General to develop strategies to prevent and respond to hate crimes, evaluate state laws and policies, and submit annual policy recommendations to the State Department of Education and the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Victims and communities impacted by hate crimes (including racial, ethnic, religious, and LGBTQ+ populations), Maryland educators and students, law enforcement agencies, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: State federal fund expenditures increase by $114,400 in FY 2024 to hire a contractual assistant Attorney General using federal grant funds. Beginning in FY 2025, the bill establishes a mandated general fund appropriation, increasing general fund expenditures by $136,300 in FY 2025 to make the position permanent, rising to $156,400 by FY 2028. Revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). The Attorney General appoints the members, serves as or designates the chair, and OAG provides staff, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact to fund an Assistant Attorney General.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates an ongoing state commission, the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention, tasked with developing hate crime prevention strategies and evaluating laws.
The Commission is mandated to submit an annual report directly to the State Department of Education containing policy recommendations to address hate crimes that occur in schools.
The bill designates a representative of the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights as a statutory member of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.
The bill explicitly designates a representative of the Maryland Center for School Safety as a statutory member of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.

The bill establishes a mandated general fund appropriation starting in fiscal year 2025 to fund a full-time Assistant Attorney General and maintain commission operations, impacting DBM's budget formulation responsibilities.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include funds in the annual state budget starting in fiscal year 2025 to staff and operate the Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the maximum fines for smoking cannabis in a public place; prohibiting a law enforcement officer from initiating a stop or a search of a person, a motor vehicle, or a vessel based solely on certain factors; prohibiting, under certain circumstances, a law enforcement officer from conducting a search of a certain area of a motor vehicle or vessel; providing that evidence obtained in violation of certain provisions of the Act is not admissible in certain proceedings; etc.
Title: Criminal Law and Procedure - Cannabis - Fines for Smoking in Public, Stops, and Searches
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 802

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Prohibits law enforcement officers from initiating stops or searches of individuals, motor vehicles, or vessels based solely on the odor of cannabis, possession of a personal use amount, or proximity of cash to cannabis without indicia of intent to distribute. It restricts vehicle and vessel searches during drugged-driving investigations, renders evidence gathered in violation inadmissible, and lowers civil fines for smoking cannabis in public.
responsible_party: Maryland State Police and other State and local law enforcement agencies, as well as the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Cannabis consumers, motor vehicle and vessel operators, law enforcement officers, State's Attorneys, public defenders, and the court system
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues decrease minimally due to lower civil fines for public cannabis smoking (reduced to a maximum of $50 for a first offense and $150 for repeat offenses) and fewer fine collections from fewer criminal cases. State and local expenditures also decrease minimally from reduced incarceration costs and fewer court proceedings, with law enforcement and judicial resources redirected to other priorities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly restricts law enforcement officers from initiating stops or searches of persons, vehicles, or vessels based solely on the odor of cannabis, possession of personal use amounts, or proximity of cash, significantly impacting the daily operating procedures and enforcement practices of the Maryland State Police.

The bill explicitly references § 8–738 of the Natural Resources Article regarding operating vessels while impaired, directly impacting the Natural Resources Police and their authority to stop and search vessels.

The bill creates an exclusionary rule rendering evidence obtained in violation inadmissible in trials and hearings, reduces civil fine maximums for public smoking, and impacts judicial caseloads and fine collections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes evidentiary exclusions for improper stops and searches related to cannabis, directly affecting criminal defense strategies, suppression motions, and caseloads for public defenders.
The bill directly impacts vehicle search limits during impaired driving investigations under Transportation Article § 21–902 and affects the operations of modal law enforcement units across MDOT.

MDTA employs a dedicated police force that conducts traffic stops and vehicle searches on state toll facilities and highways, which are directly regulated by the bill's restrictions on stops and searches.
MTA operates a sworn transit police force that conducts stops and searches across public transit networks and vehicles, making them directly subject to the bill's restrictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note anticipates a minimal decrease in general fund incarceration expenditures and inmate commitments resulting from fewer arrests, charges, and convictions.
The OAG represents the State in civil and criminal appeals that will involve litigating the bill's new statutory exclusionary rule and search-and-seizure limitations.

Synopsis: Allowing an individual or a business entity to claim a credit against the State income tax for the first $500 of the purchase price of an automated external defibrillator purchased for use at a restaurant location in the State with annual gross income of at least $400,000; prohibiting the credit from being claimed more than once by any individual or business entity for each restaurant location; and providing certain other limitations.
Title: Income Tax - Automated External Defibrillator Tax Credit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Establishes a nonrefundable State income tax credit of up to $500 for the purchase of an automated external defibrillator (AED) for use at a restaurant in Maryland with an annual gross income of at least $400,000. An individual or business entity may claim up to $1,500 in total credits per taxable year, limited to one AED credit per restaurant location, for tax years 2023 through 2027.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland restaurant owners, restaurant patrons and staff, and taxpayers
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are estimated to decrease by $1.12 million in FY 2024, $1.40 million in FY 2025, and $281,000 in FY 2026 across the General Fund, Higher Education Investment Fund, and Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), totaling approximately $2.8 million in losses through FY 2026. General fund expenditures increase by $63,000 in FY 2024 only for administrative tax system modifications by the Comptroller's Office. Local highway user revenues distributed from the TTF decrease by an estimated total of $69,000 from FY 2024 through FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering state income tax credits, processing claims, and modifying tax systems, incurring an estimated $63,000 in general fund expenditures in FY 2024 to update tax systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and regulates the Maryland Public Access AED Program, under which facilities deploying AEDs are required to register, train coordinators, and maintain compliant devices, and provided key cost data for the bill's analysis.
The bill impacts the Department of Transportation due to a reduction in Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues resulting from tax credits claimed against the corporate income tax.

Synopsis: Altering the duties and responsibilities of the Prince George's County Board of Education and certain officers of the county board; altering the voting authority of the student board member; requiring the county board to retain counsel and pay certain counsel fees and expenses incurred for defending a member in litigation involving a member's service in the member's official capacity on the county board under certain circumstances; altering certain procedures for the election of the student member of the county board; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Board of Education and School System Revisions PG 502-23

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- Electronic Comm; Language; Telecom
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill revises the governance, responsibilities, and operations of the Prince George's County Board of Education and public school system. It outlines specific duties for the board chair, mandates annual goals, retreats, and self-evaluations, expands the voting rights and alters election procedures for the student board member, allows the State Board of Education to remove members without the Governor's approval, requires the board to pay legal fees for members sued in their official capacity (applied retroactively to January 1, 2020), and increases board member compensation starting December 7, 2026.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of Education
stakeholders: Prince George's County Board of Education members, Prince George's County Public Schools students, staff, and Prince George's County voters and residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Local expenditures for the Prince George's County Board of Education increase by $48,400 in FY 2027 and by $83,000 annually thereafter due to compensation increases for the chair and elected board members. Expenditures may also increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2024 to provide legal counsel and cover legal defense fees and expenses for board members, including retroactive claims back to January 1, 2020. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing the State Board of Education's authority and administrative hearing procedures to remove members of the Prince George's County Board of Education without requiring gubernatorial approval.
The bill alters executive authority by removing the statutory requirement that the Governor approve the removal of a Prince George's County Board of Education member by the State Board.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of the inspection tax levied on marketable oysters shipped in the shell to any place outside the State from 30 cents to $1 per bushel; increasing the amount of the severance tax levied on oysters caught within certain natural oyster bars from $1 to $2 per bushel; repealing a certain requirement that a certain tax increase be used for the oyster seed program; and requiring that $1 of each $2 of the severance tax levied be used by certain county oyster committees for the repletion of natural oyster bars.
Title: Natural Resources - Oyster Inspection and Severance Taxes - Increase

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill increases the severance tax on oysters harvested from Maryland's natural oyster bars from $1 to $2 per bushel and increases the inspection tax on marketable oysters shipped out of state in the shell from 30 cents to $1 per bushel. It also mandates that $1 of every $2 collected in severance tax be used by county oyster committees in 11 specified counties for the repletion of natural oyster bars.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Commercial oyster harvesters, oyster buyers and shippers, county oyster committees, and seafood industry businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for the Fisheries Research and Development Fund increase by approximately $580,900 annually beginning in FY 2024 due to the increased severance and inspection taxes. There is no local government fiscal impact because county oyster committees are not local government entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to increase oyster inspection and severance taxes paid directly to the Department of Natural Resources for deposit into the Fisheries Research and Development Fund, impacting special fund revenues and expenditures by approximately $580,900 annually for oyster bar repletion.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that a portion ($1 of each $2 collected) of the severance tax be directed for use by county oyster committees across eleven designated Maryland counties for natural oyster bar repletion projects.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to allow a person to hunt game birds and mammals on each Sunday of the game bird and game mammal seasons from 30 minutes before sunrise until 10:30 a.m. in Wicomico County; authorizing the Department to allow Sunday hunting in Wicomico County on public land, subject to certain time restrictions; and adding Wicomico County to the list of counties in which the safety zone for archery hunters extends 50 yards from certain structures occupied by human beings.
Title: Wicomico County - Sunday Hunting and Archery Hunting Safety Zones
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to allow hunting of game birds and mammals on Sundays on private property and designated public land in Wicomico County, subject to specified time restrictions. It also reduces the archery hunting safety zone in Wicomico County from 150 yards to 50 yards from occupied dwellings and structures.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters, landowners, residents near hunting areas, and local businesses in Wicomico County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances. It may have an indirect economic impact on local businesses in Wicomico County due to hunting-related expenditures and potential reductions in deer-related crop and property damage.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article to authorize the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to allow hunting on certain Sundays on private land and designated public land in Wicomico County, and modifies the archery safety zone enforced by the department's Natural Resources Police.

Synopsis: Altering a certain exemption from property tax for real property that is located in Baltimore County that is owned by an incorporated, nonprofit fire company or rescue squad by providing that the exemption applies only if the property is used or will be used exclusively for the purposes of the fire company or rescue squad; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2023.

bill_summary: Alters the property tax exemption for real property in Baltimore County owned by an incorporated, nonprofit fire company or rescue squad, specifying that the exemption applies only if the property is actually used exclusively for company or squad purposes, or is currently unused but will be used exclusively for such purposes in the future.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Incorporated nonprofit fire companies, rescue squads, and local taxpayers in Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues and Baltimore County property tax revenues will not be significantly affected by the exemption alteration. State and local expenditures are not affected, and specific dollar estimates are not provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory criteria for real property tax exemptions for nonprofit fire companies and rescue squads in Baltimore County. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is responsible for hearing administrative appeals and resolving disputes concerning real property valuations and tax exemptions.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including appeals regarding real property tax assessments and exemption determinations originating from local assessments and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards.

bill_summary: Exempts Prince George's County from statewide business improvement district (BID) laws and creates a county-specific framework authorizing the county to establish, govern, expand, and terminate BIDs. It lowers the petition signature threshold required to create or expand a district from 80% to 51% of nonexempt property owners, details board composition and election requirements, and authorizes the county to impose and collect a dedicated BID tax on nonexempt property to fund district operations.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Governing Body
stakeholders: Prince George's County government, commercial and nonexempt real property owners, commercial tenants, residents, and small businesses located within or near proposed or established business improvement districts.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Prince George's County expenditures may increase minimally to hold additional public hearings for proposed BIDs due to the lower petition threshold. Overall county revenues and expenditures will vary depending on how many districts are established or expanded, which cannot be reliably estimated. Administrative costs for tax collection incurred by the county will be reimbursed by the districts, which are funded via a dedicated district tax imposed on nonexempt real property.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Economic Development Article to create a statutory framework for business improvement districts in Prince George's County to foster commercial and economic growth. While the Department of Commerce is Maryland's primary economic development agency, this legislation is administered locally by Prince George's County with no direct state oversight or implementation role.

The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial and tax collection authority and was consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis. However, the business improvement district taxes authorized under the bill are local taxes imposed and collected directly by Prince George's County with no state fiscal impact.

responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Contractors bidding on or performing public works projects in Baltimore County, nonprofit contractor associations, and the Baltimore County local government.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none, as the Maryland Insurance Administration can handle enforcement using existing budgeted resources. Local fiscal impact on Baltimore County is expected to be minimal because honoring certificates of guarantee is discretionary, allowing the county to require standard performance bonds when deemed necessary.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1111 amends the Insurance Article regarding certificates of guarantee used to satisfy local bond requirements. The fiscal note notes that the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees compliance within the Insurance Article and can implement any requirements using existing budgeted resources.

bill_summary: Alters the governance structure of Maryland's three regional resource centers (Eastern Shore, Southern Maryland, and Western Maryland) by establishing a governing board and a regional advisory council for each center, defining member appointment and qualifications, detailing board duties and operational rules, and clarifying the role and responsibilities of the regional resource center director.
responsible_party: Maryland State Library Board / Maryland State Library Agency
stakeholders: Regional resource center personnel, member county public library systems, library trustees, and library patrons in Western Maryland, Southern Maryland, and the Eastern Shore.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. Modifying the governance structure does not alter the State funding formulas for the centers or change the capital project approval process. Local funding is not materially impacted, and any expense reimbursements for governing board members can be covered using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency and State Library Board oversee the public library systems and regional resource centers. The bill directly impacts their oversight duties, including standards compliance, reporting requirements to the State Librarian, and approval of facility erection plans and auditor selection.

The bill mandates that the appointed director of a regional resource center must be eligible for certification as a professional library director by the State Superintendent of Schools within the Department of Education.
The bill explicitly subjects regional resource centers to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits for any State funds received.
The bill provides that any plans selected and approved by governing boards for the erection of regional resource center buildings remain subject to the approval of the Governor.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Locally operated transit systems, Maryland county and municipal governments, and public transit passengers.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies an existing grant program already administered by MDOT, with no effect on overall funding levels. MDOT anticipated providing $104.4 million in locally operated transit system grants in fiscal year 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1125 explicitly designates the Maryland Department of Transportation to administer the newly codified Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program, determining eligible expenses and managing funding sourced from state and federal transportation programs.

As the modal administration within MDOT responsible for directing state and federal grant funding and technical assistance to locally operated transit systems across Maryland's counties and municipalities, the MTA is directly involved in the execution and operations of this grant program.

stakeholders: Harford County Advisory Plumbing Board members, Harford County local government, and local plumbers and residents of Harford County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It reflects current practice in Harford County regarding appointments to the Advisory Plumbing Board, and county finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of various trades and professions, including plumbing via the State Board of Plumbing. While this bill specifically addresses the local governance, membership, and terms of the Harford County Advisory Plumbing Board with no direct state fiscal or operational impact, it relates peripherally to plumbing standards and profession regulation.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission to conduct a hospital survey and a regional needs assessment regarding operating room capacity for dental procedures requiring anesthesia or sedation, and to develop regional plans to ensure operating room availability for Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) recipients, dentists, hospitals, and ambulatory surgery centers
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission can conduct the survey, needs assessment, regional plans, and report using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of Health with conducting a hospital survey on operating room availability for dentists, jointly conducting a regional needs assessment for dental procedures requiring anesthesia/sedation, and developing regional plans for Medicaid recipients.

The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission, jointly with the Maryland Department of Health, to conduct the regional needs assessment for dental procedures requiring anesthesia or sedation, develop regional operating room availability plans, and report findings to the General Assembly.

bill_summary: House Bill 1148 establishes the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to evaluate and recommend improvements across the State's behavioral health continuum. It also creates a three-year Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) for high-risk adults, extends coverage and reimbursement parity for audio-only and audiovisual telehealth services through June 30, 2025, requires a telehealth study by the Maryland Health Care Commission, and directs MDH to apply for federal CCBHC planning grant funds and demonstration program participation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals requiring behavioral health and substance use disorder services, high-risk adult patients, health care providers, commercial health insurance carriers, and Medicaid recipients.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $397,700 in FY 2024, $723,300 in FY 2025, $728,700 in FY 2026, $734,300 in FY 2027, and $59,400 in FY 2028. This reflects contractual personnel costs to staff the commission and administer the pilot program, as well as a mandated annual general fund appropriation of $600,000 for the pilot program from FY 2025 through FY 2027. Telehealth reimbursement extension has an indeterminate overall impact on Medicaid and may increase health benefit expenditures for some local governments. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is required to administer the Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program, staff the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, apply for federal CCBHC planning grants and demonstration programs, and oversee Medicaid telehealth reimbursement provisions.

MHCC is mandated to conduct an in-depth study and submit recommendations to the General Assembly regarding telehealth delivery and payment parity. Its Executive Director also serves as a member of the newly created Commission.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is a statutory member of the Commission, and the bill amends the Insurance Article to extend coverage and payment parity mandates for telehealth services offered by commercial carriers regulated by MIA.
The Executive Director of HSCRC serves on the Commission, and the bill explicitly preserves HSCRC's authority to set hospital rates and facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access along with four dedicated workgroups to evaluate and report on the behavioral health continuum.

The Governor is required to jointly designate the Commission chair, appoint numerous stakeholder members to the Commission, include a mandated annual appropriation of $600,000 for the pilot program in the state budget for FY 2025-2027, and receive annual reports.
DBM is responsible for supervising the state budget process, which must incorporate the mandated appropriation of $600,000 annually for the pilot program for fiscal years 2025 through 2027.

The Secretary of Disabilities or a designee is a designated member of the Commission, which is tasked with examining behavioral health care for individuals with developmental disabilities and complex needs.
The Secretary of Human Services or a designee is designated by statute as a member of the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services or a designee serves as a member of the Commission, which includes a specific workgroup focusing on youth behavioral health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of DPSCS or a designee serves on the Commission, which evaluates services and infrastructure for criminal justice-involved and forensic populations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the office is designated as a member of the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: A representative from the Office of the Public Defender is appointed by the Governor to serve on the Commission, which reviews behavioral health access for court-ordered and justice-involved populations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the 22 stakeholder appointments to the newly created Commission.

Synopsis: Requiring certain Medicaid funding to be used to provide community services to individuals waiting for services through waiver programs; authorizing certain Medicaid funding to be used for expanding provider capacity in certain waiver programs; and altering the uses of certain funding appropriated to the Dedicated Purpose Account in the fiscal year 2023 budget bill.
Title: Medicaid Waiver Programs - Waitlist and Registry Reduction (End the Wait Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations

bill_summary: The End the Wait Act broadens the authorized use of funds previously designated in the fiscal year 2023 budget for Autism Waiver expansions to support Medicaid waiver expansions more generally. Specifically, it requires up to $20 million of those funds to be used to provide community services to individuals waiting for services across seven specified waiver programs, and authorizes funding to be used to expand provider capacity, recruit and retain staff, and adjust provider rates. It also allows future budget appropriations intended to reduce waiver waitlists to be used for hiring and retaining providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals on waitlists and registries for Maryland Medicaid waiver programs (including Community Pathways, Community Supports, Family Supports, Brain Injury, Home- and Community-Based Options, Medical Day Care Services, Medically Fragile Children, and Autism waivers), as well as waiver service providers and direct support staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no net impact on State revenues or expenditures because the bill reallocates existing funds rather than appropriating new money. Up to $20.0 million from the fiscal 2023 Dedicated Purpose Account appropriation is redirected to provide community services and expand provider capacity for specified waiver waitlists. There is no local government fiscal impact, but there is a potential meaningful positive impact on small business waiver service providers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for administering the Medicaid waiver programs, developing waitlist reduction plans, expanding provider capacity, and utilizing the authorized waiver expansion funds.

The Maryland State Department of Education jointly administers the Autism Waiver with MDH, receives at least $10 million in transferred funds for students with disabilities under the budget amendment provisions, and collaborates on federal waiver applications.
DBM is responsible for processing the budget amendments from the Dedicated Purpose Account and coordinating state budget development to reflect statutory funding mandates for the waiver programs.

The bill mandates that the Governor include sufficient funds in the annual budget bill starting in fiscal 2024 to carry out waitlist reduction and provider expansion for the specified Medicaid waiver programs.

Synopsis: Making certain shared appreciation agreements subject to the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law and other provisions of law that regulate certain loans of single extensions of closed end credit and revolving credit plans; and authorizing the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to adopt certain regulations regarding the enforcement of and compliance with provisions of law that regulate shared appreciation agreements.

bill_summary: This bill subjects shared appreciation agreements to the Maryland Mortgage Lender Law and state credit regulations governing closed-end credit and revolving credit plans, bringing entities offering these agreements under the oversight and regulatory authority of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation.
responsible_party: Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Residential property owners, consumers seeking home financing, and mortgage lenders or credit grantors offering shared appreciation agreements.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill codifies and clarifies existing regulatory practice and therefore does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Certain small business lenders may experience increased compliance and licensing costs if they are not already licensed as mortgage lenders.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Labor's Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation (OCFR), which oversees and regulates mortgage lenders and financial institutions in the State. The bill explicitly authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to adopt regulations enforcing compliance with credit provisions governing shared appreciation agreements.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically through its Consumer Protection Division, enforces Maryland credit and consumer financial protection laws and served as an information source on the regulation of consumer shared appreciation agreements.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, the Maryland Children's Health Program, and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for all services rendered to an enrollee by a licensed pharmacist within the pharmacist's lawful scope of practice to the same extent as services rendered by any other health care practitioner; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed by January 1, 2024.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), and certain commercial health insurance carriers to reimburse licensed pharmacists for all services rendered within their lawful scope of practice to the same extent as other licensed health care providers. It also prohibits conditioning pharmacist reimbursement on whether the pharmacist is employed by a physician, pharmacy, or facility, or acting under a physician's orders.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, independent and retail pharmacies, Medicaid and MCHP enrollees, individuals with commercial health insurance coverage, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid and MCHP expenditures (split approximately 49% general funds and 51% federal funds) increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal year 2024 to the extent that the bill increases billing for covered services. Federal fund revenues increase correspondingly. There is no material impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Local government expenditures for employee health insurance may increase to the extent that reimbursement parity increases costs for fully insured health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), which are mandated by the bill to cover services provided by licensed pharmacists to the same extent as other providers. Additionally, MDH is specifically required to apply for and obtain federal waivers or state plan amendments to implement these changes, which will have a direct fiscal impact on the department.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates private insurers, health maintenance organizations, and nonprofit health service plans in the state. The bill amends the Insurance Article to require carriers under MIA's regulatory jurisdiction to reimburse pharmacist-rendered services on par with other health care providers.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange operates the state's individual and small business health insurance marketplace, where qualified health plans must comply with state insurance mandates and benefit requirements altered by the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and was consulted regarding the bill's potential fiscal impact on state-provided health coverage.

stakeholders: Licensed residential behavioral health and substance-related disorder treatment programs with fewer than 17 residents and their clients.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can adopt the required regulations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and local finances are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health adopt regulations establishing food service facility standards appropriate for certain residential behavioral health programs with fewer than 17 residents.

stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists, authorized prescribers, and patients participating in drug therapy management contracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State governmental operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health regulates health care professionals, including licensed pharmacists through the State Board of Pharmacy. This bill modifies statutory requirements under the Health Occupations Article regarding the form and execution of therapy management contracts between pharmacists, prescribers, and patients.

responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners

fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Dental Examiners special fund revenues increase minimally beginning in FY 2024 from license application fees as additional dentists seek licensure under the bill. Any operational workload associated with processing applications can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Dental Examiners operates within the Maryland Department of Health and is the regulatory body responsible for qualifying foreign-trained faculty applicants for the ADEX examination and issuing general dental licenses.

The bill directly applies to faculty members at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry, an institution within the University System of Maryland, and requires the school to provide written letters of support for qualifying faculty candidates.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Military service members, veterans, and military spouses seeking occupational and professional licenses in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs can complete the required study and report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Department of Labor to lead and conduct the study on the utilization of the expedited occupational and professional licensing process for service members, veterans, and military spouses, and report findings to the Governor and General Assembly.

The bill explicitly mandates that the study and report be conducted by the Department of Labor in consultation with the Department of Veterans Affairs (now the Department of Veterans and Military Families).

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as it codifies existing administrative and enforcement practices following the statutory establishment of the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission.
