fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and any operational impact on Calvert County is not expected to materially affect local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Civil infractions designated to be prosecuted by county attorneys in Calvert County are adjudicated in the Maryland District Court system, which is administratively supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to file a petition for expungement of certain criminal records based on a conviction for certain hunting offenses.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Hunting Offenses - Expungement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes an individual convicted of certain misdemeanor hunting-related offenses under the Natural Resources Article to file a petition for expungement of related police, court, and other official records.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Individuals convicted of specified misdemeanor hunting offenses, court personnel, and law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase through FY 2026 due to additional clerical workload from expungement petitions, though the exact cost is indeterminate (for illustration, one contractual clerk costs approximately $46,200 in FY 2024). The Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill with existing resources. State general fund revenues increase minimally from the $30 filing fee per expungement petition. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allows individuals convicted of specified hunting offenses to petition the District and Circuit Courts for expungement of their court and police records, creating an administrative workload and potential clerical expenditure impact for the Judiciary.

The bill authorizes expungement of misdemeanor offenses under Title 10 of the Natural Resources Article, which are administered and enforced by the Department of Natural Resources and its Natural Resources Police, requiring compliance with court expungement orders.

Synopsis: Altering a certain benefit amount for certain fire and rescue volunteers; and authorizing the board of commissioners to approve an increase in benefit payment for certain fire and rescue volunteers.
Title: Calvert County - Length of Service Award Program - Benefits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill alters the Length of Service Award Program (LOSAP) in Calvert County by increasing death and burial benefits for qualified fire, rescue squad, and dive team volunteers. It also authorizes the Calvert County Board of County Commissioners to approve benefit increases for qualified volunteers matching the cost-of-living percentage increases granted to county employees.
responsible_party: Calvert County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Calvert County volunteer firefighters, rescue squad members, rescue dive team members, and their surviving beneficiaries.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Calvert County expenditures may increase by a minimum of $450,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2024 if cost-of-living increases are authorized for LOSAP benefits, with additional minimal increases resulting from higher death and burial benefit payments. Calvert County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the State Workers' Compensation Commission as the entity responsible for determining whether a qualified volunteer died in the line of duty, which triggers eligibility for the county-funded death benefit.

Synopsis: Defining "generating station" as it relates to the requirement to obtain a certificate of public convenience and necessity or approval from the Public Service Commission for a person who constructs a generating station that has the capacity to produce more than 2 but not more than 14 megawatts of electricity from a solar photovoltaic system; requiring an electric company to provide meter aggregation for certain eligible customer-generators under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Public Utilities - Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity and Meter Aggregation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water

bill_summary: This bill defines 'generating station' under the Public Utilities Article to exclude certain solar photovoltaic systems or combinations of systems with individual capacities up to 2 megawatts and cumulative capacities between 2 and 14 megawatts from Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) requirements under specified conditions. Additionally, it requires electric companies to provide meter aggregation for certain eligible customer-generators, expanding the policy to include units of State government and public senior higher education institutions.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Electric companies, solar energy developers, and eligible customer-generators (such as agricultural users, nonprofits, local governments, State government units, and public senior higher education institutions)
fiscal_impact_summary: State government operations and finances are not materially affected, though the Public Service Commission, Department of Natural Resources, and Maryland Department of the Environment may review fewer CPCN applications. Local government expenditures face an indeterminate but potentially significant impact: jurisdictions may see reduced costs from fewer CPCN intervention cases, but could incur higher costs if they independently regulate, study, or hire consultants for local energy generation projects bypassing the CPCN process. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency responsible for regulating electric utilities, issuing Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN), reviewing generating station exemption applications, and overseeing net metering and meter aggregation regulations.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents the interests of residential utility customers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding utility regulations, CPCN cases, and meter aggregation policies.

Under the bill, abandoned application deposits from proposed generating stations that fail to commence construction within 18 months are transferred to the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is administered by the Maryland Energy Administration.

The Department of Natural Resources evaluates power plant siting through its Power Plant Research Program as part of the State's CPCN review process and will experience an operational impact from having fewer CPCN applications to evaluate.

The Maryland Department of the Environment participates in the State's review and environmental analysis of CPCN applications, which may decrease as more solar photovoltaic systems qualify for exemptions.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse to study existing laws, policies, and practices relating to elder abuse and crimes commonly committed against older adults; and requiring the Task Force to submit a final report by December 31, 2024, to the Governor and the General Assembly with its findings and recommendations regarding changes to State law, policy, and practice that would aid in preventing elder abuse.
Title: Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Elder Abuse and Neglect -see also- Vulnerable Adults
Vulnerable Adults -see also- Developmental Disabilities; Eld

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse to study existing laws, policies, and practices concerning elder abuse and crimes against older adults, and to recommend legislative and administrative changes to improve elder protection and prosecution.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Older adults and vulnerable seniors in Maryland, elder care advocates, healthcare and legal professionals, and law enforcement
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $26,500 in FY 2024 and $11,400 in FY 2025 to hire a part-time contractual staff member for research and administrative support through the task force's termination. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Aging and the Long-Term Care Ombudsman as members of the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse, requires the Department of Aging to staff the task force, and directly incurs general fund expenditures for contractual staffing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force on Preventing and Countering Elder Abuse to study existing laws, policies, and practices and make recommendations on combating elder abuse.
The Governor is required to designate the chair of the task force, appoint 11 members representing various stakeholder entities, and receive the task force's preliminary and final reports.
The Attorney General (or their designee) is designated as a statutory member of the task force, which will study existing legal protections and make recommendations on prosecuting elder abuse.
The Maryland Chief Medical Examiner and a representative of the Maryland Office of Health Care Quality—both within the Department of Health—are designated members of the task force.
The Director of the Office of Adult Services, a unit within the Department of Human Services that oversees adult protective services, is designated as a task force member.
The Maryland Health Care Commission is specifically mandated to have a representative appointed to the task force by the Governor.
A representative of the Maryland State Police is required to be appointed to the task force by the Governor to contribute law enforcement perspectives on elder abuse.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in the recruitment, vetting, and processing of the multiple gubernatorial appointments required for the task force.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from parking certain vehicles in the Town of Sharpsburg, Washington County, subject to a certain exception.
Title: Town of Sharpsburg - Parking of Vehicles - Restrictions

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits parking certain commercial and large vehicles—including large trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses—on streets or highways in the Town of Sharpsburg, Washington County, unless parking is essential to the immediate use of the vehicle.
responsible_party: Town of Sharpsburg and local law enforcement
stakeholders: Owners and operators of large trucks, tractors, trailers, and buses parking in the Town of Sharpsburg, as well as town residents and motorists.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Local enforcement in the Town of Sharpsburg can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article to regulate the parking of specific vehicle classes (trucks, tractors, trailers, and buses) on streets and highways in the Town of Sharpsburg. The Department of Transportation was consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

The bill establishes statutory parking prohibitions with per-day and per-vehicle penalties that may be adjudicated through the District Court system if contested. The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Establishing a minimum training course compensation of $50 and minimum daily compensation of $250 for election judges for each election day and each early voting day actually served; requiring the State Board of Elections to reimburse each local board elections for $50 of the extra compensation that is paid to each returning election judge; and requiring the State Board to develop and implement a marketing campaign to assist in the recruitment of individuals to serve as election judges.
Title: Elections - Election Judges - Minimum Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elections -see also- Ballots; Camp Financ; Pol Cands; Voting
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill establishes minimum compensation levels across Maryland for election judges, mandating at least $250 per day for new election judges, an additional $100 per day for returning election judges, and at least $50 for each completed course of instruction. It requires the State Board of Elections to reimburse local boards of elections $50 of the extra daily compensation paid to returning election judges and to develop and implement a statewide marketing campaign to recruit diverse election judges.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Election judges, poll workers, local boards of elections, county governments, and prospective election judge recruits.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $1.6 million to $2.1 million annually beginning in fiscal year 2024, reflecting reimbursement to local boards for returning election judges ($1.0 million to $1.4 million) and a 50% share of marketing campaign costs ($0.6 million to $0.7 million). Local government expenditures increase collectively by $3.2 million to $3.8 million annually beginning in fiscal year 2024 for higher election judge compensation, the local share of returning judge pay, a 50% share of marketing costs, and a one-time voter registration system software modification ($18,300). Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1200 directly mandates the Maryland State Board of Elections to reimburse each local board of elections $50 of the extra compensation paid to returning election judges and requires the agency to develop and implement a statewide marketing campaign to recruit election judges, resulting in a direct general fund expenditure impact of approximately $1.6 million to $2.1 million annually.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and managed care organizations to provide coverage for biomarker testing that is supported by medical and scientific evidence; establishing requirements for deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for biomarker testing; and requiring the Maryland Health Care Commission to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on the impact of providing biomarker testing.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Required Coverage for Biomarker Testing

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: This bill requires commercial health insurance carriers beginning January 1, 2024, and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid, including managed care organizations) beginning July 1, 2025, to provide coverage for biomarker testing for the diagnosis, treatment, management, or ongoing monitoring of a disease or condition when supported by medical and scientific evidence. It sets rules limiting cost-sharing and requiring coverage to minimize disruptions in care, and it mandates studies and reports by the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Medicaid recipients, individuals enrolled in state-regulated commercial health plans who require biomarker testing, healthcare providers, and health insurance carriers and managed care organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures (40% general funds, 60% federal funds) and corresponding federal matching revenues will increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount beginning in FY 2026; however, these costs are likely offset by indeterminate treatment savings and cost avoidance. A minimal special fund revenue increase occurs in FY 2024 for the Maryland Insurance Administration from $125 rate and form filing fees. Reporting requirements for the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission will be absorbed using existing resources. Local government expenditures may increase to the extent that fully insured employee health benefit plan premiums increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is required by the bill to cover biomarker testing beginning July 1, 2025, and MDH must submit a comprehensive study and report to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

MHCC is specifically mandated by Section 3 of the bill to submit an evaluation report to legislative committees by December 1, 2025, analyzing the impact and access of biomarker testing coverage across demographics and insurance types.
MIA regulates private health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans subject to the new coverage mandate, reviews form and rate filings, and receives associated filing fee revenues.
DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and reviewed the bill's impact on state health plan coverage and state budget expenditures.
The Governor's Office receives the mandated report on Medicaid biomarker testing coverage and reimbursement recommendations from the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for early childhood education teacher certification completed through an alternative teacher preparation program; requiring the State Department of Education, in consultation with the Maryland Higher Education Commission, to establish specific goals for the recruitment and retention of teachers in teacher preparation programs; requiring that "high staff qualifications" for publicly funded eligible prekindergarten providers must be implemented by the 2027-2028 school year; etc.
Title: Maryland Educator Shortage Reduction Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; Leg Policy Committee
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Primary Schools -see also- Education; Private or Public Sch.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: The Maryland Educator Shortage Reduction Act of 2023 establishes initiatives to recruit and retain educators across the State. It creates the Teacher Development and Retention Program as a pilot program offering stipends to college students pursuing teaching careers who commit to service in high-needs schools or shortage areas; expands loan assistance repayment through the renamed Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award to include public school mental health professionals; modifies qualifications and service terms for the Teaching Fellows for Maryland scholarship; delays high staff qualification deadlines for eligible prekindergarten providers by two years; and requires the Maryland State Department of Education to establish recruitment and retention goals and maintain an educator diversity dashboard.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)
stakeholders: Prospective teachers, undergraduate and graduate education students, current public school educators, public school mental health professionals, eligible prekindergarten providers and staff, and local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $15.7 million in FY 2024, which includes $15.0 million in contingent budget funding ($10.0 million to capitalize the new Teacher Development and Retention Fund and $5.0 million for expanded Nancy Grasmick awards) plus $694,067 in one-time IT, evaluation, and dashboard costs. General fund expenditures remain at $5.2 million in FY 2025 and FY 2026 to support recurring loan assistance awards and ongoing operations. Special fund expenditures from the new fund increase by $1.3 million in FY 2024, peaking at $4.2 million in FY 2027. Local school boards can accommodate reporting requirements using existing resources, with no direct impact on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is a primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with establishing goals for teacher recruitment and retention, maintaining the Maryland Educator Recruitment, Retention, and Diversity Dashboard, defining high-needs schools and teacher shortage areas, and setting standards for early childhood alternative teacher preparation.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) and its Office of Student Financial Assistance are primary implementing entities responsible for administering the Teacher Development and Retention Program and Fund, the Teaching Fellows for Maryland scholarship program, and the expanded Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award within the Janet L. Hoffman LARP.

MHEC is directly responsible for administering the financial assistance programs established and modified by the bill, including the Teacher Development and Retention Program, stipends, and expanded student loan repayment assistance for teachers and mental health professionals.

USM institutions house teacher preparation programs directly affected by new recruitment and retention goals, host students eligible for stipends and scholarships under the expanded programs, and include multiple campuses identified as eligible for initial program participation.

Morgan State University operates teacher preparation programs, meets the institution of initial eligibility criteria based on student Pell Grant participation rates, and is specifically targeted for outreach and recruitment as a Historically Black University.

St. Mary's College of Maryland operates educator preparation programs, including a Master of Arts in Teaching, and is directly affected by state recruitment/retention goals and student financial support programs under the bill.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the newly established Teacher Development and Retention Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly created Teacher Development and Retention Fund.
This is an Administration initiative establishing reporting requirements to the Governor regarding program evaluations and mandating specific annual budget allocations.
DBM oversees the state budget allocations, contingent funding, and authorized personnel positions needed to implement the bill's programs.

Synopsis: Requiring an adult family member to submit a death certificate or evidence of disability to the State Real Estate Commission before the family member may carry on the business of a disabled or deceased licensed real estate broker; permitting a certain business to designate a licensed real estate broker to provide real estate brokerage services under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Real Estate Brokers - Disability or Death and Termination of Employment of a Broker

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers
Termination of Employment -see also- Work, Labor, and Employ

bill_summary: Requires an adult family member to submit a death certificate or proof of disability to the State Real Estate Commission before carrying on the business of a deceased or disabled real estate broker. It also authorizes real estate businesses to designate a replacement licensed broker if proof is not provided within a reasonable time or if a broker is terminated.
responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, real estate brokerage businesses, and family members of deceased or disabled real estate brokers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, as the State Real Estate Commission can implement the changes with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission operates within the Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill establishes requirements and procedures for the Commission regarding the reissuance of licenses and broker designations upon the death, disability, or termination of a real estate broker.

Synopsis: Authorizing a court to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs to the parent of a child with a disability who is the prevailing party in a certain special education proceeding; prohibiting a court from awarding attorney's fees and related costs to certain parents in a certain proceeding under certain circumstances; and authorizing an award of attorney's fees and related costs to a parent of a child with a disability who is a prevailing party under certain circumstances.
Title: Special Education - Judicial Actions - Attorney's Fees and Related Costs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody

bill_summary: Authorizes a court to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs, including expert witness fees, to a parent of a child with a disability who is the prevailing party in special education administrative appeals or court proceedings, subject to certain limits regarding settlement offers.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Parents of children with disabilities, students with disabilities receiving special education services, and local school systems or public education agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected, as very few proceedings involve direct State agency supervision. Beginning in FY 2024, local school system expenditures may increase to cover awarded attorney's fees and costs in cases where parents prevail (anticipated in 10 or fewer cases statewide annually); total amounts will vary and specific dollar figures are unavailable. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE oversees the State's special education system, sets standards for free appropriate public education (FAPE), assists parents with the dispute resolution and mediation process, and can be a party to due process and judicial proceedings governed by this bill.
The bill explicitly authorizes circuit courts to award reasonable attorney's fees and related costs, including expert witness fees, to prevailing parents in special education judicial proceedings.

OAH receives due process complaints, appoints administrative law judges to conduct due process hearings regarding special education disputes under § 8-413, and issues the administrative decisions that may be appealed to court.

The Maryland School for the Deaf is explicitly defined in § 8-413 as a public agency responsible for providing education to students with disabilities, making it subject to due process actions and potentially liable for awarded fees and costs.

The Juvenile Services Education Program is explicitly classified as a public agency under § 8-413, subjecting education programs serving youth under DJS custody to due process dispute provisions and potential court fee awards.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to annually proclaim January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day; and requiring the proclamation to include a declaration of the purposes of Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day.
Title: Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Requires the Governor to annually proclaim January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day, establishing it as a day of reflection and a pledge to share Holocaust history and lessons with future generations to bear witness against prejudice and hate.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland families, educators, religious communities, political bodies, media, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: Commemorating Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day has no effect on State, local, or small business finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1244 directly mandates that the Governor annually issue an official proclamation designating January 27 as Maryland Holocaust Remembrance Day and specifies the required content of that proclamation.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date by 2 years for certain provisions of law relating to Maryland Insurance Commissioner enforcement duties regarding administrative services organizations that administer a certain delivery system for specialty mental health services.
Title: Maryland Insurance Commissioner Enforcement - Specialty Mental Health Services and Payment of Claims - Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Extends the termination date by two years (to May 18, 2025) for provisions requiring the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce clean claims laws and penalties on administrative services organizations (ASOs) that administer the Medicaid specialty mental health delivery system.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Administrative services organizations (ASOs) administering specialty mental health services, Medicaid specialty mental health service providers, and Medicaid managed care enrollees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) can continue enforcement activities using existing budgeted resources. Special fund revenues for the MIA may increase by an indeterminate amount in FY 2023, 2024, and 2025 if penalties or fines are assessed on ASOs. There is no local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the statutory sunset on the Maryland Insurance Commissioner's enforcement authority regarding clean claims payment requirements for administrative services organizations (ASOs) managing specialty mental health services.

The specialty mental health services delivery system and its administrative services organization (ASO) operate under the Maryland Department of Health's Medicaid program, and findings from Insurance Commissioner investigations into the ASO must be reported to MDH.

Synopsis: Exempting a certain retiree of the Employees' Retirement and Pension Systems from a certain earnings limitation when the retiree is reemployed by a certain previous employer for a certain time period to assist with the administration of federally funded grants or projects related to the COVID-19 pandemic; and providing for the retroactive application of the Act to January 1, 2020.
Title: Employees' Retirement and Pension Systems - Reemployment Earnings Limitation - COVID-19 Exemption

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Exempts State retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health for up to five years from the reemployment earnings limitation and pension benefit offsets if they assist with the administration of federal COVID-19 grants or work with the COVID Unified Command on staffing support or contact tracing. The exemption applies retroactively to January 1, 2020, and sunsets on December 31, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: State retirees rehired by the Maryland Department of Health to assist with COVID-19 relief administration, staffing support, or contact tracing.
fiscal_impact_summary: Because the exemption applies to a limited number of individuals, it has no material effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or revenues. Any benefit offsets already applied in 2023 must be repaid to affected retirees. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental initiative requested by the Maryland Department of Health, specifically allowing the department to rehire State retirees without an earnings cap penalty to assist with COVID-19 grant administration and response efforts.

The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, oversees reemployment earnings limitations, and must process the exemption and refund any offsets previously deducted from affected retirees.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission is required to disqualify an applicant who committed a crime involving moral turpitude from holding a video lottery employee license.
Title: Video Lottery Employee Licenses - Crimes of Moral Turpitude - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- Circuit; Appeals; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: House Bill 1288 creates an exception to the disqualification criteria for a video lottery employee license, allowing licensure for individuals with a disqualifying conviction, active parole, probation, or prosecution if it involves a nonviolent misdemeanor (other than a gambling offense) and the applicant completed a problem-solving court program.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Applicants for video lottery employee licenses who have completed problem-solving court programs, video lottery operation licensees, and the problem-solving court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is not expected to significantly affect the number of license applications, administrative costs, license fee revenues, or judicial caseloads and costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the licensing disqualification standards applied by the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission when reviewing video lottery employee license applications.

The bill explicitly references problem-solving court programs under the Judiciary's Office of Problem-Solving Courts as an exception to license disqualification, which may potentially impact demand or participation in these court programs.

Synopsis: Amending certain prior authorizations of State Debt to alter the requirement that certain grantees provide certain matching funds; extending the termination date of certain grants; altering the authorized uses of certain grants; and changing the names of certain grantees.
Title: Prior Authorizations of State Debt - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Art, Music, and Cultural Affairs -see also- Mus; Theat; etc
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission

bill_summary: This bill modifies prior authorizations of Maryland State debt across several previous capital budgets by extending grant termination and expenditure deadlines, eliminating or altering matching fund requirements, updating grantee names and project scopes, and reallocating specific grant funds among new or revised capital projects.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works and Maryland Department of General Services
stakeholders: Grant recipients, nonprofit organizations, local government entities, and local communities receiving capital grant funding across various Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances because it only alters the terms, purposes, grantees, and deadlines of previously authorized State debt rather than creating new debt or appropriations. There is no local fiscal impact unless the grantee is a local government.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS administers State capital grants, manages capital project grant agreements, and was the primary agency consulted regarding the modification of these prior authorizations.
The Board of Public Works oversees and certifies matching fund requirements and approves capital expenditures and contracts funded through State debt authorizations.
The bill directly modifies the purpose and recipient specifications of capital grants allocated to the Historic St. Mary's City Fort to 400 Commission for design and archaeological survey work.
The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) is administered by the Department of Planning, and the bill explicitly repeals the requirement for a specified grantee to convey a historic easement to MHT.

Synopsis: Altering provisions relating to criminal background investigations for certain individuals who care for or supervise children; and requiring certain facilities to apply to the Central Repository for a national and State criminal history records check for each employee, employer, individual, or volunteer.
Title: Family Law - Child Care - Criminal Background Investigations
bill_summary: House Bill 1300 alters provisions governing criminal background investigations for individuals who care for, supervise, or have direct access to children. It requires child care facilities and other specified institutions to apply directly to the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository for national and State criminal history records checks on behalf of employees, employers, and volunteers, aligning Maryland statutory procedures with federal FBI standards for background check requests and information dissemination.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Child care centers, family child care homes, schools, camps, foster care providers, child care employees, contractors, volunteers, and individuals seeking adoption or guardianship.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. It ensures Maryland law conforms with federal requirements so that covered entities may continue obtaining required national criminal history records checks.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by DPSCS. The legislation directly governs and alters the operations of the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR) within DPSCS, restructuring how criminal history records checks are requested, processed, and disseminated to comply with federal FBI standards.

The bill directly affects child placement, foster care, and social service operations overseen by DHS and local departments of social services. It updates protocols for criminal background investigations and emergency out-of-home placement name-based checks, resolving prior federal compliance issues where DHS-related background check requests had been denied.

The bill impacts child care licensing and school personnel oversight under MSDE. It mandates the transmission of criminal record information to MSDE for employees and residents in licensed child care centers and registered family child care homes, and maintains MSDE's duty to cross-reference providers with the sex offender registry.
The bill applies criminal history records check requirements to employees and operators of home health agencies and residential service agencies licensed by MDH that provide services to minors.

The bill references juvenile detention, correction, and treatment facilities, and maintains a specific statutory exclusion clarifying that compensated DJS staff are not categorized as 'employees' under this subtitle.

Synopsis: Urging the U.S. General Services Administration to select for the new Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters one of the two finalist sites located in Maryland.
Title: Locating the New Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters in Maryland
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Joint Resolution 1
bill_summary: A joint resolution urging the U.S. General Services Administration to select one of the two finalist sites located in Maryland—Greenbelt or Landover—as the location for the new consolidated Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Residents and businesses of Prince George's County and Maryland, as well as Federal Bureau of Investigation personnel
fiscal_impact_summary: Compliance with the joint resolution does not directly affect State or local finances or operations. However, Prince George's County anticipates significant economic benefits if selected as the site for the new FBI headquarters.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The resolution involves intergovernmental relations and advocacy with the federal government regarding the location of the FBI headquarters, and a copy of the resolution is formally directed to the Governor.

Attracting the consolidated FBI headquarters to Maryland aligns directly with the department's role as the state's chief economic development agency responsible for job creation and business attraction.

The resolution explicitly highlights the state's mass transit connections and expresses the General Assembly's commitment to supporting employee relocation and improving transportation infrastructure at the Prince George's County finalist sites.
The resolution highlights USM member institution Bowie State University as a key asset providing a diverse talent pipeline of educated workers for the proposed FBI headquarters.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly wearing, carrying, or transporting a firearm in certain locations; prohibiting a person from wearing, carrying, or transporting a firearm onto certain property unless the owner or owner's agent has given certain permission; altering certain provisions of law relating to the authority of the Secretary of State Police to limit the wearing, carrying, or transporting of a handgun at certain times and locations; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Wearing, Carrying, or Transporting Firearms - Restrictions (Gun Safety Act of 2023)

bill_summary: The Gun Safety Act of 2023 establishes restrictions on wearing, carrying, or transporting firearms in specific sensitive locations—including areas for children and vulnerable individuals, government and public infrastructure sites, and special purpose areas—as well as inside another person's dwelling or on private property without express permission. The bill also mandates that handgun permit holders carry concealed firearms, repeals the Secretary of State Police's discretionary authority to place time and location limits on permits, and establishes misdemeanor penalties for violations.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Firearm owners and wear/carry handgun permit holders, private property and business owners, state and local government agencies, and law enforcement officers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues and expenditures resulting from new criminal misdemeanor penalties. Additionally, State and local government expenditures across multiple funds may experience a minimal increase in FY 2024 to install required signage at entrances of owned or leased government buildings. Local government expenditures may also minimally increase due to local incarceration penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Police, through the Secretary of State Police, administers handgun wear, carry, and transport permits. The bill directly alters statutory provisions governing the terms and restrictions of handgun permits under Public Safety § 5-307 and impacts MSP's law enforcement duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal misdemeanor offenses and penalties for carrying firearms in prohibited public infrastructure locations, sensitive areas, and private property without permission, increasing caseloads for public defenders representing indigent defendants.

The Judicial Branch will adjudicate new misdemeanor criminal cases resulting from the bill's prohibitions. The bill also explicitly preserves the authority of administrative heads of Maryland courts to adopt rules and orders regulating or prohibiting weapons in court facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes misdemeanor criminal penalties that include terms of imprisonment, potentially impacting state and local correctional systems, while also providing specific exemptions for correctional officers and wardens.

As the primary manager of state-owned and leased facilities, DGS is impacted by the requirement that units of State government post clear and conspicuous signage prohibiting firearms at the main entrances of government buildings.
The bill designates polling places and ballot canvassing locations as prohibited government/public infrastructure areas where wearing, carrying, or transporting a firearm is banned.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates video lottery facilities (casinos), which are regulated and overseen by this agency, as 'special purpose areas' where firearms are prohibited.
The bill designates locations licensed to sell or dispense cannabis for on-site consumption, regulated by the MCA, as 'special purpose areas' where carrying or transporting firearms is prohibited.

Synopsis: Expanding the requirement that the Department of Natural Resources make available and issue certain licenses and stamps in a digital or electronic format; and providing that, if the Department cannot issue certain licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, or certificates in a digital or electronic format because of federal restrictions, it is the intent of the General Assembly that the Department issue certain licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, or certificates in a digital or electronic format whenever the federal restrictions are eliminated.
Title: Department of Natural Resources – Documents – Digital or Electronic Issuance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses

bill_summary: Expands the requirement that the Department of Natural Resources offer and issue certain licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates in a digital or electronic format, allowing individuals to satisfy possession and display requirements electronically with specified exceptions.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Individuals holding or applying for Maryland licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, or certificates issued by the Department of Natural Resources, including hunters, anglers, and boaters.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill's provisions using existing resources, and the small business effect is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 10 directly tasks the Department of Natural Resources with expanding its digital and electronic issuance of licenses, stamps, permits, registrations, and certificates, subject to specified exemptions.

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that the Capital Debt Affordability Committee include certain debt that is secured by future federal aid within its review of State tax supported debt; altering the calculation of the maximum amount of debt secured by future federal aid that the Department of Transportation may issue; providing that the maximum amount of debt that may be issued is calculated as of June 30; establishing the Maryland Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs; etc.
Title: Department of Transportation - Financing and Commission on Transportation Revenue and Infrastructure Needs (State and Federal Transportation Funding Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Electric Motor Vehicles -see also- Motor Vehicles
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
