bill_summary: Renames the Black Bear Damage Reimbursement Fund to the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund and expands its purpose to award grants for nonlethal projects that prevent bear damage and reduce human-bear conflicts. It caps grant funding so that at least 10% of the annual appropriation is reserved for direct damage reimbursements, increases the maximum individual reimbursement limit from $3,000 to $5,000 per year, and authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of at least $50,000 in the State budget for the fund.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Farmers, agricultural producers, landowners, pet owners, local governments, parks and recreation departments, businesses, tribes, nonprofit organizations, and higher education institutions, especially in Western Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $145,600 in FY 2024, which includes an assumed $50,000 discretionary appropriation to capitalize the fund and $95,637 for DNR administrative costs (one natural resources technician, a vehicle, and operating expenses). Out-year general fund expenditures range from $115,700 to $125,100 annually. Special fund revenues and expenditures both increase by $50,000 annually beginning in FY 2024. Local governments and higher education institutions may experience an increase in grant revenues and corresponding expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR directly administers the Black Bear Damage Prevention and Reimbursement Fund, evaluates grant requests, disburses reimbursements, adopts program regulations, and requires additional staff and funding to implement the bill.

The University of Maryland Cooperative Extension Service (part of USM) is statutorily designated to evaluate and determine bear damage amounts for reimbursement claims, and institutions of higher education are also eligible to apply for grant funding under the bill.
The bill explicitly designates the State Treasurer to hold the newly renamed nonlapsing special fund.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Comptroller with accounting for the newly renamed nonlapsing special fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of at least $50,000 annually to the fund in the state budget bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing the holder of a Class 4 limited winery license to prepare, sell, or serve any food under certain conditions; altering certain requirements for off-premises and on-premises consumption at a limited winery; and removing the 14-day notice requirement for certain planned promotional events at a limited winery.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages - Class 4 Limited Winery License - Food Service

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk

bill_summary: Authorizes Class 4 limited winery license holders to prepare, sell, or serve sandwiches and other light fare, as well as broader food options if licensed as a food establishment and meeting certain food-to-alcohol sales ratios. The bill also extends standard daily operating hours for on-premises consumption to 10:00 p.m. and repeals the 14-day advance notice requirement previously required for evening promotional events.
responsible_party: Maryland Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
stakeholders: Holders of Class 4 limited winery licenses, winery visitors and consumers, and local alcoholic beverage licensing boards
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It is expected to have a meaningful positive impact on small business Class 4 limited wineries due to expanded food service and operating hours.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcoholic beverage industry in the state and is explicitly referenced in the bill. The legislation repeals the requirement that Class 4 limited winery license holders file a notice of planned promotional events with the Comptroller.

The bill allows winery license holders to prepare, sell, or serve broader food offerings beyond light fare provided they are licensed to operate a food establishment under Title 21, Subtitle 3 of the Health - General Article, which falls under the regulatory authority of the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill impacts Class 4 limited wineries that utilize Maryland agricultural products. Under the amended section, the Secretary of Agriculture has regulatory and exemption authority regarding the percentage of Maryland-grown fruit used by these wineries, and the agency was consulted on the legislation's fiscal note.

Synopsis: Altering the salary of the Washington County Sheriff to be 90% of the salary of the State's Attorney of Washington County; and repealing the requirement for the Washington County Salary Study Commission to study and issue a report that contains recommendations relating to the salary of the Sheriff of Washington County.
Title: Washington County - Sheriff's Salary - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill sets the annual salary of the Washington County Sheriff to 90% of the salary of the State's Attorney of Washington County, taking effect at the beginning of the next term of office. It also repeals the requirement that the Washington County Salary Study Commission study and recommend salary adjustments for the sheriff.
responsible_party: Washington County Commissioners
stakeholders: The Sheriff of Washington County and Washington County taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Washington County expenditures increase by a minimum of $21,100 in FY 2027 and at least $36,200 annually thereafter when the salary change takes effect with the next term of office in December 2026. Local revenues are unaffected.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of General Services, in coordination with the Department of Information Technology, to negotiate certain contracts with third parties for the acquisition or maintenance of body-worn cameras, equipment, or technology for certain law enforcement agencies; requiring the Department of Information Technology, in coordination with the Department of General Services, to study the cost and feasibility of implementing a statewide uniform storage and access system for law enforcement body-worn camera data; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Law Enforcement - Body-Worn Cameras (Body-Worn Camera Appropriation and Financing Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Department of General Services, in coordination with the Department of Information Technology, to negotiate contracts with third parties to acquire and maintain body-worn cameras, related equipment, and technology on behalf of law enforcement agencies upon request. The bill also requires the Department of Information Technology, in coordination with the Department of General Services, to conduct a study on the cost and feasibility of a statewide uniform storage and access system for body-worn camera data by December 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Department of General Services and Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: State, county, and municipal law enforcement agencies and officers, third-party technology/camera vendors, and Maryland taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $200,000 to $400,000 in FY 2024 only for the Department of Information Technology to hire a consultant for the required feasibility study, which may be mitigated by findings from previous studies. General contract negotiation duties can be handled by the Department of General Services and the Department of Information Technology with existing resources. State and local law enforcement agencies may experience administrative efficiencies and indeterminate cost effects from centralized contract negotiations. There is no effect on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is directly mandated by the bill to negotiate contracts with third parties for body-worn cameras, equipment, and technology on behalf of requesting law enforcement agencies, and post them on eMaryland Marketplace Advantage.

DoIT is required to coordinate with DGS on negotiating body-worn camera contracts and is mandated to conduct a feasibility and cost study on implementing a statewide uniform storage and access system for body-worn camera data, incurring an estimated $200,000 to $400,000 in fiscal 2024 expenditures.
As the primary state law enforcement agency required by Maryland law to deploy body-worn cameras, MSP directly benefits from administrative efficiencies and procurement contracts negotiated by DGS.
DNR operates the Natural Resources Police, a state law enforcement agency authorized to utilize contracts negotiated by DGS for body-worn cameras and associated data technology.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees law enforcement and public safety personnel who are eligible to participate in and benefit from the statewide body-worn camera procurement contracts negotiated under this legislation.

MDOT oversees modal administrations with law enforcement units (such as the Maryland Transportation Authority Police and Maryland Transit Administration Police) that can utilize the negotiated body-worn camera contracts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP previously conducted a related feasibility study regarding body-worn camera storage and access, the data and findings of which may be utilized to mitigate study costs for DoIT.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority; exempting the Authority from certain provisions of State procurement law; and altering the report on the Authority's comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy the Authority is required to submit to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly to be due by December 15, 2023, to include any procurement activities undertaken by the Authority, and to be also submitted to the House Health and Government Operations Committee.
Title: Baltimore City – West North Avenue Development Authority – Membership and Procurement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: This bill alters the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority (WNADA), extends the reporting deadline for its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to December 15, 2023, requires the inclusion of procurement activities in the report, and exempts the Authority from most provisions of State procurement law while maintaining adherence to the Minority Business Enterprise program.
responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority
stakeholders: Residents, community associations, and businesses in the West North Avenue target area and buffer zone in Baltimore City, as well as WNADA members and prospective contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Expediting procurement and altering Authority membership have minimal or no direct fiscal impact. An estimated $250,000 contract for the revitalization strategy will be funded using existing resources, independent of the $11.4 million already budgeted for WNADA operations in fiscal 2024.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly alters the membership of the West North Avenue Development Authority to add the Secretary of Commerce, or the Secretary's designee, as a voting member.
The bill specifically adds the Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO), or their designee, as a member of the West North Avenue Development Authority.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a statutory member of the Authority, which is tasked with comprehensive neighborhood revitalization, housing initiatives, and community development along West North Avenue.

The Secretary of Transportation serves as a statutory member of the Authority. Additionally, the bill maintains the requirement that the Authority adhere to the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program, for which MDOT serves as the certifying agency.
The President of Coppin State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, is designated by statute to serve as the Chair of the West North Avenue Development Authority.
The Governor appoints a member to the West North Avenue Development Authority and is the designated recipient of the comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy report due December 15, 2023.

The bill exempts the Authority from Division II of the State Finance and Procurement Article, removing standard procurement requirements and oversight typically conducted by the Board of Public Works.
As the State's central procurement authority, DGS is directly affected by statutory exemptions to Division II of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Although the bill exempts the Authority from general state procurement law, it explicitly retains compliance with Title 14, Subtitle 3 regarding the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program, which the office oversees across state entities.

Synopsis: Establishing certain procedures regarding the persons who may establish or receive distributions from an ABLE account in the Maryland ABLE Program for a certain eligible individual; and requiring the Maryland 529 Board to adopt certain procedures regarding the establishment and operation of an ABLE account by a person other than a certain designated beneficiary.
Title: Maryland Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) Program - Account Establishment - Procedures

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc

bill_summary: This bill aligns Maryland law with IRS regulations governing Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) accounts by establishing procedures and a priority order of authorized individuals (such as an agent under power of attorney, legal guardian, spouse, parent, sibling, grandparent, or SSA representative payee) who may open and manage accounts and request distributions on behalf of an eligible individual with disabilities who cannot do so themselves, while barring certain prohibited individuals.
responsible_party: Maryland 529 Board
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities eligible for the Maryland ABLE Program, their families, legal guardians, authorized representatives, and account contributors.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2024, State general fund revenues and local revenues may decrease, potentially significantly, due to increased personal income tax subtraction modifications claimed for ABLE contributions and qualifying distributions. For every 1,000 additional filers claiming the contribution subtraction, State revenues decrease by an estimated $135,700 and local revenues decrease by $88,400. Maryland 529 nonbudgeted fee revenues and distribution expenditures will increase, which may potentially reduce or eliminate the need for the annual $300,000 State general fund grant supporting the program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the Maryland ABLE Program administered under Maryland 529, authorizing the board to adopt procedures and regulations regarding account establishment, representative priority, and distributions.
The Treasurer's Office oversees Maryland 529 and the Maryland ABLE program, making it directly responsible for executive oversight and financial management of the program.
The bill impacts state personal income tax collections administered by the Comptroller due to subtraction modifications allowed for contributions to and distributions from newly opened ABLE accounts.
The Department of Disabilities consults on the management, administration, and promotion of the Maryland ABLE Program to support financial independence for individuals with disabilities.
MDH administers Maryland's Medicaid program, which is means-tested and specifically interacts with ABLE account asset exclusions under state and federal law.

Synopsis: Establishing the Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program in the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to provide eligible seniors access to affordable civil law-related services; and requiring the Governor to provide an appropriation of $225,000 in the annual budget for the Program.
Title: Maryland Legal Services Corporation - Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program
bill_summary: Establishes the Affordable Life, Wills, and Estate Planning for Seniors Grant Program in the Maryland Legal Services Corporation to provide eligible seniors access to affordable civil legal assistance regarding wills, powers of attorney, trusts, advance health care directives, and life estate deeds.
responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation
stakeholders: Maryland seniors age 65 and older with a family income not exceeding 75% of the state median family income, particularly those in rural communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $225,000 annually starting in FY 2024, with funding in FY 2024 being discretionary and becoming a mandated annual appropriation of $225,000 starting in FY 2025. Revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $225,000 for the program in the state budget and requires an annual report on the program's implementation and utilization to be submitted to the Governor.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and the bill establishes a statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $225,000 annually beginning in FY 2025.

The program directly targets Maryland residents aged 65 and older by providing affordable civil legal services, including advance directives, wills, and powers of attorney, directly aligning with the Department of Aging's mission and advocacy for older adults.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to apply to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration at the Center for Mental Health Services for federal planning, development, and implementation grant funds related to certified community behavioral health clinics for fiscal year 2025; and requiring the Department to apply to the Administration for inclusion in the state certified community behavioral health clinic demonstration program for fiscal year 2026.
Title: Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics - Planning Grant Funds and Demonstration Application

bill_summary: Senate Bill 362 requires the Maryland Department of Health to apply to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) for federal planning, development, and implementation grant funds related to certified community behavioral health clinics (CCBHCs) for fiscal year 2025, and to apply for inclusion in the federal CCBHC demonstration program for fiscal year 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals requiring mental health and substance use disorder treatment, behavioral health providers, and certified community behavioral health clinics.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Maryland Department of Health can apply for federal grant funds and inclusion in the demonstration program using existing budgeted resources. Federal fund revenues may increase in fiscal 2025 to the extent grant funds are received (at a 65% federal match rate), though such revenues were anticipated absent the bill. Costs of participation in the demonstration program are not reflected. Local Effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 362 directly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health apply to SAMHSA for federal planning, development, and implementation grant funds for certified community behavioral health clinics (CCBHCs) for FY 2025, and apply for inclusion in the federal CCBHC demonstration program for FY 2026.

Synopsis: Defining "commercial use" in Baltimore City to include multifamily residential development if the development is located within a waterfront commercial zoning district and within a 0.50-mile radius of a commuter rail station.
Title: Baltimore City - Commercial Use - Definition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: Defines "commercial use" under Baltimore City zoning law to include multifamily residential development if the development is located within a waterfront commercial zoning district and within a 0.50-mile radius of a commuter rail station.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of Municipal and Zoning Appeals and the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
stakeholders: Property developers, commercial property owners, and residents in Baltimore City within waterfront commercial zoning districts near commuter rail stations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Planning advises on sustainable growth, comprehensive land use planning, and statutory land use policy across Maryland jurisdictions, making changes to the Land Use Article regarding Baltimore City zoning classifications relevant to its advisory and oversight role.

The Department of Housing and Community Development oversees housing development policies and community revitalization initiatives. Expanding the definition of commercial use to incorporate multifamily residential housing near transit and waterfront districts directly aligns with its policy scope.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Physicians to place a licensee on emeritus status under certain circumstances; requiring the Board, under certain circumstances, to reinstate the license of an individual who is on inactive or emeritus status; exempting licensees who are on inactive status or emeritus status from continuing medical education requirements; repealing the requirement that the Board issue a license to an individual who is on inactive status under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: State Board of Physicians – Inactive and Emeritus Status

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Physicians -see also- Dentists; Med Exmnrs; Psych; etc

bill_summary: Senate Bill 375 authorizes the Maryland Board of Physicians to place eligible retired physicians on emeritus status and alters requirements for placing physicians on inactive status and reinstating their licenses. It exempts physicians on emeritus or inactive status from continuing medical education requirements and the standard three-year license expiration term, while prohibiting them from practicing medicine or delegating medical acts. Additionally, it permits emeritus licensees to use titles such as "Dr." or "physician" as long as they do not represent that they are authorized to practice medicine in the State.
responsible_party: Maryland Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Licensed physicians in Maryland, particularly retired physicians seeking emeritus status and physicians seeking inactive status, as well as the Maryland Board of Physicians.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures and workload for the Maryland Board of Physicians can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. Any net impact on special fund revenues from emeritus or inactive status fees is anticipated to be minimal. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians operates under the Maryland Department of Health as a health occupations licensing board. The bill directly impacts the Board's licensing procedures by establishing emeritus status, modifying inactive status regulations, and altering continuing education requirements for physicians.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which the payment of a benefit by a governmental unit or quasi-public corporation to a covered employee offsets the liability for benefits under the workers' compensation law; and stating that it is the intent of the General Assembly that the Maryland Association of Counties and the Professional Fire Fighters of Maryland jointly research and report data and analysis on the effects of the Act by December 1, 2024, to interested parties and certain committees of the General Assembly.
Title: Workers' Compensation - Benefits - Offset and Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill limits the workers' compensation benefit offset for covered employees of governmental units or quasi-public corporations, providing that an employer's payment of another benefit only offsets workers' compensation liability if both benefits are based in whole or in part on the same body part. It abrogates the Maryland Supreme Court decision in Spevak v. Montgomery County and requires a joint study and report by the Maryland Association of Counties and the Professional Fire Fighters of Maryland on the effects of the offset changes.
responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
stakeholders: Covered public-sector employees (including local government employees and firefighters), local governments, and workers' compensation insurers such as the Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not directly affected. Local government expenditures likely increase because narrowing the benefit offset will increase workers' compensation liability for those providing disability retirement benefits, though the precise impact cannot be reliably estimated. Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company expenditures will increase to cover additional claims, with a corresponding increase in revenues from higher premiums charged to local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission administers Title 9 of the Labor and Employment Article and adjudicates workers' compensation claims, including determining benefit offsets and making awards against employers or the Subsequent Injury Fund under § 9-610.

The Subsequent Injury Fund is explicitly named in § 9-610 of the bill, as the limitation on benefit offsets directly determines the extent to which the Fund is liable for or relieved of paying workers' compensation benefits.

Known as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the entity serves as workers' compensation insurer for many affected public entities and local governments; the fiscal note projects an increase in its benefit expenditures and premium revenues due to the restricted offset.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of certain voting and nonvoting members of the Upper Shore Regional Council.
Title: Economic Development - Upper Shore Regional Council - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

bill_summary: Alters the voting membership of the Upper Shore Regional Council by replacing the three Cecil County commissioner positions with the Cecil County Executive and two members of the Cecil County Council, while specifying that remaining county council members serve as nonvoting members.
responsible_party: Upper Shore Regional Council
stakeholders: Cecil County Executive, Cecil County Council members, and the Upper Shore Regional Council
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal effect. The local fiscal effect is minimal, as the bill adjusts the composition of Cecil County's representation to reflect its charter government structure without altering the total voting membership or providing compensation to members.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Economic Development Article regarding the Upper Shore Regional Council, which supports regional economic development initiatives in coordination with the Department of Commerce, who served as an information source for the legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory voting and nonvoting membership structure of the Upper Shore Regional Council, a state-authorized regional body.

The Rural Maryland Council fosters regional cooperation across Maryland's rural jurisdictions and works in close partnership with regional planning and development councils, including the Upper Shore Regional Council.

Synopsis: Authorizing the County Executive and County Council of Prince George's County to determine the compensation for the judges of the Orphans' Court for Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Judges of the Orphans' Court - Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes the County Executive and County Council of Prince George's County to set the annual compensation for the judges of the Orphans' Court for Prince George's County, replacing the fixed statutory salaries, with any salary adjustments taking effect at the start of the next term of office.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Executive and County Council
stakeholders: Judges of the Orphans' Court for Prince George's County and Prince George's County government
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George's County expenditures may increase or decrease beginning in FY 2027 depending on salary determinations set by the County Executive and County Council. Due to constitutional limits on mid-term salary changes, adjustments cannot take effect until the start of the next term of office following the 2026 election. County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills serves as the clerk to the Orphans' Court in each county, the entity whose judicial salaries in Prince George's County are addressed by this legislation.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judicial Branch, of which the Orphans' Court is a component, although judge compensation in this case is set and paid at the local county level.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland to study and make recommendations regarding the effectiveness and viability of certain incentives, offerings, or practices employed in other states to attract, support, and retain individuals in fire fighting and emergency medical services roles; and requiring the Commission to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2023.
Title: Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Recruitment and Hiring -see also- Work, Labor, and Emp.
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland to study and make recommendations on strategies, incentives, and practices to attract, support, and retain career and volunteer firefighters and emergency medical services personnel.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Career and volunteer firefighters, emergency medical services personnel, fire companies, and Maryland residents receiving emergency services
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $25,000 (specifically $25,041) in FY 2024 only to hire a part-time contractual employee at the Maryland Department of Labor to staff the commission and prepare the required report. Member reimbursements are minimal and absorbable. Revenues are unaffected, and there is no material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates a representative from the Maryland Department of Labor to serve on the commission, requires the department to provide primary staffing support, and results in a direct fiscal expenditure impact of approximately $25,000 in FY 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MIEMSS (or their designee) is statutorily designated as a member of the commission to study recruitment, retention, and support practices for emergency medical services across Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes a temporary advisory commission—the Commission to Advance and Strengthen Fire Fighting and Emergency Medical Services Within Maryland—to examine issues, make recommendations, and report by December 1, 2023.

The bill designates the Executive Director of the Maryland Fire and Rescue Institute (MFRI), an institute operating within the University of Maryland (USM), or their designee, as a member of the commission.
The newly established commission is required to report its findings and policy recommendations directly to the Governor on or before December 1, 2023.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to make transfers of not more than $150,000,000 subject to certain conditions to establish quasi-endowment funds; and authorizing the Board to use investment income produced by quasi-endowment funds in accordance with the University System of Maryland Policy on Endowment Fund Spending Rule to provide need-based student financial aid.
Title: University System of Maryland - Board of Regents - Quasi-Endowment Funds

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to transfer up to $150 million from fund balances held and invested by the State Treasurer to establish a quasi-endowment fund, and to utilize investment income from the fund to provide need-based student financial aid.
responsible_party: Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland
stakeholders: University System of Maryland institutions and students eligible for need-based financial aid.
fiscal_impact_summary: Assuming the full $150.0 million transfer occurs in fiscal 2024, USM fund balances decrease by $150.0 million with an equivalent increase in invested quasi-endowment funds. Starting in fiscal 2025, higher education revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $1.6 million annually due to higher investment yields, and higher education expenditures for scholarships are estimated to increase by approximately $6.4 million annually based on USM's spending policy, subject to market fluctuations. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to transfer up to $150 million from fund balances to establish a quasi-endowment fund to support need-based student financial aid.
The transfers of up to $150 million will be made out of fund balances currently held and invested by the State Treasurer, and the Treasurer receives the required annual investment performance report.
The bill requires the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to submit an annual investment performance report on its endowment portfolios to the Comptroller.
The bill requires the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland to submit an annual investment performance report on the quasi-endowment portfolio to the Governor.

Synopsis: Increasing the funding level of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund that is administered by the Home Improvement Commission from $250,000 to $1,000,000; increasing a certain Fund threshold that determines whether a fee is assessed to each contractor; and increasing the limit, from $100,000 to $250,000, on the amount of money the Commission may award from the Fund to all claimants for the acts or omissions of a single contractor, subject to a certain reimbursement to the Fund.
Title: Business Regulation - Home Improvement Commission - Guaranty Fund and Award Limits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- Dealers; Elec. Comm.; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the required minimum balance of the Maryland Home Improvement Guaranty Fund from $250,000 to $1,000,000 and raises the trigger threshold at which the Maryland Home Improvement Commission must assess a fee on contractors. It also increases the maximum aggregate amount that may be awarded from the Fund to all claimants for the acts or omissions of a single contractor from $100,000 to $250,000.
responsible_party: Maryland Home Improvement Commission
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners, claimants seeking compensation, and licensed home improvement contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational resources are sufficient to implement the bill. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund increase by an indeterminate, but likely significant, amount due to the quadrupled minimum fund balance requirement ($1,000,000) and increased maximum claim payouts ($250,000). Contractors may face increased special assessments and higher reimbursement liabilities to the Fund. Local governments are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly impacts the Department by altering the minimum balance, contractor assessment thresholds, and maximum payout limits of the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund administered by MHIC.

The statute specifies that all money collected for the Home Improvement Guaranty Fund is deposited with the State Treasurer into a special account, and the State Treasurer is statutorily required to invest the money in the Fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to establish a Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program to provide financial incentives to holders of aquaculture leases who maintain the lease in accordance with certain criteria, maintain the restorative conditions for at least 4 years, and meet certain other criteria the Department considers necessary; authorizing a holder of an aquaculture lease who is participating in the Pilot Program to meet certain requirements by shellfish seed planting only; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Natural Resources -see also- Conserv; Forest & Park; Wildlds

bill_summary: Establishes the Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program within the Department of Natural Resources to provide financial incentives to aquaculture leaseholders who maintain restorative aquaculture conditions on their leases for at least four years, and allows participants to fulfill active lease use requirements solely through shellfish seed planting.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Aquaculture leaseholders and commercial shellfish aquaculture businesses in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $144,631 in FY 2024 and rise to $196,800 by FY 2028 to hire two DNR staff members to administer the program. Additional financial incentive payments are not included in this estimate and remain indeterminate, as they depend on program design and funding sources (which may include private donations, federal funds, or specific state appropriations). There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to establish, manage, and implement the Restorative Aquaculture Pilot Program, adopt governing regulations, verify leaseholder conditions, and distribute financial incentives, resulting in direct operational and fiscal impacts on the agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires DNR to coordinate and consult directly with the statutory Aquaculture Coordinating Council to develop eligibility criteria, metrics for restorative aquaculture, and incentive payment rates.

The bill explicitly tasks the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (a USM institution) with coordinating on the development and identification of restorative aquaculture criteria and metrics.

Synopsis: Altering the amount of taxable or tax exempt bonds that the Maryland Stadium Authority may issue for certain sports entertainment facilities from $200,000,000 to $220,000,000; altering the entities from which the Authority is required to have received a request for financing and construction management services concerning a sports entertainment facility; altering the entities with which the Authority is required to enter into an agreement before issuing bonds to finance a sports entertainment facility; etc.
Title: Economic Development – Sports Entertainment Facilities – Financing and Construction

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds

bill_summary: Increases the bond issuance cap for the Maryland Stadium Authority to finance sports entertainment facilities from $200.0 million to $220.0 million. It also expands eligibility so that nonprofit organizations that own or operate sports entertainment facilities can request financing and construction management services, enter into related agreements with the Authority, and submit annual maintenance assessments.
responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations owning or operating sports entertainment facilities (such as the Hagerstown-Washington County Industrial Foundation), local governments, sports and entertainment patrons, and construction contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Sports Entertainment Facilities Financing Fund (SEFFF) increase by $15.0 million in FY 2024 and $5.0 million in FY 2025 from additional bond proceeds. General fund revenues decrease by $1.1 million in FY 2026 and by $1.5 million annually in FY 2027 and FY 2028 to cover debt service via State Lottery Fund distributions. Local revenues and expenditures may also increase to support local facility development and construction.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Stadium Authority (MSA) is the primary implementing agency of the bill, which increases its bond-issuing cap for sports entertainment facilities from $200 million to $220 million and authorizes MSA to receive financing requests and enter into agreements with nonprofit organizations.

The Board of Public Works must review and approve proposed bond issuances, financing plans, and written agreements entered into by the Maryland Stadium Authority under the increased bond authorization cap.

Synopsis: Extending the termination date, to June 30, 2024, for provisions relating to the authorization of holders of certain manufacturer's licenses to sell and deliver and to directly ship their own alcoholic beverages products to certain individuals under certain circumstances; establishing the maximum amount of beer and liquor that holders of certain manufacturer's licenses may directly ship to consumers in a calendar year; delaying the effective date for the authorization of certain manufacturer off-site permits to July 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Alcoholic Beverages – Manufacturer’s Licenses and Off–Site Permits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Alcoholic Beverages -see also- AB-By Subd; Subst Abuse; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the sunset date from June 30, 2023, to June 30, 2024, for provisions allowing certain licensed alcohol manufacturers to sell, deliver, and directly ship alcoholic beverages to consumers. It limits direct shipment privileges to manufacturers authorized by the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission on or before April 6, 2023, sets annual direct shipment caps per consumer (up to 18 standard 750ml bottles of liquor or 3,456 ounces of beer), requires reporting to the Commission, and delays certain off-site permit provisions to July 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Alcohol and Tobacco Commission
stakeholders: Holders of alcoholic beverage manufacturer licenses (such as distilleries, wineries, and breweries), delivery personnel, common carriers, and Maryland alcohol consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and expenditures for the Alcohol and Tobacco Commission are minimally maintained through the extended June 30, 2024 termination date. There is no material impact on local government finances or operations. Small business alcoholic beverage manufacturers experience a meaningful benefit from continued direct delivery and off-site sales privileges.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees tax administration, including collecting state sales and excise taxes on alcohol, which are expressly required to be paid for direct alcohol shipments under the bill. The agency's summary also identifies it as regulating alcohol industries and enforcing associated tax laws.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for the credit against the State income tax for certain film production activities to include documentaries and talk, reality, and game shows; increasing the percentage of total direct costs that qualify for the tax credit; increasing the aggregate amount of tax credit certificates that the Secretary of Commerce may issue for fiscal years 2024 through 2026; establishing the Maryland Entertainment Council to study and make recommendations regarding Maryland's film, television, and entertainment industry; etc.
Title: Film Production Activity Income Tax Credit - Alterations and Maryland Entertainment Council

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Senate Bill 452 expands eligibility for Maryland's film production activity income tax credit to include documentaries, talk shows, reality shows, and game shows, and adds compensation for Maryland-domiciled writers, directors, and producers to qualifying direct costs. The bill increases the credit percentage from 25% to 28% of total direct costs (and from 27% to 30% for television series), raises the annual aggregate credit caps for fiscal years 2024 through 2026, and establishes the temporary Maryland Entertainment Council to study and make recommendations on strengthening the state's entertainment industry.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Film, television, and entertainment production companies; Maryland resident crew, writers, directors, and producers; small and independent film entities; and local service providers (such as hospitality, catering, and equipment rental businesses).
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues decrease by $3.0 million in FY 2024, $5.5 million in FY 2025, and $8.0 million in FY 2026 due to increased aggregate tax credit caps (increasing to $15.0 million, $17.5 million, and $20.0 million, respectively, before reverting to $12.0 million in FY 2027). The revenue loss predominantly affects the general fund, alongside smaller reductions in the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and Higher Education Investment Fund. General fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2024 and FY 2025 for council study and evaluation expenses. Local highway user revenues from the TTF decrease by $0.1 million to $0.3 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce administers the Film Production Activity Income Tax Credit program, determines eligibility and issues tax credit certificates, jointly adopts program regulations with the Comptroller, and is tasked with providing staff and resources to the newly established Maryland Entertainment Council.

The Comptroller receives notifications of qualifying film production entities, processes refundable income tax credits against state income tax returns, and is required to jointly adopt regulations with the Department of Commerce.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new state advisory body, the Maryland Entertainment Council, charged with evaluating Maryland's entertainment industry assets, studying competitive policies, and submitting reports and strategic recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Governor's appointed Senior Advisor on Film, Television, and Entertainment serves as chair of the Maryland Entertainment Council, the Governor appoints multiple council members and potential honorary cochairs, and the Council submits preliminary and final reports directly to the Governor.

The bill reduces corporate income tax revenues, which directly impacts the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), decreasing TTF revenues by an estimated $0.5 million to $1.5 million annually from FY 2024 through FY 2026 and reducing local highway user grant expenditures.

Synopsis: Authorizing and empowering the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County, from time to time, to borrow not more than $56,000,000 in order to finance the construction, improvement, or development of certain public facilities in St. Mary's County, and to effect such borrowing by the issuance and sale at public or private sale of its general obligation bonds; etc.
Title: St. Mary's County - Public Facilities Bond

Piers and Docks -see also- Marinas; Ports
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of St. Mary's County to borrow up to $56,000,000 through the issuance and sale of general obligation bonds to finance the acquisition, construction, improvement, or renovation of various public facilities, schools, and infrastructure projects in the county.
responsible_party: County Commissioners of St. Mary's County
stakeholders: Residents, property taxpayers, students, and public facility users in St. Mary's County
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: St. Mary's County revenues increase by up to $56.0 million from bond proceeds to fund capital projects. County debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $3.8 million annually over a 20-year period, based on an assumed 3.37% interest rate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly exempts the bonds, refunding bonds, and associated interest income from all State, county, and municipal taxation in Maryland, which relates to the Comptroller's oversight and administration of state tax collections and exemptions.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives to study the types and impact of solar energy incentives and make recommendations regarding measures and incentives needed to ensure that the State meets the solar energy goals established in the State's renewable energy portfolio standard, minority business participation, the creation of good quality jobs, equitable access to renewable energy, and efficient use of land; and requiring the Task Force to submit its report to the General Assembly on or before December 15, 2023.
Title: Task Force to Study Solar Incentives

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives, staffed by the Maryland Energy Administration. The task force is required to study existing state and federal solar incentives, compliance fees, and incentive structures, and make recommendations to help Maryland meet its Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard solar goals, promote minority business participation, support workforce development, and encourage solar placement on previously developed land.
responsible_party: Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Solar energy developers and contractors, environmental advocacy groups, organized labor, minority business enterprises, agricultural and forestry landowners, and Maryland electricity consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly affected; the Maryland Energy Administration can handle staffing duties and member expense reimbursements using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no direct impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) is the primary staff agency for the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives. Its Director is designated as a member, appoints the Task Force chair, and MEA provides staff support and member expense reimbursements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes a temporary statutory body, the Task Force to Study Solar Incentives, to study solar incentive policies and make recommendations to the General Assembly.

The Chairman of the Public Service Commission (or their designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Task Force, and the Task Force's mandate directly concerns the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS) and solar compliance mechanisms regulated by the Commission.
The bill requires one representative of the Office of People's Counsel, designated by the People's Counsel, to serve as a member of the Task Force.
The Governor is tasked with appointing six members to the Task Force, including four solar energy industry representatives and two environmental advocacy representatives.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to state task forces and advisory bodies.

Synopsis: Establishing certain goals and programs related to land conservation; establishing the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program to provide loans to land trusts to purchase land for conservation purposes; authorizing the Maryland Environmental Trust to exercise certain remedies under certain circumstances; prohibiting a person from making any false statements affecting a Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program loan; establishing the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program to support land conservation goals; etc.
Title: Natural Resources - Land Conservation - Establishment of Goals and Programs (Maryland the Beautiful Act)

Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
