bill_summary: The Maryland the Beautiful Act sets state land conservation goals to permanently conserve 30% of Maryland's land by 2030 and 40% by 2040. It establishes the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program and Fund under the Maryland Environmental Trust to provide rolling, low-interest loans to land trusts for acquiring land or conservation easements, supported by a rapid response advisory committee. It also establishes the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program and authorizes annual funding for land and citizen stewardship grants.
responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Trust (MET) within the Department of Natural Resources, along with the Smart Growth Subcabinet
stakeholders: Local land trusts, private landowners, local governments and municipal parks departments, schools, nonprofit community organizations, and agricultural and forestry businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $6.75 million in FY 2025, $738,573 in FY 2026, and roughly $750,000–$764,000 annually in subsequent years to cover staff, operating expenses, $485,000 in annual grants, and an assumed $6.0 million initial general fund capitalization for the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund. Special fund revenues increase by $6.0 million in FY 2025 (and ongoing indeterminate amounts from loan repayments), with special fund expenditures of $3.0 million each in FY 2025 and FY 2026 to issue loans. Local government revenues and expenditures are likely to increase by indeterminate amounts beginning in FY 2025 due to grant and conservation project participation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), an entity within the Department of Natural Resources, to administer the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Program, the associated revolving loan fund, and the 40 x 40 Land Conservation Implementation Grant Program, as well as Keep Maryland Beautiful stewardship grants. It also places a DNR representative on the Land Preservation Rapid Response Advisory Committee.

The bill mandates the Smart Growth Subcabinet (staffed and led in large part by the Department of Planning) to coordinate actions across agencies, develop and publish a plan to meet the State's 30% by 2030 and 40% by 2040 conservation goals, update the plan every five years, and submit annual progress reports to the General Assembly.

The bill establishes the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund and specifically directs the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately, invest its money, and credit any interest earnings directly back to the fund.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund and administer the allocation of transfer tax revenues as modified by the bill.

The bill establishes statewide land conservation targets affecting agricultural lands, involves the Smart Growth Subcabinet on which the Secretary of Agriculture sits, and relates closely to farmland preservation programs.

The bill's conservation goals specifically include carbon sequestration, ecosystem stabilization, and greenhouse gas reduction, and MDE serves on the Smart Growth Subcabinet responsible for developing the implementation plan.
The bill authorizes multi-million dollar annual appropriations and special fund capitalizations that impact State budget preparation and fiscal management overseen by DBM.

The bill authorizes executive budget actions, including discretionary annual appropriations for the Local Land Trust Revolving Loan Fund and various conservation grants, and engages the Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment to review and update specifications for sediment control plans in a certain manner on or before December 1, 2025, and every 5 years thereafter; prohibiting the Department from authorizing the discharge of stormwater associated with construction activity under a general discharge permit unless certain requirements are satisfied; and requiring the Department to take certain public notice and comment actions if a person makes a written request within the public notification period of the permit.
Title: Sediment Control Plans, Discharge Permits for Stormwater Associated With Construction Activity, and Notice and Comment Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Erosion -see also- Sediment Control; Shore Erosion
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to review and update specifications for sediment control plans by December 1, 2025, and every five years thereafter, incorporating updated precipitation data and consulting with relevant stakeholders. It also establishes enhanced public notice and comment procedures (including a 60-day extension upon request) before MDE can authorize stormwater discharges under a general permit for construction sites disturbing five or more acres in environmentally sensitive areas, such as high-quality waters, the Critical Area Buffer, or 100-year floodplains.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Construction developers, contractors, engineering firms, certified erosion and sediment control professionals, local soil conservation districts, watershed protection organizations, and property owners near construction sites.
fiscal_impact_summary: MDE general fund expenditures increase by $83,303 in FY 2024 and by at least $100,000 annually thereafter for one regulatory and compliance engineer to manage enhanced public notice and comment requirements. Additional MDE costs to update sediment control plan specifications are anticipated to exceed $500,000 beginning in FY 2024, which MDE will seek to fund via federal grants or additional general funds. Local governments may experience increased enforcement, training, and project compliance costs beginning in FY 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory agency tasked with implementing the bill, including reviewing and updating specifications for sediment control plans every five years, consulting with designated stakeholders, and administering enhanced public notice and comment requirements for stormwater construction discharge permits.

MDOT SHA is a Phase I MS4 permittee and frequently undertakes large-scale highway and roadway construction projects that require sediment control plans and stormwater discharge permits, making it directly subject to updated specifications and possible permitting delays.

MDOT oversees state transportation infrastructure projects that involve land disturbance and earth changes, which require compliance with MDE's updated sediment control plan standards and construction stormwater discharge permitting processes.

As the primary agency responsible for planning and managing construction and capital improvements for State-owned facilities, DGS acts as a permit holder subject to the revised sediment control specifications and expanded public review requirements.

MDA oversees soil conservation programs, and local soil conservation districts serve as the primary approval authorities for erosion and sediment control plans; the Maryland Association of Soil Conservation Districts is also a required statutory consultee for updates.

The bill establishes permit conditions tied to the Critical Area Buffer (governed under Title 8, Subtitle 18 of the Natural Resources Article) and includes specific permit exemptions for projects dedicated solely to natural resources restoration.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County; requiring the Task Force to study issues related to student transportation, bus driver wages, and multiyear contracts for bus contractors in Charles County and to research best practices in surrounding jurisdictions related to the facilitation of student transportation; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the members of the Charles County Delegation to the General Assembly on or before September 1, 2023.
Title: Charles County - Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County to examine student transportation, bus driver wages, multiyear bus contracts, and regional best practices, and to report findings and recommendations to the Charles County Delegation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Charles County school bus contractors, bus drivers and contractor employees, Amalgamated Transit Union Local 689, Charles County Public Schools, and public school students
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as the Maryland Department of Labor can staff the task force using existing resources and any travel expense reimbursements for members are minimal and absorbable. The bill does not materially affect Charles County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Labor to provide administrative and operational staff support for the newly created Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Task Force to Study School Bus Operator Contracts and Wages in Charles County as a temporary study body to examine student transportation issues, driver compensation, and contracting practices.

Synopsis: Requiring that a county or municipality that operates a minority business enterprise utilization program for county or municipal procurements and has a process for the certification of minority business enterprises shall accept as certified a person that holds a certification as a minority business enterprise by the State certification agency.
Title: Local Procurements - Minority Business Enterprise Utilization Programs - Certification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Requires any county or municipality that operates a Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) utilization program and maintains an MBE certification process to accept businesses certified by the Maryland Department of Transportation under the State's MBE program.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation and local county and municipal governments operating MBE programs
stakeholders: Minority business enterprises (MBEs), small business contractors, and county and municipal governments operating procurement utilization programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: Minimal increase in certification requests for the Maryland Department of Transportation, absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Local effect: No material fiscal impact on local government finances or operations, though local governments could realize potential administrative savings if they discontinue separate local certification programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the designated State certification agency for Maryland's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program. Because local governments will now be required to accept State-certified MBEs, MDOT may experience an increase in certification applications and associated operational workload.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office oversees and coordinates the State's Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) program policy and outreach across Maryland, making changes to how local governments recognize state MBE certifications directly relevant to its core mission.

Synopsis: Altering composition of the stakeholder advisory committee to advise the Department of Natural Resources on the scope and management of Port of Deposit State Historical Park; requiring the Department to make a certain report to the General Assembly on or before September 1, 2024; extending the deadline for the Bainbridge Development Corporation to transfer certain property to the Department to June 1, 2025; authorizing the Governor to include in the State budget an appropriation of at least $400,000 for certain purposes; etc.
Title: Port of Deposit State Historical Park - Planning

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees

bill_summary: Senate Bill 517 alters provisions related to the planning and establishment of the Port of Deposit State Historical Park. Specifically, it extends the deadline for the Bainbridge Development Corporation to transfer site land to the Department of Natural Resources from June 1, 2023, to June 1, 2025, modifies the membership of the stakeholder advisory committee, requires DNR to submit a follow-up report to the General Assembly by September 1, 2024, mandates perpetual preservation for transferred property not incorporated into the park, and authorizes the Governor to appropriate at least $400,000 in fiscal year 2025 for a Phase 1 archaeological survey and soil study.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Cecil County residents, the Town of Port Deposit, Bainbridge Development Corporation, cultural and historical preservation advocates, and visitors to Maryland State Parks.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase by at least $400,000 in FY 2025 to fund a Phase 1 Archaeological Survey and Soil Study for the Tome School and Snow Hill sites. Department of Natural Resources reporting requirements are expected to be handled using existing resources. State revenues are not affected, and the bill does not directly affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency responsible for establishing, protecting, and administering the Port of Deposit State Historical Park, receiving transferred property, convening the stakeholder advisory committee, completing the required study and report to the General Assembly, and receiving potential state funding.
The bill designates the Secretary of Planning (or designee) and the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust (housed within MDP) as ex officio members of the park's stakeholder advisory committee.
The Chief Archaeologist of MDOT SHA (or their designee) is designated as a voting member of the stakeholder advisory committee for the park.
MDOT's Chief Archaeologist from the State Highway Administration is appointed as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The Secretary of the Environment (or designee) is designated as a nonvoting ex officio member of the stakeholder advisory committee.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is appointed as a nonvoting ex officio member of the stakeholder advisory committee.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of at least $400,000 in the fiscal year 2025 State budget for DNR to conduct an archaeological survey and soil study.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the composition and specifies duties and recommendations for the stakeholder advisory committee established to advise on the park's scope and management.

Synopsis: Altering the defined term "peer support counseling program" for peer services offered to fire, rescue, or emergency medical services members to be "peer support program"; and requiring peer support programs to be evidence-based.
Title: Fire, Rescue, or Emergency Medical Services Entities - Peer Support Programs

NarrowSubjects.Name: Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: This bill alters statutory terminology regarding peer support for fire, rescue, or emergency medical services (EMS) personnel by changing "peer support counseling program" to "peer support program" and replacing references to counseling sessions with interactions. It also requires that peer support programs, specialist training, and associated services be evidence-based.
responsible_party: Behavioral Health Administration (BHA)
stakeholders: Fire, rescue, and emergency medical services (EMS) personnel, peer support specialists, and the International Association of Firefighters.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State or local fiscal impact, as the bill's changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Behavioral Health Administration (BHA), a unit of the Maryland Department of Health, is statutory lead responsible for developing a report on best practices and professional standards for evidence-based peer support programs and publishing the report and an approved training list on its website.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is specifically required by the bill to be consulted by the Behavioral Health Administration in the development of the report on best practices and professional standards for evidence-based peer support programs for fire, rescue, and EMS personnel.

Synopsis: Altering the formula for the calculation of certain assessments by the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund; requiring the Board of Trustees of the Fund, under certain circumstances, to authorize the Fund to withdraw certain amounts from the money held by the Fund from a prior overassessment; prohibiting members of the Industry Automobile Insurance Association from being subject to an annual assessment under certain circumstances; requiring in a certain fiscal year that additional funds be allocated to the Fund; etc.
Title: Insurance – Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund – Assessments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicle Insurance -see also- MD Auto Insurance Fund
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill alters the formula and collection procedures for assessments issued by the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) to automobile insurers during significant operating losses, authorizes MAIF to withdraw prior overassessment funds into its surplus, requires prompt refunds or rate-filing reductions for excess member surcharges, and temporarily allocates an additional $2.0 million of uninsured motorist penalty revenues to MAIF in fiscal year 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
stakeholders: Automobile insurers operating in Maryland (Industry Automobile Insurance Association members), motor vehicle policyholders, uninsured drivers, and the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $2.0 million in FY 2024 due to an increased distribution of uninsured motorist penalties to MAIF. Nonbudgeted fund balances totaling $10.2 million are transferred to MAIF surplus in FY 2023 from prior overassessments. Nonbudgeted revenues for MAIF increase by $10.2 million in FY 2023 and $2.0 million in FY 2024. Local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) by altering its assessment calculations, authorizing MAIF to withdraw $10.2 million from prior overassessment funds into its surplus, providing an additional $2.0 million distribution from uninsured motorist penalties in FY 2024, and mandating a reporting requirement to the General Assembly.

The bill requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to verify the Board of Trustees' assessment certifications, supply aggregate net direct written premium data for member insurers, and receive notices of assessment percentages.
The bill amends Transportation Article § 17-106, modifying the statutory allocation of uninsured motorist penalties collected by the MVA to direct an additional $2.0 million to MAIF for FY 2024.
As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT is affected by the statutory reallocation of motor vehicle penalty revenues under the Transportation Article.

Synopsis: Extending to June 30, 2025, the inclusion of certain audio-only telephone conversations under the definition of "telehealth" for the purpose of certain provisions of law relating to reimbursement and coverage of telehealth by the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; requiring the Maryland Medical Health Care Commission to study and make recommendations regarding the delivery of health care services through telehealth by December 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Preserve Telehealth Access Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Extends the inclusion of audio-only telephone conversations under the definition of telehealth and extends required payment parity for telehealth services under Medicaid and commercial health insurance plans through June 30, 2025. It also directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to study telehealth service delivery and payment parity and report recommendations by December 1, 2024.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Health care providers, Medicaid recipients, commercially insured patients receiving telehealth services, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures and federal fund revenues for covered telehealth services continue through FY 2025, with an indeterminate net impact on overall Medicaid spending. The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal special fund revenue increase in FY 2024 from $125 rate and form filing fees. Local governments may experience increased health plan expenditures to maintain telehealth reimbursement parity.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) to conduct a study and make recommendations regarding the delivery of health care services through telehealth, payment parity, provider costs, and clinical effort, and to submit a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to require the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health, to extend coverage and reimbursement parity for audio-only telehealth services through June 30, 2025.

The bill amends the Insurance Article to extend coverage and reimbursement parity mandates for commercial health insurers and HMOs through June 30, 2025, which the Maryland Insurance Administration regulates, reviews policy filings for, and enforces.

The bill contains an explicit statutory clarification stating that the telehealth reimbursement requirements do not supersede the authority of the HSCRC to set appropriate hospital rates and facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth.

Synopsis: Altering the number of years before the end of the term of a video lottery operation license that a licensee is required to provide certain notice of intent to renew the license and is authorized to apply for renewal; providing for the term of a renewed license; requiring the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to renew a certain license unless the Commission makes a certain finding; requiring the Commission, under certain circumstances, to provide a licensee a certain hearing; etc.
Title: Video Lottery Operation License - Renewal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State

bill_summary: This bill extends the renewal term for video lottery operation (casino) licenses from 10 years to 15 years and establishes notice and application procedures for renewal. It requires licensees to pay a renewal fee equal to 0.75% of their average annual proceeds from video lottery terminals and table games from the preceding three-year period (calculated every five years), to be paid in annual installments into the Education Trust Fund, while remitting 20% of the paid fee back to the licensee for marketing and promotions targeting out-of-state audiences.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Maryland video lottery operation licensees (casinos), the Maryland State Department of Education, public school students and educational programs funded via the Education Trust Fund and Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Education Trust Fund revenues increase by $225,300 in FY 2026 and escalate to approximately $2.7 million annually by FY 2032 once all six video lottery facilities are renewed. Special fund expenditures for the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund increase by $1.3 million in FY 2027 and $2.6 million in FY 2032, offset by equal reductions in General Fund education expenditures. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency (and its Commission) is the primary regulatory and implementing body for the bill, tasked with processing renewal notices, establishing renewal application procedures and fees by regulation, adjudicating renewal eligibility, holding hearings, and directing renewal proceeds.

The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for disbursing proceeds from video lottery terminals upon receipt of transmittals from the Commission, including the 20% distribution back to licensees for out-of-state marketing.
The State Treasurer is responsible for the custody, investment, and reinvestment of monies credited to the Education Trust Fund, which will receive the renewal license fee revenues.

The renewal license fees directly accrue to the Education Trust Fund to support Maryland public school funding and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future programs administered under the department's purview.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Attorney General to investigate, prosecute, and remediate certain civil rights violations under certain circumstances and in a certain manner; authorizing the Attorney General to intervene in certain causes of action under certain circumstances; establishing certain penalties and authorizing the Attorney General to obtain certain relief in certain civil actions, conciliation agreements, and settlement agreements; authorizing the Attorney General to recover certain investigation and litigation costs in a certain manner; etc.
Title: Human Relations - Civil Rights Enforcement - Powers of the Attorney General

bill_summary: Authorizes the Attorney General to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations on behalf of Maryland residents. The bill allows the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief, equitable remedies, civil penalties, and restitution, creates the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund, and mandates coordination with the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights in cases of overlapping jurisdiction.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Maryland residents facing unlawful discrimination, as well as businesses and entities subject to civil rights enforcement and civil penalties.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $1,048,706 in FY 2024 to support 12 new positions within the Office of the Attorney General (budgeted via a contingent transfer in the FY 2024 budget), increasing to $1.4 million by FY 2028 for ongoing operational costs. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase from civil penalties (up to $10,000 for a first violation and $25,000 for subsequent violations) deposited into the newly created Civil Rights Enforcement Fund. General fund revenues increase minimally from interest earnings. No material impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 540 directly empowers the Office of the Attorney General to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations, obtain civil penalties and injunctive relief, promulgate regulations, and utilize the newly established Civil Rights Enforcement Fund.

The bill requires the Attorney General to coordinate and make referrals with the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights in overlapping jurisdictions, jointly adopt regulations, and share in funding and cost reimbursements from the Civil Rights Enforcement Fund.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding the newly created Civil Rights Enforcement Fund separately and investing the money in the fund.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Comptroller shall account for the newly created Civil Rights Enforcement Fund.

Civil actions, requests for injunctive relief, appointment of receivers, and civil penalties authorized under the bill are instituted in the circuit courts, directly impacting judicial branch caseload and operations.

Synopsis: Limiting, to at a minimum from 6 a.m. to midnight, the hours during which a certain person in possession of a vehicle that has been towed or removed from a parking lot is required to provide an opportunity for the vehicle owner or the owner's agent to retake possession of the vehicle; and altering a certain signage requirement imposed on the owner or operator of a parking lot relating to hours during which a towed vehicle may be reclaimed.
Title: Towing or Removal of Vehicles - Reclamation Hours
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 803

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Limits the required hours during which a storage facility or person in possession of a towed vehicle must allow the vehicle owner or agent to reclaim the vehicle to at least 6:00 a.m. to midnight, 7 days a week (down from 24 hours a day), and updates parking lot signage requirements accordingly.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Vehicle owners whose cars are towed, towing and vehicle storage facility companies, and parking lot owners and operators.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general and special fund expenditures and local government expenditures in FY 2024 to update parking lot signage if necessary. Revenues are not affected. Specific dollar amounts were not provided in the Fiscal Note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding vehicle towing and reclamation hours, and MDOT was consulted for the fiscal analysis regarding potential impacts on state facilities and signage.

MSP enforces motor vehicle and traffic laws across Maryland, including regulations related to vehicle removal and impoundment, and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

Synopsis: Establishing the Department of Service and Civic Innovation; providing that the purpose of the Department is to promote service and volunteerism in the State; establishing the Secretary of Service and Civic Innovation and the duties and responsibilities of the Secretary; altering the provisions of the Maryland Corps Program, including requiring the Department to administer the Program; establishing the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund; providing for the purposes, use, administration, and contents of the Fund; etc.
Title: Department of Service and Civic Innovation and Maryland Corps Program Service Year Option Pathways - Established (Serving Every Region Through Vocational Exploration Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc

bill_summary: Establishes the Department of Service and Civic Innovation as a principal department of Maryland State government, transferring to it the Governor's Office on Service and Volunteerism and the Maryland Corps Program. The bill restructures the Maryland Corps Program to create two service pathways—the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway—supported by dedicated special funds, providing participants with job training, mentoring, at least $15 per hour wages, and a $6,000 completion award.
responsible_party: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
stakeholders: Young adults and recent high school graduates, adult public service participants, community organizations, nonprofits, and state and local government agencies hosting service placements.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.6 million in FY 2023 and $11.35 million in FY 2024 due to contingent appropriations. The bill directs existing mandated appropriations to the MSY Pathway Fund ($5.0 million in FY 2024, $10.0 million in FY 2025, $15.0 million in FY 2026, and $20.0 million annually starting in FY 2027). Special fund revenues and expenditures increase to cover administration and $6,000 program completion awards. General fund revenues increase by $2.5 million in FY 2023, $1.0 million in FY 2024, and $38.3 million in FY 2027 due to fund balance reversions. Local government expenditures may increase if local agencies host participants and pay associated wages and benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI is established as a principal executive department and is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Maryland Corps Program, the Service Year Option pathways, and the associated special funds.
DBM oversees the state budget, personnel allocations, and the Dedicated Purpose Account transfers and general fund reversions associated with funding DSCI and the new pathway funds.

The bill codifies an Administration priority, establishes the Secretary as a member of the Governor's Executive Council, and authorizes the Governor to appoint the Secretary and members of the Maryland Corps Program Advisory Board.
The bill designates the Attorney General as legal adviser to the new department and requires the assignment of Assistant Attorneys General, including a designated Counsel to the Department.
The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest monies in the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway Fund and the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund separately from other state funds.

Program completion awards may be deposited into Maryland 529 accounts, but because the bill also allows cash stipends as an alternative, nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for Maryland 529 may be impacted.
The Comptroller is required to separately account for each revenue source for the two newly established pathway funds.
Both pathway funds are statutorily subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits, requiring DSCI to be incorporated into OLA's regular audit rotation.

DSCI is required to consult with MHEC regarding the feasibility of awarding academic credit to corps participants for their service, and public institutions must waive in-state residency requirements for program completers.
DSCI must consult with the Department of Labor regarding prior learning experience credit toward trade or vocational certification and connections to registered apprenticeships.
The bill authorizes pathway funds to be used to expand the Maryland Conservation Corps and Chesapeake Conservation Corps to support projects managing natural resources and state parks.

Synopsis: Establishing the Tricare Premium Reimbursement Program in the Military Department for the Department to award grants to reimburse certain members of the National Guard for the cost of premiums for certain health care and dental care plans; and requiring the Department to adopt regulations to administer and implement the program.
Title: Maryland National Guard - Tricare Premium Reimbursement Program - Establishment (Health Care for Heroes Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations

bill_summary: Establishes the Tricare Premium Reimbursement Program within the Military Department, authorizing the department to award grants of up to $60 per month to eligible Maryland National Guard members to reimburse costs paid for TRICARE Reserve Select and TRICARE Dental Program health and dental premiums for themselves and their immediate families.
responsible_party: Maryland Military Department
stakeholders: Maryland National Guard members and their immediate family members/dependents
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by up to $1,000,000 in FY 2024, effectuated through contingent funding in the state budget (comprising $750,000 for premium reimbursement subsidies and $250,000 towards administration). Personnel and administrative costs for three new positions require approximately $280,593 in FY 2024. Projected future general fund expenditures range from $871,300 in FY 2025 to $909,200 in FY 2028 based on assumed participation rates. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Adjutant General serves as the head of the Maryland Military Department, which is the primary agency tasked with establishing, regulating, staffing, and administering the new TRICARE Premium Reimbursement Program.
The program is specifically designed to provide healthcare and dental premium reimbursements of up to $60 per month to eligible members of the Maryland National Guard and their dependents.

Synopsis: Increasing the State minimum wage rate; repealing the authority of the Board of Public Works to temporarily suspend an increase in the minimum wage rate; and repealing the requirement that the Governor's budgets for certain fiscal years include certain provider rate increases.
Title: Fair Wage Act of 2023

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The Fair Wage Act of 2023 accelerates the scheduled increase in the Maryland minimum wage rate to $15.00 per hour for all employers beginning January 1, 2024. It also repeals the authority of the Board of Public Works to temporarily suspend scheduled minimum wage increases and repeals statutory 4.0% reimbursement rate increases scheduled for certain community and health care service providers in fiscal years 2025 and 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Minimum wage and low-wage workers, private and small business employers, community service and direct care providers serving individuals with developmental and behavioral health disabilities, and state and local government agencies employing hourly or seasonal workers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $206.7 million in both FY 2024 and FY 2025 ($109.1 million in general funds and $97.6 million in federal matching funds) for provider reimbursements; the FY 2024 funding was included in the budget contingent on the bill's passage. Mandated appropriations for 4% provider increases in FY 2025 and FY 2026 are repealed. State expenditures across all funds also experience modest increases through FY 2026 for higher education and service contracts. Local government expenditures increase, potentially significantly in some jurisdictions, in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to pay higher employee wages. State and local tax revenue increases are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees and enforces the Maryland Wage and Hour Law, including the implementation, monitoring, and enforcement of the accelerated State minimum wage rate.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to alter mandated provider reimbursement rate increases administered by the Maryland Department of Health (including Medicaid, the Developmental Disabilities Administration, and the Behavioral Health Administration), resulting in over $200 million annually in state and federal expenditure impacts.

The bill directly repeals statutory authority under the Labor and Employment Article that previously permitted the Board of Public Works to temporarily suspend scheduled increases in the State minimum wage rate.

As the State's central budget and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for monitoring state employee wage compliance and implementing the statutory budget alterations and repeal of mandated appropriations for health service providers.
The legislation is an Administration bill that repeals requirements regarding future annual budget submissions that the Governor must submit for provider rate increases.

The fiscal note identifies that higher education institutions within USM will experience expenditure increases to raise the pay of remaining nonexempt and student hourly employees to the accelerated $15.00 per hour minimum wage.

Synopsis: Establishing the Recovery Residence Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health to award competitive grants to recovery residences to support operations, services, and programs; requiring the Department to establish certain procedures; requiring the annual budget bill to include $500,000 for the Program in each of fiscal years 2024 through 2027; and requiring the Department to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly about the number of grants and the program's grant recipients by December 1, 2024.
Title: Recovery Residence Grant Program – Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: Establishes the Recovery Residence Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health to provide competitive grants to qualifying certified nonprofit recovery residences to support operations, services, and programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Nonprofit certified recovery residences and individuals in recovery from substance-related, addictive, or co-occurring mental health disorders.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually from FY 2024 through FY 2027 due to a statutory funding mandate, covering competitive grant awards and administrative costs for 1.0 MDH personnel position. Discretionary funding of $500,000 annually is assumed for FY 2028 and beyond. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Recovery Residence Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). MDH is responsible for administering the program, establishing application procedures and criteria in consultation with credentialing entities, awarding grants, and submitting an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.

The bill mandates an appropriation of $500,000 for the program in the annual State budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027, which directly impacts DBM's budget development and fiscal planning responsibilities.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a $500,000 appropriation for the program in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2024 through 2027 and requires MDH to submit an annual report on the grant program to the Governor.

Synopsis: Increasing the appropriation required by the Governor in the annual budget bill for the Maryland Meals for Achievement In-Classroom Breakfast Program from $7,550,000 to $12,050,000.
Title: Education - Maryland Meals for Achievement In-Classroom Breakfast Program - Annual Appropriation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, Seafood; Milk
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Secondary Schools -see also- Education; Private/Public Sch.

bill_summary: This bill increases the required annual State budget appropriation for the Maryland Meals for Achievement In-Classroom Breakfast Program from $7,550,000 to $12,050,000, expanding breakfast access to eligible students.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Maryland public and eligible nonpublic school students, teachers, local school systems, and participating schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $4.5 million annually beginning in FY 2024 (supported by a contingent appropriation in FY 2024 and as an increased statutory mandate beginning in FY 2025). Local school systems receive nearly all of the additional $4.5 million in State funding to spend on school meals and will also receive and expend up to $10.0 million annually in additional federal matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) administers the Maryland Meals for Achievement In-Classroom Breakfast Program in conjunction with county school boards and eligible nonpublic schools. The bill increases the program's mandated funding by $4.5 million annually, enabling MSDE to expand meal access to an estimated 266 additional schools and 179,400 more students.

The Department of Budget and Management develops and oversees the state budget. The bill increases a statutory mandated appropriation from $7.55 million to $12.05 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025, which DBM must incorporate into the Governor's annual allowance.
The bill legally mandates the Governor to include an increased appropriation of $12,050,000 for the Maryland Meals for Achievement In-Classroom Breakfast Program in the annual state budget bill.

Synopsis: Altering the name of a recipient from the Goodwill Excel Center to the Goodwill Industries of Chesapeake Excel Center in Baltimore City; and requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $500,000 to the Goodwill Industries of Chesapeake Excel Center in Baltimore City for each of fiscal years 2024 and 2025.
Title: Goodwill Industries of Chesapeake Excel Center in Baltimore City - Alterations
bill_summary: Alters the official recipient name of an existing mandated state appropriation from the Goodwill Excel Center to the Goodwill Industries of Chesapeake Excel Center in Baltimore City.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Goodwill Industries of the Chesapeake and adult students aged 21 and older in Baltimore City attending or seeking to attend the planned adult high school.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is clarifying in nature and does not alter the existing mandated appropriation of $500,000 in fiscal years 2024 and 2025 established under Chapter 359 of 2022.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The mandated $500,000 appropriation for the Excel Center is housed and distributed within the Maryland State Department of Education's Aid to Education budget.
The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for preparing the state budget and ensuring that statutory mandated appropriations are correctly designated and included.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a $500,000 appropriation under the corrected entity name in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2024 and 2025.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain service agreement for maintenance, purchase, or sale of residential property from containing certain provisions; and prohibiting the recordation of service agreements prohibited under the Act.
Title: Residential Property - Service Agreements - Prohibitions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill prohibits service agreements related to the maintenance, purchase, or sale of residential property from being effective for more than one year, running with the land, binding subsequent bona fide purchasers, creating a lien or security interest, or assigning service rights without consent. It establishes that violating agreements are void and unenforceable, classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, and imposes misdemeanor criminal penalties for recording or attempting to record prohibited agreements.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Residential property owners, homebuyers, service providers for real estate maintenance and sales, and clerks of the circuit courts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not have a material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can handle the bill's enforcement provisions with existing resources, and the criminal and civil penalty provisions do not materially affect local government operations or resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Violations of the bill's prohibitions regarding residential property service agreements are established as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill allows clerks of the circuit court to deny recording of prohibited service agreements, creates a civil cause of action in circuit courts to declare such agreements void and recover damages, and establishes a misdemeanor penalty enforceable through the court system.

Synopsis: Establishing the Behavioral Health Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program in the Maryland Department of Health to establish and implement an intensive care coordination model using value-based purchasing in the specialty behavioral health system; requiring the Governor, for fiscal years 2025 through 2027, to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $600,000 for the Pilot Program; and requiring the Department to report by November 1, 2027 on the findings and recommendations from the Pilot Program.
Title: Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program

bill_summary: Establishes the Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Health to create and implement an intensive care coordination model utilizing value-based purchasing in the specialty behavioral health system for at least 500 eligible adults.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Adults with behavioral health conditions at risk of emergency department visits or psychiatric hospital admission, and specialty behavioral health care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $276,600 in FY 2024 for contractual staff and a consultant. For FY 2025 through FY 2027, the bill establishes a mandated annual general fund appropriation of $600,000 ($1,800,000 total) to cover provider reimbursements and ongoing administrative costs, followed by $59,400 in FY 2028 before terminating in November 2027. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 581 directly establishes and requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to administer the 3-year Behavioral Health Care Coordination Value-Based Purchasing Pilot Program, coordinate with Medicaid, potentially seek federal Section 1115 demonstration amendments, collect outcome data, and report findings.

The bill mandates an annual general fund appropriation of $600,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2027, which the Department of Budget and Management must integrate into the executive budget plan and monitor.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include an appropriation of $600,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2027 and directs MDH to submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor.

Synopsis: Altering the duties of the Parkinson's Disease Registry Advisory Committee; requiring the Committee to meet quarterly beginning on July 1, 2023; requiring the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with the State-designated health information exchange, to establish and maintain a website with certain information related to Parkinson's disease by October 1, 2023; and requiring the Committee to report to certain committees of the General Assembly on recommendations for establishing a fully functional State Parkinson's Disease Registry.
Title: Public Health - Parkinson's Disease - Advisory Committee and Website

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health

bill_summary: This bill alters the duties of the Parkinson’s Disease Registry Advisory Committee by requiring it to meet at least quarterly starting July 1, 2023, consult with partners to assist the CDC in establishing a national Parkinson’s disease registry, and submit recommendations by July 1, 2024, on establishing a State registry. It also directs the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with the State-designated health information exchange, to create and maintain a public website by October 1, 2023, containing downloadable data on the incidence of Parkinson's disease in Maryland.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals diagnosed with Parkinson's disease, healthcare providers, medical researchers, and public health professionals.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $129,663 in FY 2024 to hire two part-time staff positions (a health policy analyst and an epidemiologist) to support the advisory committee and manage website data, alongside startup and operating costs. Expenditures are projected to decrease to $93,100 in FY 2025 as startup costs end and one position reduces from 50% to 25% time, subsequently rising to $106,500 by FY 2028. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland Department of Health to house and staff the Parkinson's Disease Registry Advisory Committee and, in collaboration with the State-designated health information exchange, establish and maintain a publicly accessible website containing incidence and demographic data on Parkinson's disease, resulting in direct operational and fiscal impacts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the statutory responsibilities, meeting frequency requirements (mandating at least quarterly meetings), and reporting deadlines of the Parkinson's Disease Registry Advisory Committee.

Synopsis: Altering the application of the prohibition on including a noncompete or conflict of interest provision in an employment contract or similar document or agreement that restricts the ability of an employee to enter into employment with a new employer or to become self-employed in the same or similar business or trade.
Title: Labor and Employment - Noncompete and Conflict of Interest Provisions - Application of Prohibition

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Increases the wage threshold under which noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in employment contracts are prohibited and deemed null and void, changing the threshold from employees earning $15 per hour or less (or $31,200 annually) to employees earning equal to or less than 150% of the State minimum wage rate.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees earning equal to or less than 150% of the State minimum wage rate.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Small business impact is considered minimal, primarily requiring operational adjustments to comply with the higher wage threshold.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor enforces state workplace and labor laws under the Labor and Employment Article, including statutory restrictions on employment contracts and noncompete provisions.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of State Police to submit a report to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before February 1 each year relating to the acquisition of equipment by law enforcement agencies through surplus programs; and requiring the Department of State Police to include on its public website in a prominent location a link to a certain report.
Title: Surplus Military Equipment Reporting - Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of

bill_summary: Reinstitutes reporting requirements regarding military surplus equipment by requiring the Department of State Police to submit an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly detailing equipment acquired by Maryland law enforcement agencies through federal surplus programs. It also requires the Department of State Police to host a link on its public website to the Defense Logistics Agency's report on excess Department of Defense property transfers.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of State Police can meet the bill's reporting and website requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of State Police to compile and submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly regarding law enforcement acquisitions through federal surplus military equipment programs, and to post a link to the Defense Logistics Agency's excess property report on its public website.
The bill mandates that the Department of State Police submit an annual report directly to the Governor on the acquisition of equipment by law enforcement agencies through surplus military programs.

Synopsis: Requiring a teacher preparation program to include certain training related to teaching in a virtual learning environment as a component of instruction; providing that a county board of education may authorize a county superintendent of schools, under certain circumstances, to provide virtual education days to students instead of closing the public schools in the county because of severe weather conditions; altering the requirements for virtual schools established by a county board of education; etc.
Title: Primary and Secondary Education - Virtual Education
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 804

bill_summary: Senate Bill 610 establishes comprehensive requirements and guidelines for virtual education in Maryland public schools. It permits local school boards to use virtual education days in lieu of closures for severe weather under certain conditions, updates establishment and oversight criteria for virtual schools while placing a temporary moratorium on new elementary-level virtual schools until December 1, 2024, requires county boards to maintain virtual education plans for prolonged states of emergency, integrates virtual instruction training into teacher preparation programs, and directs the Maryland State Department of Education to expand cybersecurity infrastructure and conduct a study on virtual education.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE)
stakeholders: Public school students, parents and guardians, public school teachers and staff, local school systems and county boards of education, and teacher preparation programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $100,000 in FY 2024 and $500,000 in FY 2025 for MSDE to assess and expand computer and Internet security infrastructure for virtual education, with potential additional IT costs that cannot be reliably estimated at this time. Local school systems can likely implement the bill's provisions with existing resources. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is tasked with setting virtual school standards, approving virtual schools, establishing teacher training standards, expanding computer and internet security infrastructure, convening a study group, and submitting reports to the General Assembly and the State Board of Education.

The bill requires expanding computer and internet security infrastructure for virtual education; as noted in the fiscal note, MSDE must collaborate with DoIT on infrastructure assessments, IT capacity planning, and potential cybersecurity improvements.

The bill mandates that teacher preparation programs include training in effective teaching in a virtual learning environment. Member institutions of USM offering teacher preparation curricula must update their programs accordingly and may participate in the required virtual education study group.

As an independent public university with teacher education programs, Morgan State University must modify its teacher preparation curriculum to incorporate instruction on teaching in virtual learning environments.
MHEC oversees academic program approvals and statewide postsecondary education standards, which intersect with changes to statutory requirements for Maryland teacher preparation programs.
The bill requires MSDE to submit a comprehensive report on the study group's findings and criteria for virtual schools to the Governor by September 1, 2024.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to identify and license certain independent evaluators to evaluate and rate certain sports wagering content provided by sports wagering experts, sports wagering influencers, and content partners; authorizing the Commission and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission to consider a request to amend a Class B-2 sports wagering facility license application for the purpose of altering the proposed location of the facility under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Gaming - Sports Wagering - Independent Evaluation of Sports Wagering Content and Sports Wagering Facility Application Amendments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Gaming -see also- Awards; Bingo; Casinos; Lottery; Raffles
Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State

bill_summary: Requires the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission to license independent evaluators to evaluate and rate sports wagering content created by sports wagering experts, influencers, and content partners. It permits licensed sports wagering licensees and operators to contract with these independent evaluators, sets criteria and restrictions for evaluator independence, and authorizes the Commission and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission to consider certain location amendment requests for Class B-2 sports wagering facility licenses.
responsible_party: Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission (and the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission)
stakeholders: Sports wagering licensees and operators, sports wagering content creators and influencers, independent content evaluators, and Maryland sports bettors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency administrative expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2024 to license independent evaluators and adopt regulations, though a specific dollar estimate is unavailable. There is no local fiscal impact, and the small business effect is minimal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission with licensing independent evaluators of sports wagering content, adopting regulations, and considering amendments to Class B-2 sports wagering facility licenses. The agency will experience increased administrative responsibilities and potential operational costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Sports Wagering Application Review Commission (SWARC), an independent statutory state commission, is specifically authorized under Section 2 to consider written requests to amend Class B-2 sports wagering facility license applications regarding facility locations.

Synopsis: Requiring that the members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission be appointed with the advice and consent of the Senate of Maryland.
Title: Health Services Cost Review Commission - Members - Appointment

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Requires that the members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission be appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the Senate of Maryland.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland and the Senate of Maryland
stakeholders: Members and nominees of the Health Services Cost Review Commission, the Governor, and the Maryland Senate.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The change is procedural in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory appointment process for members of the Health Services Cost Review Commission by requiring Senate advice and consent.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointment and Senate confirmation process for members of state boards and commissions.
The bill impacts the Governor's appointment authority by requiring Senate advice and consent when appointing members to the Health Services Cost Review Commission.
The Health Services Cost Review Commission is an independent commission established within the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions of law governing the Historic St. Mary's City Commission, including laws relating to membership of the Commission, appointment of certain officers, Commission meeting times, and duties; and specifying the process for the Commission to collaborate with an affiliated nonprofit organization.
Title: Historic St. Mary's City Commission Reform Act of 2023

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The Historic St. Mary's City Commission Reform Act of 2023 alters the governance, membership structure, duties, and meeting requirements of the Historic St. Mary's City Commission. It establishes formal procedures and ethics guidelines for collaborating with affiliated nonprofit organizations like the Historic St. Mary's City Foundation, requires the development of written operational policies and a maintenance plan, and subjects the Historic St. Mary's City Fund to audits by the Office of Legislative Audits.
responsible_party: Historic St. Mary's City Commission
stakeholders: Historic St. Mary's City Commission members and staff, Historic St. Mary's City Foundation and affiliated nonprofit organizations, St. Mary's College of Maryland, the Native American community, and the general public and visitors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances and operations. Small business impacts are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 639 directly reforms the governance, membership, duties, operating agreements, procurement/personnel policies, and affiliated foundation relationships of the Historic St. Mary's City Commission.

The bill directly governs the collaborative relationship, service agreements, and administrative tasks performed between the Commission and the College, and the chair of the College's Board of Trustees serves as an ex officio voting member.

The State Ethics Commission must review and approve policies regarding conflicts of interest for Commission personnel serving on affiliated nonprofits, receive notifications and annual reports, and review dual-service appointments for concerns.
The bill requires the Attorney General to review and approve operating agreements and policies for collaboration with affiliated nonprofit organizations for form and legal sufficiency.

The bill explicitly establishes that the Historic St. Mary's City Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits and mandates a reporting requirement regarding progress addressing audit findings.

The Governor appoints 14 voting members of the Commission, including distinguished scholars and a Native American community representative, and receives the Commission's annual operational and foundation reports.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the expanded and restructured Commission seats.

Synopsis: Authorizing a transfer of service credit to, and a purchase of service credit in, the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System for local law enforcement officers of the City of Bowie Police Department hired on or after January 1, 2007, and not later than December 31, 2015, under certain circumstances.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System – City of Bowie Police Department – Transfers and Purchases of Service

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Authorizes certain City of Bowie Police Department officers hired between January 1, 2007, and December 31, 2015, who were not provided accurate information regarding pension transfers, to transfer service credit from a previous employer or purchase service credit in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) on or before December 31, 2023.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: City of Bowie police officers hired between 2007 and 2015 who previously worked for another local government, and participating governmental units (PGUs) in LEOPS.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Minimal increase in pooled pension liabilities across participating governmental units (PGUs) in LEOPS due to an estimated nine affected individuals, resulting in likely no discernible effect on PGU employer contributions and no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) administered by the State Retirement and Pension System and the Maryland State Retirement Agency, requiring the agency and its Board of Trustees to provide forms, process documentation, and administer the transfer and purchase of creditable service for eligible City of Bowie police officers.

Synopsis: Requiring certain health care providers and health care facilities to provide to the local team, on request of the chair, prompt access to all relevant medical records associated with a case under review by the Maternal Mortality Review Program without undue delay; and providing that certain provisions of law related to the confidentiality of medical records do not apply to certain disclosures made to a local team.
Title: Maternal Mortality Review Program - Local Teams - Access to Records

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Requires health care providers and health care facilities to provide a local maternal mortality review team, upon request of the chair, prompt access without undue delay to relevant medical records associated with a case under review by the Maternal Mortality Review Program, and exempts such disclosures from general state medical record confidentiality restrictions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and local maternal mortality review teams
stakeholders: Health care providers, health care facilities, local maternal mortality review teams, local health officers, and families of individuals whose maternal death cases are reviewed
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact because the changes are procedural in nature and do not materially affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maternal Mortality Review Program and coordinates with the local maternal mortality review teams convened by local health officers. The bill expands the access of these local teams to medical records held by health care providers and facilities.

Synopsis: Authorizing a nursing home that contracts with or uses an electronic health information network or electronic medical record vendor to direct the network or vendor to release electronic medical records and electronic health care transactions to a business associate of the nursing home.
Title: Electronic Health Networks and Electronic Medical Records - Nursing Homes - Release of Records

Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Nursing Homes -see also- Continuing Care; Long-Term Care
