bill_summary: Authorizes a nursing home contracting with or using an electronic health network or electronic medical record vendor to direct the network or vendor to release patient medical records or electronic health care transactions to a business associate of the nursing home with patient consent under HIPAA, establishes formatting and timeliness requirements, and prohibits vendors from restricting or charging fees for releasing the records.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Nursing homes, nursing home patients and their personal representatives, electronic health networks, electronic medical record vendors, and business associates.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect state or local government operations or finances. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission certifies Electronic Health Networks (EHNs) and designates the State's health information exchange (CRISP), which are central to the technical standards, fee restrictions, and data integration mandates established by the bill.

The bill amends the Health - General Article governing medical record confidentiality and electronic transactions involving nursing homes, which are licensed and regulated by the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Establishing the State Disaster Recovery Fund to provide disaster recovery assistance to units of local government for individuals and families and for the repair, restoration, reconstruction, or replacement of public facilities, low-interest or no-interest loans to businesses and nonprofits when a federal disaster declaration is not received, and disaster-related assistance for the unmet needs of individuals and families after a federal disaster declaration or in the event of a certain denial of federal assistance; etc.
Title: Public Safety - State Disaster Recovery Fund

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the State Disaster Recovery Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to provide disaster recovery assistance to individuals, families, local governments, businesses, and nonprofits, particularly when federal disaster aid is unavailable or insufficient. The bill also authorizes direct distributions from the Catastrophic Event Account to local governments.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: Individuals, families, small businesses, nonprofit organizations, and local governments affected by disasters or emergencies in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10.0 million in FY 2024 to capitalize the new fund, with an equal increase in special fund revenues. Special fund administrative expenditures increase by at least $344,442 in FY 2024 (increasing to $473,915 by FY 2028) for 3.5 positions and operating expenses, alongside variable special fund disbursements for disaster assistance. Future general fund expenditures may be required to replenish the fund. Federal revenues may increase through reimbursements. Local government revenues and expenditures increase to the extent disaster assistance grants are awarded.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the newly established State Disaster Recovery Fund, developing eligibility criteria and regulations, coordinating disaster recovery relief and loans, and submitting annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account, which the bill amends to permit direct funding transfers to units of local government. DBM also manages the state budget process regarding ongoing appropriations to capitalize and replenish the Disaster Recovery Fund.

The Governor is authorized to include appropriations for the fund in the annual budget, may transfer funds via budget amendments after legislative review, issues state of emergency declarations that unlock fund usage, and receives an annual report on the fund's activities.

The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the State Disaster Recovery Fund separately, invest its money, and ensure all interest earnings are credited directly to the fund rather than reverting to the General Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily tasked with accounting for the State Disaster Recovery Fund and its interest earnings within the state accounting systems.

Synopsis: Requiring a real estate broker or an escrow agent, if a purchaser terminates a certain transaction under certain circumstances, to distribute trust money to the purchaser within 30 days after a certain written notice of the termination is sent; requiring a holder of trust money who makes a certain distribution to notify the seller and purchaser of the distribution within a certain period of time, subject to a certain exception; etc.
Title: Real Estate - Real Estate Brokerage Services and Termination of Residential Real Estate Contracts (The Anthony Moorman Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: The Anthony Moorman Act establishes procedures for distributing escrow or trust money to a purchaser who terminates a residential real estate contract under a contingency clause. It requires the holder of the trust money to release the funds to the purchaser within 30 days of written notice, provided the seller has not filed a court complaint or requested mediation within 10 days, while shielding trust money holders from liability for authorized distributions.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Residential real estate buyers, sellers, real estate brokers, and escrow agents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. Any effect on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Title 17 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article governing licensed real estate brokers and their statutory duties regarding trust money and escrow distributions.
The bill establishes specific judicial procedures allowing sellers, purchasers, and holders of trust money to file complaints, interpleader actions, and civil claims in the District Court.
The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees consumer protection in real estate and financial transactions and served as an informational source for the legislation.

Synopsis: Correcting certain errors or omissions in certain articles of the Annotated Code; clarifying language; correcting certain obsolete references; reorganizing certain sections of the Annotated Code; providing that this Act is not intended to affect any law other than to correct technical errors; and providing for the correction of certain errors and obsolete provisions by the publishers of the Annotated Code.
Title: Annual Corrective Bill
bill_summary: The Annual Corrective Bill corrects various technical errors, cross-references, grammatical mistakes, stylistic inaccuracies, and obsolete references across multiple articles of the Annotated Code of Maryland and uncodified laws without making substantive policy changes.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: State agencies, the judiciary, legal practitioners, publishers of the Annotated Code, and the general public relying on the Annotated Code of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The bill is strictly technical in nature and does not affect governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates statutory provisions governing the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council to reflect the agency's official designation as the Maryland Department of Emergency Management and the role of the Secretary of Emergency Management.

The bill makes numerous technical, grammatical, and cross-reference corrections to the Maryland Code of Military Justice (Title 13A of the Public Safety Article), which governs state military forces under the Adjutant General.
The bill enacts technical corrections to multiple provisions in the Education Article touching public school administration, career ladders, school health guidelines, and division terminology.

The bill corrects statutory cross-references, obsolete terms, and phrasing in the Health - General and Health Occupations Articles, including provisions regarding the State-designated health information exchange and the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program.
The bill resolves technical and tabulation errors in the Natural Resources Article relating to Program Open Space conversions, fishing regulations, and hunting permits.
The bill corrects cross-references and minor wording regarding school facility grant priorities and computerized maintenance systems administered by the Commission.
The bill updates cross-references in the State Personnel and Pensions Article regarding disability retirees and reemployment limitations for law enforcement officers.
The bill corrects an internal cross-reference in the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding nonvisual access standards for IT procurements.
The bill corrects cross-references and definitions in the Public Safety Article regarding firearm disqualifications, law enforcement standards, and reporting to the Central Repository.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill corrects a missing word in a Business Regulation statutory reference to the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission regarding wagering kiosks.

The bill corrects a cross-reference in Education Article provisions referencing four-party memoranda of understanding involving the Maryland Stadium Authority for public school construction financing.
The bill corrects capitalization and references to the Attorney General in military justice proceedings involving individuals incompetent to stand trial.

Synopsis: Applying the sales and use tax to a sale or use of certain home amenity rentals; and authorizing a county or municipality to impose a certain home amenity rental tax under certain circumstances and subject to certain limitations.
Title: Home Amenity Rentals - Sales and Use Tax Imposed and Local Tax Authorized
Status: Enacted under Article II, Section 17(c) of the Maryland Constitution - Chapter 805

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties
Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Applies the Maryland State sales and use tax to home amenity rentals (portions of residential property rented by the hour for up to 15 consecutive hours, excluding sleeping quarters) facilitated by rental intermediaries or platforms, and authorizes counties and municipalities to levy a local home amenity rental tax subject to specified rate limitations.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland and participating county and municipal governing bodies
stakeholders: Homeowners renting out residential amenities, consumers renting home amenities, home amenity rental platforms and intermediaries, and local and state tax authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund (Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund) revenues will increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount beginning in FY 2025 ($6,000 for each $100,000 in taxable rentals). State general fund expenditures may increase minimally for administrative costs. County and municipal revenues will also increase beginning in FY 2025 depending on whether local jurisdictions adopt home amenity rental taxes (subject to caps between 1% and 4%), accompanied by potential local administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller is directly responsible for administering and collecting the State sales and use tax, which this bill expands to apply to home amenity rentals.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State to exchange real property owned by the State for the use and benefit of the Department of Natural Resources with private real property under certain circumstances.
Title: Department of Natural Resources' Real Property - Exchange With Private Real Property
bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to exchange State-owned real property of five acres or less for adjacent privately owned real property without adhering to standard statutory procedures for disposing of excess State property, provided the private property owner pays all associated transaction and legal costs, required notifications are sent to adjacent owners and local officials, and the Board of Public Works approves the exchange.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Private property owners adjacent to State-owned DNR land, adjacent landholders, and local county governing bodies
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected because the bill is authorizing in nature and requires the requesting private property owner to cover all costs associated with the exchange, including legal fees, surveying, engineering, and recordation. It may have a minor operational impact on DNR, the Board of Public Works, and the Maryland Department of Planning. Local fiscal effect is minimal to none.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to exchange up to 5 acres of State-owned land under its use and benefit with adjacent private property owners without undergoing standard excess property procedures, while establishing specific notice requirements and referral to the Board of Public Works.

The bill requires DNR to refer proposed real property exchanges under the new authority to the Board of Public Works for final disposition, while exempting these transactions from certain standard statutory property disposal procedures.

Under current law, the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP) reviews excess State real property and conducts statutory disposition studies and notifications under Title 5, Subtitle 3; the bill bypasses these MDP review procedures for qualifying DNR land exchanges.

The Department of General Services oversees State real estate transactions and property dispositions under the State Finance and Procurement Article, certain provisions of which are bypassed by this legislation for qualifying DNR exchanges.

Synopsis: Authorizing members of the State Retirement and Pension System to receive service credit at the rate of 4 months for each full year of attendance at a United States service academy that interrupts the member's employment, not to exceed a total of 16 months.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Military Service Credit

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes members and eligible former members of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), as well as members of local retirement systems, to receive retirement service credit for attendance at a United States service academy at a rate of 4 months for each full year of attendance, up to a maximum of 16 months, subject to the existing 5-year cap on total military service credit.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members and eligible former members of the State Retirement and Pension System, as well as local government employees participating in local pension systems, who attended a U.S. service academy.
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 due to higher actuarial liabilities, with average costs per member claiming the full 16 months of credit ranging from $1,200 to $3,600 depending on the specific pension plan. Total State costs cannot be reliably estimated because the number of qualifying members is unknown; costs are allocated 60% general funds, 20% special funds, and 20% federal/other funds. State revenues are unaffected. Local government pension impact is expected to have no discernible effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 695 directly amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article to authorize members of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) to claim service credit for attendance at a U.S. service academy. The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers SRPS, processes member service credit applications, and implements these benefit calculations.

The Department of Budget and Management acts as the central personnel and budget agency for the State, managing state employee benefits and overseeing employer contribution requirements funded across state agencies in the state budget.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Motor Vehicle Administration from charging a fee for the issuance of a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse under certain circumstances.
Title: Vehicle Laws – Certificate of Title – Surviving Spouse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: Prohibits the Motor Vehicle Administration from charging a fee for issuing a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse upon the death of a sole owner of a vehicle, provided the vehicle's ownership is transferred according to law.
responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Surviving spouses who inherit or receive vehicle ownership from a deceased spouse who was the sole owner.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues decrease by approximately $375,000 in FY 2024 (reflecting the October 1, 2023 effective date) and by $500,000 annually in subsequent fiscal years due to the exemption of the $100 vehicle titling fee for an estimated 5,000 surviving spouses each year. Expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Transportation Article to prohibit the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) from charging a fee for a new certificate of title to a surviving spouse of a deceased sole vehicle owner, resulting in an estimated $500,000 annual reduction in titling fee revenue.
As the parent department of the MVA, the Maryland Department of Transportation is impacted by the decrease in Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues resulting from the fee exemption.

The bill references vehicle transfers occurring pursuant to testamentary disposition or intestate devolution, which involves certificates of letters testamentary or administration issued through the probate process overseen by the Register of Wills.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain deputy State fire marshal to be on probation for a period of 2 years after the date of appointment to the Office of the State Fire Marshal under certain circumstances; and specifying the pay that a certain deputy State fire marshal is entitled to on promotion.
Title: Public Safety - Deputy State Fire Marshal - Probationary Status and Promotion

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: Requires deputy State fire marshals to serve a two-year probationary period upon appointment to the Office of the State Fire Marshal and establishes specific pay rate rules applicable to them upon promotion, codifying existing departmental practices.
responsible_party: Department of State Police and the Office of the State Fire Marshal
stakeholders: Deputy State fire marshals and trainees within the Office of the State Fire Marshal
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact because the bill simply codifies existing practice regarding probationary periods, pay plans, and promotional pay.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was requested by the Maryland State Police and directly governs personnel within its Office of the State Fire Marshal, establishing a two-year probationary period and rules for promotional pay increases for deputy State fire marshals.
As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee compensation rules, probationary guidelines, and salary plans referenced in the statute.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority and the Maryland Racing Operations Fund to oversee, support, and finance thoroughbred horse racing and facilities in Maryland. responsible_party: Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority
stakeholders: Maryland thoroughbred racing licensees, horse owners, trainers, breeders, racetrack workers, the City of Bowie, and Bowie State University.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Racing Operations Fund increase by at least $15.0 million in FY 2023 due to the redirection of FY 2023 capital budget funds previously designated for Pimlico and Laurel Park. Expenditures from the fund increase beginning in FY 2024 for authority staffing, operations, and a required feasibility study. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Racing Commission are preserved through FY 2034. Local impact is minimal, though the bill guarantees $1.5 million in transfers to the City of Bowie for remediation and pre-acquisition design/analysis of the Bowie Race Course Training Center property.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Department of Labor and extends the termination date of the Maryland Horse Racing Act and the Maryland Racing Commission, which is housed within the department, by 10 years to 2034.

The Maryland Stadium Authority's Chair or Executive Director is made a member of the new Racetrack Operating Authority, MSA is authorized to transfer funds from the Racing and Community Development Facilities Fund, and prior capital budget appropriations to MSA are redirected.

MEDCO's Chair or Executive Director sits on the new Authority, and the Authority is authorized to coordinate directly with MEDCO to acquire property or contractual interests for horse racing operations.

The bill references and conditions funding on a joint use agreement between the City of Bowie and Bowie State University (a member institution of the University System of Maryland) for the Bowie Race Course Training Center property, requiring a joint report to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly designates the Attorney General as the legal advisor to the newly created Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority and requires AG approval if additional legal counsel is retained.

The State Treasurer is tasked with holding and investing moneys in the newly established Maryland Racing Operations Fund, with net interest retained by the fund as an exemption under State Finance and Procurement law.

The bill amends a prior capital budget appropriation for DHCD's Division of Development Finance (SA25), redirecting $10.0 million from backstretch housing facilities at Laurel Park to the Maryland Racing Operations Fund.

The Governor is tasked with appointing multiple voting and nonvoting members to the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority, and the Authority's operational powers can be triggered by an executive order.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the newly created Maryland Racing Operations Fund.

As of July 1, 2023, the Governor must transfer two positions and associated general funds (at least $131,275 in FY 2024) from the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives to the Maryland Department of Disabilities. Adding a member to the Maryland Commission on Disabilities does not substantively affect State operations, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly transfers the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and staffing responsibilities for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs to the Department of Disabilities, while also expanding the membership of the department's advisory body, the Maryland Commission on Disabilities.

The bill removes the State Coordinator for Autism Strategy and the responsibility to staff the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs from the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives, transferring the associated positions and funding away from the agency.

The bill requires the Governor to transfer two positions and associated general funds from the Executive Department to the Department of Disabilities and authorizes the Governor to appoint an additional member with a traumatic brain injury to the Maryland Commission on Disabilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation alters the statutory membership requirements of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities and changes staffing provisions for the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, which includes the new position on the Maryland Commission on Disabilities for an individual with a traumatic brain injury.

DBM oversees executive personnel and budget transfers across departments and the Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Disabilities.

Synopsis: Requiring that any system operated by a vehicle manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch or its affiliate for allocating new vehicles to dealers be reasonable and fair.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Allocation of Vehicles

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: Requires any system operated by a vehicle manufacturer, distributor, factory branch, or affiliate for allocating new vehicles to dealers to be fair and reasonable. It requires them to disclose the allocation method upon a dealer's written request and places the burden of proof on the manufacturer, distributor, or branch in any compliance dispute.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and franchised motor vehicle dealers (including small business vehicle dealers)
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration regulates businesses that manufacture, distribute, and sell motor vehicles in Maryland pursuant to Title 15 of the Transportation Article, which this bill directly amends.
The Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and provided agency analysis on the bill's regulatory impact on vehicle dealer and manufacturer relations.

Synopsis: Extending through fiscal year 2027 a requirement that the Comptroller distribute $14,000,000 of certain abandoned property funds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund; and extending through fiscal year 2027 a requirement that the Governor include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $14,000,000 from the Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation.
Title: Access to Counsel in Evictions - Funding

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Extends through fiscal year 2027 the requirement that the State Comptroller distribute $14 million annually from unclaimed property funds to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund, and continues the requirement that the Governor include an annual $14 million appropriation from the fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation.
responsible_party: Maryland Comptroller and Maryland Legal Services Corporation (MLSC)
stakeholders: Low-income tenants facing eviction or housing subsidy termination proceedings, legal aid organizations, and the Maryland Legal Services Corporation.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027 due to redirected unclaimed property proceeds. Access to Counsel in Evictions (ACE) Special Fund revenues and expenditures increase by an equivalent $14.0 million annually over the same period for mandated appropriations to MLSC. No direct effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Comptroller to distribute $14,000,000 annually from the State's Unclaimed Property Fund to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through fiscal year 2027, and requires the Comptroller to account for the Fund.

The bill statutorily mandates the Governor to include an appropriation of $14,000,000 from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the annual state budget bill for each fiscal year through 2027.

As the principal agency responsible for developing and supervising the state budget, DBM must incorporate the bill's mandated annual $14,000,000 appropriation through FY 2027 and account for the corresponding $14,000,000 reduction in annual general fund revenues.

Under the provisions of the bill, the State Treasurer holds the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and is responsible for investing its moneys in the same manner as other state funds.

Synopsis: Requiring an individual who provides security guard services to the individual's employer to be certified as a security guard, subject to a certain exception; regulating certain security guard employers; altering the certification and renewal standards for security guards; requiring the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to identify or establish certain training programs for the certification and renewal of certification of security guards; requiring security guards to complete certain security training programs; etc.
Title: Security Guard Agencies, Security Guard Employers, and Security Guards – Standards and Certifications

Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Senate Bill 760 expands certification requirements for security guards to include individuals employed directly by 'security guard employers' (in addition to those employed by security guard agencies), excluding unarmed employees of bars, taverns, or restaurants. It establishes initial and continuing education training requirements administered or identified by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, sets mandatory reporting requirements for use-of-force incidents, establishes commercial general liability insurance minimums for security guard employers, and establishes new criteria for certification denials, revocations, and suspensions.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Security guards, security guard agencies, businesses and entities that employ proprietary security guards, and the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $476,942 in FY 2024 for the Department of State Police to hire two administrative specialists and complete one-time technical system upgrades costing $365,000. Out-year expenditures range between $129,500 and $148,900 annually. If the Department is required to investigate use-of-force reports, expenditures could increase further by approximately $250,000 for two State Troopers and vehicles. No material effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State Police is the primary regulatory and licensing authority responsible for certifying security guards, approving applications and renewals, receiving mandatory use of force reports, confirming handgun permits, and enforcing compliance under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is required by the bill to identify or develop and publish the 12-hour initial and 8-hour continuing training programs for security guards, as well as the CJIS Central Repository used for background checks.

DGS directly employs security personnel for state facilities and is noted in the fiscal note regarding the impact of new training, standards, and certification requirements on its employed security guards.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Public Works, in consultation with the Procurement Improvement Council, to publish a model policy on or before January 1, 2024, concerning the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in procurement contracts; requiring a unit of State government to adopt a written policy that is substantially similar to the Board's policy; requiring a unit that decides not to include a liquidated damages clause under certain circumstances to obtain the approval of the head of unit; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Liquidated Damages - Policies and Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Requires the Board of Public Works to publish a model policy on the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in State procurement contracts by January 1, 2024, and requires State procurement units to adopt substantially similar policies by July 1, 2024. Additionally, it requires agency head approval when deciding not to include liquidated damages clauses or deciding not to pursue liquidated damages on contracts valued at $5 million or more.
responsible_party: Board of Public Works
stakeholders: State procurement units, primary procurement agencies, and State government contractors and vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: The Board of Public Works and State procuring agencies can implement the bill using existing resources. The bill has no effect on State revenues and no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Board of Public Works, in consultation with the Procurement Improvement Council, develop and publish a model policy concerning the inclusion and use of liquidated damages provisions in State procurement contracts.

As the State's central procurement authority and a primary procurement unit for construction, services, commodities, and IT, DGS is responsible for establishing a liquidated damages policy for procurements under its control authority and complying with the bill's documentation and approval requirements.

As a designated primary procurement unit responsible for major transportation infrastructure and service procurements, MDOT is authorized to establish its own liquidated damages policy and must follow unit head approval rules when omitting or waiving liquidated damages.

The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, serves as a primary procurement unit for State banking and insurance services, and oversees Maryland 529, which is explicitly made subject to the bill's liquidated damages provisions.
The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is directly responsible for developing and publishing the State's model liquidated damages policy.

The bill explicitly amends State Finance and Procurement Article Section 11-203(c) to apply the new liquidated damages requirements to the Maryland Stadium Authority, despite its general exemption from State procurement law.

The bill explicitly amends Section 11-203(d) to make the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System subject to the liquidated damages requirements under Section 15-113 for investment and administrative expenditures.
The bill explicitly amends Section 11-203(f) to make Maryland 529 subject to the new liquidated damages provisions under Section 15-113 for investment and asset management procurements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department administers the Maryland Corps Program, which the bill explicitly amends under Section 11-203(i) to be subject to the new liquidated damages policy and reporting requirements.
USM is a primary procurement unit and is specifically amended under Section 11-203(e)(7) to be subject to Section 15-113, requiring it to adopt and apply a compliant liquidated damages policy.
MSU is an independent primary procurement unit and public university governed by Section 11-203(e)(7) and Section 15-113, requiring it to establish and implement a liquidated damages policy.
As an independent public institution and primary procurement unit subject to Section 11-203(e)(7) and Section 15-113, the college must adopt and adhere to a liquidated damages procurement policy.
As a designated primary procurement unit within MDOT, the Maryland Port Administration has independent authority to establish liquidated damages policies for procurements within its control.
The Governor serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which is responsible for promulgating the model liquidated damages policy for State procurement.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to the Board of Public Works, which must review draft plans for responding to contractor deficiencies under the model policy, and regularly advises State procurement officers on drafting and enforcing liquidated damages provisions.

Synopsis: Requiring an application for any new qualified offshore wind project and a certain proposal for an offshore wind transmission facility to be subject to a certain community benefit agreement; requiring the Public Service Commission to request that PJM Interconnection conduct a certain analysis of transmission system upgrade and expansion options; altering the requirements for a certain report on offshore wind projects; requiring the Commission, by a certain date each year starting in 2024, to report on its Supplier Diversity Program; etc.
Title: Offshore Wind Energy - State Goals and Procurement (Promoting Offshore Wind Energy Resources Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Ren.Energy Sou; Fuel; Power Plants
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Utilities -see also- High Voltage Lines; Telephones; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The Promoting Offshore Wind Energy Resources (POWER) Act establishes a State goal of achieving 8,500 megawatts of offshore wind energy capacity by 2031. It directs the Public Service Commission (PSC) to coordinate with PJM Interconnection on transmission system upgrade and expansion analyses and solicitations for offshore wind transmission facilities. It also directs the Department of General Services (DGS) to issue a competitive solicitation for a power purchase agreement for up to 5,000,000 megawatt-hours annually of offshore wind energy, establishes labor and community benefit requirements, and authorizes developers to seek exemptions from passing along certain federal tax credits to ratepayers under specific conditions.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission and Department of General Services
stakeholders: Electricity consumers and ratepayers, offshore wind developers and transmission developers, labor unions and construction trade workers, small and minority-owned businesses, and PJM Interconnection.
fiscal_impact_summary: Public Service Commission special fund expenditures increase by $635,256 in FY 2024, by $1.4 million to $1.5 million annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027, and by $0.5 million in FY 2028, fully offset by assessments on public service companies. General fund expenditures for the Department of General Services increase by $213,905 in FY 2024 and approximately $0.3 million annually thereafter for procurement personnel. The impact on State and local government expenditures for electricity is indeterminate but potentially significant depending on future power purchase agreements and offshore wind transmission costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PSC is the primary regulatory and implementing agency tasked with coordinating transmission studies with PJM Interconnection, issuing competitive solicitations for offshore wind transmission facilities, selecting proposals, adjudicating federal tax credit exemption requests, and submitting annual diversity reports.

DGS is designated to issue competitive sealed procurements and enter into long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) for up to 5,000,000 megawatt-hours annually of offshore wind energy to meet the State's energy needs, incurring direct operational and staffing fiscal impacts.

MEA is statutorily required to consult with the PSC on the transmission upgrade and expansion analysis, criteria development for project solicitations, and intergovernmental facilitation for selected offshore wind projects.

The Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) within DNR provides conditions for the construction and operation of offshore wind transmission facilities selected by the PSC, with fiscal impacts relating to project siting evaluations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is tasked in statute with assisting potential offshore wind applicants and minority investors and establishing clear plans and participation goals for minority business enterprise inclusion.

OPC represents the interests of residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC concerning transmission project approvals, baseline net ratepayer benefits, and developer tax credit exemptions.

The bill mandates community benefit agreements adhering to prevailing wage rates determined by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry and utilizes registered apprenticeship programs overseen by MD Labor.

OAG provides legal consultation to the Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs and the PSC in setting minority business enterprise goals and ensuring compliance under statutory requirements.

The bill establishes intent for the Governor's budget submission regarding PSC funding, and PSC must submit determinations and reports regarding transmission expansion and offshore wind goals directly to the Governor.

Synopsis: Allowing multiple final tax certificates to be issued for a catalytic revitalization project in certain circumstances; and requiring the Smart Growth Subcabinet to study Maryland's historic complexes and make recommendations about an implementation plan to address the preservation and reuse of historic complexes in the State on or before December 31, 2023.
Title: Preservation and Reuse of Historic Complexes Study and Alterations to the Income Tax Credit for Catalytic Revitalization Projects

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill modifies the catalytic revitalization project income tax credit by authorizing the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to issue multiple final tax credit certificates for multi-phase projects upon completion of each phase, subject to certain limitations. It also establishes conditions for transferring initial tax credit certificates without requiring property transfer, and requires the Smart Growth Subcabinet to study and report recommendations by December 31, 2023, regarding an implementation plan for the preservation and reuse of historic complexes across Maryland.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and the Smart Growth Subcabinet
stakeholders: Developers, nonprofit organizations, and business entities rehabilitating eligible former government-owned historic complexes, as well as local communities and state agencies involved in historic property management.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues may be impacted due to the acceleration of the timing of tax credits claimed against the State income tax across multiple project phases, which could be significant in any given year, though the overall credit limit per project remains capped at $15 million under existing law. Timing impacts to the corporate income tax may also affect Higher Education Investment Fund and Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures, as well as local highway user revenues. The Smart Growth Subcabinet can complete the required study using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary administering agency for the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit. The bill directly alters DHCD's administration of this program by authorizing the Secretary to issue multiple final tax credit certificates for phased projects and establishing provisions governing the transfer of initial tax credit certificates.

The Maryland Department of Planning staffs and supports the Smart Growth Subcabinet and oversees the Maryland Historical Trust. The bill mandates that the Smart Growth Subcabinet study and make recommendations on an implementation plan to address the preservation and adaptive reuse of historic complexes across the state.

As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller processes claims, transfers, and refunds of the state income tax credit for catalytic revitalization projects, which may experience an accelerated claiming schedule under the bill.

The Smart Growth Subcabinet, an executive entity, is required to submit its findings, recommendations, and proposed implementation plan regarding the preservation and reuse of historic complexes to the Governor by December 31, 2023.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements for the registration and termination of domestic partnerships with the register of wills; repealing provisions on legitimacy and illegitimacy of children and providing for the parentage of a child born or conceived by registered domestic partners; requiring the register of wills to recognize as domestic partnerships relationships established under the laws of other jurisdictions if the laws are substantially similar to the provisions of the Act; etc.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Registered Domestic Partnerships

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Parents and Guardians -see also- Adoption; Child Custody
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes procedures for registering and terminating domestic partnerships with the register of wills, granting registered domestic partners many of the same inheritance, intestate succession, and estate administration rights and benefits as spouses, while extending an inheritance tax exemption to property passing to a surviving registered domestic partner. The bill also updates statutory definitions of parentage and child in estate law and alters intestate estate distribution shares.
responsible_party: Registers of Wills
stakeholders: Domestic partners, surviving registered domestic partners, estate heirs and personal representatives, and individuals involved in estate administration
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are expected to decrease annually due to an inheritance tax exemption for property passing to a surviving registered domestic partner. This revenue loss will be partially offset by up to a $25 filing fee for declarations of domestic partnership collected by the registers of wills. The exact net impact cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency responsible for administering the bill's provisions, including accepting and recording declarations of domestic partnership and termination, maintaining public records, establishing a certified list of recognized jurisdictions, collecting registration fees, and applying inheritance tax exemptions and intestate succession rules.

The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state revenue collection and tax compliance. The bill expands the inheritance tax exemption to cover property passing to a registered domestic partner, which directly affects state inheritance tax revenues remitted to the General Fund.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, including Orphans' Courts and judicial probate matters, which are impacted by changes to intestate succession, determination of parentage, and priority of appointment for personal representatives.

Synopsis: Establishing the Cyber Maryland Program in the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to create and execute a talent pipeline that materially reduces workforce vacancies by July 1, 2026, build an advanced cybersecurity workforce, and carry out other purposes related to the cybersecurity workforce in the State; establishing the Cyber Maryland Fund; authorizing the Governor to include an appropriation of $250,000 for the Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter; etc.
Title: Economic Development - Cybersecurity - Cyber Maryland Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: The bill creates the Cyber Maryland Program and the Cyber Maryland Fund within the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to develop a cybersecurity talent pipeline, reduce workforce vacancies, and coordinate cybersecurity education, research, and workforce programs across the State. It establishes the Cyber Maryland Board to advise and guide the program and makes changes to the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program administered by the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO)
stakeholders: Cybersecurity and IT workers, students in cybersecurity training programs, employers seeking cyber talent, public and private higher education institutions, community colleges, and local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $690,000 in FY 2024 to fund administrative, portal, and grant expenses, with ongoing annual general fund expenditures projected between $669,300 and $705,400 through FY 2028 due to mandated staffing appropriations and discretionary talent pipeline funding. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Cyber Maryland Fund increase correspondingly. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2024 to the extent local school systems or community colleges receive program grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Cyber Maryland Program and the Cyber Maryland Fund within TEDCO, tasks TEDCO's CEO with appointing the program's executive director, and requires TEDCO to manage program operations and submit annual performance reports.

The bill requires MHEC to annually expand the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program to accommodate certification trends, alters fund allocation rules, and directs unexpended funds to revert to MHEC for future program distribution.

The Cyber Maryland Program is established partly to support DoIT in improving cybersecurity posture across state and local governments, and the Secretary of Information Technology serves on the Cyber Maryland Board.

The Secretary of Labor serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and the board and program are required to coordinate with the Maryland Department of Labor on workforce development initiatives like EARN and apprenticeships.

The Secretary of Commerce (the Secretary under the Economic Development Article) is designated as a member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and the program must coordinate with Commerce on industry workforce needs.

Multiple USM institutions (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, University of Maryland Eastern Shore, and UMBC Training Centers) operate Cyber Warrior Diversity Programs governed by the funding and certification provisions in the bill.

Morgan State University is a statutory participant in the Cyber Warrior Diversity Program and is directly impacted by the bill's provisions governing program expansion, grant allocations, and unexpended funds.
The Maryland Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now Department of Veterans and Military Families) or a designee is designated as a statutory member of the Cyber Maryland Board.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Cyber Maryland Board, receiving annual reports on the program, and including mandated staff funding in the annual budget bill starting in FY 2025.

The bill mandates an annual budget appropriation beginning in FY 2025 to cover program staffing and authorizes appropriations and transfers from the Dedicated Purpose Account, impacting state budget preparation and execution.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly created Cyber Maryland Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the newly established Cyber Maryland Fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health to develop a report comparing options for offering affordable health care and dental care coverage to State residents who are ineligible for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, the Maryland Children's Health Program, qualified health plans, or stand-alone dental plans due to the individuals' immigration status; and requiring the Exchange and the Department to report to certain committees of the General Assembly by October 31, 2023.
Title: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and Maryland Department of Health - Health Care and Dental Care Coverage for Undocumented Immigrants - Report

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- HMOS; Managed Care Organizations
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health to study and develop a report comparing options, costs, and considerations for offering affordable health and dental care coverage to undocumented immigrants and other Maryland residents who are otherwise ineligible for Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, or exchange-based qualified health and dental plans due to their immigration status.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: State residents ineligible for public health programs or qualified health and dental plans due to their immigration status (primarily undocumented immigrants).
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and the Maryland Department of Health can complete the study and submit their report with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, jointly with the Maryland Department of Health, to develop and submit a report comparing options for offering affordable health care and dental coverage to individuals ineligible due to immigration status.

The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health, jointly with the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, to study and report on options for offering coverage through Medicaid and MCHP to individuals currently ineligible due to immigration status.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to provide a discount of at least $40 on annual State park passes for all first responders and law enforcement officers who are Maryland residents.
Title: Natural Resources - Annual State Park Pass - Discounts for Law Enforcement Officers and First Responders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes; Reimb Rates
Forests and Parks -see also- Program Open Space; Trees
Law Enforcement -see also- State Police, Department of
Rescue Squads -see also- Ambulances; Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to provide a discount of at least $40 on annual State park passes for Maryland residents who are law enforcement officers or first responders.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Maryland resident law enforcement officers and first responders
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues decrease minimally beginning in FY 2023 due to the discount on annual State park passes (illustratively estimated at a $9,360 reduction annually). State expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Department of Natural Resources to administer and provide a discount of at least $40 on annual State park passes to eligible Maryland first responders and law enforcement officers, resulting in a minimal reduction in special fund revenues.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of the Environment and the Maryland Department of Health, in conjunction with the Board of Environmental Health Specialists, to conduct a study on staffing needs for environmental health specialists in local health departments; requiring the Department of the Environment, in consultation with the Department of Legislative Services and the University of Maryland Agriculture and Food Systems Extension Program, to study the delegation of well and septic systems permitting authority; etc.
Title: Environmental Health Specialists and Well and Septic Systems Permitting - Studies (Environmental Health Systems Support Act of 2023)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- Col Bar; Holiday; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment and the Maryland Department of Health, in conjunction with the Board of Environmental Health Specialists, to conduct a study on local health department staffing needs for environmental health specialists. It also directs the Maryland Department of the Environment, in consultation with the Department of Legislative Services and the University of Maryland Extension, to study the implications of delegating authority regarding well and septic systems permitting.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Environmental health specialists, local health departments, well and septic system permit applicants, and well drillers
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as affected State agencies can carry out the required studies and reports using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting two studies: one on environmental health specialist staffing needs in conjunction with MDH, and another on the delegation of well and septic systems permitting authority in consultation with the University of Maryland Extension and DLS.

MDH, in conjunction with the Board of Environmental Health Specialists housed within the department, is required to conduct a study with MDE on staffing needs, wages, and licensing of environmental health specialists in local health departments. Additionally, MDH is the subject of the study evaluating the delegation of well and septic permitting authority.

The bill requires MDE to consult with the University of Maryland Agriculture and Food Systems Extension Program (part of the University of Maryland / USM) in conducting the study on the delegation of well and septic systems permitting authority.
The Governor's Office receives the required interim and final study reports from MDE and MDH.

Synopsis: Establishing the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to make grants to nonprofit organizations, including faith-based organizations, to provide security enhancements to protect against hate crimes; requiring the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to administer the Fund; and authorizing, for fiscal year 2025 and each fiscal year thereafter, the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation of $5,000,000 to the Fund.
Title: Public Safety - Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crime Prev., Youth, and Victim Service, Governor's Office of
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: Establishes the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to award grants to nonprofit and faith-based organizations for security enhancements against hate crimes. It requires a minimum set-aside of $1 million annually for faith-based organizations and authorizes the Governor to appropriate $5 million to the fund each year starting in fiscal year 2025.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, faith-based organizations, religious and minority communities vulnerable to hate crimes, and security vendors and contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 under the assumption that the authorized capitalization is provided in addition to existing grant funds. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2024 and $10.0 million annually thereafter as general funds are transferred and distributed as grants. There is no effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services (now Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy) as the primary administering authority responsible for managing the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund, establishing grant procedures, allocating funds, and reporting annually to the General Assembly.
The bill explicitly mandates the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund separately and to invest the money in the fund in accordance with state law.
The bill specifically requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $5,000,000 to the Protecting Against Hate Crimes Grant Fund in the annual state budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2025.
As the principal agency supervising state budget formulation and execution, DBM is responsible for managing the state appropriations and fiscal mechanics authorized for the fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual budget bill of $500,000 for the State Department of Education to provide grants to local school systems for expenses related to student field trips to museums of cultural import.
Title: Local School Systems - Student Field Trips - Funding
bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $500,000 in the State budget for the Maryland State Department of Education to award grants to local school systems for expenses associated with student field trips to museums of cultural import.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local school systems, and museums of cultural import
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 annually starting in FY 2025 to fulfill a mandated appropriation for grant funding, which MSDE can administer with existing resources. Local school system revenues and expenditures increase by $500,000 statewide annually beginning in FY 2025 to cover eligible field trip costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency tasked with distributing $500,000 in annual grants to local school systems for field trips to museums of cultural import and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $500,000 appropriation in the annual state budget bill starting in FY 2025.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution and must incorporate the $500,000 mandated annual general fund appropriation into the state operating budget.

The Corporation manages the Reginald F. Lewis Museum of Maryland African American History and Culture, which is explicitly designated in the bill as an eligible museum of cultural import for funded student field trips.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which public, school, college, or university libraries must permit the inspection, use, or disclosure of the circulation record of an individual.
Title: Libraries - Circulation Records - Inspection, Use, or Disclosure Requirement Revision

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Alters the standards governing privacy and confidentiality of library circulation records in Maryland. The bill specifies that public, school, college, or university libraries may only permit the inspection, use, or disclosure of an individual's circulation records if necessary for the reasonable operation of the library, with the individual's written consent, or pursuant to a subpoena or court order.
responsible_party: Maryland public, school, college, and university libraries, with oversight from the Maryland State Library Agency
stakeholders: Library patrons whose circulation records are maintained by libraries, as well as staff and administrators of Maryland public, school, college, and university libraries.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State government finances or operations, nor does it materially affect local library system finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency coordinates and provides leadership for Maryland's public library systems, which are directly subject to the revised statutory confidentiality and disclosure standards for patron circulation records.
The Maryland State Department of Education oversees public K-12 education, including school libraries that must comply with the bill's updated requirements governing patron circulation records.
The University System of Maryland operates numerous college and university libraries whose policies and procedures regarding patron circulation record disclosures are governed by this legislation.
As an independent public university, Morgan State University maintains campus libraries directly impacted by the revised restrictions on releasing patron circulation records.
Saint Mary's College of Maryland operates a public collegiate library subject to the bill's updated standards for the confidentiality and disclosure of individual circulation records.
The Maryland School for the Deaf operates school libraries subject to the state requirements regarding patron record privacy and disclosure exceptions.
The Maryland Higher Education Commission coordinates and regulates higher education institutions in Maryland, whose libraries are governed by this statutory provision.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, which issues the court orders and subpoenas explicitly authorized under the bill as valid mechanisms to compel disclosure of circulation records.

Synopsis: Establishing a Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program in the Department of Housing and Community Development to provide vouchers and housing assistance payments for low-income families that are currently on a waiting list under the federal Housing Choice Voucher Program for housing in units approved by the Department or a public housing agency, in accordance with guidelines under the federal program; and requiring the Department and public housing agencies to administer the State Program.
Title: Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program - Establishment
