bill_summary: Establishes the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development to provide rental vouchers and housing assistance payments to low-income families on the federal Housing Choice Voucher Program waiting list, with prioritization for families with children, former foster youth, veterans, homeless individuals, individuals with disabilities, and the elderly.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Low-income Maryland families on federal housing choice voucher waitlists, local public housing agencies, and rental property owners
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $255,400 in FY 2024 for DHCD administrative expenses, approximately $10.3 million annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027 (including a $10.0 million mandated appropriation and DHCD administrative costs), and approximately $10.6 million in FY 2028. Local public housing agency revenues and expenditures increase to administer vouchers, with administrative costs partially offset by a required 6% allocation of program funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary agency tasked with establishing, administering, and regulating the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program, distributing voucher funding to local public housing agencies, managing voucher operations in jurisdictions without local administrators, and reporting annually on program metrics.

DBM oversees the state budget and fiscal planning. The bill establishes a mandated general fund appropriation of $10.0 million annually for fiscal years 2025 through 2027 and requires ongoing funding for subsequent years to maintain voucher levels.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a mandated appropriation of $10.0 million for the program in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2027, along with sufficient funding in later years, and mandates an annual report submitted to the Governor.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain vacant property or nuisance property located in Baltimore City to be subject to a certain in rem foreclosure process; requiring certain procedures for an in rem foreclosure; requiring Baltimore City to take certain actions to compensate the interested parties in property that has value and is acquired through an in rem foreclosure; specifying the title acquired in an in rem foreclosure; specifying the circumstances under which an in rem foreclosure judgment may be reopened; etc.
Title: Baltimore City - Property Tax - In Rem Foreclosure of Vacant or Nuisance Property

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds

bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City to enact local laws establishing a judicial in rem foreclosure process for vacant or nuisance properties with delinquent taxes. The bill outlines required legal procedures, notice and service requirements, hearing processes in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City, compensation or public auction requirements for properties with value, and standards for reopening foreclosure judgments.
responsible_party: Baltimore City and the Circuit Court for Baltimore City
stakeholders: Owners, mortgagees, and interested parties of vacant or nuisance properties in Baltimore City, Baltimore City municipal government, and local residents and businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2024 for the Circuit Court for Baltimore City clerk's office to process additional foreclosure filings, and Annuity Bond Fund revenues may be affected depending on state property tax collection timing; specific estimates are unavailable. Baltimore City finances will be affected by administrative and maintenance costs, potential revenue from tax collections and property sales, and compensation paid to interested parties for properties retaining value.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes judicial in rem foreclosure proceedings in the Circuit Court for Baltimore City, requiring the court to handle complaint filings, hold hearings, issue judgments, and oversee the distribution of escrowed funds. The fiscal note specifically identifies potential increases in General Fund expenditures for additional staff and operating costs for the Baltimore City Circuit Court clerk's office.

The bill addresses vacant and nuisance property acquisition and tax sales in Baltimore City, directly aligning with the Department's mission and programs surrounding urban community revitalization and blight elimination.

Synopsis: Altering a certain provision relating to the storage of firearms and ammunition in a location that can be accessed by an unsupervised child; and requiring the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services to develop a youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide, with recommendations from a stakeholder committee.
Title: Firearm Safety - Storage Requirements and Youth Suicide Prevention (Jaelynn's Law)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Advance Medical Directives; Wrongful Death
Health -see also- Mental and Behavioral Health
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Jaelynn's Law expands child firearm safe storage laws by prohibiting individuals from storing or leaving firearms where an unsupervised minor (under 18) or a prohibited person is likely to gain access. It imposes restrictions on possessing regulated firearms for individuals convicted of violations, and requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop a youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide with stakeholder input and provide safe storage education grants.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services)
stakeholders: Firearm owners, minors and youth, families, local school systems, local health departments, community and behavioral health providers, firearm dealers, and law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2024 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire an external consultant to create the safe storage guide and coordinate the stakeholder advisory committee. Minimal increases in State general fund revenues and local revenues may occur from criminal penalties. State and local incarceration expenditures may increase minimally. Grant-related expenditures cannot be reliably estimated as funding was not identified in the FY 2024 budget.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that MDH's Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services establish a stakeholder advisory committee, develop a youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide, publish and distribute it to various stakeholders, administer a grant program, and submit annual implementation reports to the General Assembly.

MSP is the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing firearm regulations and restrictions on possession under Title 5 of the Public Safety Article. Additionally, the bill specifically directs distribution of the safe storage guide to instructors certified by the Department of State Police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal prohibitions and penalties regarding firearm storage and possession of regulated firearms, which has a potential fiscal impact on state correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation.

MSDE and local school systems are explicitly designated to receive and distribute the youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide, and local school systems are eligible to receive MDH grants under the bill.
DJS is specifically designated in statute to receive and make available the youth suicide prevention and firearm safe storage guide to youth, families, and programs.
The bill alters and expands criminal misdemeanor penalties and firearm possession restrictions, directly impacting judicial caseloads and court operations.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $1,000,000 annual appropriation in the state budget beginning in fiscal year 2025 to fund the safe storage guide and grant program.
DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and implementing the bill's statutory mandate requiring an annual $1,000,000 appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2025.
The bill references hunter safety certificates issued by DNR under § 10-301.1 of the Natural Resources Article as an exception to certain firearm storage restrictions.

Synopsis: Altering requirements for the removal from office of the State Administrator of Elections; and repealing the authority of the State Administrator to continue to serve in office until a successor is appointed and confirmed following a certain vote for removal of the State Administrator.
Title: State Administrator of Elections - Removal From Office

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Alters the requirements for removing the State Administrator of Elections by allowing removal upon the affirmative vote of four members of the five-member State Board of Elections, repealing requirements that removal be for cause with written charges and a hearing, and eliminating the administrator's ability to stay in office until a successor is appointed and confirmed.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections
stakeholders: The State Administrator of Elections and the State Board of Elections.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances and has no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Senate Bill 863 directly alters the legal standards and procedural requirements for the State Board of Elections to remove the State Administrator of Elections from office, impacting the agency's executive leadership governance.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Social Work Examiners in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law) by extending to July 1, 2025, the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board; establishing the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure to make certain findings and recommendations regarding examination and licensure of social workers in the State; requiring the Workgroup to submit its final report to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2024; etc.
Title: Social Workers - Sunset Extension, Notification of Complete Application, and Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees
Health Occupations -see also- specific health occupations
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications;Drivers' Licenses
Studies -see also- Committees and Commissions; Reports

bill_summary: This emergency bill extends the termination date for the State Board of Social Work Examiners by one year to July 1, 2025, under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. It requires the Board to notify license applicants within 15 business days after receiving an application or supplemental materials whether their application is complete. Additionally, it establishes the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure to evaluate social work licensing exams, assess potential bias, explore alternatives to examination requirements, and report its findings and recommendations by December 2024.
responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Prospective and current social workers, applicants for social work licensure, and the State Board of Social Work Examiners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2024 (reflecting a contingent appropriation for board operations and staffing) and $15,400 in FY 2025 for part-time contractual staff supporting the workgroup. The Board's special fund revenues and expenditures are maintained through FY 2025 due to the one-year sunset extension. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners is housed within the Department of Health. The bill extends the Board's termination date, modifies application notification timelines, tasks MDH with staffing the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure, includes the Secretary of Health as a member, and incurs MDH fiscal expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure, a temporary advisory body established to study and report on social work licensure examinations and alternatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Director of the Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, or their designee, is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure.
The Secretary of Human Services, or their designee, is appointed as a member of the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure.
The Governor is required to designate the chair of the Workgroup on Social Worker Requirements for Licensure and appoint eight members to the workgroup.

Synopsis: Generally curing previous Acts of the General Assembly with possible title defects; and generally repealing and reenacting without amendments certain Acts of the General Assembly that may be subject to possible title defects in order to validate those Acts.
Title: Annual Curative Bill
bill_summary: The Annual Curative Bill cures and validates previous Acts of the Maryland General Assembly that contained potential title defects by repealing and reenacting without amendments provisions relating to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund and prohibitions against fraudulent conduct during driver's license examinations.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland legal system, tenants seeking access to counsel in eviction proceedings, and driver's license or permit applicants.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is technical in nature and has no effect on state or local governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill cures a title defect by reenacting without amendment Transportation Article § 16-301(q), which prohibits fraudulent or dishonest conduct during driver's license and moped permit examinations and testing administered by the MVA.

The bill reenacts without amendment a provision of the Transportation Article governing driver's licensing examination fraud, which falls under the purview of MDOT and its modal administration, the MVA.
The bill cures a title defect by reenacting Real Property Article § 8-909, which designates the State Treasurer to hold and invest the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund.
The bill reenacts Real Property Article § 8-909, which specifies that the Comptroller shall account for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund.

The bill reenacts Real Property Article § 8-909, which provides that certain settlement funds recovered by the Division of Consumer Protection within the OAG are deposited into the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of a "therapy horse" under the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program.
Title: Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program – Definitions – Therapy Horse

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of a therapy horse under the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program by removing the requirement that a State-licensed stable be a premier accredited member center of the Professional Association of Therapeutic Horsemanship, International (PATH, Intl.), allowing any PATH, Intl. member center to qualify.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
stakeholders: Maryland veterans participating in service animal programs and State-licensed stables or equine therapy centers affiliated with PATH, Intl.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the change is technical in nature. Local government operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory definition of a 'therapy horse' under the Maryland Veterans Service Animal Program, which is housed within and administered by the Department of Veterans and Military Families.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Natural Resources to issue an annual fishing license and stamp exemption to governmental entities and nonprofit organizations to provide fishing clinics and instructional opportunities to certain individuals; and altering certain reporting requirements for governmental entities and nonprofit organizations that are issued certain fishing license and stamp exemptions.
Title: Natural Resources - Fishing Licenses and Stamps - Exemptions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; Gill Nets

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue annual recreational fishing license and stamp exemptions to governmental entities and nonprofit organizations that offer fishing clinics and instructional opportunities to service members, veterans, individuals participating in wellness or special needs events, scientific permit holders, and underserved residents. It also modifies reporting requirements for participating organizations.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Governmental entities, nonprofit organizations hosting fishing clinics, active-duty military service members, veterans, individuals participating in wellness or special needs outdoor events, holders of scientific collection permits, and underserved Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues into the Fisheries Management and Protection Fund and the Fisheries Research and Development Fund may increase beginning in FY 2024 if clinic participants subsequently purchase fishing licenses and stamps; however, specific dollar estimates cannot be reliably determined. Expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency responsible for issuing the annual fishing license and stamp exemptions, establishing application and reporting processes, promulgating regulations, and managing the affected special funds (Fisheries Management and Protection Fund and Fisheries Research and Development Fund).

Synopsis: Increasing the mandated appropriation that the Governor is required to include for the Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund in the annual budget bill from $250,000 to $625,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
Title: Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund - Funding - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- Driver Ed; Higher Ed; Special Ed; etc
Revenue and Taxes -see also- Dev Fees &Taxes; specific tax

bill_summary: This bill increases the annual mandated State budget appropriation for the Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund from $250,000 to $625,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2029 to support the Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation, and eliminates the mandated appropriation beginning in fiscal year 2030.
responsible_party: Office of the Governor
stakeholders: The Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation (MCCEI), construction industry employers, trainees, and students pursuing construction education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $375,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2029 to reflect the increase in the mandated appropriation to $625,000. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by corresponding amounts each year. The mandated funding terminates entirely beginning in FY 2030. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Construction Education and Innovation Fund is established under Title 11 of the Labor and Employment Article, which falls under the purview of the Maryland Department of Labor's workforce development programs.

The bill mandates an increase in the annual budget appropriation from $250,000 to $625,000 for fiscal years 2025 through 2029, directly affecting DBM's budget development and fiscal planning responsibilities.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include a specific appropriation of $625,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
The Maryland Center for Construction Education and Innovation (MCCEI), which is supported by this fund, is a public-private partnership located at Towson University, a USM institution.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Maryland Insurance Commissioner from removing from a certain list of reciprocal jurisdictions created and published by the Commissioner certain jurisdictions located outside the United States and certain jurisdictions in the United States that meet certain accreditation requirements.
Title: Insurance – Credit for Reinsurance Model Law – Reciprocal Jurisdictions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Insurance Commissioner from removing certain reciprocal jurisdictions—specifically those subject to an in-force covered agreement with the United States, EU member states, or accredited U.S. jurisdictions—from the published list of jurisdictions authorized to operate in Maryland without needing to post collateral.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Insurers and reinsurers operating in Maryland or domiciled in reciprocal jurisdictions, including accredited U.S. states and countries with covered international agreements.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the regulatory authority of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, who heads the Maryland Insurance Administration, regarding the maintenance and removal of reciprocal jurisdictions under the Credit for Reinsurance Model Law.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Historical Trust, on or before July 1, 2023, to extinguish or terminate a certain easement the Trust holds in the parcel of land known as Warner Manor (also known as Brainard Warner House and/or Circle Manor) in the Town of Kensington, Montgomery County; and requiring the Trust to complete certain necessary recordings and filings to complete the extinguishment or termination of the easement.
Title: Maryland Historical Trust - Warner Manor in the Town of Kensington - Extinguishment or Termination of Easement

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Historical Trust to terminate or extinguish an easement dated June 28, 2010, on the property known as Warner Manor (also known as Brainard Warner House or Circle Manor) located in the Town of Kensington, Montgomery County, and complete all required filings and recordings by July 1, 2023.
responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust
stakeholders: Town of Kensington, Montgomery County, property owners or managers of Warner Manor, and the Maryland Historical Trust.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact; the Maryland Historical Trust can implement the required termination and filings using existing resources, and local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Historical Trust (MHT), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Planning, extinguish or terminate a specific preservation easement held on the Warner Manor property in Montgomery County and file all necessary documentation.

Synopsis: Abolishing and repealing the Maryland 529 Board; specifying that the State Treasurer is the successor to the Maryland 529 Board; transferring to the Office of the State Treasurer the responsibility for administering the Maryland 529 Program, including the Maryland Prepaid College Trust, the Maryland College Investment Plan, the Maryland Broker-Dealer College Investment Plan, and the Maryland ABLE Program; authorizing and requiring the State Treasurer to take certain actions in administering the Maryland 529 Program; etc.
Title: Higher Education - Maryland 529 Program - Reform

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Bonds -see also- County & Baltimore City Bonds; State Bonds
Committees and Commissions -see also- Political Committees

Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill abolishes the Maryland 529 Board and transfers the administration of the Maryland 529 Program—including the Prepaid College Trust, College Investment Plan, Broker-Dealer Plan, and ABLE Program—to the Office of the State Treasurer effective June 1, 2023. It phases out the Maryland Prepaid College Trust by prohibiting new contracts or contract upgrades on or after June 1, 2023, and establishes a formal claims and settlement resolution process for account holders and beneficiaries with accounts active on or after November 1, 2021.
responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer's Office
stakeholders: Maryland 529 account holders and qualified beneficiaries (including Maryland Prepaid College Trust, College Investment Plan, and ABLE account holders) and transferred Maryland 529 employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $6.7 million in FY 2024 to support 8 new positions and operational resources for the State Treasurer's Office to implement the transition, with personnel costs continuing into future years ($810,000 to $930,000 annually). Additionally, approximately $17.0 million annually in existing nonbudgeted program operations shifts to special and reimbursable funds within the State Treasurer's Office budget. Claim settlements will be funded directly from Prepaid College Trust assets and are exempt from State and local taxes. Local revenues may see a minimal increase from foregone income tax deductions due to the phase-out of prepaid contracts; local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the State Treasurer as the successor to the Maryland 529 Board, transferring full administrative authority, assets, liabilities, and fiduciary responsibility for the Maryland 529 Program (including the Prepaid College Trust, College Investment Plan, and ABLE Program) to the State Treasurer's Office, and tasks the Treasurer with administering a claims resolution process.

The bill directly reforms and abolishes the Maryland 529 Board, transfers all of its personnel, property, duties, and programs into the Office of the State Treasurer, and closes the Maryland Prepaid College Trust to new accounts.

MHEC holds state general fund budget appropriations for Save4College matching contributions and ABLE Program administrative support that are transferred/reimbursed to STO, and the Secretary of Higher Education's ex-officio role on the Maryland 529 Board is eliminated.

The Maryland ABLE Program is administered in consultation with the Department of Disabilities; additionally, the bill adds the Secretary of Disabilities to the Financial Education and Capability Commission while removing the Maryland 529 Board seat.
The bill maintains the statutory mandate requiring the Legislative Auditor to audit the Prepaid College Trust, the College Investment Plan, the Broker-Dealer Plan, and the Maryland ABLE Program.

The Comptroller loses ex-officio membership on the abolished Maryland 529 Board, confirms taxable income for State contribution eligibility under the College Investment Plan, and oversees tax provisions affected by MPCT claims settlements and deduction changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the State Treasurer to coordinate marketing efforts with the Board of Trustees of MSRP to increase 529 program participation among state employees.
The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland had served as an ex-officio member of the Maryland 529 Board, which is abolished by this bill.
The State Superintendent of Schools served as an ex-officio member on the abolished Maryland 529 Board, and the Treasurer coordinates marketing with local school systems.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain applicant for an alcoholic beverages license in Anne Arundel County to be a resident of the State, rather than the county, when an application for a license is filed; and providing that a certain license is valid only for as long as the resident applicant remains a resident of the State.
Title: Anne Arundel County – Alcoholic Beverages Licenses – Residency Requirement
bill_summary: Alters the residency requirement for alcoholic beverages license applicants in Anne Arundel County applying on behalf of a partnership, corporation, club, or limited liability company, requiring the applicant to be a resident of Maryland rather than the county, and provides that the license remains valid only as long as the applicant remains a State resident.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants, licensees, and businesses (partnerships, corporations, clubs, and LLCs) operating or seeking to operate in Anne Arundel County, as well as Maryland residents seeking licensure.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not anticipated to materially affect Anne Arundel County operations or finances. The small business impact is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates aspects of the state's alcohol industry and oversees statutory application form requirements referenced in the bill, although the bill specifically modifies local Anne Arundel County residency requirements for alcoholic beverage licenses with no direct state fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "captive REIT" for purposes of a certain addition modification under the Maryland income tax in the amount of the federal dividends paid deduction for captive real estate investment trusts to exclude, under certain circumstances, corporations, trusts, or associations owned or controlled by certain qualified foreign entities and certain trusts owned or controlled by a listed Australian property trust.
Title: Income Tax - Captive Real Estate Investment Trusts - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of a captive real estate investment trust (REIT) under Maryland income tax law by excluding corporations, trusts, or associations owned or controlled by certain qualified foreign entities or by trusts largely controlled by a listed Australian property trust, thereby exempting them from an addition modification for the federal dividends paid deduction.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Real estate investment trusts (REITs), foreign real estate investment entities, Australian property trust affiliates, and corporate taxpayers investing in Maryland real estate.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2024, State General Fund, Higher Education Investment Fund (HEIF), and Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues may decrease by an indeterminate amount due to reduced corporate income tax liability for certain REITs. Local highway user revenues and TTF capital grant expenditures may also decrease by an indeterminate amount. A precise dollar figure cannot be determined because an analysis of individual corporate structures is required.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's tax administrator and is directly responsible for administering the corporate income tax, updating tax forms and instructions regarding captive REIT addition modifications, and adopting regulations related to REIT qualifications.

Synopsis: Requiring contractors operating State-owned nursing homes to promptly provide notice of certain deficiencies, enforcement actions, citations, and fines to the Governor, the State agency overseeing the nursing home, certain committees of the General Assembly, and members of the General Assembly who represent the district in which the nursing home is located; etc.
Title: State-Owned Nursing Homes - Deficiencies, Citations, and Fines - Contractor Reporting Requirements

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Contractors -see also- Heating & Cooling; Home Improvement
Nursing Homes -see also- Continuing Care; Long-Term Care

bill_summary: Requires contractors operating State-owned nursing homes to promptly notify the Governor, overseeing State agencies, and relevant legislative committees and members of deficiencies, enforcement actions, citations, and fines issued by monitoring agencies. It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly detailing survey activities and enforcement actions regarding contractor-operated State-owned nursing homes.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Residents and staff of State-owned nursing homes (such as Charlotte Hall Veterans Home), private contractors operating State-owned nursing homes, and state regulatory and legislative officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources, with no impact on state revenues. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly defines the Office of Health Care Quality within MDH as a monitoring agency and mandates that MDH submit an annual report to the Governor and the General Assembly detailing survey activities and enforcement actions at contractor-operated State-owned nursing homes.

The department oversees the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, a State-owned nursing home operated by a private contractor. Under the bill, contractors operating such facilities must promptly notify and provide detailed deficiency, citation, and corrective action documentation to the overseeing agency.

The Governor's Office is mandated to receive prompt notices, deficiency statements, plans of correction, and communications regarding citations/fines from contractors operating State-owned nursing homes, as well as an annual report from the Department of Health.
